title: Nick Sirianni: "I lost us that game"
summary: The NFL's decision to move the touchback from the 30 to the 35 continues to create some crazy end of game situations.
full_text: The NFL's decision to move the touchback from the 30 to the 35 continues to create some crazy end of game situations. And some interesting late-game decisions. Two weeks after the Cowboys made the wrong decision to put the kickoff into the end zone and concede the 35 against the Ravens in Rio, the Eagles made the wrong decision to put the ball in play against the Jaguars in London. With eight seconds left after a 48-yard field goal put the Eagles ahead 17-16, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni opted to kick the ball into the landing zone. Jaguars running back Ameer Abdullah caught the ball at the eight and returned it 53 yards in seven seconds. And a 57-yard field goal from Cam Little gave Jacksonville the win. After the game, Sirianni took the blame for the loss. "You know, the guys fought so hard, and then I don't make the decision that, you know, that I should make at the end of the game, and I cost us that game, and I put that fully on me," Sirianni told reporters. "At the end of the day, I didn't make the right decision and it cost us the game. You know, and so there's no other way around it. There's nothing really else to say about that. It's just, you know, I didn't do my job good enough in that situation." Sirianni was asked whether he watched the end of the Ravens-Cowboys game and other games with key decisions to make as to the strategy of the kickoff. "Yeah, I watched a ton of those," Sirianni said. "I watch a ton of those situations. You know, obviously we had one against Tennessee. I watched a ton of those situations after that Dallas game, and again, just didn't make the right decision in this particular case." Sirianni said the decision will stick with him the same way late-game mistakes that he made as a player have lingered in his memories. "It's just like you would feel if you missed a free throw at the end of the game, or if you had a drop," Sirianni said. "I've been in both of those places. And those ones stick with you, and that will stick with me for a long time. All I know is that I'll work my butt off to get better from it. But, yeah, that one will hurt for a long time. I still think about those other things that have, I've lost games for us in the past as far as, you know, when I played." Here's the key in this case. The Jaguars, unlike the Ravens, didn't have a timeout in their pocket. It would have been much easier for Philly to defend the sidelines in the area of Cam Little's maximum range. And Sirianni knows it. If nothing else, his mistake provides further guidance to everyone else as to the touchback/no touchback decision in the final seconds of a half or a game. Here's the obvious lesson: If the team that will be receiving the ball doesn't have a timeout left, put it in the end zone.
author: Mike Florio

title: Nico Collins on C.J. Stroud: That dude is hooping
summary: The Texans got their first victory of the season on Sunday, beating the moribund Titans, 26-3.
full_text: The Texans got their first victory of the season on Sunday, beating the moribund Titans, 26-3. After the contest, receiver Nico Collins talked up his quarterback, C.J. Stroud, who has been putting up solid performances — despite Houston’s current 1-4 record. “That dude is hooping,” Collins said, via transcript from the team. “Everything that is happening right now is the work you put in throughout the week. Coming in leading, as he always does. “We always got his back a thousand percent of the way and it's only right to continue to keep going, continue to be us, and continue to be 1-0.” Stroud’s first touchdown of the day came on the ground, as he ran it in from 2 yards out midway through the third quarter. “That man got a little speed on him,” Collins said. "He got in that thing, and I am proud of him. I am happy to see him touch paint, run his feet. He lowered his shoulder, it’s football.” Stroud later fired a 9-yard touchdown to Jaylin Noel. He ended the day 26-of-34 passing for 261 yards with a TD. In five games this season, he’s completed 64.3 percent of his throws for 1,402 yards with six touchdowns and no picks.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Seahawks' second-quarter blunder handed 49ers an easy touchdown
summary: Thanks to Dan Quinn's colossal clock-mismanagement error, plenty of other mistakes made by NFL coaches from Week 5 weren't as conspicuous as they should have been.
full_text: ' Thanks to Dan Quinn's colossal clock-mismanagement error, plenty of other mistakes made by NFL coaches from Week 5 weren't as conspicuous as they should have been. One possible blunder requires further consideration. With 18 seconds left in the second quarter, the Seahawks called a running play. From their own four yard line. Running back George Holani (who had dropped the ball without contact earlier in the half) fumbled, and the 49ers recovered it for a touchdown. During PFT Live , Simms said the Seahawks should have just taken a knee and ended the half. It was indeed a nonsensical decision, on the surface, to run the ball. It's not as if the Seahawks were going to pop a 96-yard touchdown run. They opened the door to a possible turnover, and the turnover happened. After the show, I took a closer look at the situation. The Seahawks had exhausted their timeouts as a 49ers' drive in Seattle territory sputtered, forcing a punt with 27 seconds left. The fourth-down play from the Seahawks' 42 resulted in a punt that was touched at the four and downed before entering the end zone. At that point, the Seahawks had a problem. The 49ers had all three timeouts in hand. If the Seahawks had opted to take a knee, and if the 49ers had used their timeouts, Seattle would have been punting out of their own end zone with roughly 10 seconds left. And even if the clock had expired on the punt, a fair catch would have set the stage for a free kick on an untimed down from the spot of the fair catch, and a potential three points. So the Seahawks tried to gain some yards and churn some clock. The problem is that Holani fumbled. The other question is whether the Seahawks should have refrained from calling their own timeouts. If that had happened, however, the 49ers could have allowed the clock to run down to the final seconds, with either a Hail Mary throw or a 60-yard field goal attempt to end the half. There was no easy way out of the maze, and the ability of the 49ers to put the ball inside the five put the Seahawks in a box. The easy solution is don't fumble. The more important consideration is whether a guy who dropped the ball earlier in the half should have been trusted to possess the ball so close to his own goal line. Regardless, that was a big moment that the Seahawks then had to fight to overcome in the second half. And while they did indeed take a 23-21 lead (and later a 26-21 lead), it would have been a lot easier for the Seahawks to win if they hadn't handed the 49ers an easy seven points right before intermission.
author: Mike Florio

title: C.J. Stroud on reuniting with Marvin Harrison Jr.: It's perfect for him
summary: Coach DeMeco Ryans twice declined to answer questions about whether the Texans had completed a trade with the Cardinals for wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr.
full_text: Coach DeMeco Ryans twice declined to answer questions about whether the Texans had completed a trade with the Cardinals for wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. The third time, as he was concluding his postgame news conference, Ryans confirmed the trade. "You guys wanna know, huh?" Ryans said, smiling. "Yes, we traded for Marvin Harrison. See ya." The move reunites Harrison with quarterback C.J. Stroud, who played with the wide receiver at Ohio State. Harrison played sparingly his freshman season with the Buckeyes but had 77 receptions for 1,263 yards and 14 touchdowns in 2022 with Stroud as his quarterback. "I think he brings a dynamic playmaker, somebody who runs great routes and can catch pretty much any ball," Stroud said after the Texans' 26-3 win over the Titans. "I'm super excited to get to work with him. I loved him in college. He's probably the hardest worker I've ever been around in my life, and then there's who he is off the field. He's a great dude, a quiet guy, but you definitely feel his presence. "I'm excited to get him here, get him learning and get him around the other guys. I think it's perfect for him. Fresh starts are good, so I'm excited to have him with us." Harrison, who was inactive for the Cardinals on Sunday with the trade looming, has five catches for 85 yards and a touchdown this season. The 2024 first-round pick has 108 catches for 1,578 yards and 13 touchdowns in his career.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jaylen Warren runs over Colts as Steelers win 34-22
summary: The running back finished with 101 rushing yards and a TD on 15 carries and six catches for 87 yards and a TD.
full_text: Jaylen Warren had an 80-yard touchdown reception and a 50-yard touchdown run, leading the Steelers to a 34-22 win over the Colts on Sunday afternoon. Warren finished with 101 rushing yards and a touchdown on 15 carries and six catches for 87 yards and a touchdown. The Steelers are 3-2 and the Colts 2-3. Aaron Rodgers had his third consecutive three-touchdown game, with Terry Bradshaw the only other quarterback in team history to accomplish that feat. Rodgers threw touchdowns of 80 yards to Warren, 1 yard to Pat Freiermuth and 17 yards to Freiermuth. Rodgers completed 22 of 31 passes for 235 yards. Freiermuth had five catches for 44 yards and Germie Bernard six for 80. The Colts were outgained 352 to 332 yards, but they went only 1-for-3 in the red zone. They kicked Spencer Shrader field goals from the 4, 22 and 10 after stalling. Indianapolis was 4-of-15 on third down and 3-of-5 on fourth down. Daniel Jones was 24-of-44 for 267 yards, with Tyler Warren catching seven for 83. Warren also had a 1-yard touchdown run. Jonathan Taylor rushed for only 45 yards on 15 carries.
author: Charean Williams

title: Kyler Murray is looking like Kyler Murray again
summary: Through a brief appearance in Week 1 and a pair of starts in Week 3 and Week 4, Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray didn't seem much like Kyler Murray.
full_text: Through a brief appearance in Week 1 and a pair of starts in Week 3 and Week 4, Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray didn't seem much like Kyler Murray . The offensive rookie of the year version. The two-time Pro Bowler version. The Road Runner version. On Sunday, "meep meep" made its way to New Orleans. Murray looked like the Murray of old again. He completed 24 of 30 passes for 229 yards, one touchdown, no interceptions, and a passer rating of 109.6. He added 51 rushing yards on 10 attempts. Per the Vikings, the performance made Murray the first quarterback in franchise history to throw for 200 or more yards with an 80-percent completion percentage while rushing for 50 or more yards. The first hint of the offense waking up came last week, after the Dolphins cut the score of the Week 4 game to 12-10 late in the third quarter. Murray engineered the drive that extended the lead to five and then, after a three-and-out, Murray guided the offense toward consuming the rest of the clock. Indeed, since Miami's touchdown on the next-to-last play of the third quarter, Murray has completed 36 of 43 passes (83.7 percent). It felt different this week, with Murray playing well from the start of the game to the finish. Even with a couple of significant momentum-shifting miscues, Murray and the Minnesota offense were never rattled. After the Saints returned a Myles Price fumble 87 yards for the game-tying touchdown, the Vikings drove 70 yards in six plays for the go-ahead touchdown. One more scoring drive provided the final margin of 23-13. Now, the Vikings enter their bye with a chance to get healthy and prepare for games against the Colts, Lions, Bills, Packers, and 49ers in a Sunday night showdown in Mexico City.
author: Mike Florio

title: Drake Maye throws for 160 yards and two TDs in first half as Patriots roll over Raiders
summary: Reports of Drake Maye's demise were greatly exaggerated.
full_text: '' Reports of Drake Maye's demise were greatly exaggerated. Maye is looking great for the second straight week as the Patriots have jumped out to a 21-7 halftime lead over the Raiders. Maye has completed 11 of 15 passes for 160 yards, with two touchdowns and no interceptions. Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins has also played well, completing 10 of 15 passes for 123 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions, but the Raiders have had a couple of long drives stall, one ending in a punt and one ending in a missed field goal. The Raiders are going to need Cousins to lead them into the end zone in the second half, or else Maye is going to roll to his second straight win.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Broncos rally late for 23-17 win, send Chargers to 0-5
summary: The Denver offense didn't show much improvement, but the Broncos got a win.
full_text: '' The Broncos still have plenty of work to do on the offensive side of the ball, but they'll get a chance to do it coming off of a win. Head coach Sean Payton's decision to take back offensive playcalling responsibilities didn't lead to a clear improvement over previous weeks, but the unit was able to do enough to take advantage of Chargers mistakes in the fourth quarter to pull out a win. The 23-17 win moves them to 3-2 on the season and it leaves the Chargers to wait at least another week for their first win. The Chargers scored a pair of touchdowns in the third quarter to jump into a 17-10 lead and they had a chance to pin the Broncos deep in their own territory with a punt with around 10 minutes left to play. Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh opted to go for it on fourth-and-1 from his own 41-yard-line, however, and Justin Herbert was stuffed way short on a sneak. Bo Nix threw a touchdown pass to Courtland Sutton on the ensuing drive and Broncos defensive lineman D.J. Jones forced a Herbert fumble on the ensuing drive. The Broncos opted to kick a field goal after their drive stalled on the 1-yard-line and then added another after safety Brandon Jones picked Herbert off on the next Chargers possession. Herbert now has nine turnovers on the season and the Chargers helped set up the first Broncos touchdown of the day with another turnover, so it was another chapter in the nightmare that has been unfolding for the team since Week 1. They'll be in Kansas City next Sunday to face a well-rested Chiefs team that's looking to move to 5-0. The Broncos only had 95 yards of offense in the second half, they went 1-of-12 on third downs and they had no first downs on any of the drives that were not set up by Chargers turnovers, so Payton certainly didn't correct all that was wrong when Davis Webb was sending in the plays. He'll have a short week to try to make progress and a tough defense to work against in Seattle on Thursday night.
author: Josh Alper

title: Lions' Tom Kennedy, Devin White will both miss time with injuries suffered Sunday
summary: The Lions lost linebacker Devin White and receiver/returner Tom Kennedy to injuries on Sunday in Arizona, and both appear likely to miss some time, but not the entire season.
full_text: The Lions lost linebacker Devin White and receiver/returner Tom Kennedy to injuries on Sunday in Arizona, and both appear likely to miss some time, but not the entire season. Lions head coach Dan Campbell didn't have a definitive diagnosis but indicated that he was concerned about both. "I think Devin's going to need surgery, broken forearm," Campbell said. "It's unfortunate. I hate it because he was doing some good things for us." Campbell had similar thoughts about Kennedy. "TK, doesn't look good. As far as anything short-term, we'll know a lot more tomorrow. I think it could be a sprain, somewhere in there, pretty good sprain," Campbell said. Campbell did indicate that both will be back before the season is over. "Neither one of them are going to be around for a little bit here. I hate that. Both players have done a good job for us," Campbell said. "I don't think it's going to be a long, long term. We'll miss them for a little bit."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Sunday Night Football: Ravens come back to beat Falcons in OT, 30-23
summary: Derrick Henry had 120 yards from scrimmage and a TD in the victory. Michael Penix Jr. had to exit late with a rib injury.
full_text: The Ravens were down by eight with two timeouts when they got the ball back with 2:25 on the clock in regulation. It took them 1:51 to score a touchdown and a two-point conversion to tie the game. Then they scored again with a Tyler Huntley 1-yard run in overtime, and Kyle Hamilton grabbed an interception to seal a 30-23 victory. With Lamar Jackson out due to an ankle injury, the Ravens were nevertheless effective on offense, with Tyler Huntley completing 24-of-32 passes for 201 yards with two touchdowns. He also had six carries for 20 yards with the game-winning TD in overtime. Derrick Henry rushed for 102 yards and caught an 18-yard touchdown to help pace the offense. Justice Hill also had 73 yards on the ground, including a 47-yard run that set up a score. The Falcons led for much of the game and even had a shot to win at the end of regulation with 40 seconds on the clock and two timeouts. But starting quarterback Michael Penix Jr. took a hard hit to his side as he was sacked with 27 seconds left in regulation and ended up suffering a rib injury. Tua Tagovailoa played one snap in the fourth quarter after Penix was injured. While Penix tried to come back in, he was clearly holding his side and looked to be in pain. After Huntley scored in overtime, Tagovailoa came back in to play Atlanta’s final drive. It actually started well with a 20-yard completion to Drake London, who finished the game with seven catches for 118 yards. But then it all fell apart, as Tagovailoa’s pass on the next snap went right to Baltimore’s Kyle Hamilton for a game-ending interception. Penix was announced as questionable to return with a rib injury. But with under three minutes left in overtime, he was, for all intents and purposes, out. Penix finished 19-of-32 for 240 with one touchdown. Bijan Robinson had 17 carries for 86 yards and caught four passes for 32 yards. Now at 4-1, the Ravens will be on the road again in Week 6 to play division rival Cleveland. The 2-3 Falcons will stay at home to play the Bears in Week 6. But they may have to play a backup at quarterback.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Dre Greenlaw could be facing another suspension
summary: NFL will review Sunday's conduct that resulted in an ejection for further discipline.
full_text: ''' The 5-0 49ers had to play without linebacker Dre Greenlaw for more than two quarters. Next Monday night against the Commanders, they could be missing him for all four quarters. Greenlaw's ejection for head-butting Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones IV (who wasn't wearing a helmet at the time) could result in a suspension. The NFL will review the situation on Monday for potential discipline. And that discipline could include preventing Greenlaw from playing in Week 6. The play itself was inherently unsafe. While not the same as the time when then-Browns defensive end Myles Garrett struck still-Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph with his own helmet, striking someone who isn't wearing a helmet in the head with a helmet should be a bright line, when it comes to discipline. Then there's Greenlaw's history. He has now been ejected three times. In 2022, Greenlaw was sent to the showers prematurely for an illegal hit on Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert. In 2023, Greenlaw was tossed after a sideline incident that first introduced a national audience to the legend known widely as Big Dom . Last year, Greenlaw was suspended for one game, as a result of his post-game interactions with referee Brad Allen following a game between the Giants and the Broncos, for whom Greenlaw played in 2025. And, just last week, Greenlaw had some harsh post-game words for Denver coach Sean Payton after a Broncos-49ers game. (Greenlaw was fined for taunting during the game.) If a suspension will be imposed, it likely will happen on Monday. An expedited appeal would follow.
author: Mike Florio

title: Packers LB Zaire Franklin: Luther Burden said he'd make us quit, but he quit Sunday
summary: The Packers blew leads late in losses to the Bears in both the regular season and playoffs last season, which would have provided Green Bay with plenty of motivation for Sunday's game at Lambeau Field all by itself.
full_text: The Packers blew leads late in losses to the Bears in both the regular season and playoffs last season, which would have provided Green Bay with plenty of motivation for Sunday's game at Lambeau Field all by itself. Bears wide receiver Luther Burden gave them a little but more ahead of the game, however. Burden said this week that the Bears wanted to "beat them real bad and make them quit" and his thoughts were noted in the Packers' locker room. After the Packers rolled to a 31-7 over their NFC North rivals, linebacker Zaire Franklin called out Burden in his postgame comments. "You got guys that never really made a real play in this league talkin' bout making somebody quit ," Franklin said, via Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com. "That's weird. We don't do that. He quit today, by the way. He ain't wanna play anymore." Burden had six catches for 47 yards in the loss.
author: Josh Alper

title: Sean Payton: Offense was good enough to win, but things we need to improve on
summary: Broncos head coach Sean Payton's return to calling the team's offensive plays didn't result in a transformation on that side of the ball against the Chargers on Sunday.
full_text: ' Broncos head coach Sean Payton's return to calling the team's offensive plays didn't result in a transformation on that side of the ball against the Chargers on Sunday. The Broncos got a touchdown on their second offensive possession of the game, but their next eight possessions featured six first downs and three points along with a turnover, a missed field goal and four punts. Two Chargers turnovers and a failed fourth down try gave the Broncos short fields that they turned into 13 points that erased a Chargers lead and lifted them to a 23-17 road win. The Broncos were 1-of-12 on third downs and their 224 yards of offense were their fewest since Week 1, so it's no surprise that Payton's main focus after the game was on the final score rather than the overall offensive production. "It was good enough to win , but there’s still a number of things that we’ve got to improve on," Payton said. Payton said there were "small steps" in the right direction, but they'll need to be clearer and more consistent moving forward for the Broncos to put all concerns about the state of the offense to rest.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mike LaFleur on possible QB change after latest loss: "Jacoby [Brissett] was not the problem"
summary: The Cardinals lost their franchise-record ninth straight home game on Sunday, in blowout fashion to the Lions.
full_text: The Cardinals lost their franchise-record ninth straight home game on Sunday, in blowout fashion to the Lions. After landing on the wrong side of a 45-21 final score, first-year coach Mike LaFleur was asked whether he's considering a quarterback change. "I've got way too many other things, you know, that I need to correct right now," LaFleur told reporters. "Jacoby [Brissett] was not the problem. We were a problem as a team today. And, again, that starts with me." The Cardinals, after winning in Week 1 at the Chargers, have now lost four in a row. The Cardinals last won at home on September 14, 2025. Next week, the face the Rams in L.A. Then, the Broncos comes to town. After that, the Cardinals visit the Cowboys. Then, the Cardinals go to Seattle. After that, the Rams visit. After that, the Cardinals play the Chiefs in Kansas City. That 1-4 record could end up being 1-10 before the Commanders arrive in Week 12. With Arizona's bye not coming until Week 14, the time could be coming for a flip from Brissett to rookie Carson Beck, if only to let the Cardinals evaluate whether they should ride with Beck in 2027 or target a quarterback with what could be a top-five pick in the 2027 draft.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jahmyr Gibbs "for sure" trying to break LaDainian Tomlinson's single-season TD record
summary: Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs scored a pair of touchdowns in Sunday's 45-24 win over the Cardinals and that pushed him ahead of a Lions legend for the most touchdowns before the age of 25 in NFL history.
full_text: '' Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs scored a pair of touchdowns in Sunday's 45-24 win over the Cardinals and that pushed him ahead of a Lions legend for the most touchdowns before the age of 25 in NFL history. Gibbs has scored 58 touchdowns, which is one more than Barry Sanders managed early in his time with Detroit. Gibbs can add to that lead over the rest of the season and he'll be way ahead if he realizes another one of his goals. After the game, Gibbs told reporters that he has his eye on LaDainian Tomlinson's single-season record of 31 touchdowns. "For sure, I’m trying to get that ," Gibbs said. Gibbs has nine touchdowns through the first five weeks of the season and the Lions aren't shying away from giving him the kind of workload he'll need to break that record. He has a league-high 132 touches and the Lions will likely keep feeding him on a regular basis given what Gibbs has shown he's able to do with the ball in his hands.
author: Josh Alper

title: Failed fourth-down play in 49ers-Seahawks shows importance of digital mapping
summary: They say football is a game of inches.
full_text: They say football is a game of inches. At a key moment in Sunday's game in Seattle, it was a game of millimeters. With the Seahawks facing fourth and 10 from the 50, quarterback Sam Darnold threw a pass to receiver Cooper Kupp, who dove for the line to gain at the sideline. As explained by NFL V.P. of instant replay Mark Butterworth in a pool report, the proper spot is where the ball is when it breaks the plane of the sideline. Given the high bar that applies to replay review ("clear and obvious evidence") it would have been impossible to overturn the ruling on the field. It would have been possible, with comprehensive digital mapping, to know where the ball was in relation to the first-down line when the ball crossed the sideline. We saw it during the World Cup, with FIFA almost instantly knowing whether a player was offside. The league currently is able to determine whether a manually spotted ball has made it to the sticks. The NFL has yet to incorporate technology into the ball itself. Sunday's situation is a prime example of how technology would have allowed the officials to pinpoint whether the ball did, or didn't, get as far as it needed to go before the ball went out of bounds. It's relatively simple. And the expense is worth it, in the name of getting the calls right. Hopefully, the NFL will eventually get there. If it already was there, there would be no doubt as to whether the Seahawks did, or didn't, keep a potential game-tying (or game-winning) drive alive.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sunday Ticket glitch keeps customers from watching all of certain late-afternoon games
summary: It should be an easy fix to ensure that those plunked down $400 will get what they paid for.
full_text: YouTube reportedly believes the NFL could " deconstruct " Sunday Ticket as of 2030. Some customers could surely think of more graphic and profane verbs to describe their preferred fate of the league's out-of-market game service. It was marketed for years as a way for a fan who, for example, doesn't live in Pittsburgh to watch all Steelers games. As the antitrust problems became more and more obvious, given the sky-high price the league attaches to the package in order to encourage fans to settle for the "free" Fox and CBS games in their local markets, the tagline became that it's a way for zealous fans to watch all games. But that continues to have a significant asterisk that YouTube and the NFL have yet to rectify. When "bonus coverage" of an early game trickles into the 4:25 p.m. ET window, a fan not in either market of the two teams involved in the 4:25 p.m. ET game won't see the early phases of it on their local Fox or CBS affiliates. And, because the game is due to eventually be available on their local Fox or CBS channels, it's completely blacked out of Sunday Ticket. It has already happened multiple times this season. On Sunday, folks not in Seattle or San Francisco (or who were getting Lions-Cardinals as the 4:25 p.m. ET game) had no way to watch 49ers-Seahawks until "bonus coverage" of the 70-minute Giants-Commanders game ended. (Our friend and former PFT Live producer Rob "Stats" Guerrera sounded off about it .) Eventually, the 49ers-Seahawks broadcast began on the Fox affiliates televising the game with 4:47 left in the first quarter. The same dynamic kept Lions and Cardinals fans not in Detroit or Phoenix from watching the early portions of the Lions-Cardinals game. It makes no sense. People pay a premium to be able to watch every minute of every game, but they can't watch on Sunday Ticket all of a game that is not yet being televised by their local Fox or CBS affiliates. Here's where it becomes even more bizarre. In Detroit and Phoenix (and wherever else Lions-Cardinals was the 4:25 p.m. ET Fox game ), folks with Sunday Ticket got to see all of the 49ers-Seahawks game. In the vast majority of the markets where 49ers-Seahawks was "America's Game of the Week," all of Lions-Cardinals was available on Sunday Ticket. It should be an easy fix. Late-afternoon games that otherwise could be partially preempted if one of the early games takes longer than three hours and 25 minutes to conclude should be available on Sunday Ticket until the game is available on their local Fox or CBS affiliates. In this age of AI (or SI, lest you be regarded an enemy of the people), a simple mechanism could be put in place to lift the Sunday Ticket blackout until the "bonus coverage" ends on the local channel. While the NFL has far bigger legal fish to fry given the antitrust issues raised by the pricing and the all-or-nothing purchasing obligation of Sunday Ticket, the league is inviting a specific class action from those folks who have plunked down $400 to see all games every Sunday, but who are kept from seeing much if not most of the first quarter of one of the biggest games of the week.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dan Quinn committed a fireable offense, and ownership knows it
summary: Quinn is ultimately responsible for one of the worst examples of clock management, ever.
full_text: As George Carlin once said, somewhere there's a doctor who is the worst doctor in the world. And he's seeing patients tomorrow. We've now seen the worst example of clock mismanagement by an NFL coach in years, if not ever. And Dan Quinn may not be working tomorrow. The inexplicable failure to attempt what would have been a game-winning field goal because the clock ran out becomes the most baffling, inexcusable failure to turn a potential win into not a win. The Commanders had the ball at the Giants' 26 with 55 seconds left in overtime, on a stopped clock. The Commanders ran the ball, gaining two yards. And the clock ticked. And ticked. And ticked. They huddled. And the clock ticked. And ticked. And ticked. The Commanders eventually snapped the ball with three seconds on the play clock, and 12 on the game clock. Quarterback Jayden Daniels began to drop back for a throw before running the ball, losing a yard. When the play ended, eight seconds remained. Then seven. Then six. They eventually realized what was happening. Then five. Then four. By the time they lined up to try to spike the ball and kill the clock, the clock had killed them. There's no explanation for it. And it ultimately lands on the man in charge of the team on game day. The question now becomes what the people in charge of the organization will do. One of the owners has already chimed in. " I’m in total disbelief my Commanders had such poor clock management in today’s overtime game against the Giants," limited partner Magic Johnson said on Twitter. "All we had to do was kick the field goal and we would have won the game!" He added a facepalm emoji. Perhaps only because there's no pink-slip emoji. It's ultimately the prerogative of majority owner Josh Harris as to whether Quinn will survive this come Monday. Even if he does, it now becomes much harder for him to survive come Black Monday.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba: I was thinking too much on late drop
summary: Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba has come through for the Seahawks many times over the past couple of seasons, but he wasn't able to do so late in Sunday's 32-29 loss to the 49ers.
full_text: Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba has come through for the Seahawks many times over the past couple of seasons, but he wasn't able to do so late in Sunday's 32-29 loss to the 49ers. After the 49ers kicked a go-ahead field goal on the first play after the two-minute warning in the fourth quarter, Smith-Njigba picked up 35 yards on a first-down throw from Sam Darnold to get the Seahawks near midfield. He took a big hit and stayed down an extra beat when Darnold tried to connect with him again on the next play, but it was the third down play that will linger as the Seahawks process their loss. Smith-Njigba was open on that play and Darnold put a pass on him, but the wideout couldn't control it and the Seahawks' chances were dashed when Cooper Kupp was ruled out of bounds short of the sticks on fourth down. After the game, Smith-Njigba reflected on the drop. “I guess I was thinking too muc h at that time," Smith-Njigba said. "Just needed to play free and catch the ball at the end of the day. . . . I had the chance to catch the ball, so really just catch the ball. Catch the damn football at the end of the day. I know I'll make the next one." Smith-Njigba did not expand on whether the first-down hit or an ankle issue that led to a heavy tape job in the first half were among the things on his mind, but it was a rare and poorly timed lapse from the Seahawks' reliable star. He'll have to shake it off quickly as the Seahawks will be back on the field in Denver on Thursday night.
author: Josh Alper

title: Commanders' OT meltdown puts plenty of players in an awkward spot
summary: The aftermath of Sunday's overtime disaster from the Commanders will resonate for the remainder of the 2026 season, and perhaps beyond.
full_text: ' The aftermath of Sunday's overtime disaster from the Commanders will resonate for the remainder of the 2026 season, and perhaps beyond. Especially because it forced the players to answer for the malpractice of the coaches. And it was malpractice. First and 10 from the Giants' 26 with 55 seconds to play and no timeouts. A run, followed by a lackadaisical effort to start the next play, which began with 12 seconds left. Then came another run, with no individual or collective awareness that the precious few remaining seconds of overtime were slipping away. Coach Dan Quinn, who was ultimately responsible for the debacle, answered for it after the game. Quarterback Jayden Daniels, who could have recognized what was happening and thrown the ball into the dirt to kill the clock, answered for it, too. Plenty of other players had to answer for something that wasn't their fault. Tight end Ben Sinnott, for example, was caught in an awkward spot when pressed for details in the locker room after the game. "I run onto the field," Sinnott said, via Scott Abraham of 7 News DC. "I get the play call and we execute the play." Did Sinnott know the Commanders were out of timeouts? "Exactly how it went, right as I said," Sinnott replied. " No comment ." No comment is needed. It was objectively awful. This is the NFL, not Pop Warner. And it was a division game in the NFC East. The Commanders had a chance to kick a potential game-winning field goal, and they froze up. They glitched. They handled the situation as poorly as they could have handled it. I know it sounds harsh, but Quinn should not be employed at this time tomorrow. Only clear and unequivocal accountability will wash the stench of what happened on Sunday away. Any other outcome will cause the confusion, the doubt, and the resentment to linger. Former Chargers head coach Anthony Lynn is the running backs coach. Put him in charge and give him a chance to earn the job for 2027. Whether the players will admit it — to themselves or to anyone else — they'll be checking out, consciously or not, when it comes to anything Quinn has to say moving forward. And Daniels isn't blameless, either. Yes, he's a potential franchise quarterback. But true franchise quarterbacks overcome random acts of dysfunction. When the coaching staff fails, the franchise quarterback finds a way to protect the franchise. Daniels's failure to take charge of the situation potentially disqualifies him from holding the title of "franchise quarterback," and it could make it even harder for him to ever earn it, in the eyes of his teammates.
author: Mike Florio

title: Three-sack game makes David Bailey favorite for defensive rookie of the year
summary: The Jets made linebacker David Bailey the second overall pick in the draft because they believed he could make game-changing plays off the edge in their defense, but his first four games led to some grumbling about his lack of impact.
full_text: '' The Jets made linebacker David Bailey the second overall pick in the draft because they believed he could make game-changing plays off the edge in their defense, but his first four games led to some grumbling about his lack of impact. Bailey had two sacks in those contests, but they didn't stop the Jets from opening 1-3. The grumbling will be harder to find after Bailey's performance in the team's fifth game of the year. Bailey had three sacks of Deshaun Watson in a 17-12 home win and Bailey said after the game that the defense "got together and sat down and made a list of things that we needed to work on as a whole and individually." That effort paid off handsomely for Bailey and the Jets on Sunday. "I’ve said it all along that his time is going to come," head coach Aaron Glenn said, via a transcript from the team. "I have all the confidence in him in the world. He did a good job today. He did a good job. There are some things that he’s got to work on. For him to come out and have, I think, three sacks, that’s who David is and we expected that." Bailey's performance led to a change in the betting markets as well. He's now the favorite for defensive rookie of the year at sportsbooks and he'll stay there if Sunday's performance was a sign of things to come.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jaguars are bringing a healthy long snapper to London for Week 6
summary: Thanks in part to a helping hand from Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni, the Jaguars survived the loss of long snapper Ross Matiscik in Sunday's win but they aren't going to risk having to scramble again in Week 6.
full_text: ' Thanks in part to a helping hand from Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni, the Jaguars survived the loss of long snapper Ross Matiscik in Sunday's win but they aren't going to risk having to scramble again in Week 6. Head coach Liam Coen told reporters on Monday morning that the team has an unnamed long snapper en route to London to join them for next Sunday's game against the Texans. Matiscik had to leave on Sunday after suffering a shoulder injury, which pushed defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton into service. Hamilton handled the job well for someone who rarely practices snapping and delivered the snap for kicker Cam Little's game-winning 56-yard field goal at the buzzer, but there was also a missed extra point and holder Logan Cooke had to do some gymnastics to get the ball down in other spots. "There was one he got it down and his foot was a little bit in the way of the spot and at the last possible second, he slightly moved his foot to get out of Cam's way," Coen said, via Ryan O'Halloran of the Florida Times-Union . "Just chaos for sure." The Jags also committed 13 penalties, turned the ball over and made questionable decisions around the goal line, so there was chaos to spare in what turned out to be an improbable 19-17 win.
author: Josh Alper

title: Fred Warner on Mike Evans: Unreal how he shows up every week and dominates
summary: Wide receiver Mike Evans built a reputation for clutch catches and consistent production over 12 years with the Buccaneers and he didn't leave any of those skills behind when he moved on to the 49ers as a free agent this offseason.
full_text: '' Wide receiver Mike Evans built a reputation for clutch catches and consistent production over 12 years with the Buccaneers and he didn't leave any of those skills behind when he moved on to the 49ers as a free agent this offseason. Evans has quickly become the player Brock Purdy looks to in big spots and Sunday's game against the Seahawks showed just how important he is to the team's offensive plans. Evans opened the scoring with a two-yard touchdown in the first quarter and he set up that score with a 13-yard grab to convert a third down on the previous play. Evans then had four catches for 75 yards on a go-ahead touchdown drive bridging the third and fourth quarters, which made it no surprise that Purdy looked his way for a two-point conversion that accounted for the final points in a 29-26 victory. Evans did all this while playing through a rib injury and his effort left linebacker Fred Warner grasping for superlatives after the game was over. "Just a walking aura ," Warner said, via 49ersWebzone.com. "I mean, I can't help it. Like, I'm on the sideline watching, dude, crazy stuff. I'm like, 'We have Mike Evans.' Like, I can't believe it. He's unreal. He really doesn't say anything. He just shows up every week and just works and then goes out there on Sunday and just dominates you. So, it's unbelievable. He's great." Evans now has 24 catches for 326 yards and three touchdowns over the 49ers' 5-0 start and the move to bring him to the team is shaping up to be a major feather in the cap of General Manager John Lynch.
author: Josh Alper

title: Robert Saleh: Cam Ward's our starting quarterback
summary: The Titans drove for a field goal to open Sunday's home game against the Texans, but any hope that was a sign of good things to come came crashing down over the rest of the afternoon.
full_text: The Titans drove for a field goal to open Sunday's home game against the Texans, but any hope that was a sign of good things to come came crashing down over the rest of the afternoon. Tennessee punted four times and turned the ball over twice before failing on two fourth downs in the fourth quarter of a 26-3 loss that dropped them to 0-5 on the season. They ended the game with 187 yards and quarterback Cam Ward was 23-of-36 for 170 yards while being sacked four times. The Titans now rank dead last in points scored and offensive yards, which led to a question for head coach Robert Saleh at his postgame press conference about whether the team needs to consider benching the quarterback in hopes of sparking better offensive results. Saleh said it is not on the team's radar. "Cam's our starting quarterback ," Saleh said. "We're going to give him every opportunity to be successful this year. We're going to continue working with him, grinding with him and trying to help him get better." There haven't been many signs that Ward is getting better and Sunday's performance suggests things may actually be moving in the other direction, but any changes made to improve the offensive output aren't going to start under center.
author: Josh Alper

title: Kenneth Walker has more rushing yards in 4 games than the Seahawks have in 5
summary: The Chiefs had their bye this week, meaning they've only played four games.
full_text: The Chiefs had their bye this week, meaning they've only played four games. But Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker still has more rushing yards this season than his former team, the Seahawks, has totaled in five games. Walker has 87 carries for 537 yards in four games. The Seahawks have 139 carries for 530 yards in five games. The Seahawks could have used a good running back in Sunday's loss to the 49ers. The two running backs Seattle had, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani, combined for 24 carries for 68 yards, an average of just 2.8 yards per carry. Seattle drafted running back Jadarian Price in the first round after the Chiefs signed Walker away, but Price is on injured reserve with a chest injury. When healthy, Price was better than Wilson or Holani, but Price isn't the player Walker is. Price averaged 39.7 yards a game in the three games he played; Walker is averaging an NFL-high 134.3 yards per game this season. Walker, who was the Super Bowl MVP for the Seahawks in February, has been one of the NFL's best playmakers for the 4-0 Chiefs this season. The 3-2 Seahawks may be regretting letting the Super Bowl MVP walk away.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Cam Skattebo: I try to fight for extra yards, it bit me on Sunday
summary: The Giants didn't win on Sunday, but running back Cam Skattebo still let out "a sigh of relief" when the clock ran out in overtime against the Commanders in Washington.
full_text: ''' The Giants didn't win on Sunday, but running back Cam Skattebo still let out "a sigh of relief" when the clock ran out in overtime against the Commanders in Washington. Skattebo fumbled with the Giants in field goal range on the first play after the two-minute warning when Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne punched the ball out of his grasp and Washington drove into position for a kick of their own as time ran down. They never got a chance to kick because they made the strange decision to run a play with 12 seconds to go and time ran out before they could line up to spike the ball after a Jayden Daniels run. Skattebo called that sequence "insane" while noting that it will lessen the amount of criticism he takes for a play that he'd like to have back. "I fumbled the ball. We can't have that," Skattebo said, via a transcript from the team. "I understand that. I'm going to go into the film room and get it fixed. I felt like I had good protection on it. The kid made a hell of a play. I think in that situation what I think I could do differently is try not to get the extra yards because we're already in a good position and continue to take care of the ball. If I get tackled for a loss at one yard, then I get tackled for a loss at one yard. I'm the player that tries to fight for as many yards as possible for this team. It kind of bit me in the ass there. I got to make sure I protect the ball for this football team. We win that game if I do." There was still a kick to make and Dominic Zvada missed three field goals Sunday, including one earlier in overtime, but it's easy to understand why Skattebo would put the result on his shoulders. Thanks to Daniels and Commanders head coach Dan Quinn, he won't have to deal with quite as much grief from anyone else.
author: Josh Alper

title: Fernando Mendoza: Good to gain some regular season experience
summary: The first overall pick of the 2026 draft made his regular season debut on Sunday afternoon.
full_text: ''' The first overall pick of the 2026 draft made his regular season debut on Sunday afternoon. Fernando Mendoza replaced Kirk Cousins as the Raiders' quarterback with Las Vegas losing 45-17 to the Patriots with about six minutes left in the fourth quarter. Mendoza went 6-of-8 for 48 yards, but couldn't put any points on the board before failing to convert a fourth down on a three-yard scramble that left Vegas just short of a first down. Head coach Klint Kubiak said the rookie did a good job in his brief appearance, but that there's no thought of a lasting change at quarterback right now. Sunday's move was made because Kubiak "just wanted to get him some exposure" to regular season football and Mendoza said he appreciated that chance because it will help prepare him for more meaningful action. “Keep on controlling the controllables," Mendoza said. "But it is good to have some regular-season snaps to go off, evaluate and get better from. So, if in the future I am called upon, I have at least a little bit of experience rather than none." The Raiders have lost two straight after a 3-0 start and a long run of losses could increase the likelihood of a lasting change under center. With the Bills, Rams, 49ers and Seahawks are four of their next five opponents, such a change of fortune would appear to be in the cards in Vegas.
author: Josh Alper

title: Big Ten admits ref blew call on Oregon's failed two-point conversion in 17-15 loss to UCLA
summary: In Saturday's 17-15 loss to UCLA, Oregon was stopped short on a game-tying two-point conversion attempt with 2:16 left.
full_text: In Saturday's 17-15 loss to UCLA, Oregon was stopped short on a game-tying two-point conversion attempt with 2:16 left. And now the Big Ten has admitted the officials botched a call that would have given Oregon a better chance of converting. Oregon quarterback Brock Thomas initially tried to run the ball in, but a UCLA player blatantly grabbed his facemask before Thomas was stopped inside the 1-yard line. The facemasking was called, but the officials gave Oregon half the distance to the goal line from the 3-yard line, and spotted the ball at the 1.5-yard line for Oregon's subsequent two-point conversion attempt, which was stopped just short of the goal line. That's not where the ball should have been spotted. The ruling should have been half the distance to the goal line from where Thomas was tackled, which was just inside the 1-yard line. So the ball should have been spotted less than half a yard from the goal line for Oregon's subsequent two-point conversion attempt. If it had been, and Oregon had run the same play, that same second two-point conversion attempt would have reached the end zone, and Oregon would have tied the game. "With 2:16 remaining in the fourth quarter of Saturday's UCLA-Oregon game, Big Ten officials incorrectly officiated Oregon's final two-point conversion attempt," the Big Ten said in a statement. "Following the first attempt that resulted in a personal foul penalty for a facemask on the UCLA defense, the ball was spotted for the second attempt half-the-distance to the goal from the original line of scrimmage of the first attempt. Per rule, the ball should have been spotted half-the-distance to the goal from the end of the run of the first attempt. The Big Ten has been in contact with its officiating team from Saturday's game regarding the error and will continue to emphasize consistent application of the playing rules." Compounding the mistake was that the referee correctly announced that the ball would be spotted half the distance to the goal line from the end of the run, but when it came time to actually spot the ball, the officials incorrectly spotted it half the distance to the goal line from the previous spot. Missed calls will always happen; the officials can't always see every single thing that happens on every single play. But misapplying the rules is inexcusable, and it cost Oregon dearly on Saturday.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Michael Penix: If we got ball first in OT, I could have stayed in
summary: The final play of Sunday night's game saw Falcons backup quarterback Tua Tagovailoa throw an interception to seal the Ravens' 30-23 overtime win while starter Michael Penix watched from the sideline with a rib injury.
full_text: The final play of Sunday night's game saw Falcons backup quarterback Tua Tagovailoa throw an interception to seal the Ravens' 30-23 overtime win while starter Michael Penix watched from the sideline with a rib injury. Penix came out for one play late in regulation after taking a big hit from Ravens linebacker Tavius Robinson, but came back in to throw an incompletion before the Falcons punted on the final play of the fourth quarter. The Ravens got the ball first in overtime and Tagovailoa re-entered the game after Baltimore's touchdown with 2:57 left on the clock. After the loss, Penix said he thinks he could have stayed in if the Falcons got the ball first but "it just started to get worse and worse as we were sitting there." Due to that, Penix "did not feel like I was going to be able to give our team what we needed to be able to win that football game because of the pain that I was feeling." Penix will have more testing done on the injury, but said he does not think it is going to be a long-term absence. "Knowing me, I am going to be ready to go next week because I've sat out enough in my career," Penix said, via the team's website. "I am going to do everything I can in the training room to make sure I get back to where I want to be. . . . I will work my tail off to make sure I'm back out there on that field." Penix was 19-of-32 for 240 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons' first loss since he returned to the lineup in Week 3. He'll try to be back out on the field against the Bears next Sunday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Marvin Harrison deal was most likely done before Sunday's games started
summary: On Sunday, the only No. 18 in Arizona was in the stands; receiver Marvin Harrison didn't play — and presumably wasn't even in the building — one day after the mysterious half-report emerged from Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport of ESPNFL that Harrison would be traded to a team to be named later.
full_text: On Sunday, the only No. 18 in Arizona was in the stands; receiver Marvin Harrison didn't play — and presumably wasn't even in the building — one day after the mysterious half-report emerged from Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport of ESPNFL that Harrison would be traded to a team to be named later. It's possible that they both knew the destination and agreed to not report it; as one source explained it to PFT, some of the #insiders (and possibly Schefter and/or Rapoport) knew Harrison had hired agents last month for the first time in his career but kept that news under wraps for as long as possible in order to ensure the effort to get Harrison traded would happen without a widespread sense of a potential Arizona fire sale emerging and, in turn, complicating the Cardinals' effort to get value for Harrison and Harrison's effort to get out of Arizona. Fast forward to one of the most bizarre trade reports in recent years, if not ever, and the question is whether the two teams were still haggling as of Saturday or whether the deal was in place. And whether the door was open for another team (or more) to get involved. Although the facts are very hard to completely uncover (the simple fact that Cardinals G.M. Monti Ossenfort and Texans G.M. Nick Caserio spent 14 years together, from 2006 through 2019, working for Lord of Secrecy Bill Belichick is the obvious reason for that), it appears that a deal was fully in place before Sunday, and that both teams wanted to delay the announcement until after they played their games on Sunday. The Texans didn't fully cooperate in that regard. At the end of his postgame press conference, Texans coach DeMeco Ryans (who was never a member of the Belichick hive) blurted it out after being asked about Harrison multiple times. The Cardinals game, which kicked off at 4:25 p.m. ET, hadn't ended. It hadn't even started. So why not announce it on Saturday? As best we can tell, the goal was to not create a distraction before Sunday's game — more for the Texans than for the Cardinals, especially since the word was out that the Cardinals were trading Harrison out of town. If the deal wasn't already done, there was no reason for the Cardinals to not wait and see whether another team that had yet to play (up to and including the Monday night game between the Bills and Rams) would develop a sudden need for Harrison due to an injury and make a better offer for the fourth overall pick in the 2026 draft. But the Cardinals didn't wait until the dust fully settled on Week 5. Which alone points to a conclusion that the deal was done before Sunday. Then there's the reality that Harrison must still pass a physical. While that's usually a technicality, it's a technicality that kept Maxx Crosby in Las Vegas after the deal was announced that would have sent him to Baltimore. Given that Harrison has been playing this season, there's no specific reason to think he'll fail the Texans' physical. Still, it's not completely done until the doctor(s) provide the official thumbs up. As to the haggling, it was apparently done before Sunday's games even started. But the fact that the information was partially reported served only to create confusion among those who consume the news, leading to the inevitable tinfoil-hat suspicions that someone was trying to make a little money in the prediction markets.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFC East makes dubious NFL history with winless Week 5 as Giants hold unlikely division lead
summary: The NFC East's Week 5 is something that has happened just four times since 2002 divisional realignment
full_text:
The NFC East just had an all-time week to remember, or if you're a fan of the Dallas Cowboys , Philadelphia Eagles , New York Giants or Washington Commanders , an all-time week to forget.
Dallas lost 24-16 at home to the previously 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers with Jalon Daniels , an undrafted rookie making his second career start, at quarterback. Philadelphia lost 19-17 in regulation against the Jacksonville Jaguars despite kicking a go-ahead field goal with eight seconds left. Last and ugliest, the New York Giants and Washington Commanders tied despite both teams reaching field-goal range in the last two minutes of overtime.
With all four NFC East teams going winless in Week 5, they have now become just the fourth occurrence of an entire division going winless despite having a divisional matchup in the 418 NFL regular-season weeks since the 2002 divisional realignment, per CBS Sports Research. That means the 2026 NFC East did something that has only happened in less than one percent of the 418 weeks of NFL regular season action, 0.96%, to be exact, since 2002.
In the case of the Giants and Commanders, they now own two of the last three ties in the NFL, with these two NFC East teams tying each other in 2022. The Cowboys account for the other tie in this span, a 40-40 home tie against the Green Bay Packers last season. Another unfathomable stat for the Giants is that they are now winless in their last six overtime games, with four losses and two ties.
Week 5's events have now created a tightly-contested NFC East division race through five weeks. The Giants are in first place at 3-1-1, but both the Eagles and the Cowboys are right behind them at 2-3. The Commanders are bringing up the rear at 1-3-1.

author: Owen OBrien

title: Nick Sirianni, Dan Quinn fail their teams in pivotal moments during dismal NFC East weekend
summary: The Eagles and Commanders squandered chances to win Sunday, and both coaches are feeling the heat
full_text:
Clock mismanagement and a pair of coaches overthinking late-game situations doomed the Philadelphia Eagles and Washington Commanders . Both teams are fighting for air in the NFC East after five weeks, and both coaches are feeling the heat.
The Eagles led the Jacksonville Jaguars with eight seconds left in London following Jake Elliott's 48-yard field goal before giving one of the NFL's most dangerous return threats, Ameer Abdullah , a shot at a big return. Abdullah answered with a 53-yard burst to set up Cam Little's game-winning 57-yard field goal as time expired, dropping the Eagles to 2-3 overall.
"I didn't make the right decision, and I lost us that game, and that's what I said to our guys," Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said. "What hurts there is the guys fought so hard, and then I don't make the decision that I should make at the end of the game and I cost us that game, and I put that one on me."
The Commanders were in game-winning field goal range against the New York Giants in overtime before the clock expired at the 25-yard line during a 27-all tie . Now 1-3-1, Washington would've moved one game back of the division leaders with a victory.
Dan Quinn said, "It falls on me," when asked about his team's failure to stop the clock and attempt the game-tying field goal without any timeouts.
Quarterback Jayden Daniels assumed responsibility after going down in the middle of the field with the final seconds ticking off the clock, but Quinn pointed fingers at himself.
"At the end, I can make life easy there," Quinn said . "We didn't need to gain more yards."
These weren't two situations that required genius decisions on the headset. In fact, both were elementary-level calls that most of us could've made from the couch.
Both coaches failed their respective franchises in a big spot, including one in a divisional game. Ironically, Sirianni nixed the idea of having his quarterback run around and burn time off the clock before attempting the go-ahead field goal, the inverse of a decision that backfired on Quinn and the Commanders.
"It hurts in the sense of the guys fought their ass off and had a chance to win the game. And then for me to not make the right decision in that, you feel like you let everyone down," Sirianni said. "That will stick with me for a long time. All I know is I'll work my butt off to get better from it."
Quinn's error was the more notable blunder, ending with the coach slamming his headset to the ground after a game that ended in a tie felt more like a loss in Washington.
Those coaching mistakes came a couple of days after Dallas Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said he was considering staff changes following his team's humiliating loss to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers .
Is there any team interested in winning the division this season?
Tampa Bay's decisive 17-point third quarter behind undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels and Bucky Irving's first 100-yard outing on the ground in two years put the spotlight on the Cowboys' second-year coach and his 2-3 start this fall.
"I'm going to look at everything," Schottenheimer said. "I'll spend countless hours trying to figure it out and getting a chance to step back, look at these five games, and see what we need to improve. ... Yeah, I think we evaluate everything, but at the end of the day, we're five games in. I am disappointed in the way we performed this evening as a football team, and that's just going to be one part of the process."
author: Brad Crawford

title: Head-scratching decisions by Commanders, Eagles; Georgia new No. 1 in college football, CFP shake-up
summary: Plus, Brewers eke out NLCS opener over Dodgers
full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
Lost in a sea of close finishes and general wackiness, you might have missed the Vikings handing the Saints a 23-13 loss in New Orleans. Minnesota is a relatively quiet 5-0, and that begs the question: Should the Vikings be considered a legitimate Super Bowl contender?
That's one of the topics our Zach Pereles explored in his Week 5 overreactions , and his conclusion was clear. Whatever reservations you have about Kyler Murray as a championship quarterback, put them aside. The defense is good enough that Murray won't have to be Superman every week.
Another team that impressed in Week 5 was the Packers . Green Bay thumped the Bears and improved to 3-2 on the season. Jordan Love threw for 367 yards, and the Packers defense allowed just 3.6 yards per play. It seems like the Pack may very well be back after a shaky start .
Of course, in the words of the great Sturgill Simpson , "It ain't all flowers, sometimes you gotta feel the thorns."
There were some teams that would rather forget Week 5 happened altogether. The Commanders are certainly on that list of losers after bungling what looked like a sure win over a division rival. The Raiders are another team who failed a big test as reality finally hit , although Fernando Mendoza saw his first NFL action .
Another No. 1 overall quarterback -- Cam Ward -- is going through hard times. Just don't expect the Titans to bench him anytime soon .
College football is always good for a little chaos, but Week 6 provided something extra. A number of highly ranked teams, included former No. 1 Texas went down over the weekend.
The Longhorns blew a lead to rival Oklahoma in the Cotton Bowl as their obvious flaws finally caught up to them . As a result, Texas has given itself a little less wiggle room in the race for a College Football Playoff berth.
As Tom Fornelli points out in his CFP Vibe Check , have the Horns inspired enough confidence for anyone to believe they won't drop a couple more games along the way?
If it's any consolation, Texas was not alone in its sadness. They had the company of a few more top-25 squads.
If you thought Week 6 was fun, just wait until you see what's in store for Week 7. There is one banger after another on the slate ( Ohio State vs. Indiana ; BYU vs. Notre Dame ; Alabama vs. Tennessee ), and you can see the odds for the biggest games right here .

title: Cover 32: Look out NFL, Drake Maye has his swagger back; plus games balls, biggest gaffes from Week 5
summary: Tyler Sullivan dives into all of the biggest items from Week 5 in the NFL, including the bizarre tie in Giants-Commanders and David Bailey's breakout
full_text:
Call it the yips, a slump, or just being downright bad, whatever had been plaguing Drake Maye through the early part of the season appears to be a thing of the past. The Patriots quarterback emphatically announced the return of his swagger with a dominant five-touchdown performance in New England's 45-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 5.
Maye looked like the MVP runner-up he was a year ago in this contest, completing 26 of 34 passes for 374 yards and four touchdowns. He added 25 yards and another score on the ground to his day as well. That helped Maye become the first quarterback in team history to have at least 300 passing yards, four passing touchdowns, and one rushing touchdown in a game. Of course, the most important element of Maye's day was the zero he posted in the turnover column.
Outside of keeping it clean in the turnover margin, Maye's eruption against the Raiders was particularly notable when it comes to his deep ball. Last year, Maye was regarded as the most efficient deep ball passer in the NFL , but that was noticeably absent in his game during the early struggles this season. On Sunday, Maye completed 72.7% of his passes (8 of 11) that went for 10-plus air yards for 206 yards and three touchdowns, giving him a 154.4 passer rating. Those passing yards and passing touchdowns were season highs for the former first-round pick.
THIS IS A DIME. @DrakeMaye2 | @EliRaridon 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/SJByiCW5zY
Really, Maye's resurgence began to sprout last week in New England's win over Buffalo. Over these last two games, Maye has completed 19 of 29 passes of 10-plus air yards for 390 yards, five touchdowns and one interception. When making the same throws over his first three games, Maye was 13 of 31 for 340 yards and four interceptions.
What has helped Maye not only stabilize his season but also return to elite form has been his ability to better handle pressure. Over the past two games, Maye's been pressured on 30 dropbacks. In that span, he has completed 12 of 26 throws for 136 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, while being sacked just twice. Conversely, on the 42 dropbacks he was pressured over the first three weeks, Maye was 12-of-28 for 183 yards and three interceptions, while being sacked eight times. A night and day difference, particularly in the turnover department.
It's funny how quickly the narrative can change in the NFL. After that 1-2 start, where Maye and the Patriots looked absolutely lost, the sky felt like it was falling in Foxborough. They've since ripped off two key wins in the AFC (including a head-to-head against the Bills in Buffalo) to move over .500 for the first time this season.
Not only that, but Maye looks like the MVP contender he was a year ago, which completely changes the complexion of this team and the overall season outlook. There's also a case to be made that his high-level play could continue or even improve with the return of A.J. Brown looming. If that proves to be the case, New England is firmly back in the Super Bowl conversation, which is something nobody thought coming off that 3-point dud they produced in Jacksonville in Week 3.
How Game Balls work: Six are awarded to standout players from the slate of teams that won their contests, and only one player on a team can get a game ball.
The No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft had his coming-out party in Week 5 as the Jets outlasted the Browns to move to 2-3 on the year. Bailey became the first rookie with three or more sacks in a game since James Houston in 2022 and just the second Jets rookie in franchise history to have three or more sacks, joining Hugh Douglas (1995). So far this season, Bailey has five sacks, which makes him the first rookie with five or more sacks through five games since Von Miller in 2011.
David Bailey generated 9 pressures, including 5 quick pressures and 3 sacks, against the Browns. His 9 pressures are tied for the most by a rookie in a game since Jared Verse in Week 7, 2024. Bailey leads all rookies in pressures (26) and quick pressures (9). #CLEvsNYJ | #JetUp pic.twitter.com/xAz8wciLTp
Watson continues to be the key cog in Green Bay's passing attack and was a go-to option early for Jordan Love amid the Packers 31-7 demolition of the Bears on Sunday. On the first offensive possession of the day for Green Bay, Love uncorked a 42-yard touchdown to Watson, which gave the Packers the lead, and they effectively never looked back. He also hauled in a 53-yard pass on a third-and-22 play in the third quarter. Watson is the second Packers player with multiple 40-yard touchdown receptions since 2000, joining Jordy Nelson .
CHRISTIAN WATSON WHAT A CATCH @CHIvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/z0TbC7WaQe
Warren has come on strong for the Steelers over the last three weeks, averaging 107 rushing yards per game over that stretch. The Pittsburgh back made his presence felt in the passing game in Week 5, taking a first-down swing pass from Aaron Rodgers 80 yards to the house midway through the first quarter. Not only did Warren lead the team in rushing, but he also was tied for the lead in receptions and led the team with 87 receiving yards. He's the first Steeler ever with a 50-yard rushing touchdown and a 50-yard receiving touchdown in the same game.
Jaylen Warren with the 80-yard touchdown! @INDvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Q49IxXTuCP
Once again, Jahmyr Gibbs put together video game-like numbers in Detroit's 45-21 win over the Cardinals . With his two rushing touchdowns, Gibbs passed Barry Sanders for the most total touchdowns (58) before turning 25 in NFL history. This was also Gibbs' third career game with 200-plus scrimmage yards, which is the fourth-most in franchise history.
. @Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs has passed @BarrySanders (57) for the most TDs scored by a player under 25 years old in @NFL history. #OnePride pic.twitter.com/vdvsTLH9KQ
While Ameer Abdullah and Cam Little get the glory for their late-game heroics that ultimately won Jacksonville the game, they wouldn't even have been in a position to go for the victory had it not been for Washington. Once again, the Jags' wideout was superb and hauled in two touchdowns in London. His last touchdown was jawdropping as the Jaguars kept the offense on the field for a fourth-and-5 attempt from the Philadelphia 27-yard line, trailing 14-10 with just over three minutes to play in regulation. Trevor Lawrence dropped back and found Washington, who made a diving one-handed catch in the end zone.
PARKER WASHINGTON, WOW. JAGS TAKE THE LEAD. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ubE4xivDcD
Evans was a linchpin to San Francisco going into Seattle and taking down the Seahawks to remain unbeaten on the season. On top of catching a touchdown earlier in the contest, Brock Purdy looked Evans' way in a critical moment of the game, converting a 2-point attempt to put the Niners up by a field goal, 29-26. Specifically, Evens came alive in the fourth quarter, totaling four catches for 75 yards to go along with that 2-point conversion over the final period.
Brock Purdy and Mike Evans are on another level right now. 49ers get the two-point conversion! @SFvsSEA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/FvlrW7MTYM
We had some late-game chaos in London as the Jaguars hit a walk-off 57-yard field goal to defeat the Eagles . The only reason why Jacksonville was within range to kick the game-winner was thanks to Abdullah ripping off a 53-yard kick return.
JAGS HUGE KICK RETURN. They're in range for one more shot at a field goal! @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/XSWbKBTvW2
UNBELIEVABLE. JAGS WIN. WHAT JUST HAPPENED?!?! pic.twitter.com/O7x8JTgPeK
That decision to give the Jaguars a returnable ball with just eight seconds remaining in regulation and a 17-16 lead was puzzling, to say the least. Head coach Nick Sirianni took the blame for the decision, which ended up costing his team the…
