title: Rams vs. Bills how to watch, prediction, odds: Matthew Stafford, Josh Allen clash in Week 5 'MNF' matchup
summary: Here's how to watch Rams vs. Bills, along with the latest odds, key matchups and our Week 5 'Monday Night Football' prediction
full_text:
In the Week 5 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Los Angeles Rams host the Buffalo Bills .
The Rams are coming off a too-close-for-comfort win over the Philadelphia Eagles , having improved to 2-2 on in the process. They have not quite been the super team many expected, though injuries have played their part. They have a chance to get above .500 if they can capture a win against the Bills on Monday night.
The Bills, meanwhile, are coming off their first loss of the season, having dropped a dispiriting game against the division rival New England Patriots . The Bills had started 3-0 behind a pair of explosive offensive performances in Weeks 1 and 2 and then a comeback victory despite turning the ball over five times in Week 3. Their defense hasn't been up to snuff, and the Rams present a tremendous challenge.
Will the Rams leave the stadium with a winning record, or will the Bills bounce back from last week's defeat? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
The Bills gained more than 400 yards and scored at least 36 points in each of their first two games of the season, playing pristine football as they secured wins against the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions . They did not turn the ball over at all and they looked like an absolute machine as they worked their way through those two defenses with relative ease.
Over the last two weeks, things have been a bit choppier, as the Bills didn't top 350 yards in either game and turned the ball over multiple times against both the Los Angeles Chargers (five) and New England Patriots (two), scoring 24 and 26 points, respectively. They were fortunate to escape with a win against L.A., but didn't get quite so lucky against New England and suffered their first loss of the season.
The Rams, meanwhile, were torn asunder by the division rival San Francisco 49ers back in Week 1, but have since been incredibly stingy on defense. They've held each of their last three opponents under 260 yards, and two of them under 185. Their pass defense, in particular, has been remarkable, but the run defense has also been quite good since that first game. And they've done it without Myles Garrett (who got knee surgery following the Week 1 game) and, last week, without Aaron Donald (who is set to return on Monday after a one-game absence).
Buffalo is without wide receiver Josh Palmer on Monday night, and could be without No. 1 target DJ Moore as well. Moore is questionable after missing two of his last three practices. That could mean Josh Allen is down to Khalil Shakir , Keon Coleman and Dalton Kincaid as his passing-game options, leaving the Bills shorthanded against what has been an excellent pass defense over the last three weeks and that gets Jaylen Watson back after he missed most of the last two games.
Allen, of course, is capable of turning any group of skill-position players into a functional one, as we saw over most of the last two years before the Bills traded for Moore. It's worth noting, though, that the Rams have entirely shut down the tight end position so far this year, allowing 12 catches for a league-low 85 yards to players at the position. Kincaid could therefore have a tough time getting going here, meaning the passing game would have to run through Coleman (who could see a lot of Trent McDuffie , who is playing at an extraordinarily high level) and Shakir. Allen can obviously make that work; it would just be more difficult than if he had Moore in addition to the other weapons.
James Cook — who led the NFL in rushing last season — is averaging an incredible and career-best 6.0 yards per carry so far this year, and has tagged two of four opponents for at least 135 yards on the ground. The Rams were run all over by San Francisco back in Week 1, but have since limited opposing backs in a big way. They haven't exactly faced a murderer's row of running games ( Giants , Broncos , Eagles) during that span, though, so they could find it tougher to contain Cook here. Cook getting going would obviously take some of the pressure off of Allen and the potentially weapons-depleted passing game.
After sputtering to just 290 total yards back in their Week 1 game in Australia, the Rams have put up at least 415 yards in each of their last three games stateside. The only thing that's kept them from truly exploding offensively has been turnovers, as they've given the ball away two times in each of their games so far this season — including those last three where they piled up all the yardage.
After throwing 46 touchdowns against just eight interceptions on his way to an MVP season a year ago, Matthew Stafford has already been picked off six times. Stafford only completed 61% of his passes, and he's down from 7.9 to 7.3 yards per attempt. Stafford, of course, didn't have Puka Nacua for two of those games, but even with Nacua back last week, he was at just 62.7% completions and 6.2 yards per attempt while being held scoreless and intercepted twice. He just has not played up to last year's standard yet.
Buffalo's defense, though, has been vulnerable through the air early on in the Jim Leonhard era. The Bills have gotten excellent pass rush from Greg Rousseau (who leads the league with six sacks and ranks third with 29 total pressures) and great play inside from Deone Walker (19 pressures and three batted passes) but the back end has been leaky, with opponents totaling the sixth-most passing yards in the league through four weeks, along with 10 touchdown passes against just two interceptions.
Christian Benford returning to the lineup after he missed last week's loss against New England will help, but the Bills could still have their hands full with Nacua and Davante Adams — the latter of whom looks reinvigorated (career-best 10.3 yards per target) after repeated red-zone touchdown connections overshadowed a significant drop in efficiency last year. (He averaged just 6.9 yards per target, the fourth-worst mark of his 13-year career.) Adams was quiet last week against Philly (four catches for 32 yards on nine targets), but during the previous two games, he caught 15 passes for 332 yards and two touchdowns in Nacua's absence.
It's worth noting that the Bills have given up the sixth-most catches, seventh-most yards and second-most touchdowns to running backs as pass-catchers so far this season. The Rams typically rarely target their running backs with the pass, but that has changed with Kyren Williams . Watch out for him on underneath routes.
Williams and Blake Corum have also been highly efficient on the ground, combining for 87 carries for 456 yards and three touchdowns. That's an average of 5.2 yards per carry, and they each have success rates over 50% while Williams leads the league with a 64.8% rate on his runs. The Bills have given up only 0.98 yards before contact per carry so far this year, per Tru Media, but they've allowed 3.05 after contact thanks to one of the highest missed-tackle rates in the league. They can't allow Williams and Corum to slip out of their grasp here.
So far this season, the Rams have alternated between looking like the Rams team we expected and a much different version than that. That's largely due to injuries that have led to inconsistencies on both sides of the ball. The pass defense has been largely excellent, though, and the return of Aaron Donald should help the run defense. I don't think Buffalo has anyone that can deal with the Puka Nacua-Davante Adams-Kyren Williams trio, so the Rams should put some points on the board here.
author: Jared Dubin

title: NFL Week 6 early odds: Eagles favored despite massive disadvantage, Packers-Cowboys line flips
summary: The statuses of Lamar Jackson, Michael Penix Jr. and Caleb Williams could dramatically reshape several Week 6 betting lines
full_text:
In lockstep with feeling even more of that fall chill in the air these days is the ramp-up in competitiveness throughout the NFL .
The league is coming out of a Week 5 slate that truly felt like teams had shaken off the rust and thrown haymakers. Specifically, we saw several underdogs bite back. That included the Green Bay Packers , who took down the Chicago Bears as a home underdog, and the San Francisco 49ers , who went into Lumen Field and took down the Seattle Seahawks . Even going back to Thursday's action, the Bucs went into Dallas and beat the Cowboys with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels under center.
What does Week 6 have in store for us? How about six divisional matchups, which include an international showdown between the Texans and Jaguars ? That should keep the momentum rolling for what has been a wildly entertaining season so far. As we turn our attention to next week's slate, let's take our first glimpse at the betting lines and see who the oddsmakers project coming out on top.
Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami, and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6.
All lines via DraftKings ; all games on Sunday unless noted
Seahawks at Broncos (Thursday)
Seahawks -155, Broncos +130
Texans at Jaguars (in London)
Panthers +105, Eagles -125
Steelers -155, Buccaneers +130
Chargers +295, Chiefs -375
Cowboys -105, Packers -115
Commanders at 49ers (Monday)
Commanders +340, 49ers -441
Seattle is coming off a grueling home loss to the 49ers and will now have to travel to face the Broncos, who outlasted the Chargers in Week 5. The Seahawks opened as a 1.5-point favorite, and that has jumped to a full field goal at -3. Denver is 2-0 ATS at home this season, and this will be the first time they're a home underdog in 2026. Last season, the Broncos were 3-0 ATS as a home dog. As for Seattle, it is 1-1 ATS this season as a road favorite.
Jacksonville played in London in Week 5 and will remain in England, while Houston will need to make the international trek later this week. The Jags pulled out a last-second win over the Eagles on Sunday, but failed the cover, dropping them to 3-2 ATS on the year. They'll welcome in a Texans team that notched its first win of the season as they took down the Titans in Nashville. That also gave Houston its first ATS win of the year. The Under of 43.5 could be a lean in this game as it's 6-3 between these two division rivals this season.
Cleveland dropped a Week 5 road matchup to the Jets and is 3-2 (SU and ATS) on the year. They're 2-0 ATS at home, but they'll head into Week 6 as a home underdog, laying 3.5 points to the Ravens, who are coming off a road win in Atlanta. This line could see some movement throughout the week once it becomes clear whether Lamar Jackson (who did not play in Week 5) will suit up.
Chicago opened as a 1.5-point favorite on the road over the Falcons, but that has since been turned on its head. Now, the Falcons are laying 1.5 points as they host the Bears. This comes after the Bears lost as a road favorite to the Packers, and Tyson Bagent was benched for Case Keenum . If Caleb Williams is able to play in Week 6, however, it wouldn't be too surprising to see the odds swing back toward Chicago. The Bears are 3-2 ATS this season and 1-1 ATS on the road. Meanwhile, Michael Penix Jr . didn't finish Sunday's loss to the Ravens due to a rib injury. If he cannot go for Week 6, that'd also shift the lines dramatically, as Tua Tagovailoa finished the overtime period with an interception last night.
Carolina is going to have quite the rest advantage over Philadelphia. The Panthers were on the bye in Week 5, while the Eagles were just playing an international game in London. That's, in part, why this line is so slim, with Philly laying just 1.5 points in this NFC matchup. Of course, given the uncertainty surrounding an array of key players for the Eagles ( DeVonta Smith , Saquon Barkley , etc.) that has helped keep this line effectively a coin flip. Under coach Dave Canales, the Panthers are 3-3 ATS when they have the rest advantage. Under Nick Sirianni, the Eagles are 9-11 ATS when at a rest disadvantage.
New Orleans was initially a 1.5 -point road favorite, but that has since flipped, and it's now the Giants laying 1.5 points. New York is coming off a tie against the Commanders, but it covered in Week 5. Meanwhile, the Saints are reeling a bit after dropping three straight home games, including a Week 5 loss to Minnesota. The Giants are 3-0 ATS at home this season, while New Orleans is 2-0 ATS on the road, so something will need to give here.
New England is a full touchdown favorite over the Jets after stabilizing its season with two statement wins over the past couple of weeks. Most recently, the Patriots dropped 45 points in a win over the Raiders, pushing them to 3-2 on the season and 3-1-1 ATS. That includes a perfect 2-0 ATS mark at Gillette Stadium. As for the Jets, they pulled out a win against the Browns, which helped them cover and improve to 3-1-1 ATS. New York is 1-1-1 ATS on the road.
Indy is up to a full touchdown favorite over the Titans after the line initially opened at Colts -6.5. Both of these AFC South clubs are coming off losses in Week 5, with the Colts falling to the Steelers in Pittsburgh while the Texans went into Nashville to beat the Titans. The Titans are 1-1 ATS on the road this season, and the Colts are 1-1 ATS at home.
The Bucs will have a rest advantage over the Steelers after coming off their mini-bye following their Week 5 matchup with the Cowboys last Thursday. Despite that, Tampa Bay is a home-field underdog, with the Steelers laying 3 points in this matchup. The Bucs are 1-4 ATS this season and are 0-3 ATS at home (0-1 ATS as a home underdog). Pittsburgh has yet to record an ATS road win this season (0-2 ATS) and is 0-1 ATS as a road favorite.
The Rams still have their Week 5 matchup to play on Monday night as we write this, but they've opened Week 6 as the biggest favorite on the board. They are laying 12.5 points at home to the Cardinals, who are coming off a 45-21 loss to the Lions at home. Arizona is 2-3 ATS this season and has been a solid bet on the road (2-1 ATS). Before Monday night's matchup with Buffalo, the Rams are 1-1 ATS at home and 2-2 ATS on the season.
The Chargers are 0-5 on the season and 0-4-1 ATS. Now, they'll have to travel to Kansas City as a 8.5-point underdog to face a Chiefs team that is coming off its bye week. That's up from the 7.5 points the Chiefs were laying at the open. Since Patrick Mahomes became the full-time starter in 2018, the Chiefs are 5-8 ATS after the bye and 18-22 ATS with the rest advantage. This season, Kansas City is 2-2 ATS and 1-1 ATS at Arrowhead Stadium. The total for this game has dipped noticeably, falling to 43.5 after opening at 45.5.
Buffalo still has its Week 5 matchup with the Rams on Monday night, but is a 6-point road favorite over the Raiders in Week 6. That's up from the 5.5 point spread at the open. Las Vegas is coming off a blowout loss to the Patriots on the road, giving them their second loss in as many weeks. The Raiders are 2-0 ATS at home this season, while the Bills are 1-0 ATS on the road (before taking on the Rams in Week 5).
The Cowboys will have a bit of a rest advantage over the Packers after playing last Thursday, but they're reeling from their loss to the Buccaneers. That, along with Green Bay's dominant win over the Bears, has seen the odds in this game flip. Now, the Packers are laying 1.5 points after Dallas initially was the 1.5-point road favorite. The Cowboys are 1-1 ATS on the road this season, while the Packers are 1-1 ATS at home.
San Francisco is coming off a statement win in Seattle, which has helped see this line jump up and cross several key numbers. Initially, the 49ers opened as a 5.5-point favorite, but that has since ballooned to -7.5. The Niners are 2-1 ATS at home this season, with an average margin of victory of 12.7 points. title: Marvin Harrison trade: A look at other top-5 picks who were traded ahead of Year 4 in the last decade
summary: Harrison is one of five players in the last 10 years to be traded in before year four as a top-5 pick
full_text:
Wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr . is joining an exclusive club that he may not want to be part of. The Arizona Cardinals have traded Harrison , who they drafted at No. 4 overall just a few years ago, to the Texans, Houston head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed on Sunday.
Arizona is trading the 24-year-old and a 2027 seventh-round pick to the Texans for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick, according to ESPN .
When the Cardinals drafted Harrison in the 2024 overall draft, like any team that picks a player in the top 10, they thought they had found a long-term star. Flash forward 33 games later, and things haven't worked out as expected for either party.
Other than Harrison, in the last 10 years, only four other top-5 picks have been traded before their fourth season. The majority of the players haven't fared too well in their careers after that initial trade. Harrison will be looking to rewrite history and turn the move into a success.
Let's take a look at the other players with similar stories and how they played before and after the trade.
Team drafted (Year/Draft No.)
Team traded to/Year traded
108 receptions, 1,578 yards in 33 games
12-21 record, 23 TDs, 25 INT
Didn't appear in a game for DEN
12-21 record, 23 TDs, 25 INTs
2-2 record, 5 touchdowns, 3 interceptions
Didn't appear in a game in the first year with DAL
22 starts over 3 years, 124 combined tackles, 2 INTs, 1 forced fumbles
44 combined tackles, 3 passes defended with ATL
31 starts, 191 combined tackles, 1 forced fumble, 2 INTs
13-25 record, 45 TDs, 39 INTs
4-7 record, 9 TDs, 13 INTs
Two-time Pro Bowler, Super Bowl champion
Harrison has just five receptions for 85 yards so far this season. He has yet to record a 1,000-yard receiving season in his first two years in the league, dropping from 885 yards in his rookie season to 608 yards last year. The wide receiver's success at Ohio State made most people believe he would be an instant star in the league, but the stat line has fallen flat.
Harrison will now have a new start with the Texans, who won their first game this week, defeating the now 0-5 Tennessee Titans 26-3. Houston will face the 4-1 Jaguars , who are coming off a last-minute thrilling victory against the Philadelphia Eagles , next week.
Quarterback Zach Wilson went from the No. 2 overall pick to a bust very quickly. In his rookie year, he went 3-10 with nine touchdowns and 11 interceptions. The next season, he started nine games at 5-4, had a slew of bad performances, and cycled between the bench and the field all season.
Since being traded by the Jets, Wilson hasn't started a single game and has made just four game appearances, all with the Miami Dolphins . Wilson's trade did not equate to a new start for the QB, and he became a career backup after his failed experiment in NY.
Trey Lance is such an interesting study, as injuries and changing depth charts left him on the outskirts of the 49ers QB situation.
He was the backup to Jimmy Garoppolo to start his career, then named the starter over Jimmy G in his sophomore season, but an injury changed his career significantly. Ahead of the 2023 season, Sam Darnold, who we'll discuss more below, and Mr. Irrelevant (aka Brock Purdy ) were listed ahead of Lance on the depth chart. The Niners no longer felt the need for Lance, with two other quarterbacks they trusted, and he was dealt to the Cowboys ahead of the 2023 season.
Lance was the Cowboys' third-string QB and didn't play all season. He made four appearances for the Cowboys during the 2024 season, most notably after Dak Prescott got hurt and backup Cooper Rush was struggling. He started one game in 2024, which was a loss.
He then signed with the Chargers ahead of the 2025 season and played one game for them, losing that start as well. Lance has only started six games in the league, going 2-4, and in his career has a 54 completion percentage, 1,289 yards, five touchdowns and five total interceptions over four years.
Cornerback Jeff Okudah was selected at No. 3 overall by the Lions in 2020. Injuries have impacted his career, including time on IR in his rookie year in 2024 with the Houston Texans and in 2025 with the Minnesota Vikings.
In 2022, he was eventually benched after starting the season as the starter. During the next offseason, he was traded to the Falcons in exchange for a fifth-round pick. He spent one year with Atlanta before going to Houston ahead of the 2024 season. He spent a year there as well before joining the Vikings for a year, his final stop in the league.
Quarterback Sam Darnold has seen the most success of anyone on this list, though it was far from immediate. He bounced around to four teams before he found his fit with the Seattle Seahawks, where he helped lead the team to a Super Bowl win. But let's start from the beginning.
Darnold was the No. 3 overall draft pick in 2018 and was with the Jets until 2020, recording a 13-25 starting record, with 45 touchdowns and 39 interceptions.
He was traded to the Panthers ahead of the 2021 season, and he went 4-7 with nine touchdowns and 13 interceptions. The next season, he lost the starter job to Baker Mayfield and would end up starting six games, going 4-2, with seven touchdowns and two interceptions.
Free agency left Darnold on the 49ers ahead of the 2023 season, after the Panthers decided not to renew his contract. He started just one game, the season finale, for San Fran.
His time with the Niners was short, joining the Vikings the next season, where he would be named the starter after J.J. McCarthy got hurt. Darnold went 14-3 in his one year with Minnesota, with 35 touchdowns and 12 interceptions.
Darnold also went 14-3 in his first season with the Seahawks. He put together an impressive playoff run that culminated in Seattle being crowned champs.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: What's wrong with Matthew Stafford? Why 2025 MVP is struggling this season, could bounce back vs. Bills
summary: Stafford has as many touchdown passes as interceptions
full_text:
The Rams ' Super-Bowl-or-bust season has started, for the most part, bust, given their great expectations.
Everything went wrong in a Week 1 blowout loss to the 49ers , from the travel plan to the on-field product to the health problems that emerged from it: Myles Garrett underwent knee surgery, and Puka Nacua missed several weeks with a hip/groin issue. Los Angeles blew out the Giants in Week 2 after Jaxson Dart left early, but collapsed in Week 3 against the Broncos and needed a late comeback to overcome a sloppy first 50 minutes against the struggling Eagles .
The Rams are 2-2 -- hardly the end of the world, but not looking close to a championship winner. One of the biggest reasons is that Matthew Stafford doesn't look close to what he was during his MVP-winning 2025. If the Rams want to live up to their superteam reputation, it starts with him.
Stafford was at the peak of his powers last season in several facets, but perhaps the most impressive was his lack of turnovers. He threw just eight interceptions, and his 1.3% interception rate was the lowest of his career.
He's already up to six interceptions this season -- only Drake Maye has more -- and his 3.7% interception rate would be his highest since his 2009 rookie season. It's been a combination of bad throws and bad decisions.
The crushing pick-six he threw to Talanoa Hufanga in Week 3? "Yeah, that was forced ... Hufanga did a really nice job of kind of fighting through the Y, and [I threw] just a little bit back behind [my target]."
The two picks against the Eagles? "Obviously, I don't ever want to turn the ball over like the first one. It was a physical mistake; the ball kind of sailed on me. On the second one, I just got too aggressive. ... I put that ball in a bad spot ..."
jumped the pass, ran a lot, took the lead What an effort by Talanoa Hufanga 🙌 pic.twitter.com/9xvvAC6uoF
The aggressive mindset is ingrained in Stafford. He wants to and can make the big-time throws. The big issues arise when you combine that mindset with inaccuracy. Stafford's off-target rate so far this season is 14.8%, on pace for by far his highest rate since PFF started tracking the stat in 2017. He's only been above 13% once, and he was at 10.9% last year.
Five of his six interceptions this year have been overthrows, underthrows or behind his target, per PFF.
Five of his six interceptions have also been on throws 10+ yards downfield, and that's arguably a more concerning issue. Stafford has a 28.3% off-target rate on throws at least 10 yards downfield this year. That's also on pace for his worst mark, and it's nearly double his rate from last year (15.5).
So was last year just an absolute heater? It's a little bit of both. From 2017-25, Stafford's off-target rate on throws 10+ yards downfield was 20.7%. He should regress toward that mean this season, even if he doesn't absolutely light it up like last year.
There have been several close misses, too. In Week 4, Stafford almost had the touchdown throw of the year to Davante Adams , but the normally sure-handed wide receiver dropped it in the back of the end zone. He also just missed Adams on another deep ball (the ball glanced off an outstretched Adams' hands) and missed Konata Mumpfield by a couple of yards on another deep ball. These are the types of throws that littered his MVP-season highlight reel last year.
Matthew Stafford almost had the touchdown throw of the year Sunday. pic.twitter.com/uNq4UDXS1u
Stafford's downfield accuracy and turnover issues should improve. For him to perform at a career-worst or near-career-worst level this season would be a stunner. It would eliminate the Rams as a Super Bowl team, and the offense will struggle all season if it's the case. Stafford has had some stretches where he turns it over a lot. Normally, it balances out.
Nacua will really help this offense; it doesn't take a football genius to know this. He had nine catches for 125 yards and a rushing touchdown against the Eagles. Since Nacua entered the NFL , Stafford has a significantly higher EPA per play, yards per attempt and explosive pass rate with Nacua on the field compared to with Nacua off it.
Another return that could help Stafford? The play-action dropback game. Last year, 37% of Stafford's dropbacks used play action. This year? It's 23%, on pace for his second-lowest mark as a Ram. Similarly, Stafford has only been under center on 44% of his snaps this season, down from 60% last year. His rollouts are also down, something ESPN's Ben Solak pointed out earlier this week.
There doesn't appear to be any reason for the lack of under-center and/or play-action plays. McVay hasn't addressed it, nor has he been asked about it, according to the team's press conference transcripts this season. Stafford doesn't appear to be any less mobile than he has been recently. Furthermore, the Rams lead the NFL in rushing success rate, which, one would think, would make play action even more effective.
Maybe McVay gets back to arguably the best weapon in his and Stafford's arsenal. It simply doesn't make much sense that he hasn't leaned on it heavily this year.
The win over the Eagles was more important than impressive. There's the major difference between a 1-3 record and 2-2, obviously, but the Rams also overcame themselves -- turnovers, drops, penalties -- and the rain, and Stafford got his first win over a Vic Fangio-coached defense. Sometimes there are just matchups great quarterbacks can't solve; Fangio has been that for Stafford.
It was also important for the Rams to see that when they needed it most, they could have it. Here were the Rams' final two non-kneeldown drives:
Across those two drives, Stafford was 12-for-15 for 140 yards. He hit Nacua on a deep ball and had two beautiful back-shoulder throws to Tyler Higbee .
"There's no style points in this league, but I do think a lot of growth can come from this," McVay said.
Stafford will need to be closer to that end-of-game level in Week 5 against the Bills , who have a high-powered offense of their own. There's a good chance for Stafford to have his best game yet. The Bills ...
Christian Benford is dealing with a toe injury and missed last week's loss to the Patriots . In that game, the previously struggling Maye threw for 269 yards and three scores, and New England's previously struggling offense scored 29 points. Maxwell Hairston gave up two touchdowns and left the locker room early without speaking to reporters . Slot cornerback Dee Alford suffered an ankle injury and did not return.
Stafford should have a great chance to exploit this defense and build on his finish to Week 4. If he can, the Rams will start to look like the powerhouse they were expected to be entering the season.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Michael Penix Jr. injury: Falcons QB hurts ribs late in regulation on 'SNF,' says he'll be ready for Week 6
summary: Penix initially only left the game for one play but then couldn't play in overtime
full_text:
The latest injury in Michael Penix Jr.'s snakebitten career was particularly cruel not only for him but for his team, too. Penix took a hard hit to his ribs late in regulation, knocking him out for overtime of the Falcons ' eventual 30-23 loss to the Ravens on "Sunday Night Football."
Here's the hit from Tavius Robinson that caused Penix's injury:
MICHAEL PENIX TAKEN DOWN HARD HE IS IN PAIN pic.twitter.com/Ref6DhrROW
Initially, Penix missed just one play -- the one immediately following the hit -- when Tua Tagovailoa entered the game and found Bijan Robinson for a 14-yard gain on second and 20. Penix returned and threw a ball away under pressure, and the Falcons punted to end regulation.
The Ravens took the ball to start overtime and produced a touchdown drive that lasted over seven minutes. Cameras panned multiple times to the sideline, where Atlanta's medical staff was working on/examining Penix's right ribs. When Atlanta came out on offense, Tagovailoa entered while Penix had a towel over his head, distraught as he could only watch from the sideline. After the game, Penix said he was emotional because he wants to finish games and is frustrated by how many times he hasn't been able to do so.
"I did take some throws on the sideline just to see how I felt, and I did not feel like I was gonna be able to give our team what we needed to help us win that football game because of the pain that I was feeling, so that's all that happened," Penix said. "I was trying to get out there. [I] feel like if we had the ball first in overtime, I probably would have been out there, but as we were sitting, what I was going through, it just started getting worse and worse as we were just sitting there. I was getting cold."
Tagovailoa found Drake London for 20 yards on Atlanta's first offensive play of overtime, but got picked off by Kyle Hamilton on the next snap.
KYLE HAMILTON PICKS IT OFF! @RAVENS WIN! pic.twitter.com/CbkK3CiuUN
Though Kevin Stefanski said the team will need to conduct more imaging and testing before establishing a timeline for Penix's return, Penix speaking to the media is a good sign.
"Knowing me, I'mma be ready to go next week because I've sat out enough my career," Penix said. "... I will work my tail off to make sure I'm back out there on that field."
Penix, who missed the first two games of the season, had been a huge reason Atlanta turned its season around from 0-2 to 2-2 and is still afloat now at 2-3. The Falcons have now had four different quarterbacks play this season already: Penix, Tagovailoa, Cooper Rush (who started the first two games) and Jack Strand (who relieved a struggling Rush in a 34-3 loss in Week 2).
Penix's ability to push the ball downfield helped free up the running game and make the passing game, mainly through London, come to life. The Falcons would very much like Penix's self-diagnosed availability for Week 6 to be accurate, given how much the team has struggled without him.
The Falcons host the Bears in Week 6.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Mike Evans trolls Trevon Diggs with name-check in 49ers' win over Seahawks
summary: Evans explained that he asked, "Who are you?" before checking Diggs' jersey and realizing who was talking trash to him
full_text:
The rivalry between the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks heated up during their Week 5 matchup, and in one instance of the tensions bubbling to the surface, 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans took his trash-talking with Seahawks cornerback Trevon Diggs to a disrespectful, albeit hilarious, level.
The two exchanged words at the end of a play, and Evans turned around, grabbed Diggs by the shoulders and twisted him so he could see the name on the back of his jersey. The name-check could be perceived as a show of dismissal, but Evans said after the game that he was legitimately curious who was talking to him.
"I was blocking him until the whistle," Evans said. "He said something like I'm doing extra, or something like that. I didn't know that was him at first. I played against him a few times, and we've always been cool. He was a good player. I honestly didn't know it was him, because in the helmet, it's hard to tell sometimes. We were talking trash, and I think I pushed him. I was like, 'Who are you?' I looked to make sure. I was like, 'Oh, it's f---ing Diggs.' Then he pushed me. Should've been a penalty."
Mike Evans and Trevon Diggs talking after the play 👀 (📺 FOX) pic.twitter.com/6pI64V6qBW
Evans would remember Diggs from the three games they played against each other with their previous teams. Evans and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers defeated Diggs and the Dallas Cowboys in the 2021 and 2022 regular seasons before the roles reversed in an NFC Wild Card game in January 2023.
Diggs made a massive name for himself during the peak of his career when he led the NFL in interceptions, earned a first-team All-Pro selection and secured the first of two Pro Bowl nods in 2021. He followed that campaign up with another standout season in 2022 and garnered a massive five-year, $97 million contract extension with the Cowboys.
In the years since, however, Diggs battled injuries and bounced from the Cowboys to the Green Bay Packers and eventually to the Seahawks. Seattle elevated Diggs from its practice squad for Sunday's game.
Name-checking a player who was recently among the league's best defensive players and is now battling for a roster spot is the kind of troll work that goes viral on social media. Evans made waves throughout the NFL community for his trash-talking theatrics.
"Mike plays with an edge," 49ers offensive tackle Trent Williams said to CBS Sports Bay Area . "He plays with a huge edge. Something that you wouldn't expect a receiver to have. But that was pretty funny."
author: Carter Bahns

title: Week 5 overreactions: Vikings legitimate Super Bowl contenders? NFC East champ to have losing record?
summary: Plus, is it time for the Commanders to fire Dan Quinn?
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings have the longest active winning streak in the NFL .
Yes, those Minnesota Vikings, who just made the Saints the latest victim of the Brian Flores torture chamber defense. This is a team that's now won 10 straight games dating back to last year. In Flores' latest masterpiece, the Vikings held Tyler Shough to 96 passing yards, no touchdowns and two interceptions. Minnesota basically doubled New Orleans in time of possession and owned a 364-142 yardage advantage.
In this column, I try not to get overboard too quickly — it's still early, yada yada — but it's time to really project forward, and the Vikings might be the least-talked-about 5-0 team in NFL history.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
Some numbers lie. These don't:
Flores is the best coordinator in the NFL. We already knew this defense was excellent, but it was encouraging to see Kyler Murray play his best game with the Vikings yet. He completed 24 of 30 passes (80%) for 229 yards and a touchdown to Justin Jefferson , and he ran the ball seven times for another 54 yards, excluding three kneeldowns. They aren't absurdly good numbers, but they don't need to be if the defense is going to be this dominant.
Here's the stuff Murray can do to take this team to another level. The Vikings were actually down 7-6 early in the third quarter before a touchdown drive where Murray scrambled for 18 yards on third-and-10 and then threw a beauty of a touchdown to Jefferson on third-and-6.
OH MY JETTAS ✈️ @MINvsNO on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/9JQWo9ugMo
Later, with the score tied, Murray sparked what proved to be the game-winning drive with a 32-yard pass to Jeshaun Jones . This was by far his best performance in Minnesota, and it makes sense considering he suffered a concussion in Week 1. The Vikings' ground game also had its best day, a byproduct of not only Murray's running but the threat of his running.
Murray doesn't have to be great. But if he can take care of the ball, find Jefferson — who made some spectacular catches — and make a few timely plays, this is a legitimate Super Bowl contender.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
Only one team — the 1992 Chargers — has made the playoffs after starting 0-4. Can the 2026 Texans join them? It shouldn't be ruled out.
The Texans thumped the hapless Titans 26-3. With DeMeco Ryans taking over play-calling, the defense was at its very best, allowing just 187 yards and 3.2 yards per play. Will Anderson Jr ., who is on track to not only win Defensive Player of the Year but potentially dominate the vote, sacked Cam Ward three times, and Houston forced two turnovers. C.J. Stroud threw for one touchdown and ran for another.
But this isn't really about this game, because the Titans are hardly a good measuring stick. Rather, it's about what the Texans still can do. Remember, this is an organization that made the playoffs after starting 0-3 last year. This year's team isn't last year's team, but it can have similar success, especially because Stroud is playing really well when Nico Collins is on the field. Plus, look at the Texans' upcoming schedule:
The Texans could be favored in all of those games, or at least the next five after the Jaguars game. If the defense is back to dominating, writing off the Texans simply because history says 0-4 teams don't make the postseason would be a mistake.
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
The NFC East did not have a banner week. The Cowboys dropped a home game to the previously winless Buccaneers , led by undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels , on Thursday. Sunday morning, the Eagles lost after taking a two-point lead with eight seconds and inexplicably giving the Jaguars a returnable kickoff. After a big return, Cam Little made a 57-yard field goal as time expired, and Nick Sirianni said, "I cost us that game."
All of that paled in comparison to the utter disaster that was the end of the Commanders-Giants game. With no timeouts left and well within field goal range, Washington somehow ran out of time with a completely incompetent final sequence.
The Commanders can't get the play off in time and this game ends in a tie pic.twitter.com/WmPp6q5hU0
That means the 3-1-1 Giants are still in first place in the division, the Cowboys and Eagles are 2-3, and the Commanders are 1-3-1 and reeling.
It becomes really, really difficult to see any team in this division reaching 10 wins, simply because each team has major issues. The Cowboys can't defend anyone. The Eagles can't score. The Giants are putting their trust in Jameis Winston , and the Commanders can't stop anyone and seem on the brink of collapsing completely.
Only once has the NFC East (as currently constructed) had a champion with a losing record. I won't go that far yet, but no team reaching double-digit wins is very much on the table.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
I hate advocating for anyone to be fired, but the NFL is a results-driven business, and the results just aren't good enough for the Commanders. As Quinn said , Sunday's tie feels like a loss, and it feels like another lost season in the nation's capital.
And that's a bummer, because Jayden Daniels looked truly excellent in his return from a dislocated elbow. The chance for the Commanders to be right in the thick of things in such an underwhelming division was right there.
Quinn put all the blame for the debacle on his shoulders, as he should have. But the idea that it's time for him to be fired goes deeper than Sunday. A week earlier, a poor fourth-and-1 decision using a third-string quarterback turned a winnable game against the Colts into a blowout loss. Sunday, he made another poor fourth-down decision, opting to punt from positive territory instead of going for it. The Giants' offense was rolling with three touchdowns on three drives to force overtime, and then in overtime, New York had moved the ball again easily but missed a field goal.
Giving the Giants a possession in a next-score-win scenario, therefore, was a bad idea. Cam Skattebo actually bailed Quinn out with a horrible fumble with the Giants again in field goal range, only for Quinn to make his worst mistake yet. Washington has now won just three of its past 17 games.
Quinn's performance has been fire-worthy. The thing is, the Commanders have two first-time coordinators. There is one former head coach on staff — running backs coach Anthony Lynn — but upending the staff would be a tough development in a season that's quickly slipping from returning to the playoffs to simply hoping Daniels can stay healthy and continue to progress. Owner Josh Harris is known for being patient (he owns the "Trust the Process" 76ers), and, in his first year as Washington's owner, he gave Ron Rivera an entire season.
Long story short, Quinn will likely keep his job at least through the end of the year, but that is more a product of circumstance than of deserving it.
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
Malik Willis was in the news this week when Bengals safety Jordan Battle told reporters he had a "tell" for when Willis would throw. And guess who picked off Willis twice Sunday ? Jordan Battle.
I won't sit here and say Willis was good Sunday. His second interception was awful. He was once again very inaccurate, and he has the highest off-target rate in the NFL this season by far.
But there are three reasons the Dolphins shouldn't bench Willis:
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
A big part of the Seahawks giving up 32 points was four(!) turnovers, including an absolutely inexcusable George Holani fumble just seconds before halftime that resulted in a 49ers touchdown.
The Seahawks now have nine turnovers this season; entering "Sunday Night Football," only four teams have more. Sam Darnold has always been turnover-prone, and he had two picks Sunday.
But what if I told you the Seahawks had 28 turnovers last year, second-most in the NFL? Surely, you can't win a Super Bowl like that, right? Wrong, apparently. After all those…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: NFL Week 5 winners and losers: Commanders botch overtime as 49ers take command of NFC West
summary: Jayden Daniels and Cam Skattebo failed to execute in the clutch, while the 49ers delivered a third divisional win
full_text:
None of the four teams in the NFC East won a game in Week 5 despite the fact that two of them played against each other. Following the Dallas Cowboys ' embarrassing loss on "Thursday Night Football" and the Philadelphia Eagles ' last-second collapse in London, the rival New York Giants and Washington Commanders played to a 27-27 tie.
If any of those teams came away from the week feeling good about themselves, it was the Giants, who escaped defeat in that draw. But they tossed away a chance to win that game, too.
On the other side of the country, there is a clear top dog in the NFC West. The San Francisco 49ers might be the best team in football. Their 5-0 start and the statement win over the Seattle Seahawks are impossible to ignore.
And back on the topic of this week's international game, the Jacksonville Jaguars stunned the Eagles with a walk-off field goal. It was fitting that they put the game away on special teams, considering the third phase was, for multiple reasons, the story of the day in England. That narrow victory improved them to 4-1 and made them one of the biggest winners in the NFL on Sunday .
Here are the other major winners and losers from Week 5.
After both teams went scoreless on their first possession of overtime, all Cam Skattebo needed to do to help the Giants defeat the Commanders was hang onto the football. He and the New York offense were on the plus side of the field in a next-team-scores situation when he coughed it up and dashed the Giants' chances of stealing one in the nation's capital.
Then the game's execution got even worse. Washington threw away the gift it received by squandering a game-winning opportunity of its own. The contest ended in an unbelievable 27-all tie .
The Commanders were in field goal range with under a minute to play and did not have any timeouts remaining. Jayden Daniels took his time orchestrating what proved to be the final play of the contest and left everyone baffled by what happened after the snap. With his receivers covered, Daniels scrambled around the pocket and went down to the ground, and he appeared unaware of the situation as he sat on the turf with no sense of urgency as the clock ticked toward triple zeroes. By the time Daniels made it back to the line of scrimmage, it was too late to spike the ball.
The Commanders can't get the play off in time and this game ends in a tie pic.twitter.com/WmPp6q5hU0
Washington coach Dan Quinn chucked his headset in frustration. Giants players celebrated as if they won the game. Nobody quite believed what they had just witnessed. It was the second time between the Giants and Commanders in their last nine meetings following a draw in 2022, and it was one that should have never ended with a level score.
The NFC West runs through San Francisco. The 49ers have already played every other team in the best division in football and defeated each of them. Sunday's 32-29 win over the Seahawks not only kept their perfect start to the season alive but also gave them a full two-game lead over the rest of the division. At this point in the campaign, that is an impressive feat, given the presence of both the reigning Super Bowl champions and the preseason favorites.
Note: Rams to play on "Monday Night Football"
The 49ers are one of just three remaining undefeated teams, and one of them (the Kansas City Chiefs ) has only played four games. San Francisco holds two of the best wins of the season with a blowout of the Rams and a road win at the Seahawks. Brock Purdy is a strong early contender for the MVP award. Mike Evans , with his 113-yard effort in Seattle, just continues to do Mike Evans things. Everything about their resume suggests the 49ers are real players in the Super Bowl race.
If the Jaguars had lost on Sunday, special teams would have been a major reason why. A missed extra point on a fourth-quarter touchdown opened the door for the Eagles to take a one-point lead with a mere eight seconds to play, but that was just enough time for the Jaguars' placekicking operation to redeem itself and walk things off in London with a win .
The failed PAT was largely a product of a high snap from defensive tackle and backup long snapper DaVon Hamilton , who took over special teams duties when starter Ross Matscik suffered an injury. Hamilton was thrust back into action minutes later when Ameer Abdullah rattled off an electric kickoff return to set the Jaguars up with a game-winning field goal attempt, and while he was a tad high with that snap, too, it was accurate enough to help Cam Little nail a 57-yarder for the 19-17 victory.
Little, known for his prowess on lengthy attempts, saved the day and prevented the Jaguars from dropping a game to the injury-riddled and highly scrutinized Eagles. His kick made up for the team's pair of fourth-and-goal failures and his prior miss while extending the Jaguars' winning streak to three games and building on an early-season cushion atop the AFC South.
Two players saw action on only one play in the Week 5 international game. Jaguars defensive end Bryan Thomas Jr . (not to be confused with their wide receiver, Brian Thomas Jr. ) and Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr . both received unsportsmanlike conduct penalties after they tangled up in a scuffle on the opening kickoff , and the officiating crew ejected them from the game.
The apple did not fall far from the tree in the Trotter family. Trotter's father, Jeremiah, was ejected ahead of the 2005 season opener when he got into a pregame fight with an opponent.
Later in the day, Dre Greenlaw had to watch about two and a half quarters of the San Francisco 49ers ' game against the Seattle Seahawks from the locker room. After he drew a flag for a late hit on Sam Darnold , the 49ers linebacker got into an altercation with several Seahawks on their sideline and head-butted linebacker Ernest Jones , who did not have his helmet on at the time. Greenlaw was ejected for that head-to-head contact.
The biggest disappointment in the NFL through three weeks is no longer a letdown. Drake Maye has the New England Patriots cooking with their first set of consecutive victories this year. The bounce back from a terrible three-game stretch has been emphatic, too. One week after they defeated the AFC East-leading Buffalo Bills , the Patriots demolished the Las Vegas Raiders in the biggest offensive performance of the Mike Vrabel era and their greatest victory, by margin, of the year.
Maye led the league in interceptions and fumbles through four games but was turnover-free for the first time this season in Sunday's 45-17 rout . He did not just limit mistakes, though. The former first-round pick was the catalyst of the high-scoring effort with his 26-for-34 passing effort, 403 scrimmage yards and five total touchdowns. It was an outing that more closely resembled those of his MVP runner-up campaign than the head-scratching first month of the 2026 season.
Sept. 28, 2025 vs. Panthers
If this is the version of Maye the Patriots see the rest of the year, they should be right back in the playoff hunt as expected. It seems as though he turned the corner, and he could be even better in the weeks to come when A.J. Brown returns from his high ankle sprain and elevates the wide receiver group's ceiling.
The Houston Texans won on and off the field in Week 5, which was quite the reversal of fortunes from the first month of the season when they went without a single victory. They have a long way to go if they are to become the first team since the 1992 San Diego Chargers to bounce back from an 0-4 start and make the playoffs, but Sunday was a start.
First, Houston convincingly defeated the Tennessee Titans in a battle between winless AFC South squads. Something had to give with their combined 0-8 record, and the Texans made sure they were the ones to avoid sole possession of last place in the division with their 26-3 rout on the road in Nashville. The defense finally lived up to expectations, and quarterback C.J.…
author: Carter Bahns

title: NFL Week 5 grades for every team: Patriots, Packers earn 'A+' while two teams get failing marks
summary: We're handing out grades for every Week 5 game
full_text:
Welcome to the Week 5 grades!
If we learned one thing this week, it's that the NFC East might want to send every head coach in the division to some sort of coaching clinic. There are four teams in that division, and somehow none of them won in Week 5, even though there was a game between two NFC East teams.
This entire week has been an absolute nightmare for the coaches in the division.
With that in mind, let's get to this week's grades, starting with the tie in Washington.

title: Are the Pack back? Green Bay, Jordan Love erupt in dominant win vs. Bears behind retooled offensive line
summary: Love's 367 yards passing are the most by a Packers QB vs. the Bears at Lambeau Field in series history
full_text:
The Chicago Bears (3-2) entered Lambeau Field in Week 5 looking to honor their recently deceased former Hall of Fame player and head coach, Mike Ditka, against their archrival, the Green Bay Packers (3-2) on Sunday.
Sunday's matchup between the NFC North foes went a lot like it did in the Brett Favre and Aaron Rodgers eras (1992-2022, 48-15 Packers, including the playoffs) than it did in Ditka's era as head coach (1982-1992, 15-5 Bears), with the Packers winning 31-7 behind a laser show from quarterback Jordan Love . Love completed 25 of his 31 throws for 367 yards and 2 touchdowns against Chicago, which makes him the Packers' record holder for the most passing yards in a game against the Bears at Lambeau Field. He beat the previous record of 345 yards passing by Lynn Dickey, set back in 1983. The victory, 24 points, ranks as the largest win against the Bears since 2014, the year Rodgers won the second of his four NFL MVPs. The Packers are now 5-3 against the Bears' in Love's eight career starts against them since 2023, including playoffs.
"We were flowing today. Executed at a really high level. I was proud of everybody. That's what it looks like when we play to our standard, and we got playmakers making plays down the field, O-line doing a great job," Love said postgame on FOX . "That's the standard for us. ... This is huge. This is a win we needed at home, getting us rolling and keep building off this."
Love went big-game hunting with regularity to both wide receiver Christian Watson (143 yards receiving and 2 receiving touchdowns on 6 catches) and wide receiver Matthew Golden (123 yards receiving on 6 catches), making Watson and Golden the first Green Bay duo with 120-plus yards receiving in a game since 2016. It last occurred when Davante Adams and Jordy Nelson accomplished the feat against the Tennessee Titans 10 years ago. Love hit Watson for gains of 42 yards (the game's first touchdown that made the score 7-0), 31 yards and 53 yards (Love's second touchdown pass that made the score 20-7 with 13:10 left in the third quarter). He connected with Golden on throws of 36 yards and 50 yards.
In total, Love connected on six of eight of his eight throws of 20-plus air yards for a career-high 258 yards and 2 touchdowns on his passes of 20-plus air yards. Per the league's Next Gen stats , only Russell Wilson (264 with the New York Giants in Week 2 of the 2025 season against the Dallas Cowboys ) had more in the NGS era (since 2016). According to ESPN Insights , Love joined Ben Roethlisberger as the only players with five completions of 30-plus air yards in a game since ESPN began tracking the metric 20 years ago in 2006.
Much of the credit for Love's game ought to go toward Green Bay's reworked offensive line. The Packers overhauled their offensive line with the signing of three veterans entering Week 4 in the aftermath of their 35-14 blowout home defeat on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 3 against the Atlanta Falcons : guard Laken Tomlinson , guard Kevin Zeitler and guard/tackle Mekhi Becton . Love had a season-high 2.76 average time to throw on Sunday against the Bears, and in each of the last two weeks at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (13.3% pressured rate) and against Chicago (23.5% pressured rate), he registered his two lowest pressured rates of the season. Not so coincidentally, Green Bay used the same offensive line starting five combination in each of the last two weeks: Jordan Morgan (left tackle), Tomlinson (left guard), Sean Rhyan (center), Travis Glover (right guard) and Anthony Belton (right tackle). Zeitler, a 36-year-old Pro Bowl guard, was active for the first time in Week 5, but he didn't register any offensive snaps in Week 5. He did contribute six snaps on special teams.
After the Bears were able to mount fourth-quarter comebacks with quarterback Caleb Williams in each of the last two meetings against the Packers, Chicago had nearly no offensive success against the Packers, averaging just 3.6 yards per play on Sunday, the lowest in a game for Bears head coach Ben Johnson in his career as an offensive coordinator and a head coach, which spans 73 games. They also tied their worst turnover margin (-5, five turnovers to zero takeaways) in a game since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger, per CBS Sports Research. Both Bears quarterbacks to enter the game, Tyson Bargent (87 yards passing and two interceptions on 12 of 21 throws) and Case Keenum (108 yards passing and an interception on 11 of 19 passing) threw interceptions, and Keenum also lost a fumble. Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze fumbling the football on a fourth-down completion accounted for the fifth giveaway.
"They were flying around today," Love said of his defense. "I don't even know how many turnovers they had, but it felt like four. They were flying around, making plays left and right. Getting us the ball back, and they have been doing that all season, so like we said, we got some losses, but ... guys just making plays."
With a rebuilt offensive line providing Love much more time to throw and a ball-hawking defense, the Packers' defense's nine takeaways are the fourth most in the NFL entering the Week 5 late afternoon games. Green Bay can envision being a playoff contender once again. On the flip side, the Bears definitely need Williams, who is out with a hamstring injury, back in the lineup. Williams' return may not be able to fix Chicago's leaky secondary on the other side of the ball.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Robert Saleh backs Cam Ward as Titans' starting QB despite 0-5 start
summary: Robert Saleh says Tennessee will give Ward "every opportunity to be successful" despite the quarterback's limited second-year progress
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans are winless and own the lowest-scoring offense in the NFL , but they will stick with the status quo at the most important position. Coach Robert Saleh committed to Cam Ward as his starting quarterback in the wake of Sunday's 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans .
Ward experienced another miserable day. He was fairly accurate at 23-for-36 but inefficient, as those completions resulted in just 170 yards and no touchdowns. He threw an interception and took four sacks. Still, the Titans intend to search for improvement on the fly rather than hitting the pause button on Ward's tenure as a starter.
"Cam's our starting quarterback," Saleh said postgame . "We're gonna give him every opportunity to be successful this year. We're gonna continue working with him, grinding with him and trying to help him get better."
Some of the struggles this week could be attributed to those around Ward and the caliber of the defense on the other side of the ball. He faced pressure on 21 dropbacks, which was the second most in a game in his career, per Next Gen Stats. He went 9-for-16 under pressure for 70 yards with the one interception.
While some of Ward's teammates have helped him avoid pressure, he has also not held up his end of the deal when under duress. Through four games, Ward averaged a league-low 2.6 yards per attempt when under pressure and tallied the fewest yards of any quarterback in the NFL in such situations.
Entering Week 5, Ward ranked 20th in the NFL in passer rating, 23rd in passing yards and 25th in EPA per dropback. His latest performance will move him no closer to the top of the leaderboard.
One of the questions facing the Titans is whether it is more beneficial to Ward's long-term future to keep throwing him onto the field in a dysfunctional offense or to pull the plug so as to prevent further damage to his confidence. He would not be the first quarterback to gain something from a benching, but at the same time, he is supposed to be the cornerstone of the franchise and needs as much experience and as many growth opportunities as possible.
"I just think my process," Ward said , is the reason he deserves to remain the starter. "What I'm willing to sacrifice each and every week to get to the player that I want to be, but also the player the team needs and the organization needs to win games. I love the criticism. I love everything that comes with the quarterback territory. At the end of the day, it's the best position in the world. Stuff goes the right way, you take all the credit. Stuff goes the wrong way, you take all the blame.
"I know I'm capable of this position. I have the right guys around me to uplift me and myself uplift them, and eventually we're going to put it together."
The jump from Year 1 to Year 2 is often the largest of a given player's career, but that has not been the case for Ward. He is on pace for fewer touchdown passes in 2026 than in his rookie season. He could exceed his interception tally from a year ago. His passer rating is worse this season than last. And it is entirely possible that he will finish the campaign with a worse record than the 3-14 mark he logged as a first-year Titan.
That is despite (or perhaps because) of a coaching change that some thought could spark a breakout. Offensive coordinator Brian Daboll has not orchestrated the kind of progress the Titans hoped to see. His quarterback coaching skills thus far in Tennessee have more closely resembled those of his New York Giants coaching tenure than those of his time as the Buffalo Bills ' offensive coordinator.
There is time for Ward to skirt "bust" status, but as last year's No. 1 overall draft pick, he needs to blossom into a capable starting quarterback at the very least in order to deliver on expectations. As the Titans flounder toward another early draft pick in 2027, they will have to decide whether Ward remains the future of the franchise. His trajectory does not indicate a breakthrough is on the horizon, but perhaps with Saleh's intention to keep him in the lineup, he and the young core around him will generate momentum by the end of the season.

title: What Commanders' Dan Quinn, Jayden Daniels said after jarring end-of-game mistake in tie vs. Giants
summary: Daniels took accountability for the mishap, saying ultimately, it's on him
full_text:
The Washington Commanders just needed to stop the clock with enough time to kick a field goal, and they had a good chance to defeat the New York Giants in the final seconds of overtime. Instead, what happened was a comedy of errors . The Commanders ran out of time, and the divisional game ended in a 27-27 tie, the first tie of the 2026 season.
On second-and-8 with 12 seconds remaining, quarterback Jayden Daniels scrambled, found no one open and held on to the ball.  He went down around the line of scrimmage with about eight seconds to go. The one thing the Commanders' offense needed not to do on that play was keep the ball in bounds and allow the clock to continue to wind.
With no timeouts remaining, time ticked down as the Commanders scrambled to get the ball lined up and snapped, hoping to spike it with enough time to kick about a 41-yard field goal.
They didn't have nearly enough time.
The Commanders can't get the play off in time and this game ends in a tie pic.twitter.com/WmPp6q5hU0
What Washington should've done was kick the field goal on second down, as the next score would win the game anyway. Instead, they got "cute," as they say, and tried to give themselves a few more yards, not just failing there, but losing any chance to win the game.
After the game, Daniels and Quinn addressed the mishap and explained, or did their best to explain, what happened.
Daniels took responsibility for the mistake and noted that everyone needs to improve.
"We all gotta be better situationally. Starts with me," Daniels said. "Everybody will say the same thing, but we just gotta be better at situational football."
When asked what his goal was on the play that ate up all their time, Daniels said , "We've got to stop the clock... We've gotta relay that as an offense. It starts with everybody — top down, but ultimately it's on me."
He was then asked if he heard anything or said anything in the huddle about not having a timeout, but he didn't give much away on whether the offense was clued into their situation.
"Um, just got to be better, just got to be better," he said.
Head coach Dan Quinn didn't place the blame solely on Daniels, also taking accountability for putting his team in that situation. He said he hadn't spoken to Daniels about it yet, but said, "It falls on me." Quinn complimented Daniel's performance outside of the final play, adding that his QB made some incredible plays and showed why "he's so unique."
He emphasized that he didn't need to put Daniels in the space to make such a mistake, noting that they could've won it then.
"At the end, I can make life easy there," Quinn said . "We didn't need to gain more yards."
The head coach said he himself feels frustrated and is frustrated for the team. While it may read as a tie in the standings, Quinn said it feels like a loss.
One play doesn't win or lose a game, but when it's so jarring and handled so poorly, it can feel that way. The Commanders had other chances to set themselves up to win, so they wouldn't need to be in a position to kick a game-winning field goal.
The Commanders fell to 1-3-1 and are in last place in a struggling NFC East division. The Giants fell to 3-1-1 and are in first place in the division, thanks to the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys both losing this week.
Washington will face the San Francisco 49ers in Week 6.
