The platform also has a support team available 24/7 via live chat, and provides contact information for state and national helplines for those who need additional help. If you think you may have a gambling problem, you can call or text 1-800-MY-RESET.
author: Owen OBrien

title: 49ers' Dre Greenlaw ejected after head-butting Seahawks' Ernest Jones during confrontation
summary: A late hit on Sam Darnold along the Seattle sideline sparked a confrontation that ended with the San Francisco linebacker head-butting a helmetless player
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks vs. San Francisco 49ers has been one of the best rivalries the NFL has had to offer in recent years, but things went a bit too far during the second quarter of their Week 5 matchup.
49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw drew a flag for a late hit on Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold along the Seattle sideline. He was then confronted by several Seahawks players, including linebacker Ernest Jones . During the confrontation, Greenlaw head-butted the helmetless Jones, which led to his ejection.
Check out what happened here:
Things are getting heated between the Seahawks and 49ers. 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/zBceUkZEHj
Greenlaw was ejected after headbutting Jones on the sideline pic.twitter.com/N8M1ucPWfD
Greenlaw is one of the 49ers' best players on defense, and entered this matchup ranked second on the team in tackles with 34. He's also their emotional leader. That was on full display during San Francisco's Week 4 victory against the Denver Broncos last Sunday, when he confronted his former head coach Sean Payton, telling him to "Get the f--k off the field." He was also fined $11,941 by the league for taunting the Broncos' bench.
"He was fired up all week," George Kittle said of Greenlaw last Sunday. "I think you could've asked anybody who played with Dre Greenlaw for his first four or five years he was here, I think 90% of the roster would say that he was their favorite teammate."
As evidenced by Sunday, sometimes that emotion can have unwanted ramifications. Greenlaw received a one-game suspension last season when he ran after an official and jawed at them following a game-winning field goal. Officials have also ejected him twice in previous games. Greenlaw was kicked out of a game in 2022 following a helmet-to-helmet hit on Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert , and then during the 2022 playoffs, when he famously got into an altercation with Philadelphia Eagles head of security Dom DiSandro .
49ers' Dre Greenlaw has been disqualified from tonight's game after this incident on the Eagles sideline. pic.twitter.com/2N4W17N8u9
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Commanders-Giants tie: Washington delivers disastrous end-of-game sequence following Cam Skattebo fumble
summary: A furious Dan Quinn watched the Commanders waste their chance to win after Jayden Daniels went down with eight seconds left in overtime
full_text:
The Washington Commanders and the New York Giants played to the NFL's first tie of the season, a 27-27 finish. The Commanders stunningly ran out of time in a complete meltdown at the end of the extra session. Here's the final play:
The Commanders can't get the play off in time and this game ends in a tie pic.twitter.com/WmPp6q5hU0
The Commanders -- who had no timeouts -- were extremely casual, letting the clock run after the previous play. They had absolutely no reason to run the clock down, considering it was a next-score-wins situation. The blunder created a surreal scene: Giants defenders jumping for joy as if they had won, Commanders players slouched over in disbelief and Dan Quinn absolutely furious.
Dan Quinn Destroyed His Headset On The Ground After This Mistake. He’s Furious. 😬 pic.twitter.com/2454ONncsk
He has no one to blame but himself.
The play appeared to be a Jayden Daniels pass, but the quarterback never threw the ball and then went down. With eight seconds left when Daniels went down, Washington could not line up for a spike in time, a shocking failure for a team that was fortunate to be in the situation anyway. Again, Washington had no reason to even run any play other than a spike. In fact, they didn't even need that. They could have simply had Drew Stevens attempt the game-winning kick from roughly 41 yards
The Giants trailed 27-13 with less than eight minutes left in regulation before two Jameis Winston touchdown passes forced overtime. New York got the ball to start overtime and drove into Washington territory before Dominic Zvada missed a 46-yard field goal.
The Giants forced a quick three-and-out, though, and went on another long drive, this time in a next-score-wins scenario. The Giants were at the Washington 24-yard line -- well inside Zvada's range -- but wanted to get closer, given that kicker Zvada had missed three field goals at that point. But Daron Payne punched the ball out from Cam Skattebo , an inexcusable mistake from the Giants' running back.
COMMANDERS BALL @NYGvsWAS on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/7PNuoNGQRw
Skattebo couldn't have known it then, but it only turned out to be the second-worst mistake of the afternoon. The Commanders not knowing the situation is truly atrocious on every level -- from Quinn to offensive coordinator David Blough to Daniels -- and an absolute gut punch for a team that had hoped Daniels' return from a dislocated elbow would provide a spark. Instead, it resulted in one of the most shocking errors anyone will see at the professional level and more scrutiny on Quinn and the entire organization.
The Giants (3-1-1) still lead the NFC East and, in fact, even gained a half-game on the field with the Cowboys and the Eagles both losing. The Commanders go to 1-3-1 in embarrassing fashion.
Both Quinn and Daniels addressed the media after the game and took responsibility for the blunder.
"We all gotta do better situationally, football starts with me, everybody will say the same thing but we just gotta be better at situational football," Daniels said. "We gotta stop the clock, we gotta know that it's 'o zone' situation, we gotta relay that as an offense. It starts with everybody, top down, ultimately it's on me."
But Quinn took all the blame.
"After the first down run, still trying to gain more for the kick. Right call is honestly we can go clock it early and don't put ourselves in that spot, and that's my responsibility, nobody else's."
But if the initial goal was to get closer, Quinn made two mistakes. Washington ran its penultimate play -- a two-yard Rachaad White carry -- with 55 seconds left in overtime, more than enough time to run multiple more plays, even without a timeout. And again, this cannot be stressed this enough: Washington had no reason to run the clock down. The Giants weren't going to get another possession if Stevens made his kick. And if it's yards Washington wanted, there was no reason to take so long between White's run and the final play, which started with 12 seconds left; even running any non-spike play at that point is risky.
Once the clock had run down so far, the final play was supposed to be a spike or a throwaway, Quinn said. Instead, it was neither.
"The sequencing of that does not fall on [Daniels]," Quinn said. "It's an out-of-bounds throw or a clock. That has to come from me. I don't even need to put him into that spot."
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Marvin Harrison Jr. trade grades: Cardinals extract near-max value from Texans for former top-5 pick
summary: Arizona dealt Harrison Jr. for multiple draft picks, including a 2027 second-round pick
full_text:
The awkward separation between wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr . and the Arizona Cardinals is now complete.
He is now a Houston Texan after his new team reportedly sent multiple draft picks to Arizona in exchange for the fourth overall pick from the 2024 NFL Draft . Houston shipped a 2027 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Cardinals in exchange for the 24-year-old wideout and a 2027 seventh-round draft choice.
Harrison Jr., the son of Pro Football Hall of Famer Marvin Harrison, is now the first wide receiver since Ahmad Rashad in 1974 to be traded within his first three years in the NFL after being selected as a top-five pick, per CBS Sports Research. Rashad was also traded from the Cardinals and was shipped to the Buffalo Bills in exchange for quarterback Dennis Shaw.
Trade compensation received
2027 2nd-round pick, 2027 6th-round pick
So, who came out with the better haul in the exchange? Here are trade grades for both the Texans and the Cardinals in terms of how they made out in the deal.
The Houston Texans are grasping at straws in 2026. They are 1-4 and enter the late afternoon games in Week 5, averaging the second-fewest rushing yards per game (57.4) and the fewest rushing yards per carry (3.0) by a team's running back group in the entire league.
Houston's disappointing start has nothing to do with quarterback C.J. Stroud . His 280.4 passing yards per game rank as the fourth-most in the NFL entering the Week 5 late afternoon games, and his 6-0 touchdown-to-interception ratio is tied for the second-best in the league. Stroud's 185 throws without an interception are now the fourth most in the league through four games in NFL history, per CBS Sports Research. That's why the Texans have made their second wide receiver trade of 2026 after dealing safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round pick to the New England Patriots this offseason in exchange for veteran wide receiver Kayshon Boutte .
Stroud will be asked to put the Texans' offense on his back this season, so why not trade for a former collegiate target of his? He and Harrison Jr. were Ohio State teammates for two seasons from 2021 to 2022, and Harrison Jr.'s 14 receiving touchdowns when Stroud was the starting quarterback in 2022 are tied for the third most in a single season in Buckeyes' history.  Harrison Jr. also set or tied career-highs in catches (77), receiving yards (1,263) and receiving touchdowns (14) in that 2022 season with Stroud.
Houston also needed another wide receiver to make an impact outside of two-time Pro Bowler Nico Collins , since once-exciting wide receiver Tank Dell's NFL career was sidetracked by a significant knee injury.  Dell went down in Week 16 of the 2024 season with a dislocated kneecap, torn ACL, LCL, MCL, and meniscus damage, and he hasn't played a game since.
Marvin Harrison Jr. (2023)
Marvin Harrison Jr. (2022)*
* C.J. Stroud was Ohio State's starting QB in 2022
Houston was desperate and filled a need, but what it spent to acquire Harrison is a little rich, given the writing was on the wall that Harrison Jr.'s Cardinals' career was coming to an end.
The Cardinals did about as good a job as they could to recoup value for Harrison Jr., with everyone and their grandma aware that Harrison Jr.'s time in Arizona was a bust and about to end. A second-round pick in the vaunted 2027 NFL Draft is ideal. Plus, they moved up a round at the back of the draft, sending a 2027 seventh-round pick along with Harrison Jr. and getting a 2027 sixth-round pick back.
Despite racking up 202 targets in Arizona, the third-most on the team since 2024, he totaled just 108 catches for 1,578 yards receiving and 13 receiving touchdowns while failing to build a consistent rapport with both Kyler Murray and Jacoby Brissett . He trailed only McBridge (362) and Wilson (241) in targets on the Cardinals since entering the league.
Arizona could have earned an A- or an A if it had gotten a first-round pick in return for the former top-five pick. Harrison Jr. is under team contract for up to a maximum of three more seasons on his rookie deal, including the rest of 2026. That's a decent value for a team that believes all he needed was a change of scenery. However, what the Cardinals did receive back was solid, all things considered.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Marvin Harrison Jr. trade: Cardinals send former top-5 pick to Texans for multiple draft choices
summary: Harrison Jr. reunites with his Ohio State quarterback C.J. Stroud in Houston after a failure to launch in Arizona
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals ' divorce with 2024 fourth overall pick wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr . is actually happening. Arizona is trading the 24-year-old, along with a 2027 seventh-round pick, to the Houston Texans for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick, according to ESPN . Texans head coach confirmed the trade on Sunday, following Houston's first win of the year, a 26-3 victory over the Tennessee Titans .
The trade was announced during the Cardinals' game against the Detroit Lions , a game in which Harrison was inactive due to the pending trade. Rumors swirled over the weekend that a trade could be imminent , and now Harrison will get a fresh start after his time with the Cardinals didn't go as expected.
Texans quarterback and Harrison's former Ohio State teammate C.J. Stroud was asked about the trade after his game.
"You want to know more? I don't know what more I can tell you," Stroud said with a smile. "I think he's a great guy, think he's a great player, and I'm excited to get him here."
The Texans were one of the top teams in the conversations surrounding a Harrison trade, in large part due to the wide receiver's connection with Stroud. The two played at Ohio State together in 2021 and 2022. On Saturday, as the trade rumors were taking over the league, CBS Sports' Aditi Kinkhabwala spoke with Stroud about Harrison.
"[Stroud] told me [Harrison's] an amazing talent, he told me he's a great teammate, he said that he still believes in what he can do. And he also said he's one of the hardest workers he's ever known ... Stroud said sometimes a fresh start can be really good," Kinkhabwala said.
If Stroud and Harrison can replicate, or even come close to replicating, what they did together at Ohio State, the Texans' offense will see a dramatic improvement. Harrison set or tied career-highs in receptions (77), receiving yards (1,263) and receiving touchdowns (14) in 2022 at Ohio State with Stroud at the helm.
Harrison Jr. struggled to stand out for the 1-3 Cardinals early in 2026 with five catches for 85 yards receiving and a touchdown. His five catches are tied for sixth on Arizona, ranking behind All-Pro tight end Trey McBride (33), wide receiver Michael Wilson (25), wide receiver Kendrick Bourne (13), rookie running back Jeremiyah Love (11) and running back Tyler Allgeier (10). For his Cardinals career, he totaled 108 catches for 1,578 yards receiving and 13 receiving touchdowns despite 202 targets, the third-most on the team since 2024. He trailed only McBridge (362) and Wilson (241) in targets in the span of his young career.
The Texans need another wide receiver to emerge for Stroud, aside from two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Nico Collins , with once-promising wide receiver Tank Dell's career derailed by injury. Dell went down in Week 16 of the 2024 season with a dislocated kneecap, torn ACL, LCL, MCL, and meniscus damage, and he hasn't suited up since.
Harrison Jr., the son of Pro Football Hall of Famer Marvin Harrison, is now the first wide receiver since Ahmad Rashad in 1974 to be traded within his first three NFL seasons after being selected in the top five of the NFL draft , per CBS Sports Research. Rashad was also traded from the Cardinals and was sent to the Buffalo Bills in exchange for quarterback Dennis Shaw.
Harrison is also now the fifth top-5 pick to be traded before year four in the past 10 years. The others in the same category are quarterback Zach Wilson (traded from the New York Jets to the Denver Broncos in 2024), quarterback Trey Lance (traded from the San Francisco 49ers to the Dallas Cowboys in 2023), cornerback Jeff Okudah (traded from the Detroit Lions to the Atlanta Falcons in 2023) and quarterback Sam Darnold (traded from the Jets to the Carolina Panthers in 2021).
Defending Super Bowl champion Darnold is the only player on the list to see actual success in their career after their initial trade, though it did take many stops before he got there.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Bad beat in South Beach: Dolphins' last-minute touchdown sets up painful bad beat
summary: Riley Patterson's missed extra point off the upright sealed a 31-24 win for Cincinnati, handing -6.5 spread bettors an improbable cover
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals took a trip to South Beach in Week 5, hoping to snap a two-game skid against the winless Miami Dolphins . The Bengals closed as seven-point favorites at most sportsbooks, and 6.5-point favorites at others. A Bengals cover didn't feel in doubt through the majority of the game.
By halftime, the Bengals had acquired a 14-point lead thanks to three passing touchdowns from star quarterback Joe Burrow . That lead increased to 18 points by the time we reached the fourth quarter after a 45-yard touchdown reception by Ja'Marr Chase .
However, Malik Willis trimmed the Bengals' lead to 10 points with a touchdown pass to Kevin Coleman Jr ., and a successful two-point conversion toss to Greg Dulcich with seven minutes remaining in the final quarter. Following a Bengals punt, defensive tackle Jonathan Allen stripped Willis of the ball deep in Dolphins territory and recovered it at Miami's 10-yard line. It looked like the game was well in hand.
The Dolphins then held the Bengals to a 26-yard field goal, which increased Cincinnati's lead back to 13 points. Willis then took his offense 61 yards down the field and punched in a one-yard touchdown to trim the deficit to seven points with under one minute to play.
Malik Willis adds another Dolphins TD @CINvsMIA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/PnNhnnRLl9
Since a two-point conversion wouldn't do anything, the Dolphins trotted out Riley Patterson for the extra point in hopes of making it a six-point game. Then, the Dolphins could try for the onside kick. But Patterson doinked the kick off the left upright!
Bengals -6.5 bettors saved by a missed extra point pic.twitter.com/WKOiD0Sqmy
The Dolphins couldn't recover their onside kick, and the Bengals took two kneel-downs to secure a 31-24 victory! Bengals -6.5 bettors scored a wild win, while the +7 bettors out there at least got a push. Talk about a bad beat for those backing the Dolphins +6.5!
The 3-2 Bengals are off to their best five-game start since 2021, the year they reached the Super Bowl , while the 0-5 Dolphins just became the fifth team since 1950 to not hold a lead in any of their first five games.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Will the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade unlock his potential? History offers hope, and a warning
summary: Harrison's time in Arizona is over. Here's what his trade value looks like and what history says about a fresh start
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals felt they were getting their next star receiver when they drafted Marvin Harrison Jr . at No. 4 overall in the 2024 NFL Draft and now, less than three years later, the team is moving on. The Cardinals finalized a deal to trade the former Ohio State star to the Houston Texans .
Harrison was told on Saturday that he would be inactive for Sunday's game against the Lions as the details of the trade were finalized.
The Harrison experiment certainly didn't go the way either side expected, as 1,000-yard seasons seemed ahead of him and frequent trips to the end zone felt like a guarantee.
When Harrison joined the league after such a successful run with the Buckeyes, it didn't take much imagination to envision what the two-time unanimous All-American's NFL career might look like and the future looked hopeful. Thirty-three games later, we're having a very different conversation: Will Harrison be better off playing somewhere other than Arizona?
Maybe. And soon we will find out.
Trading for Harrison requires believing two things for the Texans: that the Cardinals haven't gotten the most out of him, and that another team can do better. The first argument is getting easier to make. The second is where things get complicated, especially when you look at what's happened to other highly drafted receivers who fell short of expectations early in their careers.
In my recent story on Carnell Tate , the fourth pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , we looked at what teams should expect from receivers drafted in the top 10. The average rookie season over the last decade was 901 receiving yards. Harrison finished with 885 in 2024, a respectable start, even if it fell short of expectations.
But things haven't gotten better. Harrison managed 608 yards in 12 games last season, and through four games in 2026, he has five catches for 85 yards. For perspective, Seahawks rookie running back Jadarian Price , who played three games before landing on IR, has four receptions. This is the same Price who was targeted just 14 times over his final two seasons at Notre Dame. Harrison was targeted at least 13 times in four different games during his final season at Ohio State.
Through 33 NFL games , Harrison has 1,578 receiving yards. Amari Cooper , also drafted fourth overall, had 2,285 yards at the same point. Corey Davis , the fifth pick in 2017, had 1,503. Harrison's production looks much closer to Davis's than Cooper's.
Harrison vs. first-round receivers early in their careers
Yards after catch/reception
There are encouraging numbers here. Harrison's 13 touchdowns are more than Cooper (12) or CeeDee Lamb (11) had through their first 33 games. He's also ninth in explosive receptions per target. But he's near the bottom in catch rate and yards after the catch. The big plays are there; the consistent production isn't.
Perhaps the biggest concern isn't simply that Harrison has struggled. It's that he became less involved in Arizona's offense, even while playing more.
Among 41 first-round receivers in their first four appearances of Year 3, Harrison ranks 39th in receiving yards and is tied for the fewest receptions.
Harrison's disappearing opportunities
Typical Year 3 1st-round WR
That last row tells the story. Harrison was targeted on roughly one of every five routes through his first 29 games. This season, it's fewer than one in 10. And that raises a fair question: Is Harrison struggling because he isn't getting opportunities, or is he not getting opportunities because he's struggling?
There's evidence for both. Harrison ran 17 go routes in the first two games , tied for sixth most in the league, and Jacoby Brissett took some responsibility after Harrison went without a catch. But we can't blame everything on the quarterback or scheme when Trey McBride and Michael Wilson have combined for 58 receptions through four games. Harrison has five.
Despite the social-media noise, I'd be careful about giving up on Harrison. Plenty of first-round receivers have needed time to develop, but there's a difference between becoming productive and becoming the player a team thought it was drafting.
Corey Davis, Mike Williams and DeVante Parker all improved after modest beginnings. Each had at least one season that justified some of that early optimism. The problem? None consistently produced like the elite receiver his draft position suggested. And Davis was drafted the highest of the three, at No. 5 overall, one spot after Harrison.
Then there's Lamb, who went from a good young player to one of the NFL's best. But he was already averaging more than 62 yards per game through 33 appearances, considerably better than Harrison's 47.8.
How other first-round WRs developed
Williams and Parker eventually had 1,000-yard seasons, and Davis nearly got there with 984 in 2020. Harrison is young enough to make a similar leap. But Cooper and Lamb were already much more productive at this stage. That's an important distinction.
So what happens when a first-round receiver gets a fresh start somewhere else?
Amari Cooper is the obvious success story. In 2018, Oakland traded him to Dallas, where his production jumped from 46.7 to 80.6 yards per game. He followed that with consecutive 1,000-yard seasons. Brandin Cooks also flourished after New England acquired him from New Orleans in 2017, producing 1,082 yards before adding 1,204 with the Rams the following year.
But here's the difference: Both Cooper and Cooks had already posted two 1,000-yard seasons before being traded. Their new teams weren't betting on production they'd never seen. They were building on what those receivers had already done.
The other historical comparisons aren't nearly as encouraging.
I looked at first-round receivers traded in Year 3 or Year 4, the same stage of Harrison's career. Some joined better offenses or played with better quarterbacks. Most never became the players their new teams hoped they would.
First-round WR trades in Years 3-4: Price and production
3rd + two 7ths; 5th sent with Dotson
1st + 3rd; 4th sent with Cooks
E.J. Gaines + 2nd; 6th sent with Watkins
Cooper is the clearest example of a receiver taking his game to another level. Cooks maintained his production, while Sammy Watkins remained useful without ever returning to his 1,000-yard form.
But Dorsett, Coleman, Reagor, Dotson and Harry? None became the player their original teams envisioned. Injuries played a role in some cases, but changing teams didn't solve the larger problem. And that's something Harrison's new team should keep in mind when setting their expectations.
Of course, there's another reason Harrison is appealing: his contract. His new team will inherit his remaining 2026 salary and 2027 compensation, with the possibility to exercise his fifth-year option for 2028.
But what should it cost to acquire him? Houston parted with a pair of 2027 draft picks, one in the second round and another in the sixth.
The historical returns vary considerably. Dallas sent a first-rounder for Cooper. New England gave up a first and third for Cooks, getting a fourth back. Arizona surrendered a first for Hollywood Brown, with a third coming back. All three receivers had already proved themselves.
Meanwhile, Dotson cost a third and two sevenths, with a fifth going the other way. Harry and Coleman each brought back seventh-round picks.
Harrison falls somewhere in between. He wasn't going to fetch a first-rounder, but a third felt closer to his worth given his production and untapped potential. But remember, Pittsburgh got a 2028 second-round pick for Joey Porter Jr . when plenty of people thought a third was the best-case scenario.
Put another way: You never know. If Houston believes it can unlock Harrison, a second-rounder might feel like a bargain. But at that price, whoever the mystery buyer is, better have a plan for using him.
I think Harrison can be better than he's been in Arizona. We all saw what he did at Ohio State, and we've seen flashes of that ability in the…
author: Ryan Wilson

title: Raiders' Fernando Mendoza makes NFL debut: A look at how No. 1 overall pick performed
summary: The Raiders rookie QB was solid out of the gate in the Raiders' blowout loss
full_text:
It took until Week 5, but the 2026 No. 1 overall pick got to make his NFL debut. Down 45-17 in the fourth quarter against the New England Patriots , the Las Vegas Raiders opted to put Fernando Mendoza in to replace Kirk Cousins , marking the rookie's first appearance in the regular season.
Mendoza took over for Cousins, who went 19-of-28 for 243 yards and one touchdown, with just over six minutes remaining. The 2025 Heisman Trophy winner had a solid start, starting off 5-for-5, including a 16-yard pass on Vegas' final drive of the game.
The 23-year-old threw his first incompletion on 1st-and-10 on the Patriots' 20-yard line, followed by a 6-yard pass that set up 3rd-and-4 on the New England 14-yard line. An incomplete pass set up fourth down, and with nothing to lose, the Raiders went for it.
Mendoza scrambled and had a decent run, but fell just short of the line to gain, prompting a turnover on downs and an eventual victory formation for the Patriots.
The No. 1 overall pick's final stat line was 6-of-8 for 48 yards, with no touchdowns, picks or sacks taken.
Mendoza began the season as Cousins' backup and became the first No. 1 overall selected quarterback to not start Week 1 since 2018 ( Baker Mayfield ).
Heading into this week, Cousins was tied for the league high in passing touchdowns with 11.
The Patriots extended their win streak to two games and improved to 3-2 with the 45-17 win. The Raiders, who were one of the league's last remaining undefeated teams, are now 3-2, dropping their last two wins. Both teams have faced difficult AFC opponents the last two weeks, with the Patriots defeating the Buffalo Bills in Week 4 and the Raiders falling to the Kansas City Chiefs last week.
The Raiders have another challenge next week, when they face the Bills.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Aaron Rodgers passes Peyton Manning, Ben Roethlisberger in NFL record book after Week 5 win
summary: Rodgers' big day helped the Steelers improve to 3-2
full_text:
Sunday was an eventful day for Aaron Rodgers , whose farewell season is off to a 3-2 start for the Steelers following their win over the Colts .
Not only did Pittsburgh secure a 34-22 win against Indianapolis, but Rodgers made some improvements in the NFL record books, passing both Hall of Fame quarterback Peyton Manning and former Steelers quarterback Ben Roethlisberger .
Rodgers moved past Manning to No. 3 on the career touchdown pass list when he connected with Jaylen Warren on an 80-yard score in the first quarter. Rodgers and Manning had been tied at 579 touchdown passes prior to Sunday.
After the win, Rodgers spoke to what it means to him to move past such a legendary quarterback on an all-time list.
"Anytime you're in the same sentence as Peyton [Manning], that definitely does mean a lot to me," Rodgers told CBS Sports' Tracy Wolfson, adding with a smile that he thinks he "earned that one" because he took a shot on the pass.
"Anytime you're in the same sentence as Peyton [Manning], that definitely does mean a lot to me." @tracywolfson caught up with Aaron Rodgers after he moved up a historic list in a @steelers W pic.twitter.com/ksKWWp5PfE
Manning, who played from 1998-15, is the only player who has more league MVPs than Rodgers. Manning won the award a record five times (2003, 2004, 2008, 2009, and 2013), while Rodgers has won it four times (2011, 2014, 2020, and 2021).
Rodgers now trails only Tom Brady (737) and Drew Brees (608) in career touchdown passes.
Jaylen Warren with the 80-yard touchdown! @INDvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Q49IxXTuCP
Rodgers also passed Roethlisberger with his 166th regular-season win as a starting NFL quarterback. He now has sole possession of fifth all-time in that department behind only Tom Brady (251), former teammate Brett Favre (186), Peyton Manning (186) and Drew Brees (172).
On Sunday, Rodgers had his best game of the season despite three of his receivers being out due to injury. Rodgers, who threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns on 22-of-31 passing, became the first Steelers quarterback since Hall of Famer Terry Bradshaw to throw three touchdowns in three consecutive games.
Rodgers received big contributions on Sunday from Warren, tight end Pat Freiermuth , and rookie wideout Germie Bernard . Freiermuth caught two touchdown passes, and Bernard set a season-high with 80 yards on six receptions.
WIIIIDE OPEN @pat_fry5 pic.twitter.com/TJHwrFLaXb
Warren, who is enjoying his best season to date, ran for 101 yards on 15 carries and had 87 yards on six catches. He is the first player since Herschel Walker back in 1986 to have an 80-yard touchdown catch and a 50-yard touchdown run in the same game.
JAYLEN WARREN JUST RAN STRAIGHT THROUGH THE ENTIRE COLTS DEFENSE 😱 @steelers pic.twitter.com/WsM2nCdApZ
Rodgers was well-protected by an offensive line that had been under some heat following last week's loss to Cleveland. The unit, which includes a relatively new starter in rookie first-round pick Max Iheanachor , allowed just one sack and helped Pittsburgh amass 112 yards on 16 carries.
Defensively, the Steelers forced the Colts to settle for five field goals and came up with two turnovers on downs late in the game, as the Colts were attempting a comeback. It wasn't a dominant performance, but Pittsburgh's defense nonetheless showed signs of growth after its struggles in Cleveland 10 days ago.
Linebacker Payton Wilson and defensive back Jalen Ramsey specifically stood out for the Steelers. Wilson had 10 tackles and a key pass breakup on fourth down. Ramsey had nine tackles despite playing with a broken wrist. He also had a perfectly-timed hit that prevented a big play in the first half.
What a hit from @jalenramsey 😤 @INDvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/AHeRaj6MBe
With the win, Pittsburgh is now 3-0 at home this season. It'll look to pick up its first road win of the season next Sunday against the Buccaneers , who won their first game of the season last Thursday night in Dallas.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Nick Sirianni's seat getting warmer? Eagles coach accepts blame for London loss to Jaguars
summary: Philly made a controversial decision with eight seconds remaining in the fourth quarter that ultimately cost them a win
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles lost their third straight game on Sunday, falling to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, 19-17. Despite all the players who had retired, been traded or were out with injury this week, the Eagles found themselves in position to defeat one of the hottest teams in the AFC. However, a controversial decision with eight seconds remaining in the game led to a deflating loss.
With 1:35 remaining in the fourth quarter, down two points, Jalen Hurts led the offense 32 yards down the field on nine plays, setting Jake Elliott up with a chance at a 48-yard field goal. He nailed it, putting the Eagles up, 17-16, with eight seconds left on the clock.
On the ensuing kickoff, the Eagles decided to leave the ball in play instead of kicking it into the end zone, allowing Ameer Abdullah an opportunity to pick up some yards. Abdullah made the play of the game, breaking loose for 53 yards to set Cam Little up with a game-winning 57-yard field goal.
JAGS HUGE KICK RETURN. They're in range for one more shot at a field goal! @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/XSWbKBTvW2
UNBELIEVABLE. JAGS WIN. WHAT JUST HAPPENED?!?! pic.twitter.com/O7x8JTgPeK
After the game, Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni accepted blame for the decision to leave the kickoff in play and for the loss as a whole.
"I didn't make the right decision, and I lost us that game, and that's what I said to our guys, and what hurts there is that the guys fought so hard and then I don't make the decision that I should make at the end of the game and I cost us that game," Sirianni said. "I put that fully on me."
Nick Sirianni says it crystal clear: He made the wrong decision on the kickoff and he owns it Wouldn’t go into the reasoning why he decided what he did pic.twitter.com/xy0QiyIF4c
Sirianni was asked about his thought process behind his decision to kick a returnable ball, but he didn't want to elaborate. One could assume the Eagles wanted to allow a few of the eight seconds to run off the clock as the Jaguars returned the ball. However, you can't allow the returner to break loose for 53 yards.
The 2-3 Eagles are now under .500 for the first time since 2021. Sunday's loss snapped a franchise-record streak of 76 games where the Eagles were .500 or better, per CBS Sports Research. The last time the Eagles were under .500, Jason Kelce was the starting center, A.J. Brown was on the Tennessee Titans , Aaron Rodgers was still with the Green Bay Packers and Tom Brady was in his second-to-last NFL season.
Overall, it's been a bad couple of weeks in the city of Philadelphia.
Eagles lose to Case Keenum's Bears by 20 points
Flyers lose 7-0 to Penguins in season opener
Phillies eliminated by the Braves in wild-card round
Eagles blow 10-point lead to Rams at home
Franchise legend right tackle Lane Johnson retires
Eagles lose to Jaguars, 19-17
Sirianni appears to be on the hot seat , and his costly decision at the end of the fourth quarter on Sunday certainly did not help.

title: Bengals' Jordan Battle intercepts Malik Willis twice after finding tell in Miami QB's throwing mechanics
summary: Battle's huge second quarter in Week 5 may have been no coincidence
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals ' defense should take a collective bow after identifying and exploiting an advantage over the Miami Dolphins in Week 5.
Prior to the game, safety Jordan Battle revealed that the Bengals noticed a subtle tell in Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis ' throwing mechanics that they felt they could use to time their pass defense. They seemingly did just that when battle intercepted Willis twice in the first half of their meeting on Sunday.
"He has a slight little tap before every throw, so I feel like we could use that as a key to break on the ball," Battle said after the Bengals' Thursday practice . "He likes to tap the ball before he throws it, or he takes his hand off, and that gives the read to break."
How much of a role the tell played in Battle's two takeaways is uncertain. Perhaps it was a coincidence that he was the one to both point it out publicly and haul in a pair of interceptions, or maybe he and his teammates were in the right place at the right time after spotting it.
The first interception was primarily a product of the pass rush, not Battle's position group in the secondary. Boye Mafe pressured Willis and got his hand on the ball during the release, which shortened its trajectory and made it playable for Battle.
Jordan Battle intercepts Malik Willis @CINvsMIA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NJtzbBJ7vE
Five minutes later, Battle made an excellent play on the ball for his second pick of the second quarter. As Willis rolled out of the pocket, Battle left his assignment to step in front of the intended receiver and beat him to the ball.
If Willis' tell impacted either play, it is more likely that it did so on this one than the first.
Second INT of the game for Jordan Battle! @CINvsMIA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/u3fopDzcij
At the time of Willis' second interception, he had more passes caught by Cincinnati defenders than Miami receivers. He was 1-for-7 for 22 yards late in the second quarter. The Bengals capitalized on the second takeaway with a touchdown on the ensuing possession to take a 21-7 lead into the locker room at halftime.
Revealing the tell before the game was a risky move for Battle. If Willis and the Dolphins were not already keen on the tendency, they certainly were after Battle's media availability. They may have already discovered it through self-scouting, but if not, three days was not much time to eliminate the habit from Willis' mechanics.
Cincinnati entered the week with a bottom-tier pass defense, so any advantages it could identify would be welcome. The Bengals ranked in the bottom half of the league in EPA per pass, interceptions, time to throw, pass yards per game and average yards of separation. Sunday's performance should deliver a climb in the statistical rankings.

title: Beaks & Geeks: Cardinals, Lions Winners & Losers: Arizona tanks big time
summary: The Arizona Cardinals needed a win against a mediocre Detroit Lions ballclub. The Lions finished last in the NFC North Division last year, as the Cardinals finished last in the NFC West. Both clubs are involved in the “last place finish” schedule. RELATED: PETZING’S OFFENSE GETS ITS REVENGE The 1-3-0 Cardinals would end up being […]
full_text: The Arizona Cardinals needed a win against a mediocre Detroit Lions ballclub. The Lions finished last in the NFC North Division last year, as the Cardinals finished last in the NFC West. Both clubs are involved in the “last place finish” schedule. RELATED: PETZING’S OFFENSE GETS ITS REVENGE The 1-3-0 Cardinals would end up being at the bottom of the league if they lost to the Lions. As it was, Detroit took Arizona to the woodshed in a 45-21 bloodbath. The game began really good as the Cardinals went down on their first drive of the game, and scored after a 14-play drive. But in the second quarter, the Lions scored 24 unanswered points and took control of the contest with a full half to go. So, who played well for the Cardinals? Who didn’t? ——————————————————————————– BEAKS The opening drive – The Cardinals defense got Detroit to go three-and-out on their first possession, and then the offense took over on their own 27-yard line. Right off, an 11-yard catch by TE Trey McBride, followed by short receptions by TE Elijah Higgins and WR Michael Wilson. Then, a 22-yard reception and several plays later a nine-yard grab by WR Kendrick Bourne. Suddenly, Arizona was on Detroit’s 18-yard line with a third-and-10. Seven yards to Wilson set up a fourth-and-short on the Lions’ nine-yard line. The offense went for it, and QB Jacoby Brissett then found TE Teagan Quitoriano for the two-yard touchdown and a 7-0 lead. 14 plays, 73 yards, 7:54 of clock, and a temporary feeling that today would be the day. WR Kendrick Bourne – This is a guy who should have been given more reps all season long. Several good grabs to move the sticks. The 22-yard grab on the opening drive was just a preview. In the second quarter, Bourne caught an eight-yard pass that got them from being deep to manageable. Then on the next possession, Bourne corralled the Brissett pass and went 23 yards to Detroit’s 49-yard line. Led all receivers with 70 yards on five receptions. oh my McBride 😳 #DETvsAZ | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/014MXVJnXd — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 11, 2026 TE Trey McBride – Yes, the game was out of reach when McBride snagged that bobbled touchdown with 2:11 left in the game. What a spectacular catch on a poor throw. The most amazing aspect was McBride’s feet awareness, much-less his focus on the football at all times. Had the most targets with 10, but most of those were when the game was already out of reach. What gives? Two targets and one reception at the half. Nine catches for 66 yards is a travesty. Throw him the ball! S Budda Baker – If you want someone to tackle a defender, just tell Budda. Time and time again, he took down an offensive player that his teammates had whiffed on, or let go. Led all tacklers with 11. TQ's second TD of the day 🙂‍↕️ #DETvsAZ | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/xyZ8b0q9Er — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 11, 2026 TE Teagan Quitoriano – Two targets, two receptions, two touchdowns? Why isn’t this offense getting him more involved with stats like this? ——————————————————————————— GEEKS Non-tight end coverage – All game long, the Lions’ tight ends were wide-ass open. Why? Starting TE Sam LaPorta was open on all five of his catches, and scored on a 38-yard catch and run. The play before was 11-yards to LaPorta and a 12-yard reception on the series before. There goes Sam pic.twitter.com/jWOW1mJVFT — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 11, 2026 Backup TE Brock Wright snared an 11-yard reception that converted a first down. It was so bad that LaPorta led all Detroit receivers with 88 yards, and caught all five targets. We tried to see DC Nick Rallis’ defensive game plan, and are certain it states, “No need to cover the Lions’ tight ends since they are all blockers.” Offense after the opening points – As great as the opening drive was, it became a scoring desert after that: punt, punt, punt, punt, punt, INT, missed FG, until the Cardinals scored a touchdown with 5:20 remaining in the third quarter, and then it no longer mattered. Tackling – All game long, name a Cardinals defensive player, and he missed a tackle or three. Arizona’s tackling consisted of grabbing waists or jumping on shoulder pads. Remember the wild ride by Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs where a pile of players went for 12 yards? The replay was from the end zone, the pile was headed in the direction of. In the bottom of the pile, you can see Gibbs’ legs still churning. Do they no longer teach players at this level to take out legs? Or is Budda Baker the only Cardinals defender who knows this? CB Garrett Williams had three missed tackles, while LB Mack Wilson had a pair. All game long, players who bounce off Detroit ballcarriers, including two that were third-and-long that became a first down. Pathetic display of how to bring down the other team’s ballcarriers. Wonnum with the third-down SACK pic.twitter.com/buiBiRTf7z — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 11, 2026 Offensive line – Brissett rarely had a clean pocket when he dropped back, and forget about running the ball. There were simply no lanes created all game. Brissett was sacked five times and that could have been double digits if Brissett had not gotten out of the stronghold of yet another defender. This group is in trouble now that Paris Johnson is gone for the season. 56 yards on the ground is a mess. Most passing downs were two words: Jail break. Defense, beginning with Quarter 2 – In the beginning, the defense was pretty stiff. Detroit’s first three possessions were all three-and-out followed by a punt. After the Cardinals had a three-and-out to begin the second quarter, the flood gates opened for the Lions: TD, TD, TD, FG, TD, TD, TD, punt. ———————————————————————————– Bird Seed – It starts with “hold my beer” QB Jacoby Brissett – To be fair, his pocket was in shambles for most of the game. He tried his best to get out into the flats and attempt to find an open guy, but the Lions defenders were just too much for this pieced-together offensive line. 38 yards for 8⃣4⃣ moves the chains ⛓️ #DETvsAZ | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/1RfcajfkGy — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 11, 2026 Brissett had his moments, but on passing downs, unless he rolled out, he was harassed and flushed. He went 29 for 47 for 292 yards, three TD passes against one INT, sacked five times with a QB rating of 91.8. Fourth downs – The Lions went 4 for 4 on fourth downs. Ouch. But they were a dismal 4 for 13 on third-down efficiency. RB Jeremiyah Love – At no time was this young guy a threat. Finished with 12 carries for 22 yards with a long of eight yards. This Cardinals team needs premier offensive linemen and pass rushers, and yet passed on both for another running back. DT Roy Lopez – Had a productive day and was a good anchor to stop the run up the gut. Finished with six total tackles, one sack, two tackles for loss, and one QB hit. His sack of QB Jared Goff in their second possession forced a punt. In the second quarter, Gibbs caught a short pass in the flats, and Lopez tracked him down after a 23-yard gain.

(Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images If you happened to notice that WR Kendrick Bourne and rookie Reggie Virgil were getting more receptions in the blowout loss to the Detroit Lions, you weren’t alone. It just so happened that Arizona Cardinals GM Monti Ossenfort had traded WR Marv Harrison, Jr. to the Houston Texans about the time the Cardinals-Lions game had begun. RELATED: IS THE HARRISON TRADE THE NAIL FOR OSSENFORT? There had been rumors that the team had gotten a slew of inquiries as to Harrison’s rights for about two weeks now. Even though the NFL trade deadline isn’t until November 11, several key trades have already taken place. Teams wanted to know if Harrison might become available, and Ossenfort pulled the trigger on Sunday. The one certainty is that Marvin Harrison’s time in Arizona is done. Arizona feels comfortable enough to know it can and will trade Harrison, which is why he will be inactive Sunday. But no Harrison trade will be completed until after Sunday’s games are played. https://t.co/qEGc9qtht0 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 10, 2026 Harrison is now with his former college quarterback, C.J. Stroud. Houston and Arizona are both 1-4-0. The Cardinals received second-and sixth-round draft picks, while the Texans got Harrison and a sixth-round pick. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur stated during his post-game presser: “I just thought it was in the best interest of this club. I’m not going to totally get into that right now. I really like Marvin Harrison. He’s a good person. I wish him well. We did what we thought was in the best interest of the Cardinals.” Last year, Michael Wilson took command of the WR1 job away from Harrison who battled several injuries. TE Trey McBride is the team’s alpha dog in targets and receptions, and youngsters Virgil and Jalen Brooks had excellent training camp plus preseason. Basically, it became a logjam in the receiver room, and Harrison seemed to be the odd fit in LaFleur’s system. Harrison was the fourth-overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft after harvesting just about every conceivable college receiver award and distinction. He had 116 targets in his rookie campaign with 62 receptions and 885 yards, but since then has been a roller coaster. This year in four games, Harrison has been targeted just 13 times with five receptions for 85 yards and one touchdown grab. LaFleur added: “Any guy that does not play to the level that I feel like they’re capable of, I’m always going to put that on me and coaching in general.” The news caught most by surprise. When asked why LaFleur came to this decision, he stated: “I’m going to keep the details tight with us.” Harrison certainly wasn’t QB Jacoby Brissett’s favorite target, or favorite anything for that matter. The two men had a really good relationship in the locker room, but is losing him such a big deal? Brissett wasn’t looking his way in most games. Right now on the depth chart, Brooks is being penciled in as their “X” receiver spot, who had two receptions for 16 yards against Detroit. Kendrick Bourne led all Cardinals receivers with five receptions for 70 yards. While with Arizona, Harrison had 10 career drops, including one this season.

summary: It’s hard to even write about this every week. The Arizona Cardinals through five weeks are playing some of the worst football in the team’s history. I was in the South endzone at Sun Devil Stadium from 1994. I’ve seen some awful games. This is getting to the point of being unwatchable. Meanwhile, Jonathan Gannon’s […]

(Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s hard to even write about this every week. The Arizona Cardinals through five weeks are playing some of the worst football in the team’s history. I was in the South endzone at Sun Devil Stadium from 1994. I’ve seen some awful games. This is getting to the point of being unwatchable. Meanwhile, Jonathan Gannon’s Packers shut down the Bears. Kyler Murray’s Viking’s move to 5-0. Drew Petzing’s offense just had over 400 yards of offense and 45-points. Somehow, moving on, which was probably the right move in all three cases, has made this team much, much worse. Now, the question is; do they keep running it back. I get it’s only week five, but the fact that this team has given 31 or more points in each game since week one, is bad. Jacoby Brissett has moved to 2-15 as a starter, his 0.118 win percentage is the worst in Arizona Cardinals history (minimum 8 starts). This is some of the most uninspired football we have seen. Brissett had 292 yards and three touchdowns, but that second touchdown happened with 4:22 left in the third and the Cardinals down by 24. The final touchdown came with 2:11 left in the game on maybe the best play of the season by Trey McBride, down 45-14. Now the 1-4 Arizona Cardinals have to go play the Los Angeles Rams. So, is it time to see Gardner Minshew? Is it Carson Beck time? What can they do on defense? There are way more questions than answers at this point into the Mike LaFleur era.

For the Cardinals, […]
full_text: CANTON, OHIO - AUGUST 06: Owner Michael J. Bidwill of the Arizona Cardinals talks with general manager Monti Ossenfort prior to the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame Game against the Carolina Panthers at Tom Benson Hall Of Fame Stadium on August 06, 2026 in Canton, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images What could have been. The Arizona Cardinals are trading Marvin Harrison Jr. to someone (the Houston Texans right now) and then you are also unaware of what they are getting (a second round pick it sounds like) and all of this will happen after the Cardinals matchup today against the Detroit Lions. For the Cardinals, that means another of the 2024 draft class no longer on the roster. In what was supposed to be the crown jewel of Monti’s work as GM, it is now looking like one of the biggest draft class disasters in recent memory. The rundown: 1.04 – Marvin Harrison Jr. 1.27 – Darius Robinson – 25 career games 12 starts 3 career sacks 7 tackles for loss 2.43 – Max Melton 3.66 – Trey Benson 3.71 – Isaiah Adams – 19 career starts 3.82 – Tip Reimain – 21 total games played (548 total snaps) 3.90 – Elijah Jones 4.104 – Dadrion Taylor-Demerson – 30 career games played (712 total snaps) 5.138 – Xavier Thomas 5.162 – Christian Jones 6.191 – Tejhaun Palmer 7.226 – Jaden Davis We can look at 2023 and the miss on not taking Will Anderson Jr., we can look at 2025 and wonder if injuries will be an issue that cause this class to not meet expectations, but the 2024 class was supposed to be the one. Now, there are five players left, they’ve played a combined 95 games and none have been difference makers. To be fair, none of the guys no longer on the roster were difference makers either. But this Marvin Harrison Jr. trade, without knowing what they are getting, and waiting a day to make it final, is just basically unheard of. Hope this works out for the Cardinals, and quite frankly hopefully it helps Marv get a fresh start. But, this also begs the question, why are they letting Monti make deals for players if he is on the hot seat?

title: Falcons vs. Ravens recap: Ghosts converge on Atlanta in an overtime loss
summary: We knew that even a banged-up Ravens team would be a tough out for the surging Falcons, but that Atlanta could increase their chances of a win by playing a clean game that played to their considerable strengths. That’s not what we got. Instead, the offense looked shaky throughout the first quarter and into the […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 11: Michael Penix Jr. #9 of the Atlanta Falcons looks to pass against the Baltimore Ravens in the second quarter of a game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images We knew that even a banged-up Ravens team would be a tough out for the surging Falcons, but that Atlanta could increase their chances of a win by playing a clean game that played to their considerable strengths. That’s not what we got. Instead, the offense looked shaky throughout the first quarter and into the second quarter, with iffy run blocking and Michael Penix Jr. running ice cold. The Falcons defense forced a fumble that Jessie Bates took to the house to give Atlanta the lead, and Penix did get untracked in the second quarter to lead a productive drive. But the Falcons fought field position issues caused by multiple special teams penalties, struggled to consistently pick up yardage on the ground, had notable miscues in run defense, and tried to get a little too cute on key fourth down and red zone plays in ways that ended up harming the effort. The Ravens, who kept settling for field goals and sticking with what they knew they could do with Tyler Huntley under center and talented backs to bring to bear, made this a tense game as a result even as Jeff Ulbrich kept them at bay and held to 15 points through three quarters. It seemed like the Falcons would still cruise to a win when they went up eight points with not much time left in the fourth quarter, but instead Huntley found endless success on passes over the middle against a gassed defense, including a touchdown, and then Derrick Henry converted the two point try to tie things up. The Falcons, with 40 seconds left, couldn’t get close enough for a field goal try in regulation. That left overtime, and a gassed defense down CJ Henderson kept showing cracks as Huntley and Henry marched down the field. Jeff Ulbrich has had answers for just about everything this year, but as the game wore on, unproductive blitzes and iffy run defense came to doom Atlanta. That left Tua Tagovailoa, in for an injured Penix, to try to lead a heroic drive down the field to tie things up or win outright down 30-23. He connected on a nice ball over the middle to Drake London and then immediately threw an interception to end things. It felt like a game the Falcons would lose as soon as the Ravens got deep into Atlanta territory late in the fourth quarter, and one of the nastiest things I can say about this game is that it felt extremely familiar. Ghosts converged on this team from every angle. The shoddy run defense that cost them repeatedly in 2025 was especially costly against a Baltimore team that knows how to run the ball. Penix’s familiar problems with pressure and accuracy, which were largely absent the past two weeks, cost the team opportunities in a way that also proved costly. Mike Hughes’ coverage struggles and the team’s depth woes at cornerback, the former which has been consistent and the latter which we hoped was a thing of the past, hit hard, though in fairness this defense was never going to be in great shape down both A.J. Terrell and CJ Henderson. Coordinators trying things that either outright don’t work or offer quickly diminishing returns played a role in this loss, too, and you can see apparitions of Zac Robinson, Jimmy Lake, Dean Pees, Dirk Koetter, and so forth floating in the air as I type that. This team lost in large part because they were spiritually if not exactly like the Falcons team that have struggled so much in the recent past. What you make of this loss likely depends on what you made of the Falcons coming into this game, and what you thought Baltimore was capable of with Huntley at quarterback. If you thought Atlanta was showing signs of being a playoff-caliber team after their two beatdowns of Green Bay and New Orleans, this will be a bitter effort to reckon with, especially if you believed the Ravens were not going to be up to snuff with so many backups in. If you thought the Falcons hadn’t faced a true test yet and the Ravens were still one of the league’s better teams even with a backup quarterback and fourth-string center in, this one will sting, but likely only a little. Either way, the Falcons have fallen back under .500, Penix is hurt (though we don’t know how badly yet), there are fresh questions and familiar questions about everything from the run defense to Jake Matthews to the secondary, and this team is back on the roller coaster we fervently hoped they had hopped off after the past two weeks. They’re neither as bad as they looked the first two weeks nor as good as they looked the last two, but if this ends up representing what this team looks like in the middle of those two poles, it’s going to be another bumpy sort of season. On to the full recap. The Good Michael Penix Jr. is streaky. He started this game ice cold, not just missing passes but missing them badly, and the offense suffered as a result. He followed that up with a second quarter drive where he caught fire, heaving bombs to Drake London and Jahan Dotson and zipping a pass by two Ravens for a Kyle Pitts touchdown. When he’s on, he can make heroic throws downfield at a rate not many quarterbacks in this league can match, and he was on enough to give this team a fighting chance until quite late. Bijan Robinson had a run in the first quarter that left me speechless, where he seemed dead in the backfield and turned around and ripped off a 15 yard run thanks to agility, toughness, and good old-fashioned magic. On a day where Brian Robinson Jr. couldn’t get any breathing room, Bijan put up a tidy five-plus yards per carry and got 86 yards on 17 carries. He probably should have had more touches, honestly, even though there were plenty of unproductive runs along the way. I give him an enormous amount of credit for the sheer effort on a bad Penix throw on the final Falcons drive of regulation, too, even though he couldn’t quite get it. I think Penix would throw the ball to Drake London if he was deep in the Pacific Ocean and Penix was on the 35 yard line in Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The level of trust between those two is unreal, and London made huge third down grabs for first downs over and over again in this one, seemingly willing himself open just enough for Penix to laser passes in there to him. London is a great receiver who just needs competent quarterback play to produce like one, and with Penix he has a quarterback who is never going to be afraid to target him. Jahan Dotson can fly, and Michael Penix Jr. loves slinging that ball downfield. That’s looking like it’ll be a fruitful combination this year, as Penix hit him for a beautiful deep touchdown in Week 4 and got him on a 36 yard bomb that set up a Falcons score in the second quarter. Kyle Pitts was going to get involved, and after he lumbered to life a bit in Week 4, he arrived in Week 5. A nice grab and run in the second quarter was a prelude to a touchdown grab to finish off that drive. Samson Ebukam has been a really good signing, and he flashed again in this one. His play of the game was the big third down, third quarter sack of Tyler Huntley, putting a swift end to a Baltimore drive when they were down just two points. Ditto Jared Ivey, who has been in and out of the rotation at outside linebacker but had an early sack in this one where he fought through a defender around his . Cameron Thomas got a half sack and Gervon Dexter got none, but they were the team’s two most consistently impactful defenders up front from my point of view. Dexter was relentless in pursuit and caught a couple of run plays from behind, while Thomas was one of the few Falcons who consistently made Huntley uncomfortable on Sunday night. Kendal Daniels was not always stellar against the run—I saw a couple of iffy angles—but his tackling was mostly incredibly sound, he was getting his hand up constantly and managed to…

title: Week 5 Snap Reactions: A late collapse dooms Falcons
summary: Dear Reader, I regret to inform you that the Atlanta Falcons blew a fourth-quarter lead and lost in overtime to the Baltimore Ravens. Here are the Week 5 Snap Reactions. The Defensive Dam Broke The Falcons defense came undone. After playing sound defense for roughly 3 quarters, Jeff Ulbrich’s unit couldn’t keep up with the […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA- OCTOBER 11: Derrick Henry #22 of the Baltimore Ravens runs the ball during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta,Georgia. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dear Reader, I regret to inform you that the Atlanta Falcons blew a fourth-quarter lead and lost in overtime to the Baltimore Ravens . Here are the Week 5 Snap Reactions. The Defensive Dam Broke The Falcons defense came undone. After playing sound defense for roughly 3 quarters, Jeff Ulbrich’s unit couldn’t keep up with the Ravens adjustments in the 4th. After not blitzing much this season, Ulbrich turned up the heat, and it worked at first. However, the blitz stopped working toward the end of the game. The Falcons generated only one pressure on 12 dropbacks during the Ravens final two drives, per NFLPro . The unit looked exhausted on the overtime drive, and injuries finally caught up with them. Early Down Struggles Late-down heroics are unsustainable; the Falcons faced too many 3rd and long situations on offense. While the 9-5 connection bailed them out most of the game, it couldn’t when the Falcons needed to sustain drives late in the game. Credit to Jesse Minter; his defense had answers for Tommy Rees on early downs, and the young OC couldn’t adjust. Bijan hit over 100 scrimmage yards yet again, but Minter forcing Atlanta to win with Penix’s arm on 3rd down eventually paid off. https://t.co/cCh7kilYaM pic.twitter.com/NjEhop4puu — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) October 12, 2026 The Devil is in the Details A Jake Matthews drop, a wide-open Bijan missed, and Zay Flowers running through Divine Deablo. It’s the little things that come back to bite you. Penix is still struggling to hit the easy passes, and unlike the previous two weeks, the run game couldn’t overcome those misses. With the season Matthews is having as a blocker and him dealing with an injury all week, I can’t imagine why they used that play now; yes, he should’ve caught the ball, but Matthews not timing a jump correctly isn’t surprising, considering he’s not a skill player. Rees got too cute, and with the options he has on offense, we haven’t seen enough opportunities for the players paid to catch the ball. The Ravens' win probability was as low as 4.6% with 3:27 left in regulation in their 30-23 comeback win over the Falcons. It was the Falcons' seventh loss since 2016 with an in-game WP greater than 95%. Only the Eagles (8) have more such losses in the NGS era. @BALvsATL pic.twitter.com/2hAGwN56gg — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) October 12, 2026 What is Michael Penix Jr.? Is he a franchise QB? Is he done after this year? Are the injuries too much to bear? The reality is, there are still a lot of games left this season before we can reach a final verdict. As it stands, his footwork is still a problem, causing him to miss too many easy opportunities; that and his inability to access multiple arm angles—he’s stiff as a board. He can make the difficult throws scouts drool over, but routinely botches the layups. These things matter more to me than the rib injury because a better throw to Bijan late in the game prevents that injury from ever happening, and these issues exist regardless of injury. His future is uncertain, and if he can’t work through these problems, the team won’t view him as the answer under center. Michael Penix passing chart pic.twitter.com/eivNOPrcuy — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) October 12, 2026 Atlanta now sits at 2-3, back under .500 yet again. Penix’s ribs will be monitored, but the team is reeling from injuries across the board, an excuse that’s hard to swallow after losing to the Ravens sans Lamar Jackson. Kevin Stefanski and his will have their work cut out for them as they hit a tough two-game stretch against some of the NFC’s best.

title: Falcons – Ravens instant recap: The overtime letdown in primetime
summary: The depleted Ravens are still a dangerous team, something we received an all-too-potent reminder of on Sunday Night Football. The Falcons had plenty of advantages—they were at home, red hot, and had their starting quarterback, to name a few—but couldn’t summon the kind of clean, hyper-effective game they needed to win comfortably. In the end, […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 11: Nnamdi Madubuike #92, Tavius Robinson #95, and Roquan Smith #0 of the Baltimore Ravens tackle Bijan Robinson #7 of the Atlanta Falcons in the first quarter of a game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The depleted Ravens are still a dangerous team, something we received an all-too-potent reminder of on Sunday Night Football. The Falcons had plenty of advantages—they were at home, red hot, and had their starting quarterback, to name a few—but couldn’t summon the kind of clean, hyper-effective game they needed to win comfortably. In the end, they couldn’t even summon up the kind of effort they needed to win, period. Atlanta struggled with penalties, with three on special teams leaving them with poor field position and penalties on offense and defense complicating drives. They struggled with sometimes iffy play calling, like overly cute screens and a would-be touchdown pass to Jake Matthews, or blitzes late in the game that left targets open for Tyler Huntley, who was getting passes out at lightning speed. Combined with missed tackles, poor angles, and the Ravens executing their gameplan extremely well all game, the Falcons simply didn’t have enough in the tank to win this one, with the game coming down to Tua Tagovailoa’s arm after Michael Penix Jr. was injured late and ending on a Tua interception. After two straight beatdowns of the Packers and Saints, it was a bracing effort that tells us that well-coached, quality football teams can exploit Atlanta’s extant weaknesses and uncover new ones. There’s a lot to work on this week, and there isn’t a soul in Flowery Branch who is unaware of that. Now it’s time to see how the Falcons respond and recover from this latest gut punch. Here’s a drive-by-drive recap of the game you just watched. 1st Quarter The Falcons chose to defer, and the Ravens went out from the 30. An end-around to Zay Flowers picked up 12 yards after he got nice blocking and the Falcons bit on the other side. Derrick Henry then picked up seven yards up the middle. A quick throw to Justice Hill was bobbled and ultimately dropped. Hill then took a carry up the middle and picked up another big first down. Henry then stumbled through a tackle attempt and picked up another seven yards. Tyler Huntley then got away from pressure and got his receiver for a first down and 11 yards. Mike Hughes then got low on Henry to stop him just shy of a touchdown. Henry then took it out of the wildcat but was decisively stopped by the Falcons run defense for a loss, and an illegal formation penalty would’ve backed the Ravens up had it been accepted. Huntley then tried to hit Mark Andrews and it went through his hands after a bad snap. Tyler Loop was good on the short field goal, though, to make it 3-0 Ravens. Olamide Zaccheaus had a solid return backed up by a holding call on Jammie Robinson, so the Falcons started from about their own 15 yard line. Michael Penix Jr. then tried to fire on downfield to Drake London but it was well behind and knocked down by the defender. Bijan Robinson then picked up four yards up the middle. Penix then felt pressure and threw one backpedaling and hit a Ravens defender in the helmet. Punt. Henry then ran easily for a first down. On the next play, Jared Ivey did a great job fighting through a blocker wrapped around his ankle to sack Tyler Huntley. Then Sydney Brown forced Mark Andrews to fumble on a catch, Jessie Bates scooped it up, and Bates returned it all the way for a touchdown. 7-3 Falcons. Henry took his first handoff for nearly 10 yards. A direct snap to almost Henry got a first down before LaCale London tackled him. Huntley then snuck it for a yard. Huntley tried to throw it to Henry under duress, but Kendal Daniels got his hand up and knocked it away. A toss to Justice Hill looked like it was on its way to a first down, but he slipped for five yards. On third and five, Brandon Dorlus and company arrived and dropped Henry for a small loss. Punt. Bijan Robinson had a jaw-dropping run where he looked dead in the backfield and somehow not only escaped but picked up about 15 yards and a first down. Unreal stuff. A three yard carry for Robinson followed, and then Penix under pressure threw it in the dirt near London. Penix then got away from pressure and scrambled for about five yards after slight hesitation, but didn’t quite get the first. Punt, and a good one from Jake Bailey. Huntley tried to get Flowers, but he dropped it and the ball fell incomplete. After a delay of game in service of trying and failing to get the Falcons to jump offsides, they punted it and Zaccheaus returned it for about eight yards. A snap to Flowers, who was looking to throw, was brought down by Zach Harrison with an assist from Cameron Thomas. A short screen pass fell well short of a first down after Gervon Dexter caught up with the receiver from behind. Loop hit from 51 yards to make it 7-6 Falcons. Zaccheaus got crushed at the 20 on the kick return to set up poor field position again. Penix was waiting for something to open up downfield and took the sack. A screen to Kyle Pitts went for about 15 yards. Penix then uncorked one down the sideline to London, who got 17 yards. Bijan then went inside left and picked up five yards. Brian Robinson Jr. then went nowhere on second down as the defense swarmed him. Jahan Dotson then flew downfield and reeled in a deep ball from Penix that got the Falcons inside the red zone. Bijan then lost a couple of yards on first down. Penix then hit Bijan on a short route over the middle that went for a few yards. Then Penix fired one in to Pitts for a touchdown. 14-6 Falcons. A return to the 37 yard line was brought back by a hold. Huntley then connected on a low ball for a first down. Huntley then connected on a short pass that went for about five yards. A quick pass (again) to Flowers was about a yard shy of the first down. Huntley then snuck it and somehow stayed on his feet for 12 yards. On the next play, Huntley had to get rid of it under pressure, and a holding call backed up Baltimore. On the next play, Huntley got rid of it milliseconds before Cameron Thomas destroyed him. He then connected for nine yards, and got away from pressure to get Bateman for a first down. Huntley got away from a sack and then threw it away. title: Intriguing players to watch in Falcons vs. Ravens
summary: The Atlanta Falcons cap a grueling three-game primetime stretch on Sunday Night Football when they host the Baltimore Ravens in their return to Mercedes-Benz Stadium. It marks Atlanta’s biggest test yet and their first 2026 battle against a winning team. As the Falcons look to prove their recent momentum is sustainable, five key contributors will […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 05: Jake Matthews #70 of the Atlanta Falcons drops back to block during an NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome on October 5, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons cap a grueling three-game primetime stretch on Sunday Night Football when they host the Baltimore Ravens in their return to Mercedes-Benz Stadium. It marks Atlanta’s biggest test yet and their first 2026 battle against a winning team. As the Falcons look to prove their recent momentum is sustainable, five key contributors will face their own tests come Sunday night. Jake Matthews Left tackle Jake Matthews’ test centers on his status for the game and whether he’ll be healthy enough to make his 200th consecutive NFL start against the Ravens while battling a groin injury . Last week’s win marked 200 career starts, but this week would be 200 in a row, as he hasn’t missed a game since Week 2 of 2014. It’s an incredible feat of endurance, durability, and consistency, and it would be a shame if it ended this weekend. Zachariah Branch For rookie wideout Zachariah Branch, the test is whether a heavier workload leads to a breakout. The Falcons have steadily gotten Branch more involved each week, dialing up manufactured screen touches and giving him more chances to stretch defenses with his speed. It seems only a matter of time before Branch evolves from a gadget weapon into a game-changing staple in the Falcons offense. Cameron Thomas With an edge-rusher room that is plagued by injuries , Cameron Thomas faces the toughest test of his breakout season. Thomas has been a pleasant surprise through the first month, but pressure will increase for him to carry the pass rush against the Ravens as others battle injuries. Thomas has feasted in recent weeks against mostly subpar competition, but Sunday night will bring a significant uptick against Ravens left tackle Ronnie Stanley. Testing himself against one of the league’s top pass protectors will help reveal if Thomas’ early-season tear is for real. Billy Bowman and Sydney Brown Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers will test both defensive backs, Billy Bowman and Sydney Brown. According to PFF , Flowers currently leads the NFL with 282 receiving yards when operating out of the slot. Bowman primarily mans the slot when the Falcons play nickel, while Brown handles those responsibilities when the team utilizes big nickel with a third safety instead of a cornerback. So far this year, the Falcons have relied more on big nickel when the opponent threatens to run the ball. No rushing threat looms larger (literally) than Ravens running back Derrick Henry, so expect to see Brown matched up in the slot on early downs against Flowers. However, on obvious passing downs, Bowman will take over responsibilities for covering Flowers. Both players will need to pass the test of covering one of the NFL’s top receivers to keep a lid on Baltimore’s explosive potential. Even without Lamar Jackson , Baltimore has enough firepower and challenges to reveal whether Atlanta’s recent turnaround is a temporary flash or a true foundation for 2026. Can you name other Falcons who will ultimately decide whether the team passes this Sunday night test?
