title: Bengals kicker Evan McPherson continues to rewrite Bengals franchise history
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals’ 2020 NFL Draft class may have more notoriety because of Joe Burrow and Tee Higgins being their first two picks of that class, but their 2021 haul can’t be overlooked, either. Sure, they drafted Ja’Marr Chase at No. 6 overall that year, but it’s a 5th-round selection that is also continuing to […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals ’ 2020 NFL Draft class may have more notoriety because of Joe Burrow and Tee Higgins being their first two picks of that class, but their 2021 haul can’t be overlooked, either. Sure, they drafted Ja’Marr Chase at No. 6 overall that year, but it’s a 5th-round selection that is also continuing to rewrite the team’s record books. Kicker Evan McPherson is quietly cementing himself as the best at his position in team history. After going 14-of-14 as a rookie on field goal attempts in the 2021 postseason (an NFL rookie record), McPherson has continued to up his game for the team. Late in the Week 5 contest against the Dolphins, Cincinnati was deep in Miami territory after Jonathan Allen recovered a fumble from Malik Willis. That Bengals’ offensive drive stalled, but with just two minutes remaining, head coach Zac Taylor sent McPherson out for a field goal to ice the game, but more was at stake. McPherson predictably hit the 26-yard field goal, placing him above former Cincinnati kicker Shayne Graham for most consecutive field goals made by a Bengals kicker. His 22 straight, dating back to last season, pushes him ahead of Graham (also his mentor and fellow Florida Gator) for the most in team history. As noted in the tweet above, McPherson was named AFC Special Teams Player of the Month for September after a perfect three games. He has continued that streak in October, despite the team being 1-1, and has been 5-of-5 on 50-plus-yard field-goal attempts. Oddly enough, the record-breaker was a walk in the park compared to what McPherson was asked in prior games. That was his only attempt against the Dolphins (save for extra points), compared with five 50-plus attempts in the first three contests. After a tough 2024 season that ended prematurely with an injury, McPherson quietly put together a great season last year. He continued that progress with an amazing preseason, and has hit kicks from 50, 57, and 58 yards so far this year, while also being perfect on extra points. Understandably, much of both the national and local attention goes to Burrow, Chase, Higgins, and the (somewhat) previously-maligned defense performances. But McPherson is absolutely “feeling it” right now, and is a key to the Bengals’ march to the postseason. Kudos to McPherson, and another tip of the cap to Graham, who was a good kicker for the Bengals for many years.
author: Anthony Cosenza

title: Jordan Battle backs up talk with two interceptions vs. Malik Willis in Bengals’ win over Dolphins
summary: Jordan Battle had a pretty good idea of what he wanted to accomplish against the Miami Dolphins. By the time halftime rolled around Sunday, the Cincinnati Bengals safety had made his presence felt in a big way. After discussing a potential tell in quarterback Malik Willis’ throwing motion earlier in the week, Battle intercepted the […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals safety Jordan Battle (27) celebrates an interception in the second quarter of the NFL Week 5 game between the Miami Dolphins and the Cincinnati Bengals at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida, on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Jordan Battle had a pretty good idea of what he wanted to accomplish against the Miami Dolphins. By the time halftime rolled around Sunday, the Cincinnati Bengals safety had made his presence felt in a big way. After discussing a potential tell in quarterback Malik Willis’ throwing motion earlier in the week, Battle intercepted the Miami signal-caller twice in the second quarter of Cincinnati’s 31-24 victory. The back-to-back takeaways helped the Bengals establish control of a game they needed to win after consecutive losses. Battle’s performance was particularly timely. Cincinnati’s defense has faced plenty of scrutiny during the early portion of the 2026 season, and Sunday presented an opportunity to turn preparation into production. Battle did exactly that, putting himself in position to make two enormous plays and helping the Bengals head into their bye week with a winning record. "Very meaningful, especially do it at home." – Jordan Battle Jordan said he grew up a couple blocks from the stadium. Here's Jordan Battle postgame with @FOX19Jeremy after 2 interceptions in the Bengals 31-24 win. @FOX19 pic.twitter.com/s9L66brK27 — Cole McIntire (@ColemcintireTV) October 11, 2026 If you’re wondering, Battle’s reference to “home” in the above tweet is because he is a South Beach native. The veteran safety said he grew up just a few blocks away from Hard Rock Stadium. Battle turns his film study into production The storyline began before the teams ever took the field. Battle revealed during the week that he had noticed a subtle habit in Willis’ throwing motion that Cincinnati might be able to exploit. As reported by the Associated Press, Battle explained his observation this way: “He has a slight little tap before every throw,” Battle said, describing what he had noticed while studying Miami’s quarterback. Battle believed the movement could provide a useful clue for the defense when anticipating Willis’ passes. It was an interesting revelation to make publicly, giving Miami an opportunity to account for the observation before kickoff. Whether that particular tell directly influenced either interception is debatable. What isn’t debatable is that Battle and the Bengals made Willis pay for his mistakes. The first interception came when defensive end Boye Mafe got a hand on Willis’ pass, disrupting its flight and allowing Battle to come away with the football. It was a good example of the secondary benefiting from pressure up front, with Mafe creating the opportunity and Battle finishing the play. The second takeaway was an even bigger statement from the Cincinnati safety. On Miami’s next possession, Willis attempted a throw across his body toward the middle of the field. Battle read the play, broke on the pass, and intercepted it, giving Cincinnati another possession and putting the Bengals in excellent position to extend their lead. Two interceptions on consecutive opponent drives is an impressive feat under any circumstances. Doing it in the first half of a road game, against a quarterback whose tendencies had become a talking point throughout the week, made Battle’s performance that much more noteworthy. A difference-maker in a much-needed victory Battle’s second interception helped set up another Cincinnati touchdown, with Joe Burrow connecting with tight end Tanner Hudson to give the Bengals a 21-7 advantage before halftime. The Bengals ultimately held on for a 31-24 win, improving to 3-2 and putting an end to their two-game skid. Burrow threw four touchdown passes, while the defense generated critical turnovers to keep Miami from taking control of the contest. Battle’s two interceptions were the headline-grabbing plays, but his overall contribution went beyond the box score. The safety also recorded pass breakups, and his ability to recognize what was developing in front of him was a significant part of Cincinnati’s defensive effort. After the game, Battle was quick to give credit to the preparation and execution that made the plays possible. “You study players and see things,” Battle said, “but it’s just trusting the game plan and putting me in position to make plays.” That response is worth noting. Battle had identified something during film study, but recognizing a tendency and actually making a play are two different things. The Bengals still needed pressure, sound coverage, and a safety capable of reacting when the opportunity arrived. On Sunday, Battle delivered. The interceptions also gave the Bengals a timely reminder of what their defense can accomplish when its different levels work together. Mafe’s pressure helped create the first takeaway, while Battle’s instincts and anticipation produced the second. Those are precisely the kinds of complementary plays Cincinnati needs to see more consistently as the season progresses. There is still plenty of football left to play, and one strong performance doesn’t erase every concern about the defense. However, Battle’s afternoon against Miami was an encouraging development for a unit looking for momentum. While Battle’s career has been a bit “feast-or-famine”, he showed up Sunday against Miami. And, as Cincinnati’s defensive line goes (four quarterback hits, three sacks), the secondary feasts. The Bengals will now have their Week 6 bye before returning to action against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 7. If Battle can continue turning his preparation into splash plays, while also breeding more consistency, Cincinnati will have another valuable defensive weapon in its effort to climb the AFC standings. For one Sunday in Miami, the safety’s film study paid off big time, and the Bengals walked away with a win they badly needed.

title: Bengals News: Zac Taylor knows his team has plenty to clean up
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals may have beaten the Miami Dolphins on Sunday to improve to 3-2 on the season. However, it was far from the best this team has or could have looked so far this year. Head coach Zac Taylor listed the grocery list of self inflicted wounds from Sunday to reporters as he talked […]
full_text: Oct 11, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor looks on during the first quarter against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cincinnati Bengals may have beaten the Miami Dolphins on Sunday to improve to 3-2 on the season. However, it was far from the best this team has or could have looked so far this year. Head coach Zac Taylor listed the grocery list of self inflicted wounds from Sunday to reporters as he talked about how the team needs to improve: “There’s a lot of frustrating things on our end. We had two personal fouls. We fumbled twice in the red zone. We caught a kickoff on the four-yard line. We had a penalty on a field goal that led to a touchdown. Gave them four points. Give up over 200 yards rushing. So, plenty, plenty to clean up. The bye hits us at a great time. I know these guys are worn out. We’ve had some down to the wire games last three weeks. I know how hot this one was today. So the bye week comes at a great time for us. To be 3-2, these guys will regroup. We know who we are today. There’s a lot of things we have to clean up to be better when we go to Baltimore in two weeks.” This team definitely felt like they needed a bye week in the worst way. The past few weeks have been riddled with these issues, and special teams especially has been atrocious. When you’d be better off if your punt return or field goal blocking unit had just stood around and done nothing, it is a major issue. Yet, that is where the unit is currently at. Who Dey! Bengals News Postgame Quick Hits | Jordan Battle, Ja’Marr Chase Make Marquee Plays In Miami Battle had a genuinely better day tackling than last week where he had two terrible whiffs that led to first downs. His interceptions also may have saved this game from being tight enough that Cincinnati could have lost. We still have to look at the defensive unit as a whole regarding outside runs. Allowing a team like Miami to run for over 200 yards is unacceptable. Coaches and players really need this week to see what needs to change, otherwise forget any type of a deep post season run if they manage to get there. Bad beat in South Beach: Dolphins’ last-minute touchdown sets up painful bad beat It is truly insane sometimes to look back at the lines that Vegas has made for these games and how close they end up being. An extra point off an upright likely shifted millions of dollars around when it barely had an actual impact on the outcome of the game. Bengals stars shine in win over Dolphins Cincinnati needed every bit of Burrow’s magic today with four touchdowns. The 50-50 ball to Ja’Marr Chase will make most highlight reels, but the other three were either perfectly placed or timed balls that show why Burrow is considered on of the best in the NFL. NFL News Commanders QB Jayden Daniels says team’s botched final play vs. Giants ‘on me’ In one of the more peculiar finishes you will ever see to an NFL game, the Washington Commanders seemed to forget either the game would end in a tie at the end of the overtime period or that they didn’t have a timeout. They were inside the New York Giant’s 30-yard line with 57 seconds. After they ran the ball, they huddled up, walked to the line of scrimmage with no sense of urgency, snapped the ball without enough time to be able to get a spike off if needed and Daniels just ran into defenders. Even after he was tackled with under 10 seconds left, no one really moved with any urgency until time was nearly out. Just baffling that no one seemed to know the situation on the offense. NFL Network: Cardinals to trade WR Marvin Harrison Jr. to Texans Well the mystery is over after head coach DeMeco Ryan revealed at his press conference after the team’s first win of the season on Sunday they traded for Harrison. This reunites CJ Stroud with Harrison who both played at Ohio State University through the 21-22 season. A second round pick next year is also a big price to pay. A fairly big gamble considering both player’s struggles as of recent and Stroud being in a contract year. ‘It’s Even More Disrespectful’ — Ex-NFL LB Reacts to Mike Evans Addressing Viral Exchange With Trevon Diggs During 49ers-Seahawks Evans truly pulled off the coldest trash talk moves of All-Time Sunday when he had to turn Diggs around to read the name on the back of his jersey to tell who he was. It is certainly something we will see repeated going forward, but there is truly no rebuttal for that.

title: Zac Taylor says Bengals are dead tired after playing Dolphins in hottest road game in franchise history
summary: It was a blistering hot day as the Cincinnati Bengals beat the Miami Dolphins in a game that kicked off at 9o degrees, making it the hottest road game in Bengals’ history, according to Bengals.com’s Geoff Hobson. The broadcast mentioned it being about 10 degrees hotter on the Bengals’ sideline vs. that of Miami, and […]
full_text: It was a blistering hot day as the Cincinnati Bengals beat the Miami Dolphins in a game that kicked off at 9o degrees, making it the hottest road game in Bengals’ history, according to Bengals.com’s Geoff Hobson. The broadcast mentioned it being about 10 degrees hotter on the Bengals’ sideline vs. that of Miami, and they also mentioned players getting IVs to stay hydrated. It was so hot that the broadcasters even mentioned players changing undershirts midgame. The heat affected everyone, and after the game, head coach Zac Taylor said his team was “dead tired” by the end. “Nothing really at this point in October gets you ready for this heat,” Taylor said. “I mean, somebody told me it started as the hottest game here in October history, which I can attest to. I’ve coached here for four years, and pregame, I was worn out. And so our players fought through that.” Taylor said that he specifically told his team that it was the hottest October game in Hard Rock Stadium’s history, so they knew it wasn’t an issue with their bodies or conditioning. The bye week is early in the season, and with some of the injuries, tight games, and now the extreme heat the Bengals have played in, this may be the perfect time for a week off. An AFC North clash with the Baltimore Ravens is waiting for them in 14 days. Press box official : 90-degree kickoff. full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals were looking to get what should be an easy win in Miami vs. the Dolphins after a two-game slide with losses against the Steelers and Jaguars. One of the worst teams in the league, the Bengals were heavily favored going into the game against the Dolphins, and while they did pull off the win, it was often gifted to them by the Dolphins. What ended up being an easy 31-24 win should have been much bigger if the Bengals hadn’t shot themselves in the foot with unnecessary turnovers and penalties on field goals. The Bengals have the bye week coming up, and they need to use it to focus on cleaning up some of the easy mistakes they keep making, as they easily could be 5-0 right now. With that said, let’s look at the Twitter reactions to the game. full_text: Sep 29, 2022; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (1) catches a pass against Miami Dolphins cornerback Keion Crossen (27) in the second half at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-USA TODAY Sports The Cincinnati Bengals and Miami Dolphins are getting set to hit the field here soon. Both teams are feeling desperate for a win. Cincinnati looking to go back above .500, and Miami to get their first of the season. The Bengals had some big players with the questionable tag, but it seems they are getting a bit of good news going into the game on those guys. Who is inactive for Bengals C Connor Lew S Kyle Dugger OT Myles Hinton WR Colbie Young TE Jack Endries DT Landon Robinson The big news in Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins being active for this game after both exiting Week 4’s game. Both were full participants in practice on Friday and the team didn’t promote any wide receivers from their practice squad, so it definitely seemed like this was going to be what happened. All the same it is still nice to have both of these guys in what feels like a pivotal game early in the season. The team is also getting safety Bryan Cook back, who missed most of Week 3 and was out last week. A huge help for the third level of this defense. The missed tackles at that level have been a huge issue, and Cook is one of the more sure tacklers on the team. Who is inactive for Dolphins RB Kaytron Allen EDGE Robert Beal Jr. WR Caleb Douglas TE Justin Joly CB Reese Taylor OG DJ Campbell OT Chukwuebuka Godrick The biggest questionable was running back Jaylen Wright who is already filling in for De’Von Achane who is out for the season. Ollie Gordon hasn’t been bad when given the opportunity in the context of this offense. The Bengals really need to be able to stop the run after giving up some big runs these past couple of weeks, and Wright being active will certainly be able to test that. Wide receiver Douglas had a big Week 1, but he has not played since Week 2.

Led by a solid relief appearance from Tyler Huntley at quarterback, the Ravens rallied to score a touchdown and two-point conversion with 40 seconds left to send the game to overtime, and then put together a long drive to win it. Right now, it’s not confirmed if Lamar Jackson will be back for the Browns game, but the odds seem to be leaning toward that possibility. title: Rain game halts Browns momentum, reveals flaws: 4 downs to review Week 5’s loss
summary: It was fun while it lasted. The Cleveland Browns winning streak, that is. In a game in which the Meadowlands was dealing with the remnants of Hurricane Isaias, the Browns saw their winning streak come to an end at the hands of the New York Jets. It was a weird game, but it’s the NFL; […]
full_text: It was fun while it lasted. The Cleveland Browns winning streak, that is. In a game in which the Meadowlands was dealing with the remnants of Hurricane Isaias, the Browns saw their winning streak come to an end at the hands of the New York Jets . It was a weird game, but it’s the NFL; you’ll have a weird game every now and again. For Cleveland, those weird games usually happen in the Meadowlands. 1st Down: This wasn’t a trap game Let’s get this out of the way. Many fans believed that this game against the Jets was a trap game and it couldn’t be farther from the truth. New York were favored to win this game. The Browns weren’t. Despite what people will say, the Jets aren’t a bad football team. Are they good? Not necessarily, but they are in the same boat that Cleveland is in. The only difference is that the Jets have looked like a poorly coached team more times than not this season. Leading up to Sunday’s game, safety Grant Delpit said this: Full quote from Grant Delpit on if this weekend is a trap game. "Nah, listen, we're not in any position to be calling games trap games. This is the fifth game of the year. So we still got a lot to figure out. As you can see, it's been pretty sloppy for us. So glad that we've… https://t.co/oCtRNPz2DZ pic.twitter.com/aNIu7Yh3EN — 𝚂𝚙𝚎𝚗𝚌𝚎𝚛 𝙶𝚎𝚛𝚖𝚊𝚗 (@Spencito_) October 9, 2026 As he said, this is a team that is trying to figure things out, and they haven’t played their best football as of yet. In terms of the game, it was an uneven performance from both teams. Offensively, both units were bad, but the defenses did enough to keep their team in the game. The Jets were finding ways to give the game away, but the Browns failed to capitalize on those mistakes. I don’t believe this game was as winnable as many believed, but that’s fandom in a nutshell. You might believe that this was a trap game, but in reality it wasn’t; it was just a weird game with a result that the fans aren’t going to like. 2nd Down: Let’s talk about the running game, offense I am not at DEFCON 1 with this Browns running game. As stated before the season started, the running game will be a work in progress. It’s week 5, and the running game is still a work in progress. The running back isn’t the problem; the same can be said for the offensive line. What’s the issue behind the running game struggles? The lack of consistent push is making it harder for the running game to materialize. The lack of a blocking tight end is also missed. It’s not hard to find a blocking tight end (TE2 for that reason); you can trade for one or just sign one off the street. Cleveland should consider either at this point. Staying on the offense, the entire unit was bad. From an operational standpoint, quarterback Deshaun Watson was abysmal. Watson did make plays with his legs and had a decent throw here and there, but it’s about finding consistency, which has eluded him. Wide receiver Denzel Boston and tight end Harold Fannin were barely involved, and the offensive line had their issues. Overall, not a great day offensively. 3rd Down: Team is still searching for a complete game Five games in, the Cleveland Browns have yet to play a complete game in all 3 phases. Defensively, the unit held up their end of the bargain (despite a few missed tackles), but it was the offense and special teams costing the team at the worst possible time. The mistakes were eventually going to catch up to them; it just happened against a team that is in the same situation that they are in (in terms of expectations for the year). The Browns are searching for that consistency that has been eluding them since the start of the season. 4th Down: Team is ahead of schedule; everything is in front as of now Losing stinks, I know. However, it could be a lot worse. Yes, the quarterback play has been inconsistent, and the running game has been nonexistent. Yet, the team is 3-2. It’s hard to win in the NFL week in and week out, and Cleveland is still trying to figure that out. It’s too early to say that this team is a playoff team, but they aren’t as bad as people say they are. The Browns will still be playing for 1st place in the AFC North next Sunday. Next Sunday’s game against the Baltimore Ravens shouldn’t be considered a must-win in any capacity. Controversial to some, but it shouldn’t be. Progress is being made, but the team has to figure out how to play complementary football on a consistent basis. Extra Points Not completely out on wide receiver Isaiah Bond, but we see why his snaps are limited. He didn’t do himself any favors today with his performance. Outside of his speed, his route running isn’t great, and too often he jumps trying to catch the ball when he doesn’t have to. New York Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick isn’t beating the “dirty player” allegations. Committing two personal fouls on wide receiver KC Concepcion. Whether it was the facemask or the helmet-to-helmet hit that knocked Concepcion out of the game, it is enough evidence to prove it. He might be public enemy #1 in Cleveland after his hit on RB Nick Chubb’s knee a few years ago. Re-shuffling the offensive line will not fix the running game; it just creates more instability and more problems. Didn’t think right tackle Dawand Jones would reach unplayable, but it’s looking that way. The injuries might have something to do with it. 3-2 is better than 0-5. A day later, how are you feeling about the Browns loss in Week 5? Join the conversation! full_text: If it feels strange to have an article about the Cleveland Browns and the NFL playoffs, that feeling is probably a valid one. The Browns validated the early lack of trust in their 3-1 record, with a letdown game in Week 5 versus the New York Jets . There were a lot of reasons to blame for the loss , but for many, it proved that the winning streak was more fool’s gold than fact. On the other hand, Cleveland is 3-2, with a showdown with the AFC North leading Baltimore Ravens in Week 6 , with their rival traveling to the shores of Lake Erie. A win in Week 6 would put the Browns back at the top of the AFC North standings heading into Week 7. For now, the division looks like this: Ravens: 4-1 Browns: 3-2 (Owns tiebreaker due to head-to-head versus Pittsburgh and division record versus Cincinnati) Steelers: 3-2 (Owns head-to-head versus Cincinnati) Bengals: 3-2 The AFC playoff picture is also very muddled, with three AFC North teams just on the outside looking in, pending the results of Monday Night Football between the 3-1 Buffalo Bills and the 2-2 Los Angeles Rams: Kansas City Chiefs: 4-0 Baltimore Ravens: 4-1 Jacksonville Jaguars: 4-1 Buffalo Bills: 3-1 New England Patriots: 3-2 Denver Broncos: 3-2 Las Vegas Raiders: 3-2 Cleveland Browns: 3-2 Pittsburgh Steelers: 3-2 Cincinnati Bengals: 3-2 New York Jets: 2-3 Indianapolis Colts: 2-3 Houston Texans: 1-4 Miami Dolphins: 0-5 Los Angeles Chargers: 0-5 Tennessee Titans: 0-5 A myriad of early-season tiebreakers keep the Browns out of a playoff spot this week. title: Biggest contributors to Browns loss in Week 5 to the Jets
summary: The Cleveland Browns had a chance to improve their record to 4-1 against the New York Jets, but a 17-12 loss dropped them to 3-2. It was an unfortunate loss, as the Jets were one of the more winnable games on their schedule. This loss could come back to haunt them later in the season. Looking at […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns had a chance to improve their record to 4-1 against the New York Jets, but a 17-12 loss dropped them to 3-2. It was an unfortunate loss, as the Jets were one of the more winnable games on their schedule. This loss could come back to haunt them later in the season. Looking at the bigger picture, what aspects of the Browns’ performance contributed most to their loss? Special teams errors were a big factor in this matchup. From mishandled punts to missed extra points, this was a messy game for this group. Field position mattered a lot, and Cleveland giving the Jets good field position certainly contributed to the loss. Offensive inconsistency was the real nail in the coffin in this matchup. It is difficult to win a game when you score only 12 points. Going into this game, it was clear that the Browns wanted to establish the run, but they never really found their footing. Quinshon Judkins , Cleveland’s leading rusher, finished the game with just 44 rushing yards. Given the rainy conditions, there were concerns about the Browns’ ability to catch the ball heading into the game, and they certainly struggled with this at times. Isaiah Bond , in particular, struggled with drops, including a wide-open touchdown pass and another late in the game that bounced off his hands. Small moments like that really add up in a close game. title: Browns injuries: 4 starters join list of concerns, including 2 key new ones after Week 5 Jets loss
summary: A quick recap of the Cleveland Browns Week 5 experience is anything but a positive one. In the rain, the Browns lost to the New York Jets 17-12. WR KC Concepcion was knocked out of the game early due to a hit by Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick. While fans thought it was a dirty play, […]
full_text: A quick recap of the Cleveland Browns Week 5 experience is anything but a positive one. In the rain, the Browns lost to the New York Jets 17-12 . WR KC Concepcion was knocked out of the game early due to a hit by Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick . While fans thought it was a dirty play, Cleveland HC Todd Monken called it a “bang-bang play” after the contest. OT Tytus Howard was hurt, tried to tough it out, then gave OT Dawand Jones a chance to prove he was not an upgrade, which was one of our 20 (mostly negative) takeaways from the contest . A few Brownies (winners) and a lot of Frownies (losers) from the Week 5 contest , which only seemingly got worse after the game due to injuries. Cleveland went into Week 5 having ruled out seven for the game due to injuries: DT Kalia Davis – Quad – Out QB Dillon Gabriel – Back – Out DT Mason Graham – Knee, Ankle – Out DT Mike Hall Jr. – Ankle – Out OL Teven Jenkins – Back – Out TE Carsen Ryan – Calf – Out WR Tylan Wallace – Knee – Out Concepcion and Howard did not finish the game due to injuries; then RB Quinshon Judkins was seen departing the locker room in a walking boot: Shortly after that, LB Carson Schwesinger was seen in a boot: How many right foot/leg walking boots did Cleveland bring with them to New York? Judkins was seen limping late in the 4th quarter, while Schwesinger went into the blue tent during the game, only to return and force a fumble on a blitz. In a bit of positive news, Concepcion posted on social media that he is doing okay: Browns KC Concepcion posted this on his Instagram Stories after being placed in concussion protocol. Todd Monken and Deshaun Watson said he was in good spirits after the game. pic.twitter.com/v5KMT3M5kq — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) October 11, 2026 With the Baltimore Ravens next up on the schedule, the Browns injury list will be vital to follow heading into Week 6. Adding any of Concepcion, Judkins, Schwesinger, or Howard to a list that already includes Graham and Hall could be very problematic for Cleveland’s chances in next week’s AFC North matchup. title: Browns vs. Jets Week 5: Winners and losers on a typical day in Jersey
summary: The Cleveland Browns spent all week talking about how they were not going to look past the New York Jets and be caught in a trap game after winning three in a row. We also spent the week highlighting how strange things happen when the Browns are the road team against the New York Jets.  […]
full_text: (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns spent all week talking about how they were not going to look past the New York Jets and be caught in a trap game after winning three in a row. We also spent the week highlighting how strange things happen when the Browns are the road team against the New York Jets. So would anyone be surprised if we told you it was another typical trip to the swamps of Jersey on Sunday, as the Browns saw their winning streak end in an ugly game?? Here are the winners and losers from the contest. Week 5 Winners – Brownies: The defense after the first drive: It what appears to be standard practice for the Browns, the defense allowed the Jets to go 80 yards in eight plays for a touchdown on their first offensive drive. From there, the Browns were back to their dominant ways as they forced the Jets to punt on their next five possessions and forced a fumble on the sixth. The Jets managed just a field goal and a short-field touchdown after that opening drive, as the Cleveland defense did all it could to keep the team in the game. Quincy Williams gave ‘em hell: In the lead-up to the first game against his old team, linebacker Quincy Williams promised to be a nightmare for the Jets, and he lived up to it. Williams finished with a team-high 11 tackles and forced three fumbles (unfortunately, the Browns only recovered one of them). Pressuring the quarterback: Cleveland was without starting defensive tackles Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr. due to injuries, but you would not have known it as defensive tackles Maliek Collins (1.5 sacks), Sam Kamara (1 sack) and Adin Huntington (half-sack) combined for three of the four sacks the Browns tallied against New York quarterback Geno Smith. Andre Szymt on field goals: Cleveland’s second-year kicker converted both of his field goal attempts, running his streak to 24 consecutive made field goals, dating back to last season. DENZEL BOSTON TOUCHDOWN! 🙌 pic.twitter.com/gNlSJh2SH7 — Browns fan UK (@brownsfanuk) October 11, 2026 Denzel Boston, touchdown maker: Rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston caught his third touchdown pass of the season to tie tight end Harold Fannin Jr. for the team lead. The 29-yarder came in the fourth quarter to give the Browns the lead and broke a streak that saw the Browns punt on five consecutive possessions while gaining just 34 yards of offense. Good Isaiah Bond: With wide KC Concepcion knocked out of the game early in the first quarter with a concussion (more on that in a moment), Bond saw his playing time increase and responded with three receptions for a team-high 74 receiving yards. Week 5 losers – Frownies: Cleveland’s pass protection: The Jets came into the game with nine sacks on the season, so naturally they pressured quarterback Deshaun Watson all day, sacking him eight times. This is the second time Watson has been sacked eight times in a game with Cleveland (the last was in 2024 against the New York Giants), and he has now been sacked five times or more in eight games as a Brown. Bad Isaiah Bond: Those three catches, including a 30-yarder in the fourth quarter when the Browns needed to score, look good on the stat sheet. But Bond also dropped two passes (or was it three?) that would have kept the chains moving, and just missed catching a touchdown pass early in the game. Andre Szmyt on extra points: A year ago, special teams let down the Browns in the loss to the Jets by allowing a pair of return touchdowns. This year it was Szmyt’s turn to misfire as he missed his first extra point of the season after Boston’s touchdown catch in the fourth quarter. That left the Browns with just a two-point lead. Everyone misses occasionally; it just seems like the Browns always miss at the worst possible time. Rex Sunahara on long snaps: The miscues on special teams were not confined to Szmyt’s missed extra point. Four plays into New York’s next possession, Carson Schwesinger strip-sacked New York quarterback Geno Smith and Maliek Collins recovered. Cleveland went three-and-out, though, and Sunahara’s high snap went through the hands of punter Cory Bojorquez and the Jets recovered the ball on Cleveland’s 23-yard line. Three plays later, the Jets scored the game-winning touchdown. Again, these things happen. But why do they always seem to happen to the Browns at the most inopportune time? An ineffective offense: At the end of the third quarter, the Browns had seven first downs and 109 yards of total offense. After an explosive first half in Week 4 against the Pittsburgh Steelers, it was back to bad football before the fourth quarter for the Browns. The fourth-quarter magic was missing: Even after everything that had gone wrong, the Browns entered the fourth quarter trailing just 7-6, setting them up for their fourth consecutive comeback victory. It wasn’t to be, though, as after a New York field goal pushed the lead to four points, Watson hit Bond with a 30-yard reception to move into New York territory. From there, it was a comedy of errors as the Browns finished the possession: Illegal formation Sack Delay of game Incompletion Sack Punt The Browns blew an opportunity after recovering the fumble before turning the ball over on the bad punt snap, but still had two possessions while trailing by five points. The first ended in a three-and-out that gained two yards, and the final one ended with the eighth sack of Watson on the day. First Nick Chubb and now this- Minkah Fitzpatrick is trash pic.twitter.com/RUyYIqlY5V — McNeil (@REFLOG18) October 11, 2026 Minkah Fitzpatrick is the worst: On Cleveland’s second possession of the game, New York safety Minkah Fitzpatrick was called for a facemask penalty after violently ripping off KC Concepcion’s helmet. Then, just four plays later, Fitzpatrick harkened back to his Pittsburgh days and delivered a violent cheap shot to Concepcion’s head that knocked the receiver out of the game. Why the NFL puts up with this is anyone’s guess. OK, so the loss drops the Browns to 3-2, but they could still find themselves in a four-way tie for first place if Baltimore loses tonight to Atlanta. Let’s turn it over to you, Browns fans. Who were your winners and losers from today? Fire away in the comments!

title: Browns KC Concepcion ruled out after Minkah Fitzpatrick head shot; Todd Monken addresses hit after game
summary: The Cleveland Browns start against the New York Jets in Week 5 was problematic in multiple ways. QB Geno Smith had all the time in the world on the Jets first drive, which ended with a WR Garrett Wilson touchdown. On Cleveland’s second drive on offense, OT Tytus Howard limped off injured but returned a […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns start against the New York Jets in Week 5 was problematic in multiple ways. QB Geno Smith had all the time in the world on the Jets first drive, which ended with a WR Garrett Wilson touchdown. On Cleveland’s second drive on offense, OT Tytus Howard limped off injured but returned a few snaps later . Shortly after that, WR KC Concepcion was the intended receiver on a pass from QB Deshaun Watson , when former Pittsburgh Steelers safety Minkah Fitzpatrick hit him in the head. Fitzpatrick has had the ire of Browns fans for years after his helmet-to-knee hit ended RB Nick Chubb’s season a few years ago. Fitzpatrick led with his helmet and shoulder into Concepcion’s head, earning his second personal foul penalty on the drive, after ripping Concepcion’s helmet off previously: KC Concepcion got hit hard and is still down prayers for 1 pic.twitter.com/kRSBMRfcqL — wok (@wokdior) October 11, 2026 Concepcion was able to get up and walk off the field under his own power, but Cleveland ruled him out for Week 5 with a head injury as he was walking into the locker room. Following the game, Browns HC Todd Monken called this a “bang bang play” and said he doesn’t believe Fitzpatrick is a dirty player.

title: Browns vs. Jets Week 5: 20 quick takeaways as the offense fails the defense
summary: A boring game of just bad offense, not good defense, ended with the Cleveland Browns falling to 3-2 in 2026, with the New York Jets pulling off the 17-12 Week 5 victory to move to 2-3 on the year. The rain and two key injuries contributed to the Browns failures on offense. OT Tytus Howard […]
full_text: A boring game of just bad offense, not good defense, ended with the Cleveland Browns falling to 3-2 in 2026, with the New York Jets pulling off the 17-12 Week 5 victory to move to 2-3 on the year . The rain and two key injuries contributed to the Browns failures on offense. OT Tytus Howard was injured, returned, and then was replaced by OT Dawand Jones in the second half. The bigger story was another dirty hit by S Minkah Fitzpatrick , this time to the head of rookie WR KC Concepcion , taking away one of Cleveland’s best weapons. His replacement, WR Isaiah Bond , may have cost the Browns the game with multiple drops against the Jets. A few key takeaways from Cleveland’s Week 5 loss to New York: Ronnie Hickman missed tackles on first drive lead to score Has been a problem for most of the year, including late in the 2nd quarter, but Hickman’s missed tackles directly led to the Jets first score of the game. Could see more Emmanuel McNeil-Warren if the issue continues. None are true free safeties, but missing one-on-one tackles continues to be an issue for Hickman. Coverage giving time for pressure Teamwork is key on defense, with most of Cleveland’s pressure coming due to the secondary and linebackers keeping QB Geno Smith from having open receivers. The Browns still cannot get quick pressure on the outside, but the interior of the line is doing their job, with a little help from the backside of the defense. Run game needs adjustments Something has to give as RB Quinshon Judkins continues to struggle to have holes to run through, finding holes, and getting anywhere with the rushing attack. Cleveland’s line is more suited for under center, zone-based blocking, but this game required more downhill-style attack. The shotgun offense is a different, also concerning, takeaway. Minkah Fitzpatrick’s dirty hit moves him up the CLE hate list After injuring RB Nick Chubb a couple of years ago, a play that probably led to the star back’s early retirement, Fitzpatrick was at it again in Week 5 versus the Browns: KC Concepcion got hit hard and is still down prayers for 1 pic.twitter.com/kRSBMRfcqL — wok (@wokdior) October 11, 2026 Not sure where this lands him on the Cleveland hate list, but it is at least Top 10 and maybe Top 5? Field conditions, adjustments to it big Rain is not an excuse, but something worth noting. The wet turf, versus grass, was very slick and made things more difficult for anyone trying to change direction. The problem is that the Browns run game is movement-based, and the Jets used more power-based schemes in the game. Cleveland offensive players struggled with traction, while Browns defenders were easily pushed around. Shotgun offense has positives, negatives It is clear that QB Deshaun Watson is more comfortable in the shotgun, and has had some success, but the run game is impacted by everything being back so far. Play-action looks very different, fewer outside zone runs, and defenses have a very specific mesh point to attack. The Browns have had the most success when they move the pocket for Watson, something they could do more of under center with play-action boots, waggles, etc. Instead, the shotgun helps Watson, but limits the run and pass game. 2nd-and-long runs are rarely good Not sure why, but analytics-loving Todd Monken loves a good second-and-long run, something analytics believes is a terrible call for a variety of reasons. It is especially bad when the run game isn’t working. Often, Monken has Watson turning to hand the ball off on an up-the-middle run on second and nine, second and 10, with the play gaining three or fewer yards. Monken has to get out of that habit. Michael Burton, Teven Jenkins wasting roster spots Jenkins has not been healthy all year, but instead of putting him on injured reserve, he’s now taken up a roster spot for five straight weeks despite not being able to play, and only a few practices. Burton might be the bigger surprise, but doesn’t fit the shotgun scheme. In four games, prior to Week 4, Burton played one more snap on special teams than on offense (41 to 40). Seems like poor roster management work between GM Andrew Berry and Monken. Todd Monken struggling with time management things While it didn’t lead to anything horrific, Monken’s strategy, or lack thereof, at the end of the first half is concerning. Left two timeouts on the board and then gave the Jets a chance to get points by having 10 seconds left when they had to punt. Thankfully, the punt return took the rest of the time off the clock. Quincy Williams played well against his former team Big forced fumble in the third quarter with Jets inside the 10-yard line was his third forced of the game. Solid tackling overall, and speed all over the field. CBS Broadcast said that the stats only go back to 2000, but that Quincy Williams is the first #Browns player with three forced fumbles in a single game. — Ashley Bastock (@AshleyBastock42) October 11, 2026 Williams had a huge pass breakup on a 4th quarter 3rd and 1 play that led to a punt. Denzel Boston, Harold Fannin were not involved enough early Until the touchdown pass below, Boston and Fannin had just three targets in the game. Then this happened, showing how important getting the ball to their playmakers (especially with Concepcion out): OH MY GOODNESS DENZEL BOSTON! #CLEvsNYJ on CBS pic.twitter.com/sHe2ud1qdR — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 11, 2026 In the end, Boston ended up with seven targets, tying Jerry Jeudy and Bond for the team lead, while Fannin had four. While teams might be looking to take away Boston, especially with Concepcion out, it is up to Monken and Watson to get him the ball as often as possible. More zone likely due to weather concerns Most of the game, Cleveland seemed to play everything safe not wanting to give up big plays on defense or make big mistakes on offense. Given the footing issues, zone coverage is a safer call, despite the Browns defense being much better in man coverage. Offense’s drive falls apart after big Isaiah Bond gain in 4th One of Bond’s good plays, a 30-yard catch and run out of bounds, was followed by: Illegal formation on Dawand Jones, 10-yard penalty Watson sacked for a 10-yard loss Delay of game penalty Incomplete pass Watson sacked for an 8-yard loss From almost in field goal range to punting from their own 27-yard line is an impressive failure while down four points. Deshaun Watson’s legs key multiple games this year Key 20-yard scramble in the 4th quarter was big; a number of times Watson was able to extend plays with his legs instead of taking a loss. Far from perfect, as seen late in the game, but Watson’s scramble ability was key to any success the Browns had on offense. Monken noted after the game that the offense was basically just Watson running around trying to make plays. Special teams makes things difficult late times two A missed extra point made the lead just two, then they gave up a 36-yard return. A high snap and P Corey Bojorquez can’t corral, giving the Jets the ball in scoring position and leading to the game-winning touchdown. Defense keeps being big time LB Carson Schwesinger was in the blue tent and limping just before forcing the fumble that DT Adin Huntington recovered. Hard to be perfect on defense with the way the league’s rules are, but Cleveland’s defense has been darn good overall. Lack of run game leads to terrible possession after turnover Following up on the last two points, the Browns defense gives the offense the ball with a chance to build on their two-point lead with just over four minutes left in the contest. Then Judkins ran out of bounds for no gain. Then two incomplete passes led to the punt that was fumbled. Three plays, nine seconds off the clock. Not good enough. Multiple Isaiah Bond drops Late 4th quarter drop was huge. Had a big play earlier in the game, but a few drops by the youngster were a problem throughout the game when he got a chance after Concepcion’s absence. Dawand Jones is not a Tytus…

title: Cleveland Browns vs. New York Jets recap: Rain plays huge factor in turnovers, as Browns miss opportunity
summary: The rain was falling all game, which meant that offense would be hard to come by for the Cleveland Browns and New York Jets. The Jets took advantage of a hot opening drive, before the Browns’ defense shut them down the rest of the game. Cleveland used a few early field goals to stay in […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 11: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns is tackled by David Bailey #31 of the New York Jets during the first quarter of the game at MetLife Stadium on October 11, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images The rain was falling all game, which meant that offense would be hard to come by for the Cleveland Browns and New York Jets. The Jets took advantage of a hot opening drive, before the Browns’ defense shut them down the rest of the game. Cleveland used a few early field goals to stay in it. Ultimately, it set up another fourth quarter situation where Deshaun Watson needed to lead a go-ahead drive. It was a crazy fourth quarter where the offense took the lead, and the defense forced a turnover. But then the offense ran out no clock, fumbled the snap on the punt in the rain, and the Jets went back ahead with three minutes to go. Ultimately, New York held on for the 17-12 win. Let’s get to the full game recap. 1st Quarter – Browns vs. Jets With the rain falling to start the game, the Browns’ first play was a handoff to RB Quinshon Judkins that went for a loss of 4 yards, pretty much killing the drive immediately with the conditions the way they are. The next two plays were short screen passes by QB Deshaun Watson that only got back to the original line of scrimmage. P Corey Bojorquez came on for a punt that went into the end zone for a touchback. The Jets got a negative play to start things off with a holding penalty that made it 1st-and-18. But WR Garrett Wilson caught a crossing route underneath in zone coverage to pick up 17 yards, and then a short run by RB Braelon Allen moved the chains. On the next play, QB Geno Smith had all day to throw, and found Wilson wide open again across the field for a gain of 21 yards, as New York was showing no issues moving the ball early in the rain. A few plays later, Wilson continued to burn the Browns on crossing routes, as he caught it from the slot wide open, made a man miss, and went in for the 32-yard touchdown to give the Jets a 7-0 lead. spin to the TD 👏 #CLEvsNYJ on CBS, @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/JV1AezXX3r — New York Jets (@nyjets) October 11, 2026 On the Browns’ next drive, they started with a negative play again. Watson lined up in Shotgun, and he dropped the snap, picked up the ball, and then was sacked for a loss of 6 yards. On second down, Judkins ran up the middle, was bottled up, and then bounced to the outside for 14 yards to set up 3rd-and-2. Judkins got the ball again and had enough for a first down. A short crossing route to WR KC Concepcion saw S Minkah Fitzpatrick get flagged for a 15-yard facemask penalty to put the Browns in Jets territory. After two run plays, Cleveland faced 3rd-and-5 at the 34 yard line. Watson found WR Denzel Boston for 9 yards on the outside for another first down, now at the 25 yard line. On the next play, Watson found Concepcion on a nice pass, but Fitzpatrick absolutely drilled him for another personal foul (and the ball came loose), and the young wide receiver looked completely knocked out. Now facing 1st-and-10 at the 12 yard line, Watson kept it on a quarterback sweep for 4 yards to the 8 yard line. On second down, an inside screen to Judkins set up 3rd-and-5 at the 7 yard line. The Jets brought a big blitz on third down, and Watson tried getting it to Boston over the middle, but the defensive back was glued to him and helped break up the pass. K Andre Szmyt came on for a 25-yard field goal and connected to make it a 7-3 game with 3:27 left in the opening quarter. Cleveland’s defense responded much better on the second drive, forcing a three-and-out. That included on third down, when they showed a clear double team on Wilson, and then Smith was confused and sacked for a loss of 10 yards by the duo of DT Maliek Collins and DT Adin Huntington . On the punt, with Concepcion ruled out, Boston fielded it and returned it 13 yards to the Browns’ 35 yard line. Maliek leading the way for the big loss 💪 #CLEvsNYJ on CBS pic.twitter.com/EVIMm8gYl5 — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 11, 2026 Cleveland couldn’t move the ball on their third drive, as RB Jaleel McLaughlin dropped a promising first down pass, and then Harold Fannin slipped on third down to lead to a punt. Bojorquez got a nice punt downed at the 9 yard line, but to end the quarter, Cleveland had some sloppy tackling on Allen, who picked up 8 and 17 yards on back-to-back runs out to the 34 yard line. 2nd Quarter – Browns vs. Jets The Jets lost their momentum to begin the second quarter. They had a false start, then Collins immediately beat his man for a sack, and DE Isaiah McGuire read a screen pass to force an incomplete pass. that's ✌️ on the day for Maliek! #CLEvsNYJ on CBS pic.twitter.com/1L5Sm65wuD — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 11, 2026 Two plays later, the Jets punted to Boston, who called for a fair catch (even though it was hard for me to see that), and the Jets tackled him for a fair catch interference penalty. That gave the Browns the ball at their own 46 yard line to start their next drive. After a first down completion to WR Jerry Jeudy , Watson was sacked for a loss of 6 yards. He got some of it back on a run, setting up 3rd-and-11. Watson then avoided a free rusher, escaped, and found WR Isaiah Bond wide open for a 20-yard gain to the Jets 24 yard line. BIG first down to Isaiah! #CLEvsNYJ on CBS pic.twitter.com/1ssHLvRrPp — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 11, 2026 On second down, Watson stepped up in the pocket and found Bond open in the end zone, but the pass was just out in front of him for a diving incomplete pass. On third down, Watson couldn’t connect with Fannin, leading to Szmyt coming out again. From 41 yards out, he connected to make it a 7-6 game with 10:14 left in the half. The defense got to Smith again to start the next drive. This time it was a coverage sack, and eventually DT Sam Kamara got to him for a loss of 9 yards. On second down, a swing pass got it back to 3rd-and-10, and Smith was dragged down by Collins again as he just got off the incomplete pass in time. The punt unit came out again, and a short 33 yard punt gave the Browns the ball at their own 37 yard line. Sam's first NFL sack in the books! #CLEvsNYJ on CBS pic.twitter.com/7A2UpvoacI — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 11, 2026 Cleveland faced a quick 3rd-and-7, with Watson needing to put the ball through the air again. The Browns sent the rubbing back wide out, and the Jets just brought an edge blitz again, which forced Watson off his spot before any receivers could even turn around, leading to a sack and another punt. Bojorquez now got off a short punt of 37 yards, downed at the Jets’ 31 yard line with 6:13 left in the half. we see you DB 👀 #CLEvsNYJ on CBS, @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/CxeI9bFufY — New York Jets (@nyjets) October 11, 2026 DE Sam Williams stuffed Allen for a loss of 2 yards on the ground to start the next drive. Allen found more success on second down, getting to the edge for 11 yards to set up 3rd-and-1. Smith kept it for a quarterback sneak to get a first down. After an 8-yard run by the Jets, LB Quincy Williams forced a fumble on second down that the Jets recovered. A false start pushed it to 3rd-and-7, and Smith got a crossing route to TE Mason Taylor for 9 yards and a first down. Heading into the two-minute warning, the Browns were flagged for 12 men, but then the Jets were flagged for a hold, making it 1st-and-15. A jet sweep picked on 3 yards, and then on second down, Smith threw the ball in the dirt as pressure came up the middle. On 3rd-and-12, Smith had to wait, then found Wilson late, but S Grant Delpit had time to dart in and punch it out for an incomplete pass. The Jets punted from midfield, and Boston made a fair catch at the 11 yard line with 1:22 and three timeouts. Cleveland tried a screen pass on first down, but a holding penalty pushed the Browns back to a 1st-and-15 at the 6…

title: Cowboys’ coaching staff isn’t providing answers to team’s problems
summary: At some point, a bad loss stops being an isolated incident and starts becoming a reflection of the people responsible for preventing it, going all the way up to the front office. Yet, since the Cowboys are structured and operated the way they are that’s a story for another day. For now, the focus should […]
full_text: RIO DE JANEIRO, BRAZIL - SEPTEMBER 27: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer of the Dallas Cowboys watches play during the first quarter of the game against the Baltimore Ravens at Maracana Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. (Photo by Wagner Meier/Getty Images) | Getty Images At some point, a bad loss stops being an isolated incident and starts becoming a reflection of the people responsible for preventing it, going all the way up to the front office. Yet, since the Cowboys are structured and operated the way they are that’s a story for another day. For now, the focus should be on the field with the people who are making decisions in real-time. Thursday night’s 24-16 defeat to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers was another reminder that the problems plaguing this team extend far beyond one player, one position group or one unfortunate bounce of the football. Dallas lost at home to an 0-4 team starting an undrafted rookie quarterback in his second NFL start. Tampa Bay left AT&T Stadium with its first win of the season after outgaining Dallas in yardage, controlling possession for more than 39 minutes and winning the turnover battle 3-0. The Cowboys once again struggled to stop the run, failed to sustain their offense, surrendered a costly special-teams turnover and watched their final realistic opportunity disappear when Jake Ferguson couldn’t secure a pass that became the game-sealing interception. Individual mistakes played a role, but they cannot explain away the broader failure. Dallas looked unprepared to handle Tampa’s pressure, unable to stop its rushing attack and incapable of consistently executing in any phase of the game. When those problems appear simultaneously, the scrutiny has to extend beyond the players making mistakes and toward the coaches responsible for preparing them. Brian Schottenheimer, Christian Parker, Klayton Adams and Nick Sorensen all have different responsibilities, but Thursday exposed shortcomings across their respective units. Five games into the season, the Cowboys have given fans little reason to believe this staff can turn a talented roster into a consistently competitive team. Brian Schottenheimer keeps coming up short Again… I recognize Schotty has to speak. A lot. Part of the job. This is just so tone deaf at best imo. On some level I admire the tunnel vision required to do the job. But these are empty words and sound like corporate buzz speak when you are coaching like he is right now. https://t.co/mTnow5xPzd — RJ Ochoa (@rjochoa) October 9, 2026 Schottenheimer’s responsibility extends beyond calling plays. As head coach, he sets the team’s standards, oversees its preparation and ultimately answers for the product Dallas puts on the field. As offensive play-caller, he also has a direct hand in an offense that struggles at inopportune times. Dallas opened Thursday’s game with a promising touchdown drive, but managed only three additional points before its final touchdown with 5:26 remaining in the fourth quarter. Tampa’s pressure disrupted Dak Prescott, and the Cowboys never found a consistent counter until the game was nearly out of reach. When Dallas can establish its preferred rhythm, the offense has enough talent to score against anyone. When an opponent disrupts that rhythm, however, the Cowboys too often look as though they are waiting for the original plan to start working again rather than finding a different way to attack. Every play-caller has bad games, but the better ones recognize when an opponent has taken away the first option and respond before an entire half slips away. Schottenheimer’s offense failed to do that against Tampa, and Dallas finished with three turnovers while leaving too much of the burden on Prescott to manufacture a comeback. The struggles were not limited to the play calls themselves. TE Jake Ferguson’s blocking has been inconsistent, and his three-catch, 19-yard performance against Tampa ended with a drop that became an interception when Dallas was trying to mount a late comeback. Not every tipped interception is the receiver’s fault, but Ferguson needed to secure a catchable pass in that situation. Combined with his ongoing difficulties as a blocker, the play highlighted another weakness the offense has not adequately addressed. Ferguson has shown he can contribute as a receiver, but a tight end who struggles to finish blocks and cannot consistently deliver in critical moments puts his offense in difficult situations. The coaching staff must find a way to improve his execution or reconsider how heavily it relies on him. Continuing to use the same personnel in the same ways without addressing the results is not a meaningful adjustment. Schottenheimer cannot catch passes or prevent every turnover, but he can put his players in better positions to succeed. His offense needs a more adaptable approach, and his team needs greater discipline in the situations that decide close games. Until those improvements become visible, it is fair to question whether he is the right person to lead this operation. Christian Parker’s defense has no identity If Schottenheimer’s offense failed to adjust, Christian Parker’s defense failed to stop the most obvious threat in front of it. Tampa Bay ran for 241 yards, with Bucky Irving accounting for 165 on 21 carries. Irving broke off a 72-yard run to open the second half, setting up a touchdown on the next play, and later added a one-yard scoring run. The Buccaneers finished with 419 total yards while controlling the game through their ground attack. Meanwhile, quarterback Jalon Daniels completed 19 of 25 passes for 189 yards and a touchdown. He played efficiently without needing to take over the game, largely because Tampa could rely on its running game to move the chains and keep Dallas’ offense on the sideline. That is an increasingly troubling reflection on Parker’s defense. Dallas entered the season expecting a new identity under a new coordinator, but the unit has struggled to stop the run, generate consistent pressure and create turnovers. Through five games, the Cowboys have yet to record an interception, although Daron Bland just tried his best to secure one. In fairness, maybe Parker deserves some time to establish his system, and injuries have complicated his personnel decisions. Joey Porter Jr., acquired to strengthen the secondary, was unavailable Thursday because of an illness. Those circumstances deserve consideration, but they do not explain away the fundamental breakdowns against Tampa. Quinnen Williams has missed 9 tackles thus far this season, per PFF, 4 more than the next closest interior defensive linemen Donovan Ezeiruaku is tied for the 2nd-most missed tackles among EDGEs at 5 and Malachi Lawrence is tied for the 4th-most at 4. Dee Winters is tied for… — John Owning (@JohnOwning) October 9, 2026 A defense should still be able to maintain gap discipline, tackle effectively and prevent an opponent from repeatedly exploiting the same weakness. The Buccaneers did all the things Dallas needed to prevent, and the Cowboys had no effective answer. The performance also raised legitimate questions about the team’s preparation and effort, particularly on defense. Effort cannot be measured simply by looking at the final score, and a poor performance does not automatically mean players were unmotivated. But repeated failures to finish tackles, control the line of scrimmage and respond when Tampa seized momentum are difficult to overlook. These are fundamental responsibilities that should not disappear because an opponent has a favorable matchup or the game is being played on a short week. Parker’s challenge is not simply to install a scheme; it is to establish a dependable standard of execution. The issue is not that he has failed to rebuild the defense in five games, but that his unit has yet to demonstrate a reliable foundation on which that rebuild can succeed. Nick Sorensen’s special teams are another problem Special teams should…

title: Empty promises and defensive meltdowns plague Cowboys
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have descended into a deeply unsettling territory where their ongoing performances have become a recurring nightmare. For three straight weeks, we have gone into a game with this level of excitement only to realize that this team isn’t very good. They get us every time. How can we be such suckers! The […]
full_text: Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have descended into a deeply unsettling territory where their ongoing performances have become a recurring nightmare. For three straight weeks, we have gone into a game with this level of excitement only to realize that this team isn’t very good. They get us every time. How can we be such suckers! The reason we fall for it is because they do have talent. Yes, more of that talent is on the offensive side of the ball, but there is no excuse for this team to be playing as poorly as they are. No excuse. The loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers was especially frustrating because the offense, supposedly the dependable side of this team, never found a comfortable rhythm. To be fair, the Bucs have a good defense, but there was still an expectation that Dallas would move the ball and create enough offense to control the game. Instead, the Tampa defense brought pressure, put Dak Prescott in tough spots, and forced the Cowboys into uncomfortable situations. Prescott had escaped a few dangerous throws in previous games when deflections fell harmlessly away, but this time, his luck ran out. The bigger concern was that Brian Schottenheimer and the offense didn’t have an effective counterpunch. CeeDee Lamb was completely neutralized. Tyler Smith returned but could not spark the running game, and even the later success involving George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy didn’t come easily, as both of them had to make incredible catches in traffic. Sadly, this team cannot survive if they experience any type of lingering offensive drought. That is because of the real problem with this football team. The major problem. The Cowboys’ defense. There is no nice way to articulate it. This unit is outright terrible right now. The tackling has become sloppy and the coverage breakdowns have become straight-up embarrassing. Even when this team is hustling around looking as if they’re going to make a huge play, their grabby hands will come up empty and shifts into a big play for the opposing offense. And this is happening all the time. It’s hard to explain why this is happening. It’s about as puzzling as why DaRon Bland can’t stay upright and is always tripping over the ground, allowing a receiver to graze in wide-open spaces. And that is what the secondary does. Receivers are left unattended, assignments are missed, and communication disappears at the worst possible time. The most aggravating part is that they are showing no sign of improving. After the big play to Zay Flowers late in the game against the Baltimore Ravens that only took six seconds and cost them the game, you would expect such a thing to sting to the point where they would be like, never again! Instead, two games later, the Cowboys’ defense surrendered a completely inexcusable 3rd-and-21 conversion when they ever-so-desperately needed a stop. And Tampa made it look easy. That makes it even more annoying. Opponents arrive with a plan, and the Cowboys spend the afternoon reacting to it. That seems like a pretty good indicator that a team is being outcoached. We know things are bad, but where do the Cowboys go from here? That is difficult to answer because the offense still has enough talent to make noise. Prescott, Lamb, Pickens, a capable offensive line, and a functional rushing attack should form one of the league’s better groups. And they are on most days. Expecting the offense to produce at a high level isn’t unreasonable. It is the minimum requirement if the Cowboys want to remain relevant. The problem is that there is almost no margin for error because of what is happening on the other side of the ball. Dallas cannot casually take a few possessions off while the offense searches for answers, because the defense is not equipped to keep the game within reach. Every possession carries extra weight, and every stalled drive feels like the beginning of the end. The defense must find a way to be better. Asking for a takeaway almost seems absurd. A takeaway? How about they just get a stop? Make tackles. Stay disciplined. Communicate assignments. Get the correct calls in. Get off the field on third down. If they could somehow just do some of the basic things, it would feel transformational. The schedule will not wait, either. Tougher opponents and better quarterbacks are coming, and even modest progress may not be enough by then. There are reasons for some hope. Joey Porter Jr. should help. Quinnen Williams is still a great player. And rookie defenders such as Caleb Downs, Jaishawn Barham, and Malachi Lawrence offer potential. The supply cabinet is not empty. They have some tools. That’s what makes the current performance hard to excuse. Christian Parker and his staff must turn this talent into a defense that understands its responsibilities and executes them. The question is whether meaningful change can happen quickly enough. A late-season rise to mediocrity seems like the ceiling for this group, but it will likely be too little, too late. And while Parker’s failures have been on full display, Schottenheimer’s leadership deserves scrutiny as well. We’re not talking about the trivial stuff. No one should be overly bothered by the failed two-point attempt or trotting Brandon Aubrey out there for a long field goal only for it to get blocked. Criticize the execution, not the decision. The real concern with Schottenheimer is that he appears to believe this team is better than it has shown. His calm demeanor can keep him composed in a difficult post-game interview, but it also screams complacency when the same problems continue to happen. That was one of the most frustrating traits of the Mike McCarthy era. The belief that Dallas was basically fine and only needed minor adjustments. It was often good enough to win regular-season games, but never good enough to accomplish anything significant. Schottenheimer preaches accountability, yet the Cowboys keep repeating unaccountable football. At some point, there needs to be a sense of urgency. Nobody is asking him to throw furniture, but a little visible frustration would at least suggest the alarm is sounding inside the facility. Right now, the Cowboys look too comfortable with problems that should make everyone uncomfortable. And that’s not a good sign. That leaves the Cowboys in an awkward place. It is hard to imagine this team making serious noise this season, but there should be urgency in identifying how they can improve and who the people are that are going to help them achieve that noise one day. Which young players can become dependable contributors? Who needs to be replaced? The Cowboys brought in plenty of new faces, and the remaining schedule should provide a clear evaluation period. The positive is that there is enough talent to build around, but they are pressed for time. The Dak Prescott window is entering its final stages, so patience is not a luxury the organization can afford. The Cowboys have also borrowed more from future cap resources than they typically do. Fans want the front office to go all out. Well, they got it, but aggressive moves carry consequences when the wins do not follow. That makes this season particularly disappointing. The division remains up for grabs, and nobody has taken firm control of the NFC, yet the Cowboys cannot take advantage. The road only gets tougher from here. For fans, all we can do is search for progress, guard our optimism, and prepare for more turbulent waters.
author: Dan Rogers

title: Cowboys news: Dallas still firmly in division race thanks to other NFC East teams
summary: Things got a little better on Sunday morning for the Cowboys as the Eagles fell to the Jaguars thanks to late-game heroics from Jacksonville. Then, the Giants and Commanders game ended in a tie due to poor clock management from Washington. While a Commanders win would be preferable, it was a good Sunday for the […]
full_text: Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images | DeFodi Images via Getty Images Things got a little better on Sunday morning for the Cowboys as the Eagles fell to the Jaguars thanks to late-game heroics from Jacksonville. Then, the Giants and Commanders game ended in a tie due to poor clock management from Washington. While a Commanders win would be preferable, it was a good Sunday for the Cowboys, all things considered. To win the division, though, Dallas will have to start stringing together back-to-back wins. Back-to-back wins have been rare in the Schottenheimer era. All in all, we can enjoy a Sunday without the disappointment of Cowboys football. Updated NFC East Standings: Wild NFL Sunday Benefits Cowboys After Week 5- Randy Gurzi, Sports Illustrated Although Thursday night was an upsetting game for Cowboys fans, there is a silver lining after Sunday’s action. The rest of the NFC East is doing the Cowboys favors by giving them an opportunity to climb back into the division. 2. Philadelphia Eagles (2-3) Right now, the Philadelphia Eagles have the tiebreaker over the Cowboys because they are 1-0 in the NFC East, compared to 1-1 for Dallas. They should be 3-2, however, after taking a lead against the Jacksonville Jaguars with eight seconds to play. NFC East Is For Losers: Cowboys Joined By Incompetence Across Division – Adam Schultz, Yahoo Sports The division is still wide open thanks to help from other teams. However, to take advantage of the lack of success from other teams, they will need to string together wins. A task they have only done once in the Schottenheimer era. Add it up, and incredibly, all four NFC East teams played this weekend … and they combined for zero wins! The division remains there for the taking, but … Why can’t the Cowboys win back-to-back games? That is one question we are all asking in the aftermath of the 24-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday night. Cowboys’ possession battle woes, ruinous defensive penalties among maddening Week 5 stats- Todd Brock, Cowboys Wire It has been well documented that the Cowboys are the only team without a defensive interception this season. And in the moment they could have changed that and flipped the outcome of the Thursday Night Football game, they failed. 0: Interceptions by defense… on the year DaRon Bland’s blatant drop in the fourth quarter likely would have given the Cowboys a go-ahead touchdown with under four minutes to play and might have sealed a Week 5 win, but it also would have snapped a rather ugly streak of futility. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . 5 Coaches Who Could Take the Cowboys to the Next Level- Cody Warren, Inside The Star During a long week, it may be a good time to think about what if. Granted, Schottenheimer absolutely has time to turn the ship around, but if it doesn’t happen Jerry and the organization needs to think about what’s next. 1. Kirby Smart Has Earned the Top Spot Smart’s two National Championships at the University of Georgia put him first on my list, but what happened between those two titles is interesting. Georgia lost eight defenders to the 2022 NFL Draft, including five first round picks. The next team won another championship while allowing 16.0 points per game . Christian Parker turning Matt Eberflus into a sympathetic figure is rock bottom- Jerry Trotta, The Landry Hat No fan expected the Cowboys to go from worst to first defensively simply by hiring Christian Parker and getting an exciting new rookie safety. However, possibly regressing after a horrific 2025 defensive campaign seemed equally unlikely. Former Cowboys wide receiver Jesse Holley echoed a similar sentiment , tweeting that “Parker is actually doing much less with much more, making his job performance worse than Matt Eberflus.” Being a prisoner of the moment is natural after an embarrassing primetime loss. This isn’t that. There’s real credence to the idea that Parker has been worse than Eberflus.
author: Aidan Davis

title: The Cowboys have to earn trust back at this point
summary: I’ve said it before, too. Heck, I’ll probably say it again soon. “The Dallas Cowboys are a talented team.” To be clear I believe this to be true. I think they have one of the better quarterbacks in the NFL. They have arguably the best pass-catching duo in the league. Quinnen Williams is amazing. All […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - OCTOBER 04: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer of the Dallas Cowboys on the field during warmups ahead of the NFL football game between the Houston Texans and Dallas Cowboys on October 4, 2026, at Reliant Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images I’ve said it before, too. Heck, I’ll probably say it again soon. “The Dallas Cowboys are a talented team.” To be clear I believe this to be true. I think they have one of the better quarterbacks in the NFL. They have arguably the best pass-catching duo in the league. Quinnen Williams is amazing. All of these things are true… on paper. We have let paper guide us for a while now. I don’t mean to throw the paper away, to be clear. But we just watched the paper-based Dallas Cowboys drop a game at home, as 9.5-point favorites, against a UDFA quarterback making his first road start on a short week. It is impossible that they lost. It is worse when you remember that they weren’t really close for most of the game. It is time to throw the paper out. At least for a while. When you drop the easiest of possible gimmes, you forfeit the right to have that benefit of the doubt applied to you. The Cowboys are “fortuante” to play in an NFC East this year that seems gettable, and maybe they will turn the tide after this mini bye and go on a little run. I know you laughed. It is possible, though. And if it happens then we will all feel differently. So many people forget that opinions are allowed to change as information does, and right now the information is that this Cowboys team takes every moment where they have our trust and burns it up in flames. No more until they give something back themselves. It is on them now. Earn it back.
