title: Discussion: How much better do you feel about the Lions after their blowout win over Cardinals?
summary: After the first quarter of the Detroit Lions’ Week 5 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, we were staring into the abyss. Detroit was outgained 84 yards to -9 after the first 15 minutes, and it looked like we were headed for some major changes. I won’t lie. I even considered if this was the beginning […]
full_text: Oct 11, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta (87) makes a catch defended by Arizona Cardinals linebacker Mack Wilson Sr. (1) during the fourth quarter at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Kartozian-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After the first quarter of the Detroit Lions’ Week 5 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, we were staring into the abyss. Detroit was outgained 84 yards to -9 after the first 15 minutes, and it looked like we were headed for some major changes. I won’t lie. I even considered if this was the beginning of the end for the entire regime. But the rest of the game told a completely different story. The Lions offense scored on their next seven possessions, including six touchdowns. The Lions defense forced five consecutive three-and-outs and seven scoreless drives in a row. It was a complete and utter beatdown for the remaining 45 minutes, and it’s the best the Lions have looked all year by a country mile. But how much does it mean? How many of Detroit’s problems seem solved vs. how much was this just beating up on a bad Cardinals team? Today’s Question of the Day is: How are you feeling about the Lions after their blowout win over the Cardinals? My answer: I would say a little to a lot better. It’s impossible to know whether Detroit’s defensive success will carry over to future games. I find it hard to believe that they are suddenly going to be a top-half-of-the-league defense all of a sudden. Certainly, they won’t find as much success against teams with deeper wide receiver rooms and better quarterbacks. They’ll have a much bigger test out of the bye with a Green Bay Packers team that isn’t afraid to air it out deep. However, I’m not going to discount the possibility the Lions may have figured some things out. The entire defense looked far more comfortable in more man-heavy coverage looks. The back-end settled down considerably with rookie Keith Abney manning one of the safety spots. And say what you will about how bad the Cardinals are, there isn’t a single team so far that has held them to five straight three-and-outs. Hell, the undefeated 49ers defense only held them to two three-and-outs all game. In terms of Detroit’s run defense, they held the Cardinals to their lowest success rate (22.2%), second-lowest EPA/run (-0.24), and highest stuffed rate (27.8%) of the season—even after playing the Seahawks and 49ers defense. Arizona hadn’t been sacked more than twice in a game, and the Lions got to Jacoby Brissett five times. Point being, even as bad as the Cardinals are, Detroit beat them more handily than just about anyone this year, and that counts for something. I haven’t even touched on the offense, which managed to brush off a dreadful start to put together their most complete game of the year, as well. Not only did offensive coordinator Drew Petzing find some solutions in the passing game, but Detroit penetrated what had been a pretty successful run defense from the Cardinals all year. The Lions’ +0.10 EPA/rush, six rushes of 10+ yards, and +1.38 rushing yards over expected per attempt were all season highs allowed by Arizona this season. So, yes, the Lions played a crappy Cardinals team. But they played them better—or at least as well—as some of the best teams in the NFL. Going into the bye week, I couldn’t have really asked for more from one single game. So I’ll say I’m feeling a lot better. What about you?
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Several Detroit Lions honor play-by-play announcer Dan Miller following wife’s death
summary: While the Detroit Lions’ big win over the Arizona Cardinals was cause for celebration, the team did it without one of their key components of the last two decades. Lions radio play-by-play announcer Dan Miller missed the game following the death of his wife, Cindy, this weekend. Miller is beloved by just about everyone around him […]
full_text: The WJR-AM broadcast team of Dan Miller (left) and Lomas Brown on Sunday, September 20, 2020 call the action of the Detroit Lions game against the Green Bay Packers. The broadcast was done at Ford Field though the team was playing at Lambeau Field. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co While the Detroit Lions’ big win over the Arizona Cardinals was cause for celebration, the team did it without one of their key components of the last two decades. Lions radio play-by-play announcer Dan Miller missed the game following the death of his wife, Cindy, this weekend. Miller is beloved by just about everyone around him for his incredible work ethic, extreme kindness, and sharp wit. After the Lions’ 45-21 win over the Cardinals, several people within the Lions organization honored Miller and sent love his way. Of course, it started with Lions coach Dan Campbell, who fought back tears in his opening post-game statement as he dedicated a game ball to Miller. “This ball goes to Dan Miller and his family,” Campbell said. “It was hard to hear what they went through. It’s been a tough road for Dan. This is for him. Salt of the earth, Dan is salt of the earth, and I know this has been hard. But now I know Cindy’s at peace, and we love you, Dan. So appreciate you.” 💙 @DanMillerFox2 pic.twitter.com/3w964rRzGI — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 11, 2026 Even quarterback Jared Goff found himself nearly speechless when asked about Miller in a post-game interview on the field. “Yeah, we’re thinking about Dan. Yeah, sorry,” Goff said, before having to pause for a couple of seconds to regain his composure. “Yeah, we’re thinking about you, Dan. Love you, man.” “He’s just an important piece of the culture here. He really is,” Goff continued. “His voice is Lions football, and he means a lot to us. He’s a part of our family, and I talk to him weekly. I know he’s in our hearts right now and all of our prayers.” An emotional @JaredGoff16 sends his thoughts to @Lions radio play by play announcer Dan Miller 💙 pic.twitter.com/QvzwSexHJx — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) October 12, 2026 Also noteworthy is the reaction of Miller’s daughter Rikki, who posted on Twitter just how much the Campbell family has meant to them while they navigated Cindy’s battle with cancer. 💕 MCDC and Holly have been incredible throughout my mom’s entire cancer journey, from literally day one. So grateful for them https://t.co/JFRjP4QBDT — Rikki (@rikkimiller) October 11, 2026 And former Lions tackle Taylor Decker shared his love for Miller, as well. ❤️❤️❤️ Dan Miller and his family. https://t.co/7jnFfAOwLJ — Taylor Decker (@__taylordecker) October 12, 2026

title: 6 takeaways from Detroit Lions’ 45-21 win against Arizona Cardinals
summary: The Detroit Lions had a long build-up to their Week 5 game against the Arizona Cardinals. Outside noise about the poor defense was loud. It was a major talking point when discussing the Lions as a team, but the offense also deserved some criticism. Both had a sluggish start, but once the second quarter started, […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 11: Jameson Williams #1 of the Detroit Lions catches a second quarter touchdown against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions had a long build-up to their Week 5 game against the Arizona Cardinals. Outside noise about the poor defense was loud. It was a major talking point when discussing the Lions as a team, but the offense also deserved some criticism. Both had a sluggish start, but once the second quarter started, they came out and turned the game around, winning 45-21. Here are my six takeaways from the Lions’ Week 5 win against the Cardinals. DJ Wonnum proving his worth While the Lions defensive line had a strong day against Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett overall, EDGE DJ Wonnum had the best game. Wonnum finished the game with two tackles, both sacks. He’s been what the Lions have needed on the defensive line: a player opposite EDGE Aidan Hutchinson who can cause havoc and win one-on-ones. Wonnum with the third-down SACK pic.twitter.com/buiBiRTf7z — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 11, 2026 Sure, he isn’t a superstar, but he’s playing well and has been a big boost for this Lions pass rush. Hutchinson on the edge and defensive tackle Alim McNeill were once the focus of opposing offenses, but with Wonnum now on the other end, teams have to start respecting him enough and not devote all their resources toward Hutchinson and McNeill. We’ve seen McNeill get 3.5 sacks in five games this season, and Hutchinson has four of his own. Who’s the leader of the group? Wonnum is now the leader with 5.0. Detroit has a pass rush now, and if the secondary can get figured out, uh-oh. Gotta give the secondary its props When the opening drive happened, I thought it would be a long day for the Lions’ secondary. The Cardinals moved down the field with ease, and once again, the tight end position was off to a good start with a touchdown. Afterward, it was five straight three-and-outs, and secondary coverage was part of the reason. On the sixth drive, defensive back rookie Keith Abney II picked off a pass to end the half. Yes, the tight ends still had a strong game for Arizona, gathering 14 catches for 138 yards and three touchdowns. The secondary didn’t play perfectly, but they made plays and forced incompletions when it mattered most. It was a step in the right direction, which is what this unit needed. You got to give them props for not folding after that first drive. After a month of struggles, allowing quarterbacks to have good games against them and offenses to move the ball with ease, the secondary showed up. Changes will be coming with Brian Branch returning soon—and potentially safety Kerby Joseph—so help is on the way. This is a sign things are going in the right direction, and with a bye week to keep tweaking and make it even better, this defense still has time to turn it around. Cade Mays, please come save the day Detroit’s offensive line has been average to start the year, but Sunday was its worst look yet. The offense had a forgettable first quarter, but the line allowed three sacks. It’s frustrating to see the Lions’ offensive line struggle, but change is coming. Lions starting center Cade Mays is returning soon, with his practice window opening earlier in the week leading up to the game. The line cleaned up its act and didn’t allow Goff to be sacked again for the final three quarters, but it still isn’t comfortable to see that happen so quickly. Detroit has a bye week next week, and Lions head coach Dan Campbell thinks he could debut against the Packers . With Mays returning soon, I think we’ll see this offensive line take a positive step forward. Offense must figure out quick starts Most of the criticism Detroit has gotten so far this season has been on defense, which is understandable, but that doesn’t mean the offense is perfect. Detroit’s offense continues to start out slow, another three-and-out to start the game, and for the entire first quarter, the Lions had a total of -9 yards on plays with three straight three-and-outs. If Detroit was playing a tougher opponent, this game could’ve been 21-0 real quick. Remember Week 2? That wasn’t even a month ago, and this offense is still coming out slow and lethargic. The offensive line had a horrible start, having quarterback Jared Goff on his back often, and running back Jahmyr Gibbs had no lanes to run in. Detroit’s offense can’t come out flat and put pressure on the defense out of the gate because Week 2 could be a weekly occurrence, and this team can’t live like that every week. Gibbs makes history Gibbs had a slow start on Sunday but finished strong, getting 25 carries for 151 yards and two touchdowns, plus five catches for 56 yards. Gibbs’ first touchdown made history, putting him on the same level as Hall-of-Fame Lions legend Barry Sanders and tying him for the most touchdowns scored in NFL history by a player under 25. . @Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs has tied @BarrySanders (57) for the most TDs scored in @NFL history by a player under 25 years old. #OnePride pic.twitter.com/Ge67JNkKOv — Detroit Lions PR (@LionsPR) October 11, 2026 Gibbs would break that record later in the game, and he has a chance to put himself firmly ahead of the pack, as he doesn’t turn 25 until March 2027. Gibbs has had a strong start to his career and remains a big part of this offense. He’s one of the best running backs in the league, and if he is already breaking records set by Sanders, I can only imagine what other records he can break. Jameson Williams have a day The 2026 season has been a slow start for Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams. After a strong training camp where he made insane catches, drops have slowed him down early on. He was held to under 50 yards in the first three games before getting over 100 against the Carolina Panthers in Week 4. In Week 5 against the Cardinals, Williams finally found the end zone twice. GOT EM pic.twitter.com/N7YI1INqQF — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 11, 2026 Sunday marked Williams’ first-ever multi-touchdown game, and he now has 12+ touchdowns of 35+ yards or more, according to the Detroit Lions. Williams didn’t break 50 yards, but it doesn’t matter when he finds the end zone. This offense has needed more deep shots, and Williams has dropped a few this season. Teams can try to take Williams out of games, but eventually he’ll get his.
author: Brandon Knapp

title: 10 winners, 4 losers from Detroit Lions’ win over the Arizona Cardinals
summary: How about some stress-free football to calm some nerves? The first quarter may have instilled some panic for Detroit Lions fans, but the second quarter onwards was a dominant performance from the road team. The Arizona Cardinals, inversely, started hot but wound up getting smothered by a previously-permeable Lions defense. The Lions now head into […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 11: Sam LaPorta #87 of the Detroit Lions celebrates reacts against the Arizona Cardinals during the second quarter at State Farm Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images)2 | Getty Images How about some stress-free football to calm some nerves? The first quarter may have instilled some panic for Detroit Lions fans, but the second quarter onwards was a dominant performance from the road team. The Arizona Cardinals, inversely, started hot but wound up getting smothered by a previously-permeable Lions defense. The Lions now head into their bye week sitting at 3-2. There is optimism that Detroit has the pieces to be a playoff threat, but there is still a long way to go. For one, the offense needs to continue to churn out impressive performances like these. Additionally, the defense needs to prove that this outing was not a one-off. If they can get some reinforcements over the bye week and clean up some sloppiness on both sides of the ball, the Lions could go into their tilt with the Green Bay Packers on a high note. Which players walked away from Sunday’s beatdown as winners or losers? Note: The label of “loser” is used to evaluate and contrast in-game performance and is not an indictment of a player’s ability, value, or character. The term is not intended to be disrespectful in nature. Winner: Drew Petzing, OC It was revenge week for Petzing against his former team. Things started off slowly (three straight three-and-outs) and after a scoreless first quarter, there was a modest sense of panic. However, Petzing was able to lock in his offense and put together some dominant drives. In the second quarter alone, the offense scored 24 points! The final drive of the half featured this bit of trickery: Dialing up a little razzle-dazzle pic.twitter.com/BMMCTMIu5z — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 11, 2026 The Lions offense is far more talented than the Cardinals defense, so the expectation was that the Lions would deliver a beatdown, but that is never guaranteed in the NFL. The personnel on offense looked very similar in 2025, yet poor play calling led to it faltering too often. With Petzing at the helm, the offense is dominating its opponents with both talent and playcalling. Winner: Sam LaPorta, TE I think it’s time to pay the man. While his contract status is still up in the air, his impact on the field is anything but. Early on when the offense was disjointed and sputtering, it was key grabs by LaPorta that kept the Lions offense moving. His first came on a fourth-and-3 at a pivotal point of the game, with the offense having gone three-and-out on the prior three drives. That drive ended with a touchdown—Detroit had life. On the ensuing drive, LaPorta made a man miss on a short catch on third-and-12, rumbling his way to an 11-yard gain (although upon review, it certainly looked like he made the first—the league did not agree). LaPorta put that questionable spot in the rearview mirror by turning the fourth-down attempt into an easy 38-yard touchdown grab. Everything went Detroit’s way from that point onward, en route to 45 points scored on offense. LaPorta finished the day as the Lions’ leading receiver with 88 yards on five catches. Reliability is at the forefront of LaPorta’s game. When things look grim, Jared Goff and Drew Petzing can turn to LaPorta for a spark. Winner: Keith Abney, S The Lions have been in a dire situation at safety to start the season, but they might have some solutions. For one, Brian Branch could return before long, perhaps on pace for a post-bye game against the Green Bay Packers. However, Lions also saw some success with rookie Keith Abney playing deep safety. With injuries to Avonte Maddox and Thomas Harper, the Lions had previously leaned on Chuck Clark for that role. While Clark has intangibles for the position, he was simply lacking the athleticism—the Lions need their deep safety to be a roaming missile, and Clark is not that. This week, it was Abney getting a look at safety, and he was largely impressive. Abney impressed in both run defense and pass coverage, recording six tackles while only allowing 25 yards on his targeted routes. He also secured the first interception of his career on a pre-half Hail Mary, a play in which he looked like a true centerfielder and snagged the floating pass. However, perhaps the best part of his game was the lack of obvious mistakes. The rookie rarely looked out of place. He did not make many misreads. He was communicating and coordinating well with the other defensive backs, avoiding the crucial big plays that had plagued the defense. Barring Kerby Joseph returning to the lineup, I think the Lions have to roll with Abney at safety until he proves otherwise. This is important because… Loser: Chuck Clark, S I credited Clark’s intangibles in the prior section, but they were seriously lacking against Arizona. Whereas Abney was sound with his assignments, a majority of the Cardinals’ big plays came at the expense of Clark. On one play, Clark erroneously broke downhill on a catch like Elijah Higgins, leading to a massive 38-yard gain. He was clearly frustrated afterwards, jumping up and down as though there was a miscommunication. Perhaps there was, but given how the other defensive backs played it, I would wager that Clark misread the situation. Later on in the third quarter, Clark again took a shallow read and allowed an easy touchdown catch for Teagan Quitoriano. With Branch set to return before long and Abney playing well at free safety, I do not see a reason to start Clark going forward. Winner: Jared Goff, QB It feels like we are not appreciating how great Goff has been to start the season. Through five games, he has over 1,400 passing yards, 12 passing touchdowns, and zero interceptions. The stats alone don’t tell a full picture, however. The Lions offense has had some ups and downs to start the season, but rarely has Goff been at fault for the miscues. Ill-timed turnovers had hurt him in the past, but so far in 2026, he has been perfect at avoiding them (aside from that bizarre non-fumble against the New Orleans Saints). I think “steady” is the best descriptor for Goff. He will not wow people with his legs (though he did sneak for a touchdown today). He will not fire howitzers downfield (though he can still throw some deep shots). However, he is reliable and facilitates success for the players around him. Players like Sam LaPorta or Amon-Ra St. Brown are talented players in their own right, but Goff also brings out the best in them. The same can be said with Drew Petzing as offensive coordinator—Goff is a coordinator’s best friend because you can build a scheme around him and he can and will execute it. Goff might not be a hot MVP candidate unless he puts up gaudy numbers, but there is no questioning his value to this offense. Loser: Juice Scruggs, C For as good as the offense was post-first quarter, Scruggs was lagging behind for most of the afternoon. Scruggs was neither impressive in pass protection nor in run blocking. Early on in the game, Scruggs was beat soundly by Roy Lopez for a sack. The Cardinals also recorded a sack by Budda Baker on a blitz up the middle, and while Scruggs was not solely responsible, he did little to impede the blitzers. Despite Jahmyr Gibbs’ impressive day on the ground, that success rarely came running behind Scruggs. Lopez in particular gave the offensive line some fits. With Cade Mays on pace to return after the bye, it seems like Scruggs will be relegated to a reserve role. Even though this was a down performance, he nonetheless filled in admirably to start the season. Winner: Jameson Williams, WR Williams quietly needed a game like this. He had been touchdown-less prior to this week, and while he had a 100-yard performance against the Carolina Panthers last week, he had been lacking consistency—it was very boom or bust for Williams. Drops had been an issue for Williams,…
author: John Whiticar

title: Lions, Cardinals recap: Detroit dominates in all 3 phases in blowout win, 45-21
summary: For the first quarter of the game, it looked like the Detroit Lions’ woes were here to stay. The Arizona Cardinals outgained the Lions 84 yards to -9, and it seemed Detroit was going to head into their bye week thinking about massive changes. But the rest of the game was a complete reversal. The […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 11: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions celebrates after a rushing touchdown against the Arizona Cardinals during the third quarter at State Farm Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the first quarter of the game, it looked like the Detroit Lions’ woes were here to stay. The Arizona Cardinals outgained the Lions 84 yards to -9, and it seemed Detroit was going to head into their bye week thinking about massive changes. But the rest of the game was a complete reversal. The Lions defense forced five straight three-and-outs. The offense shook off three straight three-and-outs to start the game, and scored on seven straight drives, including six touchdowns. The rout was on as the Lions were finally firing on all cylinders: offense, defense, and special teams. It ended in a decisive 45-21 victory for Detroit. The win moves the Lions to 3-2, tied with both the Packers and Bears for second place in the NFC North—all behind the undefeated Vikings. Here’s how the entire game unfolded. First quarter The Lions won the coin toss and opted to take the ball—a shift in their normal strategy. But it didn’t help provide a spark as Detroit quickly went three-and-out following two short runs and a sack on third down by Cardinals safety Budda Baker. Budda was alll over that 😤 #DETvsAZ | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/LEKgt21DHg — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 11, 2026 The Lions defense took over and ran into some familiar problems. Mainly, their third-and-long woes. On third-and-11, Jacoby Brissett hit Kendrick Bourne for a 22-yard gain, beating Roger McCreary in man-to-man coverage. That moved Arizona into field goal range. Then on third-and-6, the Cardinals converted again on a pass to Michael Wilson for 8. They faced yet another third-and-long, but Detroit got a stop… to force a fourth-and-1. Arizona opted to go for it, and a trick play—reverse pass—made for an easy conversion. Michael Wilson completes the pass to Jacoby Brissett. Yes, you read that right. @DETvsAZ on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/efimoLBGVO — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 One play later, the Cardinals cashed in on a 1-yard touchdown catch to Teagan Quitoriano. 7-0 Cardinals. That's @teaganquito14 in the endzone for 6️⃣ #DETvsAZ | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/G2vk11fRCU — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 11, 2026 Detroit answered with another three-and-out. Goff was sacked on first down, and he failed to connect with Isaac TeSlaa on third-and-long. But Detroit’s defense finally responded with a three-and-out of their own. Brissett tried to target McBride downfield, but he was covered well by Jack Campbell, helping force an incomplete pass. Tom Kennedy tried to provide a spark with a 22-yard punt return into Cardinals territory. It didn’t work. The Lions went incomplete pass, sack/fumble, screen pass for 2 yards. Second quarter Detroit’s defense got another three-and-out, thanks to a pressure from Alim McNeill on second down and sticky coverage from D.J. Reed on third down. Tom Kennedy got another decent punt return (11 yards), but his lower body bent awkwardly when tackled, injuring the special teamer. Kennedy was eventually carted off and listed as questionable to return with a knee injury. The Lions, again, failed to convert a third down, still looking for their first conversion of the game. But on fourth-and-3, at midfield, the Lions went for it, and Sam LaPorta made an impressive contested catch—and got another 15 yards tacked on due to a roughness penalty. Jahmyr Gibbs followed it up with a 16-yard run to move the Lions inside the 5-yard line. Two plays later, Gibbs was in for the touchdown. 7-7 tie. Jah punches it in at the goal line 💪 pic.twitter.com/3kKBTNLfHE — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 11, 2026 Detroit answered with another strong defensive series. McCreary batted down a third-down pass to get off the field, and Amon-Ra St. Brown, filling in for Kennedy, took the punt return 30 yards into Cardinals territory. Luckily for Detroit, they recovered a late fumble by St. Brown on the play. On the subsequent drive, LaPorta came up with a big play on third-and-12, juking a defender and diving forward to pick up what appeared to be a first down. Officials ruled him short, and that ruling stood upon a Lions challenge. That set up a fourth-and-1 from the Cardinals’ 37-yard line. Detroit ran a play-action, and Goff found a wide-open LaPorta for a 37-yard touchdown and a 14-7 Lions lead. There goes Sam pic.twitter.com/jWOW1mJVFT — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 11, 2026 The Cardinals went three-and-out for their fourth straight possession after another pass breakup from McCreary, and a deep shot on third down that fell incomplete when the receiver fell down. Detroit immediately threatened again, thanks to a screen pass to Gibbs for 23 yards. Then Gibbs had an excellent rep in pass protection, allowing Goff to find Brock Wright for 11 yards. Then the Lions running back picked up 18 yards on the ground to get into the red zone. But on third-and-4 from inside the 10-yard line, Goff missed an open Isaac TeSlaa for the touchdown. Detroit made the controversial decision to go for it, but Goff and Jameson Williams proved Dan Campbell right with an 8-yard touchdown. 21-7 Lions. Jamo's turn on fourth down 🙌 pic.twitter.com/yRaVNpXB4z — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 11, 2026 Detroit forced a fifth straight three-and-out thanks to a coverage (!!) sack on a third-and-short. Brissett couldn’t find anyone open, and DJ Wonnum brought him down for the first sack of the game. Wonnum with the third-down SACK pic.twitter.com/buiBiRTf7z — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 11, 2026 The Lions offense avoided a return three-and-out with a well-timed screen pass to St. Brown for 11 yards, pushing the game into the two-minute warning. Out of the break, the Lions pulled off a reverse flea-flicker screen for 18 yards. Dialing up a little razzle-dazzle pic.twitter.com/BMMCTMIu5z — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 11, 2026 But Detroit’s drive stalled in field goal range when they failed to convert a third-and-6 with a conservative draw play. Jake Bates lined up for a 46-yard field goal and nailed it to move the game to 24-7 Lions with 53 seconds remaining. With no timeouts, the Cardinals looked to cut into the lead and possibly double-up at each side of halftime. They converted a third-and-10 with a 22-yard strike up the seam to Bourne. But Wonnum’s second sack of the game essentially ended their bid. Rookie Keith Abney picked off a hail mary attempt to close out an impressive second quarter from the entire Lions team. Ok, @keithabneyjr !! pic.twitter.com/ktRZTqpkRH — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 11, 2026 Third quarter Arizona started the second half with an explosive play. A missed assignment in the secondary left a wide-open Elijah Higgens for a 38-yard gain. 38 yards for 8⃣4⃣ moves the chains ⛓️ #DETvsAZ | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/1RfcajfkGy — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 11, 2026 But the defense stiffened up from there. D.J. Reed made a nice tackle for loss in the run game, and Alim McNeill followed it up with a sack. DREAM LOCO pic.twitter.com/aA6ijVnS6W — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 11, 2026 That set up a third-and-21, and the Cardinals just checked down to improve field goal range. But Chad Ryland pushed the 53-yard field goal wide right. The Lions were putting together a promising drive until St. Brown absorbed a big hit and fumbled the ball—turning a 6-yard gain into a 6-yard loss when Tate Ratledge fell on the ball. But the Lions dug out of the hole with a 39-yard bomb to Jameson Williams for his second touchdown of the day. 31-7 Lions. GOT EM pic.twitter.com/N7YI1INqQF — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 11, 2026 The Cardinals needed to score, and they needed to score quickly to get back in the game. They methodically worked their way down the field with a steady and productive passing…

title: Detroit Lions vs. Arizona Cardinals live chat, discussion

Through two games, the Lions sit at an uninspiring 2-2 record. All the talk has been around Detroit’s defense, which ranks in the bottom five in just […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 22: Quarterback Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions throws a pass during the NFL game at State Farm Stadium on September 22, 2024 in Glendale, Arizona. The Lions defeated the Cardinals 20-13. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tee Detroit Lions are a day away from the bye week, but how they’ll feel during their break is going to heavily depend on how Sunday afternoon goes. Through two games, the Lions sit at an uninspiring 2-2 record. All the talk has been around Detroit’s defense, which ranks in the bottom five in just about every statistical category. Without a doubt, the Lions won’t be able to win a Super Bowl with the defense playing like that. But is there still time to right the ship? This is a good week for defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard to take the heat off of himself. The Cardinals offense has not been explosive all year, and one of their top weapons—former first-round pick WR Marvin Harrison Jr.—is inactive, because Arizona is expected to trade him. They’re also missing two starters on the offensive line. Lions opponents have been beat up before, and Detroit has failed to stop them. This week feels like a potential last straw. That said, Lions coach Dan Campbell has put some high expectations on the offense this week. They’ve been good, but Campbell expects greatness. Again, this feels like a good week to get right, as the Cardinals pass defense has been arguably worse than Detroit’s. Win and control the play on both sides of the ball, and the vibes in Detroit could be much better during the bye week. Lose, and the outside noise for some b ig changes will only grow louder. title: Packers By The Numbers: Stats from the Week 5 win over the Bears
summary: As we do every week in this space, we’re looking at some stats from the Green Bay Packers’ most recent game, courtesy of SumerSports. Today we’re looking at the 31-7 victory over the Chicago Bears in Week 5. Offense Last week we saw a drastic decrease in the Packers usage of 11 personnel (1 RB, […]
full_text: Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) passes the ball against the Chicago Bears on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. The Packers won the game, 31-7. Tork Mason/Green Bay Press-Gazette | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co As we do every week in this space, we’re looking at some stats from the Green Bay Packers’ most recent game, courtesy of SumerSports . Today we’re looking at the 31-7 victory over the Chicago Bears in Week 5. Offense Last week we saw a drastic decrease in the Packers usage of 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR), and a big uptick in their usage of 13 personnel (1 RB, 3 TE, 1 WR). Their usage of 11 jumped a bit from last week, but this feels more like the area they want to live in if given the opportunity. Here was the Packers personnel usage this week: The running game was still churning out negative numbers no matter which personnel grouping they were in, but their passing game was positive EPA in every grouping they trotted out. It’s worth noting that most running offenses post a negative EPA per Play. The Packers posted a rush EPA per Play of -0.09 in both 11 & 12 personnel, which would put them 20th in the league. They posted a 50% Success Rate when running out of 12 personnel, which is a very good rate. In terms of Success Rate, their 12 and 13 personnel packages were doing work in the passing game. They posted a 70% success rate in 12 and 50% in 13. I don’t need to tell you all, but Jordan Love was chucking the ball. He averaged 2.54 seconds to throw. He was still operating off a quick release (his average time to throw in 2025 was 2.89 seconds), but 2.54 seconds is something that can resemble a functional offense. (For reference on that time to throw, Aaron Rodgers had the fastest time to throw in 2025 and he averaged 2.59 seconds to throw. So it could be better, but, based on how the first few weeks went, I’ll take 2.54 seconds.) OH MY GOSH 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/qyqGYPEsIB — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 11, 2026 Loved turned in an absolutely absurd game when throwing deep. Look at those numbers, man. They’re beautiful. He was also very good against the blitz. When blitzed, Love was 8/10 for 130 yards (+0.6 EPA per Play). When not blitzed, he was 17/21 for 237 yards (+0.43 EPA per Play). He was absolutely shredding this week, man. Their run/pass ratio on the game looked a lot like last season. For the game, they were passing 55.9% of the time, but that’s in part due to taking the air out of the ball in the 4th quarter. They came out relatively conservative (52.6% pass rate in the 1st quarter), cranked up the rate in the 2nd quarter (77.8%), kept their foot on the gas in the 3rd quarter (75%), then throttled down the pass rate in the 4th quarter (26.7%). Even then, they didn’t truly let off the gas until midway through the 4th. They opened the 4th with a 66.7% pass rate and didn’t go run-heavy until there was 8:26 left in the game, holding a 31-7 lead (it’s worth noting that they broke a 23 yard run after winding down the game). That’s how I’d like to see them operate. Set some stuff up in the 1st, attack in the middle quarters, then finish the game off. Zero complaints with the run/pass mix this week. Let’s talk receivers because, buddy, they were putting on a show. Christian Watson caught 6 of his 8 targets for 143 yards and 2 TDS (+1.29 EPA per Reception). Matthew Golden caught 6 of his 7 targets for 123 yards (+1.08 EPA per Reception). We also saw Tucker Kraft show up, catching all 5 of his targets for 64 yards (+0.62 EPA per Reception), with 38 yards after the catch. Defense You know who else showed up? My guy Dani Dennis-Sutton. 😤 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/4X3w0n5gFg — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 11, 2026 He posted a 25% pressure rate, with a 50% pressure rate on stunts (34.8% above the NFL average). When he’s been on the field he has looked like a monster. In terms of personnel, the Packers primarily lived in Nickel in this game (85.3% Nickel, 13.2% Base, 1.5% Dime). That makes sense given the Bears approach in this game. Here is their personnel breakdown: The Packers dialed down their blitz rate significantly in this game, choosing instead to drop back into coverage. After being pretty blitz-heavy through the first 4 weeks, the Packers only blitzed on 14.9% of dropbacks this week, 15.2% below NFL average. Despite that, they generated pressure on 40.4% of dropbacks, +0.58% above NFL average. That pressure rate was more due to forcing the QB to hold the ball than anything else. Their quick pressure rate of 17% was 2.9% below NFL average. For the QBs, Tyson Bagent averaged 2.67 seconds to throw while Case Keenum averaged 2.92 seconds to throw. Albums listened to: The Rocky Valentines – Happy Halloween EP ; The Tallest Man on Earth – Just Beyond Endless Mountain ; Bon Iver – Bon Iver, Bon Iver

title: Green Bay Packers News: Unlike Bears, Packers won first and talked second
summary: The Chicago Bears talked a big game heading into their Week 5 matchup with the Green Bay Packers. That didn’t exactly work out well for them when the two teams actually played their game on Sunday afternoon. The Packers dropped bomb after bomb on the Bears’ defense as Jordan Love connected with Christian Watson, Matthew […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 11: Zaire Franklin #44 of the Green Bay Packers celebrates after a play during the third quarter of the NFL football game against the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field on October 11, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears talked a big game heading into their Week 5 matchup with the Green Bay Packers. That didn’t exactly work out well for them when the two teams actually played their game on Sunday afternoon. The Packers dropped bomb after bomb on the Bears’ defense as Jordan Love connected with Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, and Tucker Kraft in an impressive aerial display. When the dust cleared, the Packers emerged with a 31-7 win, pulling even with the Bears on record at 3-2 and earning an important early-season head-to-head win. After the game, a few Packers players made it clear that they didn’t appreciate the comments that they heard the Bears making during the offseason and during this week. And so they went out and did something about it — they worked on themselves during the week and attacked their opponent’s greatest weakness, the secondary. Love finished the day with the most passing yards by any Packers quarterback against the Bears in a Lambeau Field game, 369, and both Watson and Golden had more than 120 receiving yards. The defense cleaned up with five turnovers. And all in all, the team avoided the self-inflicted mistakes that have cost them wins this year. The two teams will meet again on Christmas Day. But for now, the Packers can be the ones to talk for a while — if they want to. Rapid reaction: Packers’ offense getting there, but still ‘a ways to go’ | Packers.com The deep ball returned with a vengeance for the Packers, but there’s still plenty of meat on the bone for the offense to find, particularly in the run game. Packers’ focus was on themselves, not Bears rivalry or trash talk | Packersnews.com ($) The Bears were all talk and not much action, and the Packers instead let their play do the talking. Packers maul Bears, then fire back at Burden for ‘quit’ talk | ESPN Well, the Packers at least waited until after the game to talk. After the game, the veteran linebacker had plenty of words for the outspoken young Bears receiver. Were These the Real Packers? 3 Reasons To Be Truly Excited After Rout of Bears | SI.com Perhaps one of the best reasons to be excited was that the Packers didn’t beat themselves — they committed just four penalties for 25 yards, a season-low in both categories, and they won the turnover battle 5 to 0. These are the funniest wildlife photos of the year — and you better believe there’s a ‘sexy mantis’ | The Independent Unfortunately, this year’s nominees do not have a single photo of a bear doing something embarrassing. But that’s okay because Ben Johnson’s squad did enough of that on Sunday. Ba-zing! Go Pack Go—wherever you go! title: Packers vs. Cowboys odds: Opening lines for Week 6 matchup
summary: The Green Bay Packers just dismantled their oldest rivals, the Chicago Bears, 31-7 on Sunday afternoon. The Dallas Cowboys just lost to an 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at home on Thursday Night Football, falling to 2-3 in the process. Somehow, however, the Cowboys are actually the favorites for their game at Lambeau Field on Sunday […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 28: Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers signals against the Dallas Cowboys during the first quarter in the game at AT&T Stadium on September 28, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers just dismantled their oldest rivals, the Chicago Bears, 31-7 on Sunday afternoon. The Dallas Cowboys just lost to an 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at home on Thursday Night Football, falling to 2-3 in the process. Somehow, however, the Cowboys are actually the favorites for their game at Lambeau Field on Sunday Night Football in Week 6 as the sportsbooks opened on Sunday afternoon. Why is that? Your guess is as good as ours. But the fact remains that the Cowboys are 1.5-point favorites in next week’s matchup, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The Packers went into Week 5 as 1.5-point underdogs to the Bears as well, and won against the spread for the first time all season in their blowout, upset victory. They’ll look to do it again next week unless the line moves over the next seven days. To find the last time that the Packers were underdogs in back-to-back home games, you would need to go way back to 2023. That year, the team found themselves as 2.5-point underdogs against the Lions in Week 4 and 1.5-point dogs when facing the Vikings in Week 7. The Packers lost both of those games outright, bookending a four-game losing streak that included road losses at the Raiders and Broncos in between. For next Sunday’s game, however, the books expect a fairly high-scoring affair. The points total for the game is currently set at 52.5, which is tied for the highest total in any Week 6 game and well higher than any other game in the Packers’ 2026 season so far. UPDATE: As of about 10 AM on Monday morning, the line has flipped; FanDuel now lists the Packers as 1.5-point favorites, though the moneyline is almost even (Cowboys -106, Packers -110). title: Packers Winners and Losers: Week 5 vs. the Bears
summary: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson said he wanted blowouts, and a blowout is exactly what he got as the Green Bay Packers hosted their division rivals and won in commanding fashion, 31-7. After a ton of well-warranted criticism that the Packers couldn’t hold onto leads, they took complete control of the game on Sunday, […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 11: Head coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears embraces head coach Matt LaFleur of the Green Bay Packers after the Packers defeated the Bears 31-7 at Lambeau Field on October 11, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson said he wanted blowouts , and a blowout is exactly what he got as the Green Bay Packers hosted their division rivals and won in commanding fashion, 31-7. After a ton of well-warranted criticism that the Packers couldn’t hold onto leads, they took complete control of the game on Sunday, and never took their foot off the gas. Let’s take a look at the best and worst as the Packers come out of Week 5 with a 3-2 record. Loser: Trey Smack We’re starting with our big loser today, and honestly, I don’t even care. The rookie kicker battled against the elements in an extremely windy stadium on Sunday, and missed 2 FGs and an XP as a result. It’s obviously not ideal, and the team will want Smack to improve moving forward. In a 24-point win, however, it almost felt like good practice. Smack’s lone successful FG was 35 yards, and he made 2 XPs. Winner: Matthew Golden The WR’s breakout year continued in convincing fashion on Sunday. On more than one occasion, the deep threat found himself wide open, and the Packers took advantage of it. When the team needed a first down, Golden was there. When they attempted a 2-pt conversion to make up for Smack’s missed XP, he was there again. His hands were super solid this week, a welcomed sight after some ugly drops to start the year. Golden finished the day catching 6 of 7 targets for 123 yards, and returned 2 punts for 27 yards with a long of 17. Keep targeting Matthew Golden. Packers offense is absolutely on fire pic.twitter.com/akyjTOQqyK — Billy M (@BillyM_91) October 11, 2026 😮‍💨 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/VoI7mIvg7i — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 11, 2026 Winner: Christian Watson Look, I knew a WR duo of Matthew Golden and Christian Watson had the potential to feed families…but I was still unprepared. After years of trying to reassemble the receiving corps in the wake of the Davante Adams trade, it feels like we finally did it. It was a fun 4 years with Romeo Doubs. Dontayvion Wicks never reached his full potential with the Packers. But these two…I feel like the heavens are shining down upon me. Like Golden, Watson was left wide open multiple times on Sunday. Jordan Love found him again and again, for some big gains, and big scores. When Christian Watson is this open, there’s no stopping him. Say it with us now… LET'S GO!!! 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/zLLSOq0xW5 — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 11, 2026 Even when he wasn’t wide open, there was no stopping him. His second touchdown catch of the day was one of the best catches I’ve seen from a Packer, and he brought it in like it was nothing. Same Micah, same. CHRISTIAN WATSON WHAT A CATCH @CHIvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/z0TbC7WaQe — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 Watson finished the game leading all receivers with 6 catches on 8 targets for 143 yards and 2 TDs. In 7 career games against Chicago, Watson has 22 catches for 456 yards, 46 rushing yards (you are reading that correctly) and 6 total TDs. We’ve got ourselves a new Bear Killer. Winner: MarShawn Lloyd After a frustrating few weeks for the Packers RB, he finally turned things around, and it couldn’t have come at a better time. Lloyd’s vision and decision making seemed a lot better on Sunday, and as a result, he scored the first two rushing TDs of his NFL career. He also sent CB Jaylon Johnson straight into a brick wall, which was fun. Lloyd finished the day with 10 rushes for 31 yards, 1 catch for 6 yards, and 2 rushing TDs. MarSHAWN LLOYD LAMBEAU LEAP 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/TVSKwKFBVW — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 11, 2026 Winner: Xavier McKinney After an unsuccessful first drive for the Bears offense, they stepped onto the field for drive #2, ready to respond. They certainly did respond, by throwing the ball into triple coverage, and gifting S Xavier McKinney his first pick of the game. McHIMMY 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/7erp637G1R — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 11, 2026 It didn’t end there for X. In the second half, as the Bears were trying to kickstart a comeback, they were denied when McKinney came down with his second pick of the day. This one was impressive. Xavier McKinney intercepts it for the second time! @CHIvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/64InTW9DdB — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 Winner: Keisean Nixon CB1 has been having a pretty outstanding season so far, and Sunday’s game was no exception. He was on his receivers like glue, and forced multiple incompletions which prevented touchdowns and forced punts. Had any of these catches been completed, the game could’ve gone in a totally different direction. Nixon has always talked the talk, and today he continued to walk the walk. Winner: Dani Dennis-Sutton The rookie LB had the best game of his career thus far, and what a joy it was to see. He had some massive stops, including one on 3rd down as the Bears offense was approaching the redzone. Their resulting FG attempt was then missed. He also had the below demolition of QB Case Keenum to close things out. Dennis-Sutton finished the day with 3 tackles, 2 TFLs, 2 QB hits, 1 sack, and 1 PD. Micah Parsons told DDS to be ready to work when he was drafted by the Packers. I think he listened. 😤 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/4X3w0n5gFg — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 11, 2026 Winner: Jordan Love It’s always a good day when QB Jordan Love gets to Sling that Thing™. The offensive line did their job today, and as a result, the receivers were able to get open, and Love was able throw deep pass after deep pass. Look at this beauty of a passing chart. Jordan Love: 6 completions on throws of 20+ air yards Bears entering Week 5: 7 completions on throws of 20+ air yards (3 of those were from Caleb Williams) pic.twitter.com/sfLlXEAYE2 — Kole Noble (@AtoZ_Slaw) October 11, 2026 Love had some absolutely gorgeous throws today, including his TD passes to Christian Watson, and the below heave to Matthew Golden. For the first time this season, the Packers were able to crack 30 points, and it looks like things are finally clicking for the offense. Love finished the day 25 of 31 (80.6%) for 367 yards, 2 TDs, and 0 INTs for a 137.5 rating. His 367 yards are the most by a QB against the Bears at Lambeau Field. Everything is coming up Jordan Love today ‼️ @CHIvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/yzQQJ2IQ98 — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 The Packers have won two straight games now, and are looking to keep it rolling in Week 6 as they stay at home to face off against the 2-3 Dallas Cowboys during Sunday Night Football . Will Micah Parsons be back on the field against his former team as the Packers seek their third straight win?

title: Packers Week 5 Snap Counts: Kaleb Johnson slides
summary: The Green Bay Packers beat the Chicago Bears 31-7. It was very enjoyable. We should do this every weekend. Beyond the win, though, let’s look at the Packers’ snap counts to see what is staying the same and what is changing as the season unfolds. For the most part, we know what this squad is, […]
full_text: (Photo by Daniel Bartel/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers beat the Chicago Bears 31-7. It was very enjoyable. We should do this every weekend. Beyond the win, though, let’s look at the Packers’ snap counts to see what is staying the same and what is changing as the season unfolds. For the most part, we know what this squad is, but there are a couple of change-ups from Week 5. Quarterback Jordan Love: 57 snaps Tyrod Taylor: 2 Tyrod Taylor was on the field for the kneel-downs. Don’t make too much out of this one. Running Back MarShawn Lloyd: 26 Pierre Strong Jr.: 24 Kaleb Johnson: 9 Pretty early on, it was obvious that not only was MarShawn Lloyd going to out-snap Kaleb Johnson, who led the Packers in rushing last week, but that Pierre Strong Jr., fresh off his practice squad promotion, also displaced Johnson. It’s going to be interesting to see how Green Bay plays the roster number game once Josh Jacobs returns to the lineup and Chris Brooks is brought back from the injured reserve. It’s going to be impossible to keep all these backs on the 53-man roster when they’re all active. At some point, cuts are going to have to happen. Most of Johnson’s action came late in the game in garbage time. He did not play a single snap in the first half. Receiver Christian Watson: 48 Matthew Golden: 45 Bo Melton: 28 Skyy Moore: 11 J. Michael Sturdivant: 7 With Skyy Moore going down with an injury, Bo Melton took over the slot role. Melton is the third receiver to play that role for the Packers, following injuries to both Moore and Jayden Reed. For what it’s worth, J. Michael Sturdivant and Savion Williams, who is now practicing with the team despite still being on Green Bay’s injured reserve list, have seen the vast majority of their snaps as outside receivers. If Moore, who was seen wearing a walking boot post-game, is out for any substantial amount of time, assume you’re going to see Melton taking over full-time in the slot. Tight End Tucker Kraft: 45 Mark Redman: 21 Jonnu Smith: 21 Josh Whyle: 10 Josh Whyle continues to be the fourth tight end in the pecking order, while Mark Redman and Jonnu Smith split the TE2 job behind Tucker Kraft. We have not received any updates on tight end Luke Musgrave, who has spent all of the regular season on the PUP list with a neck injury. Offensive Line Jordan Morgan (LT): 59 Laken Tomlinson (LG): 59 Sean Rhyan (C): 59 Travis Glover (RG): 59 Anthony Belton (RT): 59 After the team played six different lineups in the first three weeks of the season, the Packers have been steady with their offensive line the last two weeks. The only question now is when Kevin Zeitler, who was active on Sunday, will take over at right guard for Travis Glover. Zeitler was just signed two weeks ago and is still getting ready for his first crack at snaps. Defensive Line Karl Brooks: 39 Devonte Wyatt: 32 Javon Hargrave: 30 Chris McClellan: 29 Jonathan Ford: 17 Defensive lineman Javon Hargrave apparently tore his Achilles on Sunday , which is going to end his season. Karl Brooks and Devonte Wyatt will still be the team’s top 3-4 defensive ends/nickel defensive tackles, but the Hargrave injury does hurt depth at the position. Chris McClellan plays the Brooks/Wyatt/Hargrave roles, while also spelling Jonathan Ford — the team’s starting 3-4 nose tackle. The big question is whether or not Anthony Campbell, who wasn’t active today due to an injury, will be able to backfill for McClellan moving up in the pecking order. Edge Defender Lukas Van Ness: 39 Brenton Cox Jr.: 34 Dani Dennis-Sutton: 32 Barryn Sorrell: 31 The edge defenders were in a heavy rotation this week, and starter Barryn Sorrell actually finished the game with the fourth-most snaps among the group. I wouldn’t be surprised if rookie Dani Dennis-Sutton starts to earn more snaps down the line, as he’s looking like one of the team’s two most talented players at the position (at least until Micah Parsons comes back). Off-Ball Linebacker Zaire Franklin: 63 Ty’Ron Hopper: 38 Isaiah McDuffie: 32 Ty’Ron Hopper and Isaiah McDuffie both played the Will linebacker position opposite of Zaire Franklin this week, replacing the injured Edgerrin Cooper. Both Wills are significant special teams contributors, so this might be a way for the team to split a starting role so neither has to be taken off teams to keep their legs fresh. Cornerback Brandon Cisse: 68 Keisean Nixon: 60 Carrington Valentine: 9 Kamal Hadden: 7 I think Kamal Hadden played nickelback in garbage time of this game, but I will have to watch the film on Monday to check. Keisean Nixon was sat in garbage time to give Carrington Valentine an opportunity. Valentine played right cornerback (Nixon’s spot) instead of left cornerback, where he spent virtually all of camp while pushing Brandon Cisse for a starting job. Safety Evan Williams: 68 Xavier McKinney: 60 Javon Bullard: 52 Kitan Oladapo: 8 Not too much to note here (Kitan Oladapo played safety for Xavier McKinney in garbage time), other than that the Packers played 76 percent of their snaps in nickel sets on Sunday. The Bears usually like to play multiple tight end sets, but it’s possible they had to ditch that personnel group when they were down multiple scores.

title: Packers fear Javon Hargrave tore his Achilles
summary: Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur opened up his press conference on Sunday by stating that the win over the Chicago Bears was “bittersweet,” as it didn’t “look good” for defensive lineman Javon Hargrave. Hargrave went down late against the Bears in garbage time and was carted off the field. When asked for more […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur opened up his press conference on Sunday by stating that the win over the Chicago Bears was “bittersweet,” as it didn’t “look good” for defensive lineman Javon Hargrave. Hargrave went down late against the Bears in garbage time and was carted off the field. When asked for more details, LaFleur said, “early indications look like Achilles.” Hargrave would be the fourth season-ending injury for the Packers already, if the diagnosis is correct. Green Bay previously lost receiver Jayden Reed (neck), right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele (Patellar tendon) and linebacker Edgerrin Cooper (Achilles) for the season. The Packers have five defensive linemen on the roster, beyond Hargrave, but Anthony Campbell was held out of action in Week 5 and came into Sunday with a questionable status due to an injury. Karl Brooks (starting 3-4 defensive end), Devonte Wyatt (starting 3-4 defensive end), Jonathan Ford (starting 3-4 nose tackle) and Chris McClellan (third-round rookie) are healthy in the unit. Whenever Hargrave gets deactivated, he’ll be the ninth Packers player to hit the injured reserve, on top of the three players who are on the physically unable to perform list. The good news? At some point, defensive linemen Warren Brinson (IR) and Jordon Riley (PUP) will come back and contribute to the unit. Currently, Green Bay’s sixth option at defensive tackle is practice squadder David Blay Jr., who was signed by the team in Week 4. The Packers have had their practice squad options poached this year, as Nazir Stackhouse was claimed at the cutdown deadline and Jaden Crumedy was plucked from the practice squad to the Houston Texans’ roster in-season. To replace Crumedy, Green Bay initially signed Eric Johnson II, but they let go of him after about two weeks. Two days later, the team signed Blay. The Packers almost always carry five defensive tackles on their 48-man game-day roster, so Campbell’s health will be a major focus this week. If he can’t go, Blay might need to be activated for game action.

title: Packers vs. Bears Final Score: Jordan Love dismantles Chicago with deep ball in 31-7 win
summary: Maybe facing the Chicago Bears really was what the doctor ordered after all. On Sunday in Week 5, and for the first time all season, the Green Bay Packers looked like a team capable of contending in 2026. For all of his downplaying of any personal animosity against Ben Johnson, Matt LaFleur kept sticking with […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 11: Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers celebrates a touchdown pass against the Chicago Bears during the third quarter at Lambeau Field on October 11, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Maybe facing the Chicago Bears really was what the doctor ordered after all. On Sunday in Week 5, and for the first time all season, the Green Bay Packers looked like a team capable of contending in 2026. For all of his downplaying of any personal animosity against Ben Johnson, Matt LaFleur kept sticking with the deep ball up by 24 points in the fourth quarter, finally living up to the “All Gas, No Brake” mantra he espoused earlier in his tenure as Packers head coach as his team dominated the Bears from the opening whistle in a 31-7 victory. Jordan Love had his best game of the season and was immaculate with the deep ball, throwing for more than 250 yards on balls 20-plus yards downfield. Love finished the day 25-for-31 passing with 367 yards overall, the most ever by a Packers quarterback at Lambeau against Chicago, and he threw for two scores on bombs to Christian Watson. The Packers’ top receiver continued his impressive scoring streak with those touchdowns, which brought him up to six on the season, while ending the day with a stat line of 6 catches for 143 yards. Matthew Golden got into the act as well with six catches of his own for 123 yards, including two explosive plays of his own. Credit the Packers’ offensive line as well for a good performance ahead of Love, as the team rolled out the same starting five as last week in Tampa. The run game still struggled — the team gained just 70 yards on the ground — but the Bears only recorded two sacks and three more QB hits in the game as Love was able to drop back and wait for deep routes to develop. Meanwhile, the Packers’ defense was swarming to the football, recording three interceptions on Bears quarterbacks and five turnovers overall. Two of the picks came from Xavier McKinney, who recaptured a bit of his All-Pro form after a bit of a down start to the season, while Ty’Ron Hopper recorded the third to all but end the Bears’ comeback attempt early in the fourth quarter. With the win, the Packers moved over .500 for the first time all season, improving to 3-2 and into a tie with the Bears — though with a win in hand — for second place in the NFC North (pending the Lions’ game against Arizona later in the afternoon). The Packers also recorded their first two-game win streak since last season’s back-to-back wins over the Lions on Thanksgiving and the Bears the following week, while that Thanksgiving game was the last time Green Bay had scored more than 30 points prior to this performance. On the Bears’ first possession, Tyson Bagent hit D’Andre Swift out of the backfield for a 13-yard gain early, but he took a sack on 2nd-and-long to lead to a punt. Green Bay took over from their own 9-yard line and proceeded to move the ball well, cruising into Bears territory. On a first-and-10 after a Tucker Kraft sneak to move the chains on 3rd-and-1, Love dropped back and found a wide-open Christian Watson on a go route, dropping a perfect pass in for a 42-yard touchdown and an early Packers lead. Say it with us now… LET'S GO!!! 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/zLLSOq0xW5 — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 11, 2026 The touchdown was Watson’s fifth on the young season, and two plays later, the Packers’ defense gave the offense a golden opportunity. Tyson Bagent threw into double coverage and Javon Bullard tipped the pass into the waiting arms of Xavier McKinney at the Bears’ 45-yard line for the game’s first turnover. After a few nice gains, the Packers faced a 4th-and-1 at the Bears’ 23-yard line, and Pierre Strong punched through the line to move the chains. Strong supplanted Kaleb Johnson in the lineup as the Packers’ RB2 throughout the first quarter, and the Packers ended the frame inside the 10-yard line. On the first play of quarter two, Lloyd obliterated Jaylon Johnson in a hole off right tackle and cruised into the end zone for his first career rushing touchdown, giving Green Bay a 14-0 lead. MarSHAWN LLOYD LAMBEAU LEAP 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/TVSKwKFBVW — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 11, 2026 The Packers forced a three-and-out on the next Bears’ drive, but they returned the favor on offense and Chicago finally got something going. The Bears ripped off their first long drive behind D’Andre Swift and Luther Burden, picking up four first downs, but Green Bay appeared to get a stop in the red zone only for Zaire Franklin to get called for holding to keep the drive alive. Chicago eventually got Swift into the end zone just inside the two-minute warning, converting on 4th-and-goal from the two to cut the Packers’ lead to seven points. A false start penalty before the Packers’ first down play put them in a tough spot. Two passes to the boundary and an incomplete pass took barely 20 seconds off the clock and forced a punt. Fortunately, Daniel Whelan’s punt was a 68-yard bomb, and with a holding penalty on Chicago, the Bears started from their own 10. Brandon Cisse made back-to-back big plays to give the offense one more chance, though, sacking Bagent on 2nd down and breaking up a deep pass for Rome Odunze on third down. Matthew Golden’s punt return — with Skyy Moore banged up — set up the Packers at midfield with 40 seconds and two timeouts. Love took a sack on first down then the Packers got an illegal formation penalty to force them into a 2nd-and-20 well outside field goal range. Austin Booker sacked Love a second time on third down to send the game into halftime at 14-7. But on the first play of the second, half, Watson delivered an explosive play as Love found him over the middle for a gain of 31 yards. A few plays later, the Packers had a long touchdown to J. Michael Sturdivant wiped off the board on 3rd down, as the rookie receiver was flagged for offensive pass interference, so Love just chucked one deep again. This time it was Watson over the middle of the field once again, who elevated to make an incredible catch over safety Dillon Thieneman for a 53-yard score. OH MY GOSH 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/qyqGYPEsIB — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 11, 2026 Trey Smack’s extra point went wide left, however, as Green Bay’s lead stuck at 20-7. Chicago got back to work on offense, picking up chunks of yardage, but the Packers’ defense got a stop thanks to Dani Dennis-Sutton sniffing out a wide receiver screen on third down. Cairo Santos’ 43-yard field goal hooked wide left, keeping Green Bay’s lead at 13 midway through the third quarter. One first down and a punt sent the ball back to Chicago, but Zaire Franklin delivered a big stop. Franklin knifed through the line to tackle Roschon Johnson for a loss on a 3-and-1 run, giving the ball back to Green Bay’s offense once again. The first play saw Love roll out to the left and Tucker Kraft got wide open on a post across the field, hauling in a deep ball for a gain of 46 yards, immediately putting the Packers into the red zone. They couldn’t do much more with it, however, and Trey Smack came on for a 35-yard field goal to give Green Bay a 16-point lead at 23-7. The Bears converted a 4th down on their next series, getting a conversion from Bagent to Colston Loveland on 4th-and-4 from their own 40, but on the very next play, McKinney struck again. He lurked and broke on another Bagent throw over the middle, jumping a route by Loveland and intercepting his second pass of the game. Two passes from Love to Matthew Golden for 36 and 15 yards on the next two plays set Green Bay up with goal-to-go as the fourth quarter began. MarShawn Lloyd didn’t make Packers fans wait long, cutting outside and walking untouched into the end zone on the very next play. A two-point conversion to Golden made it a 24-point lead. The Bears weren’t quite done, however, as Zavion Thomas took the ensuing kickoff 61 yards…

title: Value of Things: In the Rearview Mirror
summary: These are happier times at least for the time being. Even our model for this particular piece changes as we slide over to great, good, and bad in lieu of good, bad, and ugly. The Texans defeated the Titans 26-3 in a game that felt competitive for all of one quarter. Furthermore, you were 7.5 […]
full_text: These are happier times at least for the time being. Even our model for this particular piece changes as we slide over to great, good, and bad in lieu of good, bad, and ugly. The Texans defeated the Titans 26-3 in a game that felt competitive for all of one quarter. Furthermore, you were 7.5 point favorites on the road which is practically a double digit line for an 0-4 football team. That probably tells you everything you need to know about the Tennessee Titans. They will be in a race with the Miami Dolphins for the first overall pick. So, this win feels good in the same way you feel good when you pass a first grade spelling test. You feel more relieved. At any rate, it was an infamous get right game in a lot of respects and that is particularly true on the defensive end. They generated multiple times for the first time on the season and also managed four sacks on the afternoon. It will help the bottom line as the aggregate now says that the Texans are a solid defense. Obviously, two of their games would say otherwise, but let’s take a look at the numbers from the game. The Key Numbers Total Yards: Texans 63/328, Titans 58/187 Rushing Yards: Texans 27/79, Titans 18/57 Passing Yards: Texans 36/249, Titans 40/130 Third Downs: Texans 6/12, Titans 4/11 Fourth Downs: Texans 0/0, Titans 0/2 Sacks: Texans 4, Titans 2 Turnovers: Texans 0, Titans 2 Penalties: Texans 11/95, Titans 7/83 Time of Possession: Texans 34:29, Titans 25:31 Of course, we will get into this in more detail throughout the week as the biggest news occurred away from the field on Sunday. This is the kind of game we could have predicted from the Texans. The Titans just aren’t good at football. They haven’t been good at football since they let Mike Vrabel walk for reasons. They are likely fighting for the number one overall pick with the Miami Dolphins. So, you do nothing but hold serve in this one. The Great Will Anderson is good at football. I’ve said that three weeks in a row now. He added three sacks in this one and he is making his quest to be the Defensive Player of the Year. He probably will have to put up a few more games like today to get into that conversation, but he is at the point where he is stacking great efforts back to back. Cam Ward wiggled out of three or four sacks on the afternoon or this could have been a historic effort from a defense we thought would be historic coming into the season. Yes, DeMeco Ryans was calling plays this time around, but we need to hold off before anointing this defense as back. This was a historically bad offense on the other side of the field. Still, they did what they were supposed to do. They smothered a weaker opponent and never let them get hope outside of an opening field goal. Those guys are paid to play football too, so you can’t simply just show up and have it happen. These guys clearly put in some work and it could be the first building block to getting back into the season. The Good C.J. Stroud now has his own section, so this one goes to Woody Marks. The numbers show he caught four balls for 23 yards and rushed 15 times for 62 yards. More importantly, it looks like he might be taking over as the featured back after David Montgomery’s groin injury. Sometimes, performance dictates a change and sometimes fate knocks you across the dome and you are forced to make a change. Four yards a carry won’t make anyone forget Arian Foster, but it is credible and credible is that the Texans are hoping for. You can acquire all of the wide receivers in the world, but if you don’t have a credible running game it really doesn’t matter. The Bad Nothing can be truly ugly in a 26-3 game, but we focus on things in victory we wouldn’t overlook in defeat. This team commits too many stupid penalties. One of them cost you a Woody Marks touchdown. These are things that slide by in a 26-3 win over a terrible football team. They don’t slide by when you are facing a team like the Glitter Kitties. It would be one thing if this were a one time thing, but this is a weekly occurrence. It is safe to say it has cost you at least one football game if not two. We would feel far differently at 2-3 or 3-2 than we currently do at 1-4. Focus on Stroud The stat sheet will say that Stroud was 26 for 34 with a 107.5 quarterback rating. That obviously raises both the completion percentage for the season but also the overall quarterback rating for the season. More importantly, this game was a sign that the team is slowly turning over the keys to the kingdom to Stroud. Naturally, that might not be a complete vote of confidence. It could be the total lack of a consistent running game, but adding a Marvin Harrison Jr. doubles down on that thought as they try to give him as many weapons (and one he is familiar with) as they possibly can. That tells me two things. First, they definitely have made up their mind about the future of the quarterback position as not only has he played well, but they are giving him more and more responsibility for this offense. Secondly, they brought in a familiar target because they want him to be happy. That recognizes that he had reason not to be.David Mulaghetta is not above shopping for new homes for his clients. A 2-15 or 3-14 season could have made Stroud and company think twice about committing to the Texans. Now, they see that they went out and got a buddy. Will that work? It remains to be seen, but it is a clear signal of where this offense is going.

title: BREAKING: Texans trade for Marvin Harrison Jr.
summary: Ultimately, some of this reads like commentary. There is a family tradition where we play golf and a poker game every year. On a few occasions, someone has placed a certain part of the male anatomy on the table to cover a wager. Obviously, that is hyperbole when it is done and done for simply […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 04: Marvin Harrison Jr. #18 of the Arizona Cardinals makes a catch for a touchdown against Deonte Banks #2 of the New York Giants during the first quarter at MetLife Stadium on October 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ultimately, some of this reads like commentary. There is a family tradition where we play golf and a poker game every year. On a few occasions, someone has placed a certain part of the male anatomy on the table to cover a wager. Obviously, that is hyperbole when it is done and done for simply a series of laughs, but this is one of those moments when an NFL general manager placed a proverbial body part on the table to cover a wager where he is potentially light. Trade: the Arizona Cardinals have agreed to trade WR Marvin Harrison Jr. and 2027 7th-round pick to the Houston Texans in exchange for a 2027 2nd-round pick and 2027 6th-round pick, per @rapsheet and me. pic.twitter.com/ziepfRIPr4 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 11, 2026 So, essentially, that means the Texans just traded a 2027 second round pick for Marvin Harrison Jr. He is in the third year of a four year rookie deal with the fifth year option for first rounders. Let’s ignore for a moment what his current numbers are. This deal brings forth two distinct questions that every Texans fan has to grapple with now that the Texans are 1-4. First, are you one football player away from being a playoff team? It is a fair question. Two teams in NFL history have come from 0-4 to make it to the playoffs. The San Diego Chargers were the last to di it and they aren’t even in San Diego anymore. Perhaps the 17th game changes the calculus on that some. Perhaps they are looking at the middle of their schedule and hoping they can get back to around .500 before the tough stretch to close the season. Perhaps, getting the Marvin Harrison that the Cardinals thought they were getting would unlock that. The second question is whether wide receiver was the player they needed to make that jump. Let’s ignore whether it is THIS wide receiver that was needed. You could make credible arguments for an upgrade on the offensive line, maybe a better running back, or maybe someone to shore up your linebacking core. Then, there are the questions about Harrison himself. Even ignoring this season, he hasn’t been the number one wide receiver everyone thought he would be. From a value standpoint, this one is a risk. If Harrison turns into another Tee Higgins (1B to Nico Collins 1A) then the Houston offense could be transformed into something different than what we have seen. We need to keep in mind that Jayden Higgins was a second round pick and that kind of performance would be far and above what Higgins did last season and was likely to do this season. Still, we haven’t seen it yet and it remains to be seen whether Nick Caley is the play caller to bring that out of him. Stepping away from it all and you have to wonder what this means for Nick Caserio. Caserio was on track to get another go at it next season even if the club misses the playoffs. When you make it the postseason three years in a row then you get that mulligan on spec. This deal changes that. If it goes well then he probably extends his time in Houston another season or two. If it blows up in his face he could have just put himself on the hot seat. It will be interesting to see how it all pans out.

title: Texans play get right game in Nashville
summary: Imagine you are a normal high school student walking the halls and an 80 pound weakling challenges you to a fight. What’s the upside there? If you accept the challenge and win then of course that is what is supposed to happen. If you accept the challenge and lose then you are the laughingstock of […]
full_text: Imagine you are a normal high school student walking the halls and an 80 pound weakling challenges you to a fight. What’s the upside there? If you accept the challenge and win then of course that is what is supposed to happen. If you accept the challenge and lose then you are the laughingstock of the school. If you decline then you are the laughingstock for being the coward. There literally is no upside here. Playing the Tennessee Titans is a similar situation. Of course, there is no declining option. You play who is on the schedule, but it’s not like Sunday’s 26-3 victory has anyone feeling really good about the Texans. It just means you don’t end up feeling worse. It really delays some of those hardened questions on both sides of the football. They will have to wait another week when the Texans face a real football team in London. Obviously, game balls go to the Texans defense that generated two turnovers and had two turnovers on downs as well. They allowed a field goal on the first drive of the game and nothing else when it mattered. The pass rush was relentless even if they only had four sacks on the afternoon. As usual, it was Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter getting in on the fun as the two continue to be the best one-two punch at defensive end in the NFL. Offensively, C.J. Stroud had another very good day as he completed more than 70 percent of his passes, threw a touchdown pass, and added a rushing touchdown of his own. That was enough to win this one going away. I hate to make light of the Titans. Clearly, all Texans fans should be kinder because we have been in their shoes. You our outmanned from the moment you leave the bus. Cam Ward had a decent enough day outside of his interception, but there just isn’t enough there. Maybe it’s coaching. Maybe it’s scouting. Maybe they are just destined to be bad. We certainly had days when we felt like that was going to be our permeneant reality. Obviously, most of Sunday was taken up by the rumors that the Texans will add another target to the wide receiver room. We will obviously have something more substantial when we hear something more substantial. At any rate, this was your lime wedge after the first month of straight lining tequila. Let us know if you feel any better in the comments and stay tuned to more in-depth coverage throughout the week as more news comes down the pike.
