title: Finish a few more drives and the Colts’ story might be different
summary: The Indianapolis Colts had a bad day in Pittsburgh. That’s the simplest way to sum it all up. It wasn’t a beat down, but it was rough. The team can’t say it didn’t have some opportunities to walk away with a win though. That’s the most frustrating thing about it. If the Colts had finished […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 11: Spencer Shrader #3 of the Indianapolis Colts kicks a field goal during the first quarter of a game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts had a bad day in Pittsburgh. That’s the simplest way to sum it all up. It wasn’t a beat down, but it was rough. The team can’t say it didn’t have some opportunities to walk away with a win though. That’s the most frustrating thing about it. If the Colts had finished more drives by coming away with touchdowns instead of field goals, they might be singing a different tune today. Let’s give Spencer Shrader some credit in this one because without his strong, accurate leg, things would have been a lot worse. His field goals of 57 and 56 yards were enough to keep the Colts close early. His kicks from 22, 40, and 28 were enough to drive Colts fans crazy. First and goal from the 3-yard line produced a total gain of -1. The 40-yarder was tough because the Colts could have pulled back to within one or tied the game with a two-point conversion. A case to forgive that one can be made, though. There is no forgiveness for the last field goal made under the 30. Daniel Jones and Jonathan Taylor got the Colts down to the Pittsburgh 10-yard line, but three straight incompletions forfeited all momentum. A touchdown would have given the Colts the lead with less than a quarter to go. Yes, the Steelers scored a touchdown on their next possession, but a Colts touchdown might have changed things. We will never know. All we know is that the Colts made five field goals with only one touchdown and lost the game. Maybe turning two field goals into touchdowns does the trick, but then again, maybe it doesn’t. That doesn’t mean it won’t have a major impact on wins and losses going forward, though. Having someone like Spencer Shrader is a great weapon, but it would be better if he mainly kicked extra points. Use him for those 57-yarders, but too many more 22-yarders will spell disaster for the Colts.

full_text: Tennessee Titans helmet rests on the field during a training camp practice at Saint Thomas Sports Park Thursday, July 29, 2021 in Nashville, Tenn. Nas 0728 Titans Camp 003 | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Indianapolis Colts are picking up divisional play in Week 6 against the Tennessee Titans. It’s a welcomed return home after a road trip that produced mixed results. After traveling to London and collecting a win, things went sideways in Pittsburgh. FanDuel Sportsbook is giving the Colts the edge against the winless Titans with a 6.5-point spread advantage. The money line is at -330 with the over/under starting at 43.5. The Colts did what they do; they lost in Pittsburgh. Unable to finish drives and giving up huge plays on defense was the story of the afternoon. After going up 3-0, they never regained the lead. Every time the Colts got close, they had to settle for 3. Luckily, Spencer Schrader was on his game, but it wasn’t enough. An 80 and 50 yard score by Jaylen Warren was too much to overcome as the Colts fell, once again, to the Steelers in Pittsburgh. The Titans and Texans were entrenched in the battle of the winless as one team would get off the schneid and the other would sink further down. Cam Ward and the Titans might really be that bad. They scored the first 3 but then allowed the Texans to rattle off the next 26. Jobs might be on the line as the season is quickly slipping down the drain. Lose again and the Titans might be eyeing a replacement for Ward in the draft with the No. 1 pick. The Colts have work to do, but the Titans might be the best remedy to what ails them. Nothing is certain, but this is a great opportunity to get to 3-3 and finish the first third of the season at .500. Finding the end zone and putting up 6 in place of 3 is a great place to start. The Colts can do it, but they have plenty to tighten up before then.

title: After Colts’ sluggish road showing, Pittsburgh remains franchise ‘House of Horrors’
summary: The Indianapolis Colts hadn’t won in Pittsburgh since 2008, and after another sluggish road showing in ‘The Steel City on Sunday, that rather surprising franchise losing streak only continued—as the Horseshoe fell 34-22 as their late comeback attempts fell short. Offensively, the Steelers once again bottled up Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor and the […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PA - OCTOBER 11: Pat Freiermuth #88 of the Pittsburgh Steelers catches a 17-yard touchdown pass against the Indianapolis Colts in the second half at Acrisure Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts hadn’t won in Pittsburgh since 2008, and after another sluggish road showing in ‘The Steel City on Sunday, that rather surprising franchise losing streak only continued—as the Horseshoe fell 34-22 as their late comeback attempts fell short. Offensively, the Steelers once again bottled up Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor and the Indy ground game, as Taylor was held to just 45 total rushing yards on 15 carries (3.0 ypc. avg.). Colts starting quarterback Daniel Jones and the Colts passing attack weren’t able to counter with a big afternoon on the other side, as despite Jones throwing the ball a whopping 44 times, it only amounted to 267 total passing yards and 0 passing touchdowns. Jones didn’t win the Colts the game (obviously) with 0 passing touchdowns, but he didn’t lose them the game either with 0 turnovers. His ball security was improved this go around, albeit in another losing Pittsburgh road effort. That being said, Colts fans have been spoiled in the past with having starting quarterbacks such as franchise greats Peyton Manning and Andrew Luck elevate their teammates offensively and cover up glaring roster deficiencies, and right now, Jones is just a serviceable to average starting NFL quarterback. Nothing more, nothing less. He might be above average to good on one of his better passing days, but he’s not carrying Indy offensively by any means right now. Perhaps most ‘dooming’ for the Colts offense was their inability to fully capitalize on their long or promising scoring drives, as while placekicker Spencer Shrader was individually great in this one, he kicked (and made) five field goal attempts. It doesn’t take a mathematician here to know that 3 points is less than 7 points, especially when multiplied a handful of times over the course of a game. If there was a bright spot for Indianapolis offensively, it was tight end Tyler Warren, who led them with 7 receptions for 83 total receiving yards, as well as added a 1-yard rushing touchdown midway in the 2nd quarter. Defensively, the Colts secondary really struggled, particularly regarding its linebackers’ coverage middle-of-the-field. Rodgers was perfect on his first 10 passing attempts , as the Indianapolis allowed the longtime veteran quarterback get in initial rhythm and really dissect them surgically early on. On the afternoon, Rodgers completed 22 of his 31 passing attempts for 235 total passing yards, 3 passing touchdowns, and 0 interceptions. He was complemented very well by Steelers running back Jaylen Warren, who had a big afternoon against the Colts front seven, averaging an enormous 6.7 yards per carry on his 15 total carries and just eclipsed 100 yards. Right now, the Colts seem like a mediocre football team, which has been the status quo for a while here. Indianapolis will beat the teams they should on their schedule given the home/away matchup and lose to the NFL teams they should respectively. The Colts dip below .500 again to 2-3, but with an opportunistic home matchup against the winless Tennessee Titans next weekend (0-5), they have a great chance to reach .500 status again for at least another week (before traveling to the currently undefeated 5-0 Minnesota Vikings)

title: It’s time to fire Lou
summary: Five games into a season is usually too early to talk about firing a coordinator. I think Lou Anarumo has made a pretty convincing case for an exception. The Colts are 2-3 after Sunday’s 34-22 loss to Pittsburgh, and once again the defense was one of the biggest reasons they lost. Jaylen Warren finished with […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - SEPTEMBER 27: Indianapolis Colts defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo looks on during the NFL game between the Houston Texans and the Indianapolis Colts on September 27, 2026, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Allio/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Five games into a season is usually too early to talk about firing a coordinator. I think Lou Anarumo has made a pretty convincing case for an exception. The Colts are 2-3 after Sunday’s 34-22 loss to Pittsburgh, and once again the defense was one of the biggest reasons they lost. Jaylen Warren finished with 188 yards from scrimmage, including an 80-yard receiving touchdown and a 50-yard touchdown run. Aaron Rodgers threw three touchdowns and repeatedly found ways to extend plays despite being 42 years old. This is not one ugly performance that can be written off. Three of the Colts’ first five defensive performances have been horrible. Baltimore put up 41 points and 506 yards in Week 1. Kansas City followed with 33 points and 523 yards. Pittsburgh just scored 34 while Warren ran through and around the defense all afternoon. The two games where the defense actually played well need some context too. Houston was without Nico Collins, by far its best offensive player, and still came within a late field goal of winning. Washington was already starting backup Marcus Mariota because Jayden Daniels was injured, then lost Mariota in the first quarter and had to play rookie third-string quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis the rest of the way. The Colts are allowing 27.6 points per game through five weeks. They have faced two elite quarterbacks in Lamar Jackson and Patrick Mahomes. They have also faced a Houston offense missing its No. 1 receiver, a third-string quarterback in London and a 42-year-old Rodgers. At some point, this cannot keep being explained away by the opponent or individual mistakes. Anarumo was brought to Indianapolis because the Colts wanted a more aggressive, adaptable defense. Five games into his second season, the defense still looks confused too often, still cannot generate consistent pressure, still gives up huge plays and seems to feature a different defensive back getting exposed every week. I have spent plenty of time criticizing Chris Ballard for the construction of this defense, especially the front seven. The roster is not perfect and Anarumo did not choose every player on it. That does not give the defensive coordinator immunity when this many problems keep repeating themselves. Three bad games out of five is enough The Baltimore game should have been the wake-up call. The Colts gave up 506 yards and 41 points at home in Week 1. They struggled getting lined up, had communication problems, got destroyed in man coverage and were pushed around against the run. The performance was so disorganized that the Colts changed the green dot from Cam Bynum to Akeem Davis-Gaither immediately afterward. The following week in Kansas City was better competitively, but not defensively. The Chiefs gained 523 yards, including 371 through the air and 152 on the ground. Mahomes threw for 382 yards and three touchdowns, Kenneth Walker III had 178 yards from scrimmage and Travis Kelce went over 100 receiving yards. That’s as close to flawless an offense can get. Indianapolis survived Houston and handled Washington, but neither performance convinced me the defense had suddenly turned a corner. Collins did not play for Houston, while Washington spent almost the entire game with its third quarterback. Then Pittsburgh happened and Jaylen Warren did essentially whatever he wanted. The Steelers hit explosives, Rodgers escaped pressure and extended plays, and the Colts again looked like a defense that could not consistently get off the field when it needed to. Five games is not a huge sample, but we are no longer talking about one bad afternoon. Three times in five weeks, the Colts defense has been taken apart and that’s a very concerning pattern. Akeem Davis-Gaither is Anarumo’s guy I wrote last week asking where CJ Allen was because I could not understand why the Colts’ top draft pick had played only 11 defensive snaps through four games. Anarumo’s explanation was essentially that Allen is a MIKE linebacker and Davis-Gaither is playing well, so there have not been enough snaps available for Allen. Well, Davis-Gaither is Anarumo’s guy. He has the green dot. He played for Anarumo in Cincinnati. The coaching staff wants him on the field as much as possible, and Anarumo has repeatedly defended his play. Then when the Colts needed their linebackers to tackle Jaylen Warren on Sunday, Davis-Gaither was part of the problem. In fact, he was the biggest part of the problem. There were opportunities to get Warren on the ground where the Colts simply did not finish. Davis-Gaither was responsible for missed tackles that helped turn manageable plays into much bigger ones. In fact, Davis-Gaither was directly responsible for a missed tackle that led to a 50-yard touchdown from Warren. Watch 51 on the run below. Jaylen Warren's last 3 games: 176 yards 126 yards 149 yards (and counting) The last 3 players to have 3 consecutive 125+ yard games were Kenneth Walker, Derrick Henry, and Bijan Robinson. pic.twitter.com/ucHdNrmTJ3 — Underdog (@Underdog) October 11, 2026 Davis-Gaither has played better over the last couple of weeks than he did at the beginning of the season. I am not arguing he should be benched entirely, especially now that he is responsible for communicating the calls. I am arguing that nothing about his play should make him untouchable. He is not a great linebacker. He’s not even a good linebacker. That makes Anarumo’s refusal to find snaps for Allen even more frustrating. If Davis-Gaither is going to stay at MIKE because of the green dot, then use Allen at WILL. Take snaps away from Jaylon Carlies (who was injured today) and Bryce Boettcher. Boettcher was also responsible for an ugly missed tackle on another Warren tackle. So Allen is watching all the linebackers ahead of him on the depth chart missing tackles that are leading to big touchdowns. Why is a different corner getting exposed every week? The Colts have invested heavily in their secondary. Sauce Gardner is one of the best cornerbacks in football. Charvarius Ward has played at a very high level during his career. Cam Bynum is a good safety. Justin Walley was highly regarded internally before his injury and was given an important role immediately upon returning. Yet seemingly every week, another member of the secondary looks bad. Walley was cooked by Zay Flowers in Week 1. Ward was picked on today against the Steelers and has had ugly reps where his feet get stuck and he is beaten vertically. Gardner has had games where offenses have gone directly at him and won much more often than anyone is accustomed to seeing. The worst of those performances came against the Commanders. Every cornerback gets beaten. Sauce Gardner is not suddenly washed because he loses a matchup. Ward did not forget how to cover when he arrived in Indianapolis. Walley missing his entire first season means there were always going to be growing pains. When multiple good players are consistently looking late, confused or uncomfortable, though, coaching has to enter the conversation. This was supposed to be the strength of the defense. Ballard spent two first-round picks to acquire Gardner. Ward was brought in as another proven outside corner. Bynum was a major addition at safety. The Colts finally had enough talent on the back end that the secondary should have been able to carry some of the weaker areas of the defense. Instead, Baltimore found matchup after matchup. Kansas City threw for almost 400 yards. Pittsburgh continued finding openings. Good players can have bad games. When a collection of good players keeps having bad games in the same defense, I start looking at the person responsible for putting them…
author: Andrew Aziz

title: Warren runs wild as Colts fall 34-22 on road to Steelers
summary: The Indianapolis Colts could not capitalize on their goal-to-go opportunities and fell 34-22 Sunday to the Pittsburgh Steelers at Arcisure Stadium. Indy’s offense missed two chances to plunge into the end zone from short field distance, while its defense allowed Jaylen Warren to lead the game in both rushing and receiving by piling up 188 […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PA - OCTOBER 11: Indianpolis Colts tight end Tyler Warren #84 rushes for a 1 yard touchdown in the first half against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts could not capitalize on their goal-to-go opportunities and fell 34-22 Sunday to the Pittsburgh Steelers at Arcisure Stadium. Indy’s offense missed two chances to plunge into the end zone from short field distance, while its defense allowed Jaylen Warren to lead the game in both rushing and receiving by piling up 188 scrimmage yards and two highlight-reel touchdowns. The Colts held a 3-0 lead for the ensuing kickoff, but it took only one snap for the Steelers to seize control and lean on their defense to keep the stampede out of the end zone. Indy scored on six of its 10 drives but reached the end zone just once, settling for five field goals in a franchise-record-tying performance from kicker Spencer Shrader. The 27-year-old kicker did his part to vie for AFC Special Teams Player of the Week by demonstrating just how valuable it is to rely on a kicker who feels automatic when deployed onto the field. Spencer Shrader today 5/5 FG 1/1 XP 21.0 fantasy points KICKER. ONE. pic.twitter.com/RzLnXluspe — PFF Fantasy (@PFF_Fantasy) October 11, 2026 The opposing pregame sentiment from DK Metcalf was “He gotta guard me”, which also meant the Colts had to face a Steelers’ offensive unit led by Aaron Rodgers, Jaylen Warren and Metcalf. On the Steelers next offensive snap, Rodgers recognized he was about to absorb a massive hit from Grover Stewart and fired a quick swing pass to Jaylen Warren in the flat, who broke away from rookie linebacker Bryce Boettcher, turned upfield and raced down the sideline for an 80-yard touchdown. Metcalf delivered a pair of key blocks downfield to spring Warren for an instant house call to take a lead Pittsburgh would never relinquish. Warren finished with a game-high 101 rushing yards and scored two touchdowns, while adding six receptions for a game-high 87 receiving yards. Anthony Gould gave Indy an immediate opportunity to respond, returning the ensuing kickoff 56 yards into Steelers territory. The Colts offense could not capitalize on the short field and had to settle again as Shrader drilled a 56-yard FG between the uprights, trimming the deficit to 7-6. After a defensive pass interference penalty on third down against cornerback Charvarius Ward extended the Steelers’ possession near the goal line, Rodgers capped a 17-play march into the end zone with a 1-yard touchdown pass to tight end Pat Freiermuth. Pittsburgh made it difficult for Indy to move the chains, but the Colts converted twice on fourth down during the next drive, including a key quarterback sneak by quarterback Daniel Jones. After three consecutive attempts from Jonathan Taylor were stuffed at the goal line, it was Tyler Warren who punched in a fullback dive on fourth-and-goal to score the lone touchdown for the Colts. It was truly the Warren showcase providing much of the production for both squads as Tyler Warren led the Colts with seven receptions for 83 receiving yards, while adding his second-career rushing touchdown. The 2025 first round draft pick became the second tight end in NFL history to score two rushing TDs in his first two seasons. TYLER TOUGH 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/IV3n4e4NUo — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) October 11, 2026 The red zone problems followed the stampede into the second half. Indianapolis drove deep into Steelers territory twice, but Taylor was once again stuffed in the backfield and Jones could not find an opening, which forced Steichen to settle for consecutive chip shots to stay within striking distance. Jones completed 24-of-44 pass attempts for 267 passing yards and the eighth-year veteran managed to protect the football against a defense that entered Sunday with eight takeaways — the second-most in the league — but there were moments where his pass felt intended to avoid the turnover. The rushing attack was non-existent as Taylor was held to 45 rushing yards on 15 carries, forcing Indianapolis to find other ways to move the ball. One of those 15 carries even featured an explosive 20-yard gain, meaning Taylor’s other 14 carries gained a combined 25 rushing yards. Defensive tackle DeForest Buckner gave the Colts a slight spark, wrapping around a stunt to secure his 75th sack on Rodgers and force a punt. The Colts responded with a promising drive, leaning on Taylor to bounce outside and convert a third-and-2 before breaking loose for the aforementioned 20-yard gain behind the elite run blocking of left guard Quenton Nelson. Once again, the Colts were forced to settle for another field goal from Shrader. With the game still in the balance, Rodgers extended a crucial possession by escaping the pressure from edge rusher Jaylahn Tuimoloau and found receiver Germaine Bernard near the sideline, who raced into Colts territory for a 25-yard catch-and-run. The Colts were able to force a fourth down, but Jaylen Warren bulldozed his way to convert a fourth-and-2 near the red zone and keep the clock rolling. Faced with third-and-6 midway through the final frame, the Steelers ran a pick concept and Rodgers found Freiermuth wide open on a slant for his second touchdown to extend Pittsburgh’s lead to two possessions. The Colts ran 44 offensive plays inside of Steelers territory, but weren’t able to win the battle in the trenches to punch the ball into the end zone enough. The Steelers needed just 22 offensive plays in Colts territory before taking a pair of knees to seal the victory. The Colts host the winless Tennessee Titans (0-5) next Sunday inside Lucas Oil Stadium, with kickoff scheduled for 1 p.m.

full_text: The Indianapolis Colts are on the road to take on the Pittsburgh Steelers for week 5 of the 2026 season, kickoff is at 1:00 p.m. EST. Last week we saw the Colts even up their record to 2-2 against a very injured Washington Commanders team, in London. Ultimately, Indy won by multiple scores, so I’m not going to complain about their level of play, I won’t do a deep dive on how the final score didn’t really tell the story of how the game went, I won’t do those things. I will, however, tell you that if they play like they did in week four, in week five against these Steelers, the outcome will look much different for the Colts. The Colts do have the deck stacked against them this week. Pittsburgh is coming off of a ten day stretch since their last game, after playing on Thursday Night Football in week four. Indianapolis played in Europe last weekend and will be playing on the road just seven days later. Even before you consider the fact that, for some reason, the Colts haven’t won in Pittsburgh since Peyton Manning was breaking records in blue and white, this game was cursed from the moment the schedule makers put ink to paper. Further complicating matters is that it has been raining in Pittsburgh all week, the Pitt Panthers played a division one college football game on the same field just yesterday (losing to the North Carolina Tarheels) and the current forecast is calling for steady rain until around 4 p.m., and all of a sudden you have a strong likelihood that today will be a very ugly game. Side Note: I told you about this last week but I’m probably going to keep reminding you each week because I think it’s important, especially for everyone who enjoys these gameday threads. The SB Nation app makes commenting, especially in these game feeds, so much easier. At this point I roll my eyes every time someone asks me to download another app, but this one really does improve the experience so much that even I am telling you that if you like to hang out here, chat, celebrate, commiserate, and argue in the comments, this app is actually worth your time. Links are directly below. Join Stampede Blue on game day! Stay on top of every Colts update and debate every snap with other diehard fans. Game-day discussion is smoother in the SB Nation app. Fewer ads Jump easily between conversations Faster commenting and posting Download on iOS or Android . The good news for the Colts is that this Steelers team is a mess. Aaron Rodgers has had more screaming matches with his head coach, than touchdown passes this year and last week T.J. Watt called up his defensive coordinator during the game to give him a piece of his mind, too. So you know, things could be far worse for Indy. Today I expect a very sloppy game from two teams who, thus far, have both played an extremely boring brand of football. Between the rain, field conditions and the strengths and weaknesses of both teams, expect a lot of rushing attempts, fumbles, and oddities this afternoon. Given the Colts travel schedule and Pittsburgh’s (theoretical) state of rest, I’m not feeling great about the outcome of this one for Indy. Prediction: Steelers: 19 Colts: 17 As always, go Colts. summary: The Indianapolis Colts (2-2) travel to another notorious franchise ‘House of Horrors’ to take on the Pittsburgh Steelers (2-2)(-2.5), at 1 PM EST, with expected rainy weather conditions at Acrisure Stadium for Sunday afternoon. Rather shockingly, the Colts have not beat the Steelers in Pittsburgh since November 9, 2008, when Peyton Manning was the starting […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 02: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers hugs Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts after the Steelers beat the Colts at Acrisure Stadium on November 02, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts (2-2) travel to another notorious franchise ‘House of Horrors’ to take on the Pittsburgh Steelers (2-2)(-2.5), at 1 PM EST, with expected rainy weather conditions at Acrisure Stadium for Sunday afternoon. Rather shockingly, the Colts have not beat the Steelers in Pittsburgh since November 9, 2008, when Peyton Manning was the starting quarterback, and Indianapolis narrowly won 24-20 that Sunday afternoon. For those looking to watch the game, it will be aired on CBS with Jim Nantz (play-by-play) and JJ Watt (analyst) covering for the television broadcast. It can also streamed on NFL+ and YouTubeTV, etc. The NFL TV map can be found here . Regarding those tuning in, the game can be listened to on 93.5 and 107.5 The Fan and 97.1 Hank FM, with Matt Taylor (play-by-play), Charles Arbuckle (analyst), and Larra Overton (sideline) on the radio call per usual. For SiriusXM subscribers, you can find the Colts game on Channel 267 or 813. Indianapolis is coming off a 2-game winning streak and currently ranks 13th in points scored (25.5 avg. ppg.), while surrendering the league’s 22nd most points (26.0 avg. ppg.). Meanwhile, Pittsburgh is 24th in points scored (19.3 avg. ppg) behind longtime veteran starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers, and is allowing the NFL’s 14th most points (21.8 avg. ppg.) with veterans Cam Heyward and TJ Watt still anchoring their defensive line. There will be no former Colts wideout Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) “revenge game,” as he was recently played on injured reserve by the Steelers and is not healthy enough to face his old Indianapolis teammates. Temperatures at kickoff are expected to be in the mid-to-high sixties, with persistent rain, potential thunderstorms, and projected wind gusts in the low teens reaching to the high twenties in miles per hour, due to lingering weather bands from Hurricane Isaias over the past week. This week’s officiating unit will be head official Shawn Smith and his crew. Pittsburgh has largely dominated this series all-time, holding the distinct advantage 28-8-0, and Pittsburgh earned the victory the last time these two teams played, winning 27-20 at Pittsburgh last year, on November 2, 2025. title: 3 Numbers to Know From the Jaguars’ Win Over the Eagles
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars scraped by the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 5 to move to 4-1 on the season. Wahoo! Here are a few stats that stand out from the victory. 6% That was Jacksonville’s win probability with eight seconds left in the game, per NFL Pro. Jake Elliot had just knocked through a 48-yard field […]
full_text: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 11: LeQuint Allen Jr. of the Jacksonville Jaguars celebrates with a flag after the 2026 NFL London Games match between Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 11, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by James Fearn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars scraped by the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 5 to move to 4-1 on the season. Wahoo! Here are a few stats that stand out from the victory. 6% That was Jacksonville’s win probability with eight seconds left in the game, per NFL Pro. Jake Elliot had just knocked through a 48-yard field goal to put the Eagles up by one point. If the Jaguars had any timeouts remaining, they might’ve been able to pick up a chunk completion before stopping the clock and attempting a lengthy walk-off field goal. But the Jaguars didn’t have any timeouts, and the Eagles made sure they’d have even less time by kicking off short of the endzone to prevent a touchback. Then Ameer Abdullah happened. JAGS HUGE KICK RETURN. They're in range for one more shot at a field goal! @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/XSWbKBTvW2 — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 “Man, we got the perfect call with the perfect kick,” Abdullah said. “We knew that we could hit ‘em in the alleys — that’s the one that Josh Cameron had one called back earlier in the game — so we knew that if we got the right kick, we had an opportunity. “And having a kicker like Cam Little, we knew, if we got anywhere near midfield, get down and let him handle the job.” Boy, did Little handle it. Moments don't get any bigger than this. @NFLUKIRE | @Jaguars pic.twitter.com/L0AAShGvca — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 It’s easy to say that the Jaguars should’ve lost this game. They were digging their own grave. Long snapper Ross Matiscik and left tackle Anton Harrison exited mid-game, which contributed to questionable coaching decisions and frustrating player mistakes. I don’t know about y’all, but I felt like ripping my hair out the entire second half. That was one of the craziest, dumbest, wildest football games these eyes have ever seen. I suppose that would be the case regardless of whether Little’s last kick went through the uprights. But since his 57-yarder did in fact win the game, it makes this one of the most dramatic victories in franchise history. Per ELIAS: This is the first game, regular season or playoffs, where each team had a go-ahead score in the final 10 seconds of regulation in the Super Bowl Era (since 1966). Eagles took a 17-16 lead with 8 seconds to play and Jaguars won it on Cam Little's 57-yard field goal. — Michael DiRocco (@ESPNdirocco) October 11, 2026 “Man, the resolve on this team is special,” Abdullah said. “I’ve never played on a team like this, that ‘it’s not over until it’s over.’ These guys fight through adversity. We started off slow, another big penalty game, we were shooting ourselves in the foot, but it seems like guys just get stronger and stronger with every rep.” “That just shows me the resolve and the toughness and just the experience that these guys have been through with being down, being up, and understanding it’s just the same.” 15 That’s how many years it’s been since an NFL team won consecutive games with 13+ penalties in each game. The Jaguars are the first team to do so since the Seahawks in Weeks 10 and 11 of the 2011 season, per NFL Pro. “Every time we went positive, we went negative,” Liam Coen described. “It was like, every time we’d have an 8-to-10-yard run, we’d have a penalty. I mean, we had 13 [penalties] again, for 100 [penalty yards]. And it felt like they were all after good plays.” “We had them in how many 3rd-and-XLs defensively and let them off the hook? So I never really felt like we were just getting flat-out outplayed. Like it just never felt that way. We were kicking ourselves in the foot—we’re 0 for 3 in the red area—and how many of those were inside the 5? Right, so you’re in scoring position, what should that game have been—I can’t say.” “To come out of it on top, it’s obviously—you always want to live in the process. You get so wrapped up in the results. But, to have one second left and the team still fighting and the team still going through it, I mean I got to be proud of that.” 8 That’s how many snaps DaVon Hamilton played at long snapper on Sunday, per PFF. 4 snaps as a field goal long snapper, 4 snaps as a punt long snapper. Hamilton is a nose tackle. He was thrust into emergency action following the aforementioned injury to Matiscik. It’s never ideal to lose a player with such a specific skill set, but Hamilton has already shown in the past that he’s up for the job. the film cut up you’ve all been waiting for every rep of DaVon Hamilton at long snapper: pic.twitter.com/Ib96qjpko6 — Gus Logue (@gus_logue) December 1, 2025 There were understandable concerns. Jacksonville became even more aggressive than usual on 4th downs, and Little missed a late extra point that probably should’ve led to overtime. But ya gotta give credit when credit is due. D-Ham stepped up big time to help steal the win on Little’s final kick. Other numbers to know: 5 : International career wins by Trevor Lawrence, breaking a tie with Tom Brady (4) for the most in NFL history. 45 : Rushing yards allowed by Jacksonville in the past two weeks (22 in Week 4, 23 in Week 5). The Jaguars are one of seven teams in the Super Bowl era to allow 25 or fewer rushing yards in consecutive games. 1 : Other teams in the Super Bowl era that did not allow an individual rusher to reach 40+ yards in their first five games of a season. That team was the 1969 Dallas Cowboys. 11 : Consecutive games Jacksonville has held its opponents to under 20 points. It’s a franchise record and the NFL’s longest active streak. 5 : Consecutive games Bhayshul Tuten has rushed for 65+ yards. He is the third Jaguar to do so, joining Fred Taylor (2003) and Maurice Jones-Drew (2011). 22 : Carries by Bhayshul Tuten on Sunday, the most of his career. He has 13+ carries in every game this season after seeing double-digit carries just once last season. 5 : Career field goals of 55+ yards for Cam Little, the most in franchise history. 1 : Banger of a post by ArtButMakeItSports . title: Jaguars Winners & Losers From Week 5: Little Wins It In London
summary: That win counts, right?  In a disasterclass of a morning London kickoff, the Jacksonville Jaguars somehow escaped the lowly Philadelphia Eagles, 19-17, behind a Cam Little game-winner. The Jags (4-1) were competing against basically a practice squad and yet had to bomb a 57-yarder to walk off as winners. It was the epitome of an […]
full_text: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 11: Parker Washington of the Jacksonville Jaguars celebrates scoring his teams first touchdown during the 2026 NFL London Games match between Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 11, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) | Getty Images That win counts, right? In a disasterclass of a morning London kickoff, the Jacksonville Jaguars somehow escaped the lowly Philadelphia Eagles, 19-17, behind a Cam Little game-winner . The Jags (4-1) were competing against basically a practice squad and yet had to bomb a 57-yarder to walk off as winners. It was the epitome of an ugly game, but nonetheless the Jaguars were victorious. Now, there needs to be some conversations surrounding whatever the hell that play calling was from Jacksonville or what’s up with these penalties. The Jags have escaped two injured teams in back-to-back weeks for wins, but this isn’t sustainable. The field goal make was cool and all, but this team isn’t even close to firing on all cylinders when they play away from EverBank Stadium. The Jags, and especially the coaches, are getting in their own way. Eventually, that could be the very downfall of a squad many think can compete for a Super Bowl. Even though the Jags won, there were plenty of losers and loser moments in Tottenham. WINNERS Special Teams If you can recall after all the heart-stopping and mind-numbing moments from Sunday’s game, it all started with a weird special teams play. And it ended with one as well. Rookie Josh Cameron housed the opening kickoff, which of course was called back due to penalties, and then a “fight” ensued . Two players were ejected. And then the game officially began. We should have known right then and there this one was about to be bizarre. Behind Little’s leg, Logan Cooke’s hands and the big arms of DaVon Hamilton, the Jags somehow won. Who would have guessed that Hamilton snapping one to Cooke to pull down for Little would be the way the Jags would beat a team who simply can’t score in the second half. BIG HAM 🍖 > @dmhamilton53 | #PHIvsJAX pic.twitter.com/S2aEdAO10z — Jaguars UK and IE (@JaguarsUKandIE) October 11, 2026 Hamilton should be the Special Teams Player of the Week for his efforts Sunday. Yes, his snaps were high but at least he stepped in and delivered in a huge pressure moment. Cooke deserves a lot of credit too for not dropping a single snap from Hamilton. And then you have Ameer Abdullah, who set the whole win up after the Eagles inexplicably kicked short. Parker Washington scored both touchdowns but special teams won that game. It should never have been that close, but thankfully the Jags have the special teamers to make magic happen. Fitting that a game in London should end with a kick. The end of game sequence.. They let Abdullah run it back all the way passed the 50 and then Legend Cam Little kicks it for the win pic.twitter.com/JNNE9ot8cs — Fitz (@LaurieFitzptrck) October 11, 2026 Parker Washington Speaking of Washington, I think it’s high time for the Jags to pay this dude. He’s simply playing at an unbelievable level right now. Washington pulled in two scores and 124 yards receiving, averaging over 20 yards a catch on his six catches. His one-handed touchdown grab (which for some reason was on a fourth-and-5 but that’s for later) saved the game and Jacksonville’s chances of winning. Even earlier, his 51-yard weaving touchdown grab made me think briefly that the Jags would win going away. How naive was I? Sunday was Washington’s first multi-touchdown game which almost feels wrong given how impactful he has been of late. I can say with almost certainty that it won’t be his last multi-score game. Whatever that guy wants on his contract, it should be given. Washington is just downright incredible. Parker Washington TOOK OVER in London against Philadelphia. 6 REC, 124 REC YDS, 20.7 AVG, 2 TD vs Eagles Washington scored both of Jacksonville’s touchdowns in a huge 19 to 17 win. pic.twitter.com/NtQy6Jojgo — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) October 11, 2026 Josh Cameron While it’s Washington who’s going to get the credit Sunday, Cameron has looked really solid for a rookie. He needs his flowers too. Sure, the opening kickoff was negated by a flag but he still was able to house that ball. And he was third on the team in receiving when all was said and done with 43 yards. Cameron has multiple catches in three of his first five NFL games. That’s saying something for a team that has a deep wide receiver room. Cameron runs extremely hard and has sure hands. For a sixth-round rookie, anyone would have to be pleased with his production to this point. You almost forget that the Jags have guys like Jakobi Meyers or even Travis Hunter to throw to on offense because of how important Cameron has been. Josh Cameron Takes It To The House To Start The Kickoff, OMG. That’s A Statement. 🔥 pic.twitter.com/PhXI3oACqv — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) October 11, 2026 LOSERS Liam Coen Ok, fun time is over. Head coach Liam Coen was cooking up some bullshit in London. You know when people make fun of British food because it looks all pale or mushy or just straight up like diarrhea? That was what Coen was pumping out across the pond. The Jags had 13 penalties on Sunday, the second straight game with 13 penalties. No, all of that isn’t on Coen but there has to be something the head coach can do to get his team snapping the ball properly or not committing a holding on every running play. There has got to be some sort of institutional control from the guy in charge. Outside of the general ire with penalties, the playcalling was insane. The Jags had the ball inches from the goal line and we have Wyatt Milum outside? We decide to run the jet sweep from the one? Even the Washington one-handed score was crazy because if that ball is dropped, the Jags likely just lose outright. The shortest way between two points is a straight line. For some reason, Coen and offensive coordinator Grant Udinski think the shortest way to gain a yard is to run laterally. The “I’m the smartest guy in the room, I know best” shtick gets old after a while. Run the damn ball in a straight line, man. Eagles deny the Jaguars at the goal line! Eagles head into the half with a 14-7 lead. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/K1f1ZnsWCj — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 There was also a big disconnect in getting the snap off on Sunday. Trevor Lawrence and Robert Hainsey were nowhere near on the same page. With a former quarterback at head coach, you’d think maybe there would be some way to fix that on the fly too. It all just looked so disjointed and hard at every turn. The penalties thing dates back to last year. These weird struggle games do as well. If Coen were someone like Todd Bowles or even Nick Sirianni, he’d be fired yesterday. There’s certainly zero reason to think Coen’s job is going anywhere, but he has to look in the mirror and realize that it doesn’t have to be this hard. He does so much good. Why make the small stuff hard when it doesn’t need to be? Clean up the penalties and make the playcalling reasonable and you have a winning formula. Don’t, and your season could spiral. At least Sunday gave us a new variant of the old Doug Pederson head-down on the podium meme. Liam Coen after Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars get STOPPED on fourth down trailing 14-10 😬 Jacksonville had three penalties called at the goal line and come up empty on the drive. pic.twitter.com/Rk7B57HDAN — Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) October 11, 2026 The Secondary Speaking of those practice squad players, the Jags secondary didn’t do themselves any favors against the likes of Darius Cooper and Dontayvion Wicks. On paper, this should have been a feast for the Jags and Travis Hunter and Jarrian Jones. In practice, a lot of those Eagles pass catchers ran wild. DARIUS COOPER, 62-YARD TOUCHDOWN EAGLES TAKE THE LEAD. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on…

title: 3 reasons why the Jaguars beat the Eagles
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars have made a habit of producing memorable moments in London, but Sunday’s 19-17 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium might just take the biscuit. Liam Coen’s team overcame 13 penalties, some baffling playcalling, and enough self-inflicted wounds to fill an entire medical ward before Cam Little delivered a 57-yard […]
full_text: The Jacksonville Jaguars have made a habit of producing memorable moments in London, but Sunday’s 19-17 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium might just take the biscuit. Liam Coen’s team overcame 13 penalties, some baffling playcalling, and enough self-inflicted wounds to fill an entire medical ward before Cam Little delivered a 57-yard field goal with one second remaining. It was spectacular, ridiculous, and quintessentially Jaguars. Here are three reasons Jacksonville escaped with the win. Sheer Luck Jags had 1st and goal at the 1 and then 5-yard false start penalty 2 yard rush 5-yard delay of game penalty Incomplete pass 5-yard delay of game penalty 9 yard completion Incomplete pass pic.twitter.com/DiiQ9Uz0ti — PFF (@PFF) October 11, 2026 Let’s get one thing straight: the Jaguars should have lost this game. Not because Philadelphia were particularly impressive, but because Jacksonville seemed determined to sabotage themselves at every available opportunity. There are bad performances, there are frustrating performances, and then there is whatever the hell the Jaguars served up in North London. Thirteen penalties for 100 yards told only part of the story. Jacksonville’s offense repeatedly found ways to turn promising situations into disasters, with questionable playcalling and sloppy execution threatening to undo everything Trevor Lawrence and company had worked for. The most glaring example came in the fourth quarter, when the Jaguars had first-and-goal at the one-yard line. Three procedural penalties later, they had somehow turned a golden opportunity into a turnover on downs. Considering the way the first half ended in similar circumstances, it was enough to test the faith of even the most ardent fan. And that wasn’t even the end of the madness. Jacksonville had a 90-yard kickoff return touchdown wiped off the board by a holding penalty on the opening play, while a missed extra point following Parker Washington’s second touchdown left the door open for Philadelphia to steal the game late. The Jaguars finished with 408 yards of offense, compared to Philadelphia’s 232, yet somehow managed to make this contest considerably closer than it needed to be. They had opportunities to put the Eagles away and repeatedly refused to take them. Sometimes, winning football games requires discipline, precision, and execution. Other times, it requires the opposition to make a mess of things and a little good fortune at precisely the right moment. Jacksonville got plenty of the latter on Sunday. They’ll take it, of course, but Liam Coen will know his team cannot afford to be quite so generous with its mistakes every week. Parker Washington, London’s favourite son PARKER WASHINGTON, WOW. JAGS TAKE THE LEAD. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ubE4xivDcD — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 If Jacksonville has discovered anything during its time playing across the Atlantic, it’s that London has a soft spot for the Jaguars. And if Parker Washington has learned anything from his visits to the British capital, it’s that this city might just be his personal playground. Washington announced himself as a London legend in October 2024, when he took a punt 96 yards to the house against the New England Patriots at Wembley Stadium. It was the longest punt return touchdown in Jaguars history and an unforgettable moment for the UK faithful. Two years later, he was at it again, torching the Philadelphia Eagles for 124 yards and two touchdowns at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Some players simply enjoy playing overseas. Washington appears determined to make London his own. Washington’s second touchdown was arguably the most important. With the Jaguars trailing late in the fourth quarter, he hauled in a 27-yard pass from Lawrence on a fourth down conversion to put Jacksonville ahead 16-14. It was precisely the sort of big-time play the Jaguars needed from a receiver who has increasingly demonstrated an ability to deliver when the pressure rises. Of course, the subsequent missed extra point meant Washington’s heroics didn’t immediately translate into a comfortable lead. Because apparently, nothing can ever be straightforward when the Jaguars are involved. Still, Washington was one of the biggest reasons Jacksonville was in a position to win at all. His combination of speed, elusiveness, and reliable hands gave the Eagles’ defense plenty to think about, while his ability to turn a routine completion into a game-changing play provided Lawrence with a vital weapon. London has been good to the Jaguars over the years, and Washington seems particularly keen to keep that relationship going. Two touchdowns, 124 yards, and another memorable performance in front of the UK faithful? Not a bad day’s work. If the Jaguars keep bringing performances like that to London, they might have to start considering Washington for an honorary British passport. Nick Sirianni: Thank you, Coach! Liam Coen's reaction to the @Jaguars game-winning field goal is unreal. pic.twitter.com/NG6W8DBtZz — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 And finally, we arrive at the moment that will have Jaguars fans buying Nick Sirianni a pint the next time he visits London. With eight seconds remaining, Jake Elliott had just kicked a 48-yard field goal to give Philadelphia a 17-16 lead. The Eagles had seemingly done enough to snatch victory from a game in which their offense had struggled badly after halftime. All they needed to do was prevent Jacksonville from getting into field-goal range with virtually no time remaining. The sensible option? Boot the ensuing kickoff through the end zone. Force the Jaguars to start at their own 35-yard line, leave them with precious little time, and make Lawrence produce something approaching a miracle. Instead, Philadelphia kicked short. Ameer Abdullah collected the ball and returned it 53 yards to the Eagles’ 39-yard line, leaving Jacksonville with one second on the clock. One. Single. Second. Enter Cam Little. The Jaguars kicker, who had already experienced the frustration of a missed extra point earlier in the game, was handed an opportunity to redeem himself in spectacular fashion. From 57 yards out, he split the uprights to give Jacksonville a 19-17 victory and send the traveling Jaguars faithful into delirium. It was an extraordinary finish, made possible by Little’s composure and Abdullah’s return. But Philadelphia’s decision to give Jacksonville that opportunity deserves plenty of scrutiny, too. With eight seconds remaining, why risk allowing a return that could put the opposition in scoring range when a touchback would have forced the Jaguars to travel considerably further? Sirianni and his special teams unit will have plenty of time to reflect on that decision during the flight home. Meanwhile, Coen, Little, and the Jaguars can enjoy a victory that seemed increasingly unlikely with every passing minute. Jacksonville didn’t just snatch victory from the jaws of defeat. They were practically feeding themselves to the beast before Philadelphia helpfully opened the gates. So, thank you, Nick. Your contribution to the Jaguars’ London adventure will not be forgotten in a hurry. Everyone in teal will know they need to improve if the Jags are going to reach the levels they are capable of this season. But a win is a win, and the first leg of the London trip is complete. Bring on the Houston Texans at Wembley.

title: Jaguars Lose Anton Harrison, Win a London Thriller
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars pulled off a stunning last-second victory in London, surviving a wild finish against a hobbled Philadelphia Eagles team. What appeared to be a golden opportunity for Jacksonville to make a statement instead turned into a chaotic battle that came down to the final moments. The Jaguars escaped with the win, but the […]
full_text: American Football - NFL - Philadelphia Eagles v Jacksonville Jaguars - Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, London, Britain - October 11, 2026 Jacksonville Jaguars' Anton Harrison is stretchered off after sustaining an injury Action Images via Reuters/Peter Cziborra | Action Images via Reuters The Jacksonville Jaguars pulled off a stunning last-second victory in London, surviving a wild finish against a hobbled Philadelphia Eagles team. What appeared to be a golden opportunity for Jacksonville to make a statement instead turned into a chaotic battle that came down to the final moments. The Jaguars escaped with the win, but the dramatic finish leaves plenty to unpack about a team that continues to find interesting ways to snatch victory from the hands of defeat. Here’s everything you need to know from Jacksonville’s Week 5 19-17 victory at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Favorite Highlight: Whether it counts in the record books or not, Josh Cameron’s opening play 90-yard kick return likely should have counted, based on the tape. Linebacker Branson Combs was called for holding during the play (with additional offsetting penalties afterward). However, the replay seems to show him being bowled over, with the defender falling on top of him. With the opening kick flags, the NFL’s first kick return touchdown of 2026 was wiped off the board, but Duval remembers. Josh Cameron Takes It To The House To Start The Kickoff, OMG. That’s A Statement. 🔥 pic.twitter.com/PhXI3oACqv — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) October 11, 2026 In Case You Missed It The Jacksonville Jaguars, in consecutive weeks, begin the day with a significant problem with penalties and issues blocking up front. However, in this matchup, struggles in the red zone became a new talking point. The Jacksonville offense answered the early call, despite penalties opening the game with a Parker Washington touchdown. HE'S GONE 💨 Parker Washington hit a max speed of 19.74 MPH on this 51-yard touchdown, according to @NextGenStats @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/wkO8Nlpuby — NFL+ (@NFLPlus) October 11, 2026 However, an inability to slow down the Eagles’ pass rush, paired with an inexperienced safety room struggling to limit the explosives, resulted in a true dogfight for the first time in 2026. The London opener was, notably, the first time this season that Jacksonville went into the half without a 10, or more, point lead. In this one, Jacksonville failed to score a tying touchdown on four plays from the one-yard line. Halftime Stats: Score: 14-7 Third Down Defense: 4/6 (66.7%) Turnovers forced: 0 Rushing yards: 33 to 16 Jacksonville Passing yards: 162 to 138 Jacksonville Redzone: 0/1 vs 1/1 Philadelphia Points off turnovers: 7-0 Jacksonville (*turnover on downs) QB Trevor Lawrence ended the half 13/19 for 154 yards, 1 touchdown, and no turnovers. Meanwhile RB Bhayshul Tuten had 9 carries for 19 yards (2.1 average), with Parker Washington leading the receiving room with 74 yards on three catches. Following the half, both defenses tightened up, forcing a back-and-forth, field-position slugfest. The Jacksonville defense pitched a second-half shutout, while the Jaguars’ offense, again, was held scoreless in the red zone from first and goal from the one-yard line with 6:40 left in the fourth quarter. However, following a punt on the next drive, Parker Washington, again, became the needed spark for the team, bringing in an incredible one-handed, go-ahead touchdown. An unbelievably clutch play from Parker Washington. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/C7Y6hQ0Coc — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 Following quick three-and-outs from both offenses, the Jaguars’ defense allowed the Eagles’ offense to drive 32-yards in 83 seconds to drill the game-winning field goal with 8 seconds remaining. However, a 53-yard kick return by Ameer Abdullah allowed Cam Little just one second to kick a walk-off field goal to take home the victory. The final sequence for the @Jaguars to get the win in London was truly WILD. pic.twitter.com/5viJ5yIdIX — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 Notable statistical gaps: First downs: 18 to 13 Jacksonville Time of possession: 35:02 Jacksonville Third & Fourth Down Defense: 6/17 (35.3%) vs 7/20 (35.0%) for Philadelphia Defensive Sacks: 2 to 1 Philadelphia Rushing yards: 102 to 22 Jacksonville Yards per rush: 6.0 to 3.9 Jacksonville Passing yards: 306 to 210 Jacksonville Passing yards per attempt: 7.5 to 5.1 Jacksonville Redzone: 0/3 (0%) vs 1/1 (100%) Philadelphia Penalties: 13 for 100 yards Turnovers forced: 3 to 2 – Philadelphia forced two turnovers on downs and an interception. Jacksonville forced two turnovers on downs and no turnovers. Points off turnovers: 7-0 Jaguars (*turnover on downs by Philly) Post-game notables: 1. Early Penalties Again Pop Up Following a Week 4 first half against Cincinnati, where Jacksonville collected 10 early penalties for 100 yards, in Week 5, the team ended Sunday with 13 penalties in consecutive weeks. The constant pre-snap penalties on offense are the ones that are most noticeable, as they share a similarity to those that Jacksonville struggled with for much of the early 2025 season. QB Trevor Lawrence (3) – Delay of Game (x3) LT Anton Harrison – False Start LT Walker Little – False Start LG Emmanuel Pregnon (3) – Offensive Holding (x3) C Robert Hainsey – False Start TE Brenton Strange (2) – Illegal Shift (declined) & Offensive Holding (declined) WR Jakobi Meyers – Offensive Holding (negating a 12-yard Chris Rodriguez first down rush) DE Bryan Thomas Jr – Personal Foul (BTJ ejected; penalty not accepted with kick return TD negated) LB Branson Combs – Holding (offsetting penalties; kick return TD negated) CB Jarrian Jones – Pass Interference CB Travis Hunter – Pass Interference 2. What to Do in the Safety Room It was a rough opening half for Jaguars safety Ray Lane, who initially was juked by Dontayvion Wicks on a first-down catch. He later missed the tackle on the Will Shipley touchdown run later in the drive. Will Shipley finds pay dirt and gets the @Eagles on the board. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Dmgr7pJzYt — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 Lane then took a bad angle on the Darius Cooper touchdown, not landing a hand on the receiver as the deep safety. DARIUS COOPER, 62-YARD TOUCHDOWN EAGLES TAKE THE LEAD. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/eKpCwhW8QZ — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 With Eric Murray ruled out in pregame with a concussion, Lane and Antonio Johnson were the starting safeties on Sunday, with Kaevon Merriweather seeing snaps in three-safety looks. Interestingly, Anthony Campanile went with the veteran Merriweather over rookie safety Jalen Huskey. The back end was noticeably quiet following halftime, however and it’s possible the young safety just needed time to settle in. 3. Offensive line struggles Sunday’s biggest news is clearly the loss of Left Tackle Anton Harrison, who was carted off from Tottenham Stadium in the third quarter with a knee injury. Walker Little took over at left tackle with Anton unavailable. Even before Harrison’s exit, the offensive line had struggles slowing down Jalen Carter early on. This forced fumble from Jalen Carter 👀 @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/p3X9q75C12 — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 While Jacksonville was fortunate to recover both fumbles in the shadow of their end zone, it was clear from the onset that the deep passing game would be limited in this one. Jalen Carter forces ANOTHER fumble, but the Jags recover it again. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NqPVFUNipO — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 Game balls: Special Teams: Punter Logan Cooke: Multiple high snaps on extra points and field goals were snagged in a game where every single point counted. However, it’s hard not to give this award to DT Davon Hamilton, RB Ameer Abdullah, or K Cam Little for their huge plays that also…

title: The Chiefs could put a stranglehold on the AFC West over next 3 weeks
summary: After a week off, the Kansas City Chiefs will be at the facility this week, preparing to host the Los Angeles Chargers at Arrowhead Stadium for a Week 6 divisional matchup. Two weeks after playing the Chargers, the Chiefs will hit the road and play the Denver Broncos. The games will be the team’s third […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a week off, the Kansas City Chiefs will be at the facility this week, preparing to host the Los Angeles Chargers at Arrowhead Stadium for a Week 6 divisional matchup. Two weeks after playing the Chargers, the Chiefs will hit the road and play the Denver Broncos . The games will be the team’s third and fourth divisional games this season. The 4-0 Chiefs are 2-0 in the division, which has given them an early lead in the AFC West. Division Standings after Week 5 Chiefs (4-0) Las Vegas Raiders (3-2) Broncos (3-2) Chargers (0-5) The Chiefs could put a chokehold on the division race if they come out of the bye week and take care of the lowly Chargers, then find a way to go to Denver and leave with a win in Week 8. Even if the team falls to the Seattle Seahawks on the road in Week 7, wins in Week 6 and Week 8 would strengthen the divisional record and the record against conference opponents, the two tiebreakers for division standings at season’s end. The Chiefs already have four wins against AFC opponents, while the Raiders are 2-2 in those matchups. The Broncos’ only conference loss so far is to Kansas City, but sweeping Denver in the season series would give them the season-end tiebreaker regardless of AFC games. If the Chiefs enter the second half of the regular season with a 4-0 division record and both wins over the Broncos, it gives the team some margin for error as it navigates the rest of the schedule, which features plenty of games against playoff contenders. The two remaining divisional games are the season’s final games: a road trip to Los Angeles, then a home game against the Raiders. If Kansas City wins the rivalry games ahead of them over the next three weeks, neither game may matter for the divisional standings by the time the Chiefs get there.

title: Analyzing the Chiefs’ defensive snap counts through 4 games
summary: Kansas City Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has described the first quarter of the season, the first four games, as a period to settle into the scheme and learn his personnel. It’s been a strong start to the year, but the young, fresh-faced unit needs to improve moving forward. Schematic changes in Week 6 and […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kansas City Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has described the first quarter of the season, the first four games, as a period to settle into the scheme and learn his personnel. It’s been a strong start to the year, but the young, fresh-faced unit needs to improve moving forward. Schematic changes in Week 6 and beyond could be based on what the group has put on film so far. Don’t be surprised if the rotation gets tweaked immediately after the bye week. So let’s dive into the snap counts, courtesy of Pro Football Focus, to see how the group is shaping up and what it suggests for the rest of the season. The 11 “starters” The top 11 players by defensive snaps through Week 4 Linebacker Nick Bolton (100% of snaps) Safety Alohi Gilman (97%) Cornerback Nohl Williams (93%) Defensive end George Karlaftis (86%) Linebacker Drue Tranquill (84%) Safety Jaden Hicks (80%) Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (77%) Defensive tackle Chris Jones (70%) Cornerback Mansoor Delane (56%) Defensive end R Mason Thomas (53%) Defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah (48%) While Bolton has never left the field, Gilman has been a mainstay in the back end of the Chiefs’ pass defense that has allowed the fifth-lowest passing yards per attempt (6.2) so far this season. He has played free safety on 65% of his snaps, putting Hicks, Conner and Sneed in position to roam the middle of the field and play closer to the line of scrimmage. Safety Chamarri Conner played 75% of the defensive snaps in his only game against the Las Vegas Raiders , indicating he will be part of this top-11 moving forward. Hicks has played well enough to maintain a consistent role in the starting defense, regardless. Chris Jones has been primarily used as a pass rusher, getting after the quarterback on 69% of his snaps this year. He has aligned over or outside the offensive tackle on 56% of his snaps, but has generated pressure on only 8% of his pass-rush snaps, with just two quarterback hits and no sacks. Thomas (68%) and Anudike-Uzomah (64%) have also been tasked with pass rushing on the majority of their snaps. While Thomas has stuck to the edge, Anudike-Uzomah has lined up in the B-gap for 47 snaps. His impact as an interior pass rusher has generated eight pressures over 84 pass-rush snaps (9.5%) and has the third-most quarterback hits (4) on the team. The rotational players 4 players that are just outside of the top-11 for snap counts Defensive tackle Peter Woods (46%) Nose tackle Khyiris Tonga (44%) Cornerback Kristian Fulton (42%) Defensive end Ashton Gillotte (41%) Woods leads the Chiefs in B-gap snaps (95) through four weeks; 75% of his snaps have aligned as the three-technique Jones has excelled at throughout his time in Spagnuolo’s scheme. It speaks to Woods’ impact on early downs, spelling Jones and being a handful for blockers on both run and pass plays. 43% of Woods’ snaps have been to defend the run; he has three Stops (tackles that constitute a failure for the offense), which is one less than Jones and Thomas. Tonga has seen the eighth-most run-defense snaps (66) through four weeks, indicating that he is a regular on neutral downs. When the downs get long and the game situation becomes late in the half or late in the game, he isn’t on the field. That speaks to the team’s success, playing with a lead for the majority of the season. Fulton may not be on the field as much with Delane healthy, but he has an impressive stat line in his rotational role so far: eight targets, four catches, 19 yards, one interception, and a 16.7 passer rating allowed when targeted. 46% of Gillotte’s snaps have come against the run; he has played more run-defense snaps than Anudike-Uzomah and Thomas. Sub-package players 2 players who only see the field for specific roles Linebacker Jack Cochrane (25%) Safety Christian Roland-Wallace (20%) When the Chiefs run base formations, Cochrane has been the third linebacker. It will be interesting to see whether second-year linebacker Jeffrey Bassa can fill that role in packages moving forward; he has only seen 18 snaps so far this year. When Kansas City plays dime defense, with six defensive backs on the field, Roland-Wallace has appeared as the second slot defender opposite Sneed most of the time. The bottom line Kansas City’s back-end rotation will need to sharpen with Conner’s return; Hicks is making too many downhill plays to keep him off the field, but Conner makes similar plays. It will be interesting to see how the team deploys the two. Woods seems to be properly spelling Jones, so the All-Pro pass rusher needs to take advantage of that and be more disruptive when he is on the field. The Chiefs’ defensive backfield looks strong on the perimeter, but watch for Williams or Delane to play more in the slot at some point this season to maximize the group’s talent.

title: Examining the Chiefs’ short-yardage offense through four weeks
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are enjoying an early-season bye week, sitting at a perfect 4-0 record. The only undefeated team left in the AFC, the Chiefs have one of the best offenses in the NFL and are currently third in the league with 1,648 yards of total offense. Running back Kenneth Walker has breathed new […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs are enjoying an early-season bye week, sitting at a perfect 4-0 record. The only undefeated team left in the AFC, the Chiefs have one of the best offenses in the NFL and are currently third in the league with 1,648 yards of total offense. Running back Kenneth Walker has breathed new life into the Chiefs’ offense and has led the NFL in rushing so far with 537 yards through the four-game stretch. Walker has helped the Chiefs offense in dozens of ways, but even with his ability, the Chiefs have still been inconsistent in short-yardage situations this season. At times, third-and-fourth-and-short conversions have been automatic, but in recent weeks the Chiefs have struggled to convert. Let’s dive into what works and what the team needs to improve on. A look at the numbers The offense ranks 10th in the league in 4th-down conversion percentage at 62.5%, while ranking 12th in red-zone touchdown rate at 63.16%. As many remember, the Chiefs led the league in 4th-down conversion percentage last year at a whopping 75%, thanks largely to Kareem Hunt’s dominant short-yardage season. The Chiefs weren’t quite as good in the red zone, but they still finished 12th in the league with a 56.3% touchdown conversion rate once they entered the red zone. The season is only a quarter old, but this appears to be an area where the Chiefs may have regressed early in the season in short-yardage-to-go situations. A look at the tape shows that a few tweaks could help the Chiefs improve as the season progresses. What’s worked On opening night, the Chiefs wasted no time rolling out a “jumbo” package on the first 4th-and-short. Out of a full house set with an overloaded offensive line, the Chiefs needed only a yard. With nose tackle Khyiris Tonga lined up at fullback, the Chiefs go with their version of a dive play up the middle. Only needing a yard, Walker uses good vision to find an opening and slip through for three yards and a first down. On the next fourth-and-short, the Broncos would try to take away the middle, but the Chiefs had a bigger play in mind. The defense tries to pinch to take away the middle, but the Chiefs run power to the left and catch the Broncos slanting inside, with safeties crashing in. The play isn’t well blocked, but Tonga gets just enough to buy Walker time to get outside and break it to the house. A week later, the Chiefs would show a few wrinkles in short yardage to keep defenses guessing. To keep defenses respecting Tonga, the Chiefs have given him the ball a few times this season, and in Week 2 against the Indianapolis Colts , it worked perfectly when he blasted ahead and rode the offensive line’s momentum for a first down. Later in the game, with the defense keyed in on Walker and Tonga, the Chiefs executed a beautiful play-action look in the low red zone. Out of the jumbo look with Tonga as the fullback in an I-formation, the Chiefs go with a play-action look. Jalen Royals lines up as a Y, as the Chiefs have shown on prior looks, but on the snap, he releases and is wide open in the end zone. In the first couple of weeks of the season, the Chiefs’ short-yardage attack looked unstoppable, but in the last couple of weeks, it has struggled. Issues In Weeks 3 and 4, the Chiefs struggled to convert on fourth and short, and the issues started up front. On fourth down, the Chiefs go with their jumbo set with Walker as the single back. On the snap, they run power, and Walker tries to cut inside quickly, but he is stuffed and falls short of the first down. The defense penetrates through the down side of the offensive line, and Kansas City’s front creates little push. Walker had to make a quick decision and tried to cut it up the middle, but he could not get through. Last week against the Las Vegas Raiders , the Chiefs still struggled to convert on fourth down, and once again the defense penetrated the front to stuff Walker. The Chiefs go with zone out of the full-house set and a jumbo offensive line. Once again, penetration through the B-gap causes a hold-up and stops momentum. Walker tries to navigate around it, but the Raiders linebackers fill quickly and close the hole to stop him before he can break free. The bottom line The Chiefs have all the talent to convert fourth down at will, so the issues over the last two weeks have been concerning, especially since they showed what they are capable of in the first two weeks of the season. Converting on fourth and short is about creating a charge at the line and having the ball carrier make a quick decision off it. Penetration from the defensive front ruins looks and can change the game’s outcome. So far, these issues haven’t affected the Chiefs’ win-and-loss record, but they must improve in this area moving forward. The talent and play calls are there; the team must simply execute in these critical moments.

In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Looking at advanced stats behind the Chiefs’ hot start The Chiefs are currently running about 40% of their offensive plays from under center (up from about 18% in 2025). Walker’s addition is also allowing Mahomes to reach a career-high 33% play-action percentage on passing plays. The only other time Mahomes exceeded 30% as a starter was in 2018, when he played most of the season with second-year running back Kareem Hunt. One curiosity of the start is the usage of rookie running back Emmett Johnson. With only five receptions (on five targets), Johnson already has a cumulative 5.8 receiving EPA. Because of a -3.6-yard average depth of target, Johnson has been credited with 92 yards after the catch while officially having 74 receiving yards for the year. title: Los Angeles Chargers news: Bolts earn ‘C’ grade in loss to Broncos
summary: The Chargers were truly this close to finally earning their first win of the 2026 season and they nearly managed to do it against a divisional opponent. The Chargers held a seven-point lead several minutes into the fourth quarter. Every ounce of momentum they had seemed to get flipped on its head the moment Jim […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 11: Hayden Rucci #40 of the Los Angeles Chargers celebrates after a receiving touchdown with teammates Charlie Kolar #88 during the third quarter of the game against the Denver Broncos at SoFi Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers were truly this close to finally earning their first win of the 2026 season and they nearly managed to do it against a divisional opponent. The Chargers held a seven-point lead several minutes into the fourth quarter. Every ounce of momentum they had seemed to get flipped on its head the moment Jim Harbaugh’s fourth-down risk failed, however. With roughly 10 and a half minutes left in regulation, the Chargers’s quarterback sneak attempt was stuff and the Broncos took over at the Chargers 41-yard line. From there, Denver scored 13 unanswered points and basically played the remainder of the game inside Chargers territory. Justin Herbert and the offense turned it over two more times on consecutive drives to help turbo the fourth-quarter collapse. Even with such a cataclysmic ending, the Chargers still came away with an average “C” grade for their performance from CBS Sports’ John Breech. Here’s what he had to say: “ It’s official: The Chargers offense looks broken. You can blame it on Mike McDaniel or you can blame it on the rash of injuries, but whatever the reason, this team just can’t do anything on offense. This week, the Chargers were forced to play without starting left tackle Rashawn Slater, and it showed. Justin Herbert barely had time to breath in this game. Every time he dropped back to pass, the Broncos were on him, which led to five sacks (Herbert only threw for 121 yards). It seems almost impossible to believe that this team made the playoffs last year, because, at the rate things are going, they might be eliminated from the playoff race before we get to December this year. ” Is this the correct grade for the Chargers?
