title: Chargers-Broncos Game Recap: Jim Harbaugh, Bolts implode in ugly 4Q
summary: The Chargers held a 17-10 lead over the Broncos when they took possession with 12:05 remaining in regulation at their own 32-yard line. Denver kicker Will Lutz just missed a 42-yard field goal. Momentum was running high for the Chargers, but it was also running out fast. Following an electric 42-yard touchdown run by Kimani […]
full_text: The Chargers held a 17-10 lead over the Broncos when they took possession with 12:05 remaining in regulation at their own 32-yard line. Denver kicker Will Lutz just missed a 42-yard field goal. Momentum was running high for the Chargers, but it was also running out fast. Following an electric 42-yard touchdown run by Kimani Vidal to end the third quarter, the Bolts followed it with a three-and-out where they overall went backwards eight yards. Now with the ball once again, they needed points of any king to turn it into a two-possession. At minimum, they at least needed to bleed out some clock. Here’s what happened to the Chargers offense from that 12:05 mark until the end of the game: Chargers go for it on fourth-and-one from their 41-yard line and are stuffed (Broncos score to make it 17-17) Justin Herbert is stripped and the Broncos recover at the Los Angeles 32-yard line (Broncos kick a field goal to take lead 20-17) Herbert is intercepted by defensive back Brandon Jones and returns it seven yards to the Los Angeles 32-yard line (Broncos kick another field goal to make it 23-17) Herbert is sacked at the Denver 46-yard line before he could even get the pass off on the Hail Mary attempt The vibes around the Chargers were immaculate to begin the fourth quarter. They had a touchdown lead on a divisional opponent despite being down to three healthy wide receivers dressed and four rookie offensive linemen starting in front of Herbert. Ladd McConkey was active but did not play. Quentin Johnston and Brenen Thompson were inactive. Tre’ Harris was injured and left in the third quarter. Then, Jim Harbaugh entered the chat. Earlier in the first half, Harbaugh used both of his team’s challenges. He lost both and the Chargers were without any red flags to throw throughout the final 30 minutes. On the third down play before the Chargers turned it over on downs, Herbert looked to have scrambled at or just behind the first down marker. The replay showed Herbert’s elbow down within inches of the mark, but the official on the field pulled his spot back nearly a full yard. Without a challenge in hand, Harbaugh was powerless. The power he had left was deciding if his team should roll the dice and go for it on fourth-and-one. Maybe the statistics said it was a green light and that’s what they went off of, but did the numbers take into account the offensive line? Did Harbaugh forget who was blocking for quarterback? Did he forget who was on the other side of the line from his rookies? None of it mattered. Herbert was stuffed and the beginning of the end came hard and fast. After the turnover on downs, the Chargers overall went backwards five yards while losing a fumble and throwing an interception, both of which came within their own 40-yard line. Three turnovers on three-consecutive drives turned into three short fields and 13-unanswered points for the Broncos that inevitably sunk the Chargers to 0-5 on the season. The Chargers losing this game isn’t what is surprising or what most should take from this game. It’s how fast and violently they lost it. Harbaugh by no means had to go for it on that fourth down. He punts up seven points with a little over 10 minutes on the clock at that point. He could have forced the Broncos to drive the length of the field and let Chris O’Leary’s group — who had been playing very well all game long — keep them at bay with plenty of grass behind them. Again: Rookie offensive linemen, two off-the-street receivers healthy and a return man, and a hobbled Herbert. Harbaugh still felt strong enough to not just go for it, but put it all on his quarterback’s bruised and battered body. This level of game management and situational awareness is not what the Chargers signed up for when they made Harbaugh one of the highest-paid coaches in the entire NFL. They did not sign up for a head coach that gets defensive when the media pushes on the team’s shortcomings. After all, if a head coach can’t handle some semi-pointed questions behind the podium, how is he going to handle the onslaught of outside noise now that will come as his team slowly headed towards a potential winless record through the first half of the season? The Chargers are 0-5 for the first time since the 2003. If they lose to the undefeated Chiefs on the road in Week Six, they’ll be 0-6 for the first time since 2000 when they finished 1-15. Harbaugh and this entire franchise can only expect the noise to grow exponentially with each new loss and low-point. If things are this bad after just five weeks, where in the world will this team be after the next 13 weeks? Who could possibly know. Continue on below to read the entire recap of Sunday’s loss to the Broncos. First Quarter The Chargers won the coin toss and chose to defer. Denver’s offense was up first and managed a decent drive with a pair of first downs before the Chargers defense clamped down just after passing midfield to force a punt. Justin Herbert and the Bolts offense came out with two consecutive runs by Omarion Hampton, but behind a line that featured four rookies, he gained zero yards. On third down, Herbert found tight end Charlie Kolar for what looked like a big gain and a first down, but Kolar was stripped and the Broncos recovered inside Chargers territory. It took the Broncos just four plays to find the end zone behind a two-yard run by J.K. Dobbins who waltzed into the end zone untouched on the play. On the Chargers’ second drive of the game, the offense moved the chains for the first time behind some tough running by Hampton and Kimani Vidal. On third-and-two, Herbert broke from the pocket and looked as if he was going to scramble for the first down. Before crossing the line of scrimmage, however, Herbert launched a pass deep downfield to tight end Oronde Gadsden II. The Broncos defender obviously held Gadsden enough to warrant a DPI penalty, but the officials chose not to throw a flag and the Chargers punted. The Chargers defense continued their high-energy start to the game, capitalizing on a Broncos penalty deep in their own territory to force them to punt out of their own end zone after a three-and-out. After a 10-yard catch by Kolar to begin the next drive, the offense went three more plays, including a sack of Herbert for eight yards to end the quarter. Second Quarter After forcing another three-and-out early in the quarter, the Chargers offense finally got on the scoreboard with a 10-play, 33-yard drive that ended in a 42-yard field goal from Cameron Dicker. The Broncos responded with their own drive ending in a field goal, going 60 yards in 14 plays to bring their lead back to seven. Facing a 10-3 deficit, the Chargers could have used some points at the end of the half before they receive the second half kickoff after halftime. Unfortunately that culminated in a three-and-out where the Chargers gained zero yards. With a little under 90 seconds remaining in the half, the Broncos looked to get into field goal range quick. On the first play of the drive, the Chargers were called for defensive pass interference (Deane Leonard) and the Broncos were moved forward 37 yards to the LAC 43-yard line. Luckily that early momentum disappeared after an offensive holding flag was thrown on wideout Courtland Sutton. Nix was sacked for a loss of five yards by Akheem Mesidor on second down and their third-down attempt was well short of field goal range. Denver let the half tick out and both teams headed to the locker room with the Broncos up by seven. Third Quarter Herbert and the offense came out of the locker room with renewed vigor. Facing third-and-16 following a holding call on guard Cole Strange, Herbert found wideout Theo Wease — who was elevated from the practice squad this week — for 16 yards and a first down. Another penalty on the drive — this one a holding call on offensive tackle Daniel Brunskill — put the Chargers back behind the chains once again, but a 10-yard scramble from Herbert and an eight-yard grab by…

title: Rams could have a punt return upgrade on the roster already
summary: The Los Angeles Rams continue to have the league’s worst special teams units, an ongoing problem for Sean McVay that dates back years, and one of the glaring issues this season is at punt returner. The Rams waived punt returner Xavier Smith before Week 4 and pivoted to Alex Bachman, but in his first game […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams continue to have the league’s worst special teams units, an ongoing problem for Sean McVay that dates back years, and one of the glaring issues this season is at punt returner. The Rams waived punt returner Xavier Smith before Week 4 and pivoted to Alex Bachman, but in his first game he had four opportunities and gained just 30 yards. Sn even better option would be running back Dean Connors. Signed to the 53-man roster two weeks ago, Connors should immediately take over for Bachman as the punt returner . And they should do so before Monday night’s game against the Buffalo Bills because the Rams special teams currently ranks 32nd in the NFL in Special Teams DVOA (-14.5%). One bad punt and it’s over https://t.co/u3Q0mS0Gf9 — Dean Connors (@deanconn0rs) August 1, 2022 The Case for Dean Connors Connors could provide a more dynamic option for a Rams team looking to create explosive plays and improve its field-position battle. Punt returning is about much more than simply catching the football and avoiding a turnover. The position requires sound decision-making, reliable hands, quick acceleration, vision, and the ability to turn an ordinary return into a game-changing play. In fact, I think the most important part of a returner’s game is the ability to read blocks, make cuts, and ball security. Connors background as a running back offers that skill and better fits what the Rams need from the position. We all saw his ability to read blocks and make cuts in the preseason. Why not place him back there to field punts? Connors ball security has makes sense considering the Rams have been knocked out of the playoffs (2017 & 2025) because of punt fielding issues. Xavier Smith fumbled the punt, Sean McVay doesn’t like it. Special teams 🤦‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/sKZMAbrNXG — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) January 26, 2026 The Case Against Alex Bachman The biggest question to ask here is: Does Bachman possess the ability to change the game with the football in his hands? I think the answer is pretty straightforward: “No.” There is a reason that Bachman has played for 4 separate teams since 2019: New York Giants, Houston Texans, Las Vegas Raiders, and the Los Angeles Rams. His career average for punt returns is 6.3 yards/return. Nothing to write home about. Bachman is also in the middle of his age 30 season. The burst and twitch is far less than a guy like Dean Connors (23). No offense, but Bachman is just not the guy. So, who do you want fielding the Rams punts? Keep with Alex Bachman? Use Dean Connors? Or it is someone else, like an elevation for Brennan Presley? It’s not like it can get any worse than what the Rams have experienced the last 3 years. Connors would be the best choice in Week 5.

title: The 49ers, not the Rams have started 2026 the hottest
summary: The NFL season is a long one for players and coaches, but it usually goes fast for the fans, and so much can change quicky, but almost 5-weeks into the 2026 season the San Francisco 49ers look like the strongest team in the NFC. Not the Los Angeles Rams. When the Rams kept Matthew Stafford, […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 11: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates after defeating the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on October 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL season is a long one for players and coaches, but it usually goes fast for the fans, and so much can change quicky, but almost 5-weeks into the 2026 season the San Francisco 49ers look like the strongest team in the NFC. Not the Los Angeles Rams. When the Rams kept Matthew Stafford, added Trent McDuffie, Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald and more, the question was: Who can beat the Rams? The 49ers answered that question in Week 1. The Denver Broncos answered that in Week 3. The Philadelphia Eagles almost beat the Rams in Week 4, and in Week 5 the Rams take on Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills. Injuries As Week 5 wraps up, more and more teams are stacking injuries. The woundings are all over the league. The 49ers know all about it as each week they lose more and more players, but they are still 5-0. It’s remarkable. For the Rams, they are hoping their early season woundings are just that, early season woundings. All this to say, the Rams can get hot later in the year and snatch some of SF’s shine, but as it stands the 49ers look like the best team in the NFC. Literally about a month ago it was supposed to be the Rams. Never a dull year in the NFL. 49ers report card from win over Seahawks: A+ for entertainment in latest entry of division rivalry (mercurynews) “A day after announcing the birth of his son, Christian McCaffrey fathered the 49ers’ game-winning drive that started with runs for 8 and 13 yards, then a 3-yard catch. Kaelon Black then cut up the middle for an 11-yard run, and after a 4-yard McCaffrey catch and 5-yard Black run, the 49ers were in position for a winning field goal. They had just 94 yards as a team, but McCaffrey had 68 yards on 11 carries, including his fifth touchdown run this season.” 49ers Grades After 32-29 Win Over Seahawks: Mike Evans Dominates Seattle (si.com) “Brock Purdy was clutch against an elite defense, and he gets credit for that. When the game was tight in the fourth quarter, Purdy played his best because he threw repeatedly to Mike Evans, his only good wide receiver. That was smart. Earlier in the game, Purdy got intercepted because he forced a pass to his worst wide receiver, Jacob Cowing. That was not smart. Overall, Purdy did the best he could with a depleted supporting cast, and eventually found the Seahawks’ weakest link — cornerback Josh Jobe. As opposed to Sam Darnold, who essentially lost the game for the Seahawks with his two turnovers. Purdy didn’t have to win this game — he just had to let the Seahawks lose it, and they did.“ Mike Evans stars in 49ers’ win: ‘Exactly why he’s here’ (espn) “SEATTLE — After 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans introduced himself to the team’s rivalry with the Seahawks on Sunday, the superlatives from his teammates and coaches flowed as freely as the coffee that pumps through Seattle. Linebacker Fred Warner called Evans “a walking aura.” Running back Christian McCaffrey said Evans is “everything we want in a receiver.” Wideout Brandin Cooks referred to Evans as a “first-ballot Hall of Famer.” Center Jake Brendel kept it simple, noting Evans is an “official grown man.” Rams need Byron Young to lead the charge once again against the Bills (ramblnfan) “Without Garrett, with sophomore edge rusher Josaiah Stewart managing a recent groin injury, and with Aaron Donald in and out of the lineup as he navigates his NFL return, Young is the Rams’ best bet to singlehandedly wreck plays and generate pressure up front. Rams will rely on Young to lead the pass rush once again vs. Bills The defense will need to create such chaos against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills. Young’s speed off the edge could prove crucial to keeping Allen contained or at least forcing him to scramble in the opposite direction, allowing the Rams time to shift the defense accordingly.“ Bills-Rams anytime touchdown scorer predictions for Monday Night Football (usatoday) “The Los Angeles Rams have been almost as good defensively as we expected coming into the season — even with Myles Garrett on injured reserve and Aaron Donald in and out the lineup. They rank second in the NFL in fewest yards allowed, they’re top-10 in points allowed and they haven’t allowed a touchdown to a running back all season. And yet, those things mean nothing when Josh Allen rolls into town Monday night. We can expect Matthew Stafford and the Rams to put up points on a weak Buffalo Bills defense in this Week 5 matchup. But don’t be surprised if the Bills respond and turn this game into a shootout between the last two MVPs. Below are my favorite anytime touchdown scorer bets for the game.“ Why losing Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett might have made the Rams’ defense even stronger (nypost) “Kobie Turner played 48 defensive snaps, nearly 80% of the total. Braden Fiske logged 44, his heaviest workload since the middle of last season, and generated seven pressures. Poona Ford and Tyler Davis combined for 48 snaps, while Larrell Murchison and Ty Hamilton contributed another 23. Even undrafted rookie Wesley Bailey got 29 snaps, with Desjuan Johnson adding seven more. Those aren’t meaningless numbers buried deep in the stat book. They’re investments in a defense that might need every one of those players when the stakes become considerably higher later in the year. “I think it’s key and critical to continue to build camaraderie and continue to understand who we are rushing with and playing beside,” Turner said. “That’s what those games do for us.” Turner is right. Defensive line chemistry isn’t something coaches can manufacture with a whiteboard and a motivational speech. Camaraderie and cohesion is forged through hundreds of collisions, knowing when your teammate is going to twist inside, recognizing when he’s lost contain and instinctively covering the gap before an opposing quarterback exploits it.“ Is Myles Garrett playing for Rams tonight on MNF vs. Bills? (sports.yahoo) “Garrett is not expected to be available when the Rams take on quarterback Josh Allen and the Bills , according to McVay: “It’s week to week in terms of how he feels, but I would say it’s more likely that we do not start his clock next week.” Garrett last played against the Bills on Dec. 21 of last season while he was still a member of the Cleveland Browns . Garrett was credited with a tackle and 0.5 sacks.“ 2026 NFL season, Week 5: What We Learned from Sunday’s games (nfl.com) “ London Jacksonville Jaguars 19, Philadelphia Eagles 17 Early Window Cincinnati Bengals 31, Miami Dolphins 24 New England Patriots 45, Las Vegas Raiders 17 Minnesota Vikings 23, New Orleans Saints 13 New York Jets 17, Cleveland Browns 12 Pittsburgh Steelers 34, Indianapolis Colts 22 Houston Texans 26, Tennessee Titans 3 New York Giant 27, Washington Commanders 27 (OT) Green Bay Packers 31, Chicago Bears 7 Late Window Denver Broncos 23, Los Angeles Chargers 17 Detroit Lions 45, Arizona Cardinals 21 San Francisco 49ers 32, Seattle Seahawks 29 Sunday Night Baltimore Ravens 30, Atlanta Falcons 23 (OT) “ Bills vs. Rams prediction, odds, time: ‘Monday Night Football’ picks from proven model (cbssports) “After 10,000 simulations of Bills vs. Rams, the model is going Under 54.5 points at betting apps . The Under has hit in each of Los Angeles’ last two games as the home team. The Under is also 1-0 in Rams’ games when the line is over 48 points. Los Angeles’ defense is second in he league, allowing 247.5 yards per game. The Rams have also allowed the ninth-fewest points on the season at 20.8. Quarterback Josh Allen leads the Buffalo offense. In four games, he has completed 66.4% of his passes for 1,039 yards and six touchdowns with three interceptions. Los Angeles quarterback Matthew Stafford has been up and down. title: Rams can catch Seahawks with Monday night win over Bills
summary: Sunday afternoon brought a major development in the NFC West divisional standings because the San Francisco 49ers beat the Seattle Seahawks 32-29. This gives the Los Angeles Rams a chance to catch the Seahawks and be tied for second place in the division, if they can beat the Buffalo Bills on Monday night. The Rams […]
full_text: Sunday afternoon brought a major development in the NFC West divisional standings because the San Francisco 49ers beat the Seattle Seahawks 32-29. This gives the Los Angeles Rams a chance to catch the Seahawks and be tied for second place in the division, if they can beat the Buffalo Bills on Monday night. The Rams would then be 3-2 and keep pace with the undefeated 49ers. 1st – San Francisco 49ers: 5-0 2nd – Seattle Seahawks: 3-2 3rd – Los Angeles Rams: 2-2 4th – Arizona Cardinals: 1-4 The 49ers have now taken down both the Rams and Seahawks, and as noted this outcome makes L.A.’s need to beat Buffalo even more critical. As Kenneth Arthur wrote last week, if the Rams lose, they will now be 3 games plus a tiebreaker behind San Francisco in the standings . Yes, there is a lot of season left, but Sean McVay’s team would need to be near perfect or actually perfect for the rest of the season to catch the Niners. LA won’t see San Francisco again until Week 14 in mid-December. A lot can happen between now and then. Somehow the 49ers look unbeatable despite their roster being littered with injuries. The Rams also have a long while until they see Seattle. These two teams will clash in two of the final three weeks of the regular season: first on Christmas day and then in the Week 18 season finale. But it’s at least comforting that—for as much as gone wrong for the Rams—they have a chance to climb into second as soon as Week 5. Beating the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football would mean second place despite all of the following obstacles in their way: Only 1 game with Myles Garrett where he was evidently injured Aaron Donald not providing an overwhelming impact The offense performing closer to average than top of the league Missing Jaylen Watson for at least 1.5 games Missing Puka Nacua for two weeks and Terrance Ferguson for longer Things seemed bleak when the Rams fell to 1-2. Defeating the Bills would put a renewed wind into their sails. And whatever happens against the Bills, Los Angeles is probably primed for a run anyways : Week 6 vs Arizona Cardinals Week 7 at Las Vegas Raiders Week 8 vs Los Angeles Chargers Week 9 at Washington Commanders Week 10 at Arizona Cardinals Week 11 – BYE Week 12 vs Green Bay Packers It’s not how you start. Finishing is much more important. While the home stretch of the Rams’ schedule will almost certainly be difficult, LA has a path in front of them to find out who they want to be this season. Is this truly a “super team”? The early indications suggest not. They can still be a force to be reckoned with, and they must prove how dangerous they are over the next 6-8 weeks. At least for Week 5, the Rams have a golden opportunity to pull even with the Seahawks. That didn’t feel possible just a few weeks ago.

title: Ramalytics: Don’t blitz Josh Allen
summary: The Los Angeles Rams don’t blitz that often. Currently they send extra rushers on 30.7% of their plays. That ranks as the 21st most frequent across the NFL. But LA’s defensive has grown more aggressive in recent weeks, partly because of the absences of Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald: Week 1 vs San Francisco 49ers: […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - OCTOBER 4: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills stands on the sideline during the national anthem prior to the NFL game against the New England Patriots at Highmark Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams don’t blitz that often. Currently they send extra rushers on 30.7% of their plays. That ranks as the 21st most frequent across the NFL. But LA’s defensive has grown more aggressive in recent weeks, partly because of the absences of Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald: Week 1 vs San Francisco 49ers: 11.1% Week 2 vs New York Giants: 35.3% Week 3 at Denver Broncos: 31.4% Week 4 at Philadelphia Eagles: 46.9% The Rams have been rewarded as they’ve ratcheted up the aggressiveness. They absolutely stifled Jalen Hurts and the Eagles offenses after pretty much bottling up the Broncos and Bo Nix until the very end of Week 3. LA is learning that—with their revamped back-end coverage players—they can rattle opposing quarterbacks by sending the blitz. They are better for it. But that could also walk the Rams into a trap of their own making. LA will host Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in Week 5. Allen has been deadly against the blitz and is punishing defenses for sending extra rushers. Blitz Josh Allen at your own peril. Allen when not blitzed: 54/84 (64.3%) for 722 yards, 5 TD’s, 3 INT’s, 96.43 passer rating Allen when blitzed: 25/35 (71.4%) for 317 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT’s, 108.87 passer rating Allen ranks 18th in passer rating and 20th in completion percentage when he isn’t blitzed. Those rankings escalate to seventh and ninth, respectively, against the blitz. Defenses know Allen is capable against extra rushers and play it safe. He faces a blitz at a rate less than 30%, which we know based on the Rams’ own frequency that this would place the opposing defense in the bottom third of the league. We know Allen is one of the most unique and complicated quarterbacks to face. He will beat you with his legs. He will complete passes other quarterbacks simply don’t have at their disposal. But if you sit back and remain patient, Allen will give you opportunities to create takeaways . He puts the ball in harm’s way at the sixth-highest rate among all signal callers. The Rams defense must take advantage. Ill-advised passes cannot fall harmlessly to the turf. Beating Josh Allen is no small task. While the Rams have fared well with a more aggressive approach in recent weeks, they will need to be more patient on Monday night at SoFi Stadium.

title: Marvin Harrison Jr. traded; Rams won’t face WR next week
summary: The Arizona Cardinals traded Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans, so the receiver is not playing in Week 5, and he definitely will not be playing against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 6. For about 24 hours it was a mystery where MHJ was heading, but Houston head coach DeMeco Ryans revealed on […]
full_text: The Arizona Cardinals traded Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans, so the receiver is not playing in Week 5, and he definitely will not be playing against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 6. For about 24 hours it was a mystery where MHJ was heading, but Houston head coach DeMeco Ryans revealed on Sunday that the Texans will be acquiring the young wide receiver. #Texans HC DeMeco Ryans said they are trading for #Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison Jr. https://t.co/mvJbMi4Txm— Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) October 11, 2026 The Rams obviously need to worry about Week 5 against the Buffalo Bills first, but come Week 6 they’ll presumably have one less weapon to prepare for with Harrison Jr. off Arizona’s roster. Harrison’s departure could be good for the Rams given that MHJ had his best game in the NFL during his rookie season against L.A. when he put up 130 receiving yards and two touchdowns. But he hasn’t quite lived up to the hype for the Cardinals since being taken fourth overall in the 2024 NFL Draft. The Texans are offering Harrison Jr. a change in scenery as he reunites with his former college quarterback C.J. Stroud. He wasn’t being featured for the Cardinals in 2026, and his 5 catches for 85 yards with one score reflected that. Perhaps he’ll do damage in Houston and live up to his projected potential. Harrison has plenty of talent, but he hasn’t dominated at the NFL level with less than 2,000 yards in his roughly two and a quarter seasons in Arizona. It’s a newsworthy trade, and it will continue to be interesting to see what other trades go down on and before the November 10th trade deadline. The Rams may not be able to swing anymore big trades in 2026, but that shouldn’t stop fans from speculating. However, speculating about the Rams making the rare in-division trade for Harrison is now off the table.

title: Struggling Bills CB looks forward to Rams: ‘I love it’

full_text: Maxwell Hairston was the Bills’ first-round pick in 2025, but he’s coming off of his worst game of the season after allowing two touchdowns in a loss to the Patriots. However, that hasn’t stopped Hairston from saying that he’s excited to face the Rams on Monday, where he could be matched up against receivers like Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. “I love it,” Hairston said this past week on the opportunity to face Matthew Stafford’s Rams . “I think it would be a great time for me to go against those guys as I’m trying to get myself together, this defense get together. Max Hairston (1) what kind of effort is this? #BillsMafia pic.twitter.com/dtdSQThCzq — Buffalo Sports Talk (@BUFSportsTalk) October 4, 2026 Drake Maye targeted Hairston eight times in Week 4, completing four passes for 44 yards and two touchdowns. Hairston is allowing a passer rating against of at least 100.6 on 20 pass attempts, per ProFootballReference. Although some sites have it as even worse than that. In fact, all the Bills corners are struggling on defense. #Bills CBs passer rating allowed when targeted this season: 🔻Christian Benford: 124.4 🔻Davison Igbinosun: 115.2 🔻Maxwell Hairston: 114.2 🔻Dee Alford: 100.8 YIKES 😳😬 #BillsMafia — Kevin Siracuse (@kevin_siracuse) October 5, 2026 Hairston’s disappointg career after being the 30th overall pick out of Kentucky in 2025 has drawn the ire of Buffalo fans and media alike over the past year. After his poor game against the Patriots, Hairston also “stormed out of the locker room” and avoided facing the media, an act that he later apologized for . Max Hairston just stormed out of the locker room and declined an interview postgame. — Matt Parrino (@MattParrino) October 4, 2026 Bills head coach Joe Brady insisted that the team hasn’t lost confidence in Hairston, even against the reigning MVP with Nacua and Adams. “He’s going to be out there this Monday, and he’s going to make a play,” Brady added. “That’s the confidence that we have in him, and I need him to have that confidence in himself. Jim Leonhard on Maxwell Hairston denying media after Patriots loss: “I think he’s an emotional player that the emotions are getting the best of him right now.. He’s got a ton of pride.. It’s our job to get emotions out of the way.. Extremely talented.. Wants it so bad.” pic.twitter.com/opubFJYVHy — alex brasky (@alexbrasky) October 5, 2026 If Hairston isn’t the main problem, then he at least represents (for fans) bad drafting, bad coaching, and bad effort by some of Buffalo’s defensive players. The first still shows exactly where Maxwell Hairston & Hunter Henry were positioned on the field at the point of Henry's catch. He could've closed. pic.twitter.com/d8gmEWi6ki — Renaissance Man (@Billsfandiehard) October 4, 2026 So Hairston may be looking forward to facing the Rams. title: The Rams should call up Brennan Presley to return punts
summary: What if the Los Angeles Rams had a player with a long history of both punt and kickoff returns, that at the risk of being over dramatic, is just languishing on the practice squad? Brennan Presley is on the Rams’ practice squad and he could be the answer to rekindle some explosivity to their return […]
full_text: What if the Los Angeles Rams had a player with a long history of both punt and kickoff returns, that at the risk of being over dramatic, is just languishing on the practice squad? Brennan Presley is on the Rams’ practice squad and he could be the answer to rekindle some explosivity to their return game if they call him up. It is only Week 5 and the L.A. special teams unit is already in disarray. It’s not a new topic, it feels like a year-to-year discussion since Sean McVay parted ways with John Fassell after the 2019 season. Fans have been weighing in on the current regime since early spring and TST has had plenty to say about it. The Rams coverage units are 30th in punt return average allowed (14.4) and 22nd in kickoffs (27.0). Return units rank 18th for punts (9.0) and 31st in kickoffs (21.9). While the Rams have made a concerted effort to shore up leaky coverage with outside players, they don’t appear to have done the same due diligence in the return game. Brennan Presley will go down as an Oklahoma State legend. In his time in Stillwater @bprezzle proved he could do it all and showed he had the heart of a warrior. He leaves Stillwater as the all time receptions leader and amassed 315 rec 3,315 yards 23 Tds 30 rushes 160 yards 6… pic.twitter.com/CEAq2xam3i — Dustin J (@405pokefan) December 11, 2024 Signed by the Rams in 2025, out of the undrafted ranks. 24 years old and diminutive in stature, 5’ 8” 175 lb. Left Oklahoma State at or towards the top of their all-time receiving, all-purpose and return lists Since he didn’t get into a regular season game in 2025, to grade and project Presley, fans have to go by his work and numbers from college days at Oklahoma State. He started in 44 of 63 games played and left as OSU’s all-time leader in pass receptions and towards the top in all receiving categories, chalking up 315 catches for 3315 yards and 23 scores. To compliment those receiving yards, he averaged over 1000 yards per season in all-purpose production, chipping in 160 yards rushing, 1427 in kickoff return yardage, and 240 yards on punt returns. Presley posted strong athletic testing numbers at the Big 12 Pro Day. To go along with very good long speed (4.46) he showed plus burst, balance, flexibility, change of direction (6.71 shuttle) and short-area agility (4.07 3cone) to go along with very good long speed. His ability to run with the ball stands out. A jitterbug style with slippery-fast change of direction and makes his cuts at speed. If given sliver of space, he seems to always beat the first tackler, played running back in high school and runs with willing physicality for a small player. Presley is not what I would grade as a “can’t miss” returner, but does bring the right skillset and background. His darting open-field style hasn’t been seen a pro game, but he’s looked solid in preseason work. Because of his ability with ball in his hands, he does double duty as a receiver and his traits carry over to both. Oklahoma State flooded him with a lot of short/mid range routes to utilize that advantage. He was predominantly a slot receiver, but also saw reps outside, in bunch sets, and in motion. He came to L.A. needing to expand his route tree, but showed off good hands, ball tracking, and body control to reel in imperfect passes. Like most small receivers, he’ll need to adjust physical press coverage and could have issues at the catch point against bigger, longer secondary players. He does have a good feel for soft areas in zones and works back to his quarterback when flushed from the pocket. At a very good price, Presley can wear a lot of hats as a versatile special teams piece piece to go along with work on offense. In fact, during his first three college seasons, he not only worked as a returner, but played on coverage units as a gunner as well. He was lauded by coaches for his work ethic, leadership and competitive juices. Ty Simpson to Brennan Presley for the TOUCHDOWN‼️ pic.twitter.com/vzIexlolbg — Ethan Shirazi (@Ethanshirazi24) August 28, 2026 Are the Rams ready/willing to make this decision? Probably not. Just a week ago, we fans found out how much weight should be given to what L.A. special teams coordinator Bubba Ventrone offers on the unit’s progress, or lack thereof.. In a 10/1 Thursday presser, Ventrone gave Xavier Smith, the Rams primary punt returner for three seasons, his public support and 24 hours later, the XMan was jettisoned. While very few fans would disagree with the move, how the Rams handled it does cause some raised eyebrows. Sean McVay wasted no time in naming Alex Bachman as the new returner, deep on both kickoffs and punts. In all fairness, grading Bachman on one game is a tiny sample, but the film of the Eagle game left a lot to be desired. After nine seasons, his only playing in 24 total games, with 27 punt returns (22 last year) and eight kickoff returns doesn’t inspire much confidence. Last Sunday, I offered six candidates for the Rams return game and said this about the Rans decision to install Bachman as of now, the primary kick returner, “…I have to wonder how many would consider this move an upgrade. Although Bachman fielded a fair amount of kicks for the Las Vegas Raiders last year, he does not have a history as a returner., nor is he known as an open-field runner. His production was only mediocre It appears a lateral move, at best.” The Rams need to see what they’ve got with Brennan Presley. The status quo is not making anything better.

full_text: The Rams defense needs to corral Buffalo Bills QB Josh Allen (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images After two weeks on the road, the Los Angeles Rams get back home to SoFi Stadium for an October 12 matchup with the Buffalo Bills. The Monday Night Football kickoff is set for 5:15 p.m. PDT. Back onto even ground at 2-2, L.A. will try to get on the plus side of the ledger against a 3-1 Bills team whose only blemish came in last Sunday’s fourth quarter loss to the New England Patriots. Limiting the Buffalo run game and forcing them into a one-dimensional offense would pay dividends for the Rams. James Cook has pretty much been a one-man band for the Bills rush attack, while he’s not a power back, his vision and one-cut style make him a solid fit into Buffalo’s outside zone-based run game. He’s possesses the open-field moves and speed to gash defenses. Although quarterback Josh Allen hasn’t accrued a lot of yards in 2026, he’s still quite dangerous extending plays by breaking from the pocket or on designed runs. His size and athleticism creates big problems down near the goal line. Already this year, he’s got seven touchdowns on the ground. The Rams lead the all-time series by a 9-6 margin, a limited Rams/Bills history. Although Buffalo was a founding member of the American Football league, there was no inter-league play until the 1970 NFL/AFL merger. Since Sean McVay took charge of the Rams in 2017, the two squads have met three times and Buffalo holds a 2-1 advantage. Here’s how to follow the game! Location: SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Ca. title: Las Vegas Raiders officially on fraud watch after embarrassing loss to New England Patriots
summary: The stage was set for the Las Vegas Raiders heading into their Week 5 matchup against the New England Patriots. The Raiders were one of the biggest surprises in the NFL during the first month of the 2026 season, starting 3-1 with a hard-fought loss to the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs the week prior as […]
full_text: (Photo by Winslow Townson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The stage was set for the Las Vegas Raiders heading into their Week 5 matchup against the New England Patriots. The Raiders were one of the biggest surprises in the NFL during the first month of the 2026 season, starting 3-1 with a hard-fought loss to the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs the week prior as the only blemish on the record, leading to some early playoff hopes. Meanwhile, the Patriots were searching for answers at 2-2 and had several key players out with injuries, including four cornerbacks and star defender Christian Gonzalez. However, to say Las Vegas had a missed opportunity would be an understatement. The team was flat-out embarrassed. Not only did New England win by four scores, but the Pats also outgained the Silver and Black by 230 yards, won the time-of-possession battle by almost nine minutes, and dominated pretty much from the jump. The Patriots’ defense managed to force a three-and-out on the opening possession of the game, and the offense followed that up with a five-play, 79-yard touchdown drive to go up 7-0. Las Vegas did manage to respond with a touchdown, but New England just went right back down the field to retake the lead and never looked back. As a result, the Raiders went from being a postseason hopeful to officially being placed on fraud watch, while the internet isn’t exactly taking it easy on the Silver and Black. title: Raiders-Patriots: 16 things we learned
summary: All of last week, after their first loss of the season, first-year Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak talked about his team having a opportunity to learn from adversity. Now, the Raiders’ locker room will get a chance to learn their first awful performance of the young Kubiak era. The Raiders were throttled 45-17 […]
full_text: (Photo by Winslow Townson/Getty Images) | Getty Images All of last week, after their first loss of the season, first-year Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak talked about his team having a opportunity to learn from adversity. Now, the Raiders’ locker room will get a chance to learn their first awful performance of the young Kubiak era. The Raiders were throttled 45-17 by the New England Patriots on Sunday. They were outclassed in every area, including coaching. After dominating in the first three weeks and competing to the whistle against the undefeated Chiefs last week, the Raiders were completely outclassed Sunday. It was something the Raiders hoped would no longer happen in the Kubiak era. But this was a familiar Raiders’ performance in terms of awful defense, out of sync offense and maddening penalties against a Patriots’ team decimated by injuries. Now, it’s time for Kubiak to overcome this self-inflicted adversity and the schedule is not getting any easier as games against the high-powered Buffalo Bills and the Los Angeles Rams at home loom in the next two weeks as they Raiders try not to let their momentum they built toward playoff contention slip away. Let’s look at the key aspects of this game: Defense gutted: The defense has been a problem for the past three games as they have allowed 102 points combined in that stretch. The Patriots had 536 yards of offense. The Patriots came into the game leading the NFL in turnovers and the Raiders were among the league leaders in taakeaways. but Las Vegas could just get one takeaway and one sack. Patriots’ quarterback Drake Maye was brilliant as he threw for 374 yards and accounted for five touchdowns. The Raiders’ secondary had a brutal day. Next up are Josh Allen and Matthew Stafford. Bowers is offense: At the end of the day, the fact that the Patriots were playing without four cornerbacks, including their stars, didn’t really matter. But Raiders’ star tight end Brock Bowers had a big day. He had eight catches for 110 yards (his second 100-plus yard receiving effort in three games) and a score. He was a weapon on third down. Ground game stinks again: This is becoming a problem. The Raiders have the worst ranked run game in the NFL and they had 38 rushing yards on 18 attempts. Starting running back Ashton Jeanty played despite ankle and foot injuries. He didn’t make an imapct as he had 27 yards on 10 carries. The Raiders’ longest run of the day was five yards. Rookie Mike Washington only had one carry despite Jeanty not being 100 percent. Kubiak is doing a good job, but he needs to figure it out on the ground. Lost in the trenches: The Raiders offensive and defensive lines were beaten pretty routinely Sunday. That’s where the Patriots’ domination started. Raiders’ defensive ends Maxx Crosby and Kwity Paye were credited with just one tackle each. After a strong Week 1, Paye has been quiet with just a total of six assisted tackle in the past four games. Also, the Raiders’ allowed a season-high three sacks. Mendoza debuts: There was some excitement late in this stinker as No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza played down the stretch. It was his NFL debut. Mendoza moved well as he completed six of eight passes for 48 yards in garbage time. It was a valuable experience for a player who will be a starter at some point. So, this lost Sunday proved to be a good time to get Mendoza’s NFL feet wet. No Marvin Harrison trade: The Raiders were rumored to be a potential trade partner for Arizona Cardinals’ wide receiver Marvin Harrison. But Sunday he was sent to the Houston Texans for a package that included a 2027 second-round pick. While Harrison is out, the Raiders could still look for help at the position. They are injured at the spot and their receivers combined for eight catches Sunday. Penalties a problem: The Raiders had just 120 penalty yards in the first four games. However, the flag was not their friend Sunday as the Raiders had eight penalties for 101 yards. The refs were busy. The Patriots were flagged 12 times for 116 yards. So, the officials were not the reason why the Raiders lost this game Big miss: After the Raiders recovered a fumble in New England territory, Matt Gay attempted a49-yard field goal, but missed it. The keep the score 14-7 late in the second quarter. It was Gay’s first miss after he made his first 10 field-goal attempts. Big hit for Patriots: The Patriots lost standout offensive lineman Will Campbell and running back Treveyon Henderson in the first half. The Patriots came into the game battered. Porter replaces Masses: Rookie Zeke Masses replaced second-year player Darien Porter as a starting quarterback earlier this season, but Porter replaced Masses in the second quarter Sunday. Masses played to begin the second half and he committed penalties on the second and third plays of the series. Porter later replaced him. We will see how that plays out moving forward. Porter played just three defensive snaps in Week 4. Linderbaum struggles in this area: New Raider’s star center Tyler Linderbaum has been a terrific free-agent addition. But Sunday hew as called for being offsides on a tush-push play for the second time this season. Kind of a rare call. Tough start for Stokes: Raiders’ cornerback Eric Stokes was called for two pass interference penalties on the Patriots’ first two drives of the game. They scored on both drives. Streaks broken: The Raiders went seven gamed dating back to last season, not allowing any opening drive points. The Patirots scored on their first drive Sunday. Also, the Patriots hadn’t allowed any first-quarter points until the Raiders scored a touchdown Sunday. JPJ starts: As expected, Jackson Powers-Johnson was back in the starting lineup Sunday after he missed last week’s game with a groin injury. He was spelled by second-year player Caleb Rogers, who struggled in pass protection. Thompkins is returner: Wide receiver Devin Thompkins, who was elevated from the practice squad for the game, was a kick returner with Dylan Laube. Dareke Young, who fumbled a kickoff last week, has been replaced, for at least, this week. Inactive again: Second-year defensive tackle JJ Pegues and rookie safety Dalton Johnson were both inactive after they both played for the first time last week. With Pegues out, Former top-of-the-rotation defensive tackle Jonah Laulu was active again.

The Patriots struck first […]
full_text: (Photo by Edward Monigan IV/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are playing at the New England Patriots on Sunday. Here is everything to need to know about the contest: First quarter The Raiders went three and out on the first drive of the game as the Patriots won the coin toss and deferred to the second half. The Patriots struck first with a long touchdown pass from Drake Mayee. But here come the Raiders. Kirk Cousins hit star tight end Brock Bowers with two big-tiem pass plays including a 13-yard touchdowb pass to tie the game at 7-7 with 8:19 to go in the quarter. The Patriots cruised down the field to take a 14-7 lead with 1:30 to go. Then, the Patriots cruised down the field to take a 21-76 lead with 24 seconds to go in the half. They get the ball tp start the third quarter. Second quarter: . The Raiders got a break when they recovered a fumble in New England territory. But Matt Gay missed his first field-goal attempt of the season, keeping the score 14-7 with 1:56 to go before halftime. Third quarter: The Patriots continued to pout on as they easily went down the field n just two minutes to take a 28-7 to open the second half. Matt Gay connected on a 46-yard field goal to make it a 28-10 game with 8:30 to go in the third quarter to end a streak of 21 unanswered points by the home team. The Patriots answered right back with a Drake Maye running score. They are up 35-10 with 3:10 to go. Brutal day. Fourth quarter: The Patriots took a 38-10 lead in the quarter. Final score: Patriots 45, Raiders 17. Now that the game is over, let’s take a look at the key aspects: Team records: The Las Vegas Raiders are 3-2. The New England Patriots are 3-2. What the win/loss means for the Raiders: The Raiders lost for the second straight week after starting the season 3-0. They lost to another AFC team that may complicate their playoff hopes. The Raiders have to get bac on track as this season-defining stretch moves forward. Turning point of the game: After Gay’s missed field, the Patriots scored at the end of the first half and then scored to start the third quarter. Ball game. Injury report: Raiders’ defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway went to the blue medical tent in the first quarter. He left the game with stinger/neck injury. Defensive end Patrick Johnson went to the medical tent in the second quarter with a stinger. Dareke Young was shaken up in the third quarter. What’s next for the Raiders: The Raiders are hosting at the Buffalo Bills next Sunday. Kickoff is at 1:25 p.m. PT. Raiders Week 5: Meet the Patriots

title: The Good, Bad & Ugly from the Miami Dolphins Week 5 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals
summary: The Miami Dolphins welcomed Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, Chase Brown and company to Hard Rock Stadium for a clash in sunny South Florida on Sunday — with Jeff Hafley’s squad looking for their first win on the season. Unfortunately for Miami, as the dust settled, the Dolphins fell to their opponent once again — dropping […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins warms up before a game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins welcomed Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, Chase Brown and company to Hard Rock Stadium for a clash in sunny South Florida on Sunday — with Jeff Hafley’s squad looking for their first win on the season. Unfortunately for Miami, as the dust settled, the Dolphins fell to their opponent once again — dropping their record to a disappointing 0-5 on the season. There were some positives to take away from Sunday’s 31-24 loss, including another encouraging outing from running back Ollie Gordon II. Unfortunately, Miami’s special teams continued to be a problem, and quarterback Malik Willis delivered a performance that made overcoming the team’s other shortcomings nearly impossible. As we do after every game, let’s take a look at the good, the bad, and the ugly from Miami’s week five loss to Cincinnati. GOOD Ollie Gordon II continues to make the most of his opportunity Losing De’Von Achane to a season-ending knee injury was a significant blow to Miami’s offense. Achane was one of the Dolphins’ most explosive playmakers, and replacing that kind of production was never going to be easy. Enter Ollie Gordon II. The second-year running back continued to show that he deserves a significant role in Miami’s offense, finishing Sunday’s contest with 88 rushing yards and a touchdown on 18 carries. Gordon averaged 4.9 yards per attempt and repeatedly gave the Dolphins a reliable option on the ground with his hard running style. Gordon opened the scoring for Miami with a one-yard touchdown run in the first quarter, capping off the team’s opening drive and giving Dolphins fans a reason to believe this offense might finally be finding something to build around. While the Dolphins ultimately came up short, Gordon’s performance was another encouraging sign. He ran with physicality, showed patience by allowing his blocks to develop, and did a good job turning his opportunities into productive gains. Miami needs to find an offensive identity without Achane, and Gordon is making a strong case that the ground game can remain a meaningful part of that identity. Miami’s power-back deserves credit for stepping into a larger role and delivering. Predictably, there are very few bright spots on this winless football team, but Gordon’s continued development is certainly one of them. BAD Miami’s weak special teams unit strikes again While going against Burrow, Chase and and the rest of the Bengals’ offense was always going to be a tough match-up, the Dolphins immediately made things harder for themselves by allowing an 81-yard return on the opening kick. That massive kickoff return set up and easy opening drive for Cincinnati — which ultimately ended in just three plays with a touchdown pass from the opposing quarterback. Miami had barely settled into the game before finding themselves in a hole, and the special teams breakdown immediately put additional pressure on a team that has struggled to play complementary football all season long. A strong special teams unit could be a source of stability for a struggling ball club. Instead, Miami continues to surrender field position and give opponents easy opportunities they should have to work for instead. The problems weren’t limited to the opening kickoff, either. Dolphins’ kicker Riley Patterson also missed an extra point following Kevin Coleman Jr.’s fourth-quarter receiving touchdown. It didn’t matter much in the end since Miami didn’t recover the ensuing onside kick (surprise, surprise), but leaving a point on the field only added to the frustration of the day. The Dolphins have enough problems to address without their special teams unit adding another one to the weekly checklist. UGLY Malik Willis’ three turnovers sink Miami There’s plenty of season left, but Malik Willis’ performances are leaving more to be desired thus far — to put it lightly. His three turnover day on Sunday was the defining story of the Dolphins’ latest defeat. Willis finished with 15 completions on 27 attempts for 136 passing yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions. He also lost a fumble — bringing his Sunday total to three turnovers. His late rushing touchdown provided a little life to his statline, but it couldn’t erase the damage done earlier in the contest. The turnovers were bad enough, but the decision-making and inconsistency surrounding them made matters worse. Miami needs their quarterback to protect the football, make sound decisions, and give the offense a chance to compete. Instead, Willis repeatedly put the Dolphins in difficult situations by going “big-play-hunting” instead of taking what the defense gave him — making an already challenging afternoon even harder. The first half was particularly damaging, as Miami struggled to sustain drives while Cincinnati built a 21-7 lead. The Bengals capitalized on their opportunities, while the Willis-led Dolphins failed to make the plays necessary to keep pace. To be fair, Willis isn’t operating in a perfect situation. His supporting cast is largely inexperienced and they’ve had their own struggles, but a good quarterback lifts his team up when times get tough, and Willis isn’t doing that at the moment. Despite his struggles, the flashes he’s shown, while infrequent, should remind the fanbase that his athleticism can be a mighty weapon — as demonstrated by his 39-yard scramble late in the game. He finished the contest with six carries for 63 rushing yards. However, the turnovers are impossible to ignore. A quarterback can survive an occasional bad throw. He can overcome a stalled drive or a negative play. What he cannot do is consistently hand the opposition extra possessions and expect the rest of the team to compensate. At 0-5, the Dolphins need to determine whether Willis can be a dependable part of their future or whether they need to explore other options. Sunday’s performance did little to inspire confidence, but again, there are plenty of games to go. For the sake of the franchise, let’s hope he turns things around. ___ The Dolphins find themselves sitting at 0-5 heading into a much needed bye week. They have a lot of things to work on in all aspects of the game. Do you think they can come back from their off week with a victory against the New York Jets? Let me know in the comments below or on Twitter at @MBrave13 . Fins up.

(Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins lost to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, marking their fifth straight loss to start the 2026 NFL season and heading into bye week still searching for answers. A young team that had shown growth each week regressed against the Bengals and could not keep up for most of the game. The Dolphins found a spark late in the game and tried to mount a comeback, but the game effectively ended when an onside kick rolled out of bounds. It was not the cleanest, most confidence-producing game Miami has played this season, and they will need to use the bye week to re-focus their efforts for the remaining 10 games on the schedule. The Palm Beach Post’s Joe Schad broke down the Dolphins’ passing attack during the game, with quarterback Malik Willis finishing 15-of-27 for 137 yards, 1 touchdown, and 2 interceptions, for a 51.0 passer rating. Schad broke his analysis into an overall grade, along with specific looks at Willis’s arm strength, accuracy, poise/leadership, decision-making, and mobility. For Willis’s decision making, Schad wrote: Decision-making: C- Malik Willis could have thrown underneath for TE Will Kacmarek but tried to force it down the field and was intercepted when the ball was tipped as he was under pressure in the second quarter. Willis threw late and across his body on a second interception, intended for Kevin Coleman in the second quarter. Willis was nearly intercepted a third time in the end zone, trailing 21-7 in the third quarter. Willis wants to drive the ball down the field but he needs to take easier completions underneath. He needs to lean on his checkdowns. There are also times where it seems Willis could step up into the pocket to deliver a throw when under edge pressure. title: Malik Willis frustrated with Miami Dolphins’ offensive struggles
summary: The Miami Dolphins fell to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday by a score of 31-24. One of the main reasons why Miami lost the game was the poor performance of their quarterback, Malik Willis, who had three turnovers — two interceptions and a fumble lost — on the day. Following the defeat, Willis met with […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins passes against the Cincinnati Bengals during the second quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins fell to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday by a score of 31-24. One of the main reasons why Miami lost the game was the poor performance of their quarterback, Malik Willis, who had three turnovers — two interceptions and a fumble lost — on the day. Following the defeat, Willis met with the South Florida media and seemed visibly frustrated with how the game played out. When asked by Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN when it was reasonable to expect results from this year’s squad, Willis had this to say: “It is too much and too hard to keep saying, ‘Oh, we’re just young. Oh, we’re trying to build this and build that.‘ At the same time, we gotta hold each other accountable, because we can’t keep doing this to ourselves. If we’re going to be in games against good teams, we gotta be able to take advantage of it and go and win those games. Cause there’s no point to be in the game if you can’t go and win it.” Willis was then asked about a backbreaking sack he took when the offense had a first-and-goal situation from the half yard line. “I felt just dejected for our defense because of how hard they were playing and trying to give us stops and keep going. And I think that we are better than that and that’s what I talk about when we have missed [opportunities] like that, just because we miss an assignment, that’s when it’s frustrating. Because it’s like, okay, we had the opportunity to go and do it. We just didn’t execute. And we didn’t do it… I didn’t throw it away. I took a sack. I wanted to make a play… Unfortunate. Bad play by me.” The Dolphins will have extra time to regroup and prepare for their next opponent, the New York Jets, with a bye week on the schedule. Willis and the rest of Miami’s offense have plenty of work to do if they hope to turn things around, secure their first win of the season, and finally give themselves a reason to breathe a sigh of relief.

title: Bengals vs. Dolphins final score, immediate reactions: Offense cannot get it done
summary: The Miami Dolphins hosted the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 5 and were very accommodating to the visitors. Miami’s offense never got out of its own way, turning the ball over three times and converting on only six of 12 third downs. The defense struggled to contain the Bengals’ offense, but the discussion of the day […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Ollie Gordon II #0 of the Miami Dolphins celebrates a first down against the Cincinnati Bengals during the third quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins hosted the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 5 and were very accommodating to the visitors. Miami’s offense never got out of its own way, turning the ball over three times and converting on only six of 12 third downs. The defense struggled to contain the Bengals’ offense, but the discussion of the day will be on Miami’s offensive failures. From interceptions and fumbles to settling for field goals after a first-and-goal from inside the one-yard line, Miami’s offense never put it together to threaten the Bengals’. The good news for Miami is that their 24 points are a season-high. Final Score Bengals 31 – 24 Dolphins Immediate reactions Snap Winners and Losers Winners Ollie Gordon, running back : Losing De’Von Achane to a season-ending knee injury in Week 3 could have decimated Miami’s offense. Instead, it has allowed second-year running back Ollie Gordon to emerge. Initially seen as the power back to complement Achane and Jaylen Wright, Gordon has established himself as Miami’s back of choice this season. Achane and Gordon as a duo in 2027 could be deadly. Kevin Coleman, wide receiver: A rookie receiver who caught his first touchdown pass made our winners list. He had only two catches for seven yards, but one of them was a touchdown. Bradley Pinion, punter: I have been tough on Pinion this year. He has been inconsistent, with some poor punts. On Sunday, he was (a) good and (b) the definition of consistency. On a day when special teams were rough (more below), Pinion punted twice: once for 59 yards and once for 57. He boomed kicks that changed field position, and he was consistent in doing so. Losers Note: “Losers” is not a judgment on the talent or character of any individual. It is simply a categorization of the play in one game – no disrespect is intended or should be inferred. Malik Willis, quarterback: This was just beyond rough. In a season when the Dolphins are focused on improving every week, Willis is doing absolutely nothing right now. He plays like the game is too fast for him, trying to make the perfect play instead of just making a play. He overlooks an open player to find a bigger option, which leads to bad throws that fall incomplete or get picked off. Until completing four passes in the final drive of the first half, Willis was 1-for-7 for 23 yards and two interceptions, giving him a 0.6 passer rating. That does not seem ideal. The second half was better – not great, but better – and Willis showed some flashes of why the coaching staff and front office believe he might be the quarterback of the future for the team. He finished the game 15-for-27 for 137 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions, giving him a 51.0 passer rating. Jackson Woodard, linebacker: This is the definition of a snap winners/losers analysis. Woodard lands on this list because the two times I noticed him in the game, it was on bad defensive plays. The first, Woodard took off down the field, seeming to think he needed to cover someone, but Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow then scrambled for 11 yards in the giant vacancy Woodard left. Then later, Woodard got lost in coverage and was trailing the play when tight end Erick All caught the ball and picked up 14 yards. He finished the game with four tackles, including one for a loss, and maybe he was a solid part of the defense, but he lands here based on the two times I noticed him. Immediate thoughts Special teams anything but special The Dolphins’ special teams do not deserve to be called special anymore. They will be just teams until something changes. On the opening kickoff, the Bengals returned the ball 81 yards to set up a tight end Mike Gesicki touchdown three plays later. The Dolphins have enough problems on offense and defense as they work through this rebuild, they cannot afford to be allowing opponents giant chunks of yards on a kickoff return to open the game. The second kickoff, following Miami’s first touchdown, resulted in a penalty because the ball did not reach the landing zone inside the 20-yard line. The ball was placed at the 40-yard line for Cincinnati following the kick, but the Dolphins got lucky with an unnecessary roughness penalty on the Bengals, pushing the ball back to the 25. Third-down defense disappears The Dolphins are not a team good enough to allow opponents extra chances with the ball. When they have the opportunity to get the defense off the field and the ball back for the offense, they have to capitalize. They did not do that on Sunday. Miami forced the Bengals into a third down 13 times during the game. The Bengals converted a first down on nine of those plays. That seems decent enough for Miami’s defense, but when you consider the Bengals converted eight of their first 10 third down attempts before worrying more about running out the clock than converting first down, it shows just how off Miami’s third-down defense was on Sunday. Pass rush regresses after breaking out last week Last week, Miami recorded five sacks against the Minnesota Vikings. This week, they struggled just to get anywhere near quarterback Joe Burrow. They were credited with four quarterback hits, two from Chop Robinson, one from Zach Sieler, and one from Jordan Phillips, but other than a Robinson sack that was called back because he was in the neutral zone before the snap, there was nothing that really seemed to have an impact on Burrow’s day. Does Miami have to do something at quarterback? During the game, I posted on X this: There is a non-0 chance that, if I were a decision maker, I would be calling Atlanta to see if they would consider a trade of a backup quarterback who might be familiar with Bobby Slowick's system, has a $1.2 million cap number, and is a FA after the season. Not saying I would… pic.twitter.com/565fGbHUq5 — The Phinsider (@thephinsider) October 11, 2026 I was not seriously thinking Miami should consider a trade to bring quarterback Tua Tagovailoa back to South Florida, but the more Willis struggles, the more it seems Miami has to do something. The goal this year is to get a read on Willis and assess whether he can be the team’s quarterback of the future. Right now, the team might need to decide if he is the quarterback for Week 7 when they come out of the bye week. No, I do not think they need to get Tagovailoa. But they need to do something to spark Willis. The hope is that he can prove to be a quality starter who can handle the position at least through 2027, giving Miami a chance not to use their first pick on a quarterback in the spring. Right now, it looks like Miami might be forced to use their opening pick on a quarterback, despite this not shaping up to be a great quarterback draft class.

Miami’s inactive list started with those four. Along with the injured players, Miami also listed running back Kaytron Allen, guard DJ Campbell, and tackle Chukwuebuka Godrick as inactive. Allen was claimed off waivers this week from the Washington Commanders and likely needs more time to get up to speed on the playbook. The Dolphins elevated running back Carlos Washington from the practice squad to provide depth behind Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon II.

The fans seem to appreciate those signs of improvement. Heading into Week 5, the Dolphins will face a struggling Cincinnati Bengals team. After a 2-0 start to the year, they have dropped their last two contests to fall to 2-2 and now sit last in the AFC North. Cincinnati will come into this game looking to take advantage of a winless Dolphins team and right the ship. Miami should expect the Bengals to throw everything they have at this game. Can Miami do enough to pull off the Week 5 upset as they head into their bye week in Week 6? According to the oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook , the Bengals are seven-point favorites for today’s game. Dolphins fan confidence A 0-4 start to the season typically tanks the fan trust in a team. For example, the SB Nation Reacts fan confidence survey for the Los Angeles Chargers this week came back with just six percent of their fans trusting in the direction of the team. Beginning the year with four-straight losses is typically time for the fan base to panic. Not when it comes to the Dolphins in 2026. Miami is expected to struggle this year. They tore the team down to the bare bones during the offseason and have started rebuilding, but it will likely take more than one offseason. The positives this year are the experience a team built primarily around rookie and second-year players can gain and the growth they can show. They are doing exactly that, and the fan confidence continues to grow with them. Last week, 79 percent of responses said fans trust the team, just one percent below our season high. This week, we blew past that mark. Miami may be 0-4, but 87 percent of the fans seem to think the team is headed in the right direction. title: Vikings Week 5 Stock Market Report
summary: The Minnesota Vikings extended their win streak to ten games, dating back to last season, with a 23-13 victory over the New Orleans Saints on the road. The Vikings were able to overcome a couple fumbles on offense with elite defense and special teams and an otherwise methodical offense led by Kyler Murray. The game […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 11: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings throws as Carl Granderson #96 of the New Orleans Saints pressures during the first half of a game at Caesars Superdome on October 11, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings extended their win streak to ten games, dating back to last season, with a 23-13 victory over the New Orleans Saints on the road. The Vikings were able to overcome a couple fumbles on offense with elite defense and special teams and an otherwise methodical offense led by Kyler Murray. The game was more lopsided statistically for the Vikings, who held the Saints to their lowest yardage output in five years offensively and dominated time of possession and most other statistics. A Saints fumble recovery for a touchdown kept the game closer in the second half than it was otherwise. The Vikings road win takes them to 5-0 heading into their bye-week with a dominant #1 defense, elite special teams, and an ascending offense that will get Jordan Mason, Christian Darrisaw, Jordan Addison, and T.J. Hockenson back from injury. They also have a two-game lead in the NFC North division race. Stock Up Kyler Murray. He played nearly flawless football, moving the chains with his arm and feet en route to 24/30 (80%) for 229 yards and a TD passing, 109.6 passer rating, plus an additional 51 yards on ten carries on the ground. That combined for an 81.3 QBR, highest of the season for the Vikings. He also had an 86.2% adjusted completion percentage, which is a gauge of accuracy, with no turnover-worthy plays. Byron Murphy Jr. He turned two gifts from Tyler Shough into two interceptions and otherwise allowed just 3 receiving yards in coverage. Isaiah Rodgers. He allowed just one reception for a 5-yard loss and had a pass breakup to deny a third-down conversion. Team Defense. Brian Flores’ unit doesn’t really have any superstars. But they don’t really have any weak links either. The combination of an aggressive scheme that is challenging to play against with players that don’t make many mistakes and are relentless is suffocating for opposing offenses. Jake Golday. He had the forced fumble on special teams and had already been an elite special teamer this season. Risk and Reward Aaron Jones. He had 113 yards on 25 carries (4.5 ypc) and a touchdown, but also a turnover in the redzone that cost the Vikings points. Myles Price. He had some nice returns again and a couple nice receptions, but his fumble was returned for a Saints touchdown. Justin Jefferson. He had a couple incredible catches- including a key touchdown catch- and 79 total receiving yards, but also a turnover-worthy pass that should have been a turnover on an ill-advised trick play that should probably be deleted from the playbook. It was technically a fumble as a backward pass that the Vikings recovered. Stock Down Ryan Van Demark. He had a couple penalties that proved to be drive killers. He also allowed 3 quarterback pressures. Can live with a couple quarterback hurries, but can’t have the penalties. Buy Vikings ability to win with a ball possession offense combined with a dominant defense and elite special teams while missing some key pieces on offense. The Vikings had the top defense and special teams units in the league prior to the Saints game, and the results only widened the gap with the second-best units. Sell Vikings offense continuing to be near the bottom of the league. Kyler Murray is slowly getting more comfortable and confident running the Vikings offense despite missing some key pieces and missing two games himself. And after the Vikings bye-week, they will get Jordan Mason, Jordan Addison, Christian Darrisaw, and T.J. Hockenson back. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford
