title: Eagles vs. Jaguars: The good, the bad, and the ugly
summary: This was a tug of war of football incompetence. What team could do more self-destructive damage? For 59 minutes and 59 seconds on Sunday, the Jacksonville Jaguars had Nick Sirianni and the Eagles pretty well overmatched. Then the tide turned in the form of a last-second runway to victory. This setback will no doubt haunt […]
full_text: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 11: Nate Boerkircher of the Jacksonville Jaguars is tackled by Zack Baun of the Philadelphia Eagles during the 2026 NFL London Games match between Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 11, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) | Getty Images This was a tug of war of football incompetence. What team could do more self-destructive damage? For 59 minutes and 59 seconds on Sunday, the Jacksonville Jaguars had Nick Sirianni and the Eagles pretty well overmatched. Then the tide turned in the form of a last-second runway to victory. This setback will no doubt haunt Eagles’ fans for a while. The Eagles lost to a team whose defensive tackle is about as wide as he is tall serving as the emergency back-up long snapper; to a team that committed 11 penalties for 100 yards, including three calls inside the Eagles’ 10; and to a team that was 0-for-3 in the red zone, including two squandered drives that reached the Eagles’ one-yard line. The Jaguars were supposed to be gargantuan world beaters at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London, England. They looked anything but that, escaping with a last-second, walk-off Cam Little 57-yard field goal for a 19-16 victory. There are no such things in the hardboiled NFL world as moral victories. Flat out and simple, despite playing extremely shorthanded without starters Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, Drew Kendall, Jonathan Greenard and Marcus Epps, the Eagles should have won. The Eagles have now dropped to 2-3, and are on a three-game losing streak for the second time in two years. They are in free fall with nothing to grab on the way down. It marks the first time in five years that the Eagles have slid below .500 since they were 6-7 in Sirianni’s first season as head coach in 2021—a 9-8 season that is looking good from this current view. Little knew exactly where to run after nailing the game-winner, right towards the mix of Kelly and midnight green section of the end zone, raising his arms, and then being raised by his teammates in victory. This loss was reminiscent of the infamous 21-20 Eagles’ Monday night loss in Dallas on September 15, 1997, with the botched Tommy Hutton hold on an Eagles’ potential 22-yard game-winning field goal —with one second left —during a bleak period for the Eagles franchise that it appears to be entering again. Jacksonville defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton was a key figure in the Jags’ victory, nearly losing the game on a high snap that caused a missed extra point in the fourth quarter, and coming back with a strong snap on the game-winning kick. Jacksonville was lost when Jalen Hurts directed what looked like a game-winning drive to set up Jake Elliott for a 48-yard field goal with 8 seconds left. Then the unbelievable happened when Ameer Abdullah took off through the right side of the Eagles special teams on a 53-yard return, setting up Little’s heroics. It was not Hurts’ fault the Eagles lost this game, although some, as they have a habit of doing, will blame him, despite the fact he completed 21 of 40 for 220 yards and a touchdown. Trevor Lawrence posted highly impressive numbers, completing 24 of 39 passes for 331 yards and two touchdowns, and also threw an interception. Though Lawrence was striking, directing the Jags to 12 points in the second half, nearly half as many as the Eagles have scored in the second half (23 points) this season, the Jags were not. They made a myriad of mistakes, especially in the red zone, and if not for Abdullah’s kickoff return and Parker Washington’s brilliance, they should have lost to an Eagles’ team that fielded a preseason roster. Sirianni will no doubt try to come up with answers to fix this sinking mess of a season, though none seem available. But he does not deserve the blame here. That actually may fall on general manager Howie Roseman for not providing as deep of a roster as he has done in the past. That was transparent by the way the Eagles depth players performed during preseason. Coming up next are Carolina, Dallas and Washington, which are all currently better than the Eagles are. Yes, 9-8 is looking good right now. There was a lot of good for 59 minutes, and 59 seconds, some bad and a tall hill of ugly in the Eagles’ 19-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Good The defense. For the first time this season, they put pressure on the quarterback. They held Jacksonville to six three-and-outs, while the Jags entered the game with four three-and-outs all season. Kicker Jake Elliott coming through again, hitting the 48-yard field goal with 8 seconds left. Elliott sometimes seems overlooked and forgotten, but he’s made plenty of clutch kicks in his Eagles’ career—and he is a two-time Super Bowl-winning kicker. Not many present NFL kickers faced the crucial situations in big games as Elliott has. This would have been up there among his most prominent, if not for the Abdullah kick return breakdown (which Elliott was a small part of). Backup linebacker A.J. Epenesa , playing in place of the injured Jalyx Hunt, stepping up and making a big play, deflecting a Trevor Lawrence pass on a third-and-five at the Eagles’ 27 with 3:30 to play, forcing a crucial fourth down. Unfortunately, Jacksonville’s Parker Washington made an incredible over-the-shoulder catch by cradling in his lap a 27-yard touchdown pass, where Riq Woolen had great coverage with 2:07 to play. The Eagles’ second goal line stand with 6:35 left to play, which had a lot more to do with Jacksonville’s utter ineptitude than it had to do with the Eagles’ defense. Jacksonville went from a first-and-goal at the Eagles’ one, to having three penalties called, two were delay calls, which irked Lawrence causing him to spike the ball, and one false start call. The Jags went backwards from first-and-goal at the one, to a third-and-goal at the Eagles’ 14. The whole thing came to an end when Lawrence threw an incompletion out of the back of the end zone. Cornerback Quinyon Mitchell’s first career regular-season interception at the Eagles’ 26 with 2:15 left in the third quarter. It was the third takeaway this season for the Eagles and came after the Eagles lost the ball on downs, leaving Jacksonville in good field position. The second quarter. The undermanned Eagles turned around a bad start with probably their strongest second quarter of the season. The Eagles converted two of three first downs, and scored twice—the first two times anyone scored on Jacksonville in the first half all season. Hurts completed 11 of 16 passes in the first half for 122 yards and a touchdown. The offensive line gave him time, and opened holes. Hurts was only pressured twice on 17 drop backs. Jalen Carter was a one-man wrecking crew causing havoc up front and making the Jags move and adjust to everything he did, creating opportunities for everyone else. The Eagles went into halftime holding a 14-7 lead against one of the better teams in the NFL that was projected to stomp into pulp. The Eagles’ goal line stand at the end of the first half, punctuated by Zack Baun taking down Bhaysul Tuten for a six-yard loss, reading the outside sweep perfectly on the final play of the first half. All he does is score touchdowns. Hurts’ 62-yard touchdown reception—on third down—to Darius Cooper for a 14-7 lead with 5:31 left in the first half. It was Cooper’s sixth catch of the season, four of which were touchdowns. It was really uplifting to see the Eagles’ offense working on third down. Jacksonville had not given up a first half touchdown this season and the Eagles score twice against the Jags in the second quarter alone. The Eagles’ third possession. It resulted in the Eagles’ first score. Hurts converted two third downs, one a third-and-eight at the Jags’ 37 on a 10-yard pass to Dontayvion Wicks, followed by and a third-and-10 at the Jags’ 27, again a reception to Wicks, for 18 yards to the Jacksonville 9. The play led to a Will Shipley two-yard…

full_text: (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL is filled with underrated and underappreciated stars. The Pittsburgh Steelers’ best offensive player in 2026 has been running back Jaylen Warren, who has introduced himself to the outside world with his breakout campaign. Steelers fans knew how dynamic the running back was, but this season Warren has taken his game to another level. With over 100 rushing yards, Warren added 87 as a receiver, including an 80-yard house call on a screen from Aaron Rodgers as the Steelers nailed down a much-needed victory over the Indianapolis Colts. Last season was Warren’s first 1,000-yard rushing season, and the former Oklahoma State Cowboy is well on his way to shattering that with 410 rushing yards on just 70 carries. A 5.9-yard-per-rush average would be another career high, besting his previous high mark of 5.2 in 2023. Warren has completely broken out, and it comes at the best time for the Steelers and their offense. Here is Monday’s Three Rivers Report. full_text: (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson suffered a finger injury in the team’s Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts. According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, he’ll miss multiple games because of it. “Steelers WR Roman Wilson is expected to miss a couple of weeks due to a finger injury suffered Sunday, per source,” Fowler reports . “He’s still gathering info and seeking a second opinion.” Wilson injured his finger on his lone target of the day on Sunday. The ball hit him in the hand while being contested by a defender and fell to the turf. Wilson grabbed his hand and left the game. The Steelers also lost Ben Skowronek during the win with a leg injury. If he is unable to go this week, that would leave Pittsburgh without three of their receivers, as Michael Pittman was placed on IR with a foot injury. It’s almost guaranteed the Steelers will hit the market to bring in at least one other body at receiver ahead of their Week 6 matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers due to the growing list of injuries at the position. At the time of writing, their only healthy receivers are DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard, Kaden Wetjen, and Brandon Smith, who was elevated from the practice squad. title: Aaron Rodgers surpasses Ben Roethlisberger, Peyton Manning in major achievements
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the Indianapolis Colts 34-22 to get to 3-2 on the season and back into a three-way tie for first place in the AFC North. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers had a terrific showing, completing 22-of-31 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns. The win featured multiple milestones for the future Hall of Fame […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the Indianapolis Colts 34-22 to get to 3-2 on the season and back into a three-way tie for first place in the AFC North. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers had a terrific showing, completing 22-of-31 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns. The win featured multiple milestones for the future Hall of Fame signal-caller. Rodgers tied the Steelers franchise record with his third consecutive game of three or more touchdowns, with Terry Bradshaw and Ben Roethlisberger the only other two to ever do it. With those touchdowns, he passed Peyton Manning for most touchdown passes in the regular season and postseason combined. His first touchdown pass on the day to Jaylen Warren gave him 580 for his career, and two touchdowns to Pat Freiermuth gives him 582m which is third all-time. “Anytime you’re in the same sentence as Peyton [Manning], that definitely does mean a lot to me,” Rodgers told Tracy Wolfson after the game. With the win, Rodgers now has 166 as a starter, which breaks a tie with Ben Roethlisberger for fifth all-time. With five more wins, he’ll tie Drew Brees. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Steelers stock report after Week 5 win over Colts
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers bounced back in a big way in Week 5, as they defeated the Indianapolis Colts 34-22 at Acrisure Stadium. It was a complete game from the offense, who scored 34 on a Indianapolis defense that had only allowed an average of 13 points to their opponents over its previous two games. Now […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers bounced back in a big way in Week 5, as they defeated the Indianapolis Colts 34-22 at Acrisure Stadium. It was a complete game from the offense, who scored 34 on a Indianapolis defense that had only allowed an average of 13 points to their opponents over its previous two games. Now that the Steelers are 3-2, let’s take a look at our weekly stock report after their massive win over the Colts. Stock Up RB Jaylen Warren We are all witnesses to the Jaylen Warren breakout. Warren got the scoring going for Pittsburgh today with an 80-yard catch-and-run. It was a bit of a quiet day for Warren on the ground in the first half, that was until he broke free for a 50-yard touchdown scamper midway through the third quarter. It was the third consecutive game that Warren posted at least 100 scrimmage yards. The veteran back is the engine of the Steelers’ offense and will continue to get a feature role all season. QB Aaron Rodgers Over the last three weeks, the Steelers offense has looked significantly better than it did at the start of the season. Their veteran quarterback has undoubtedly been a huge part of their success. Today marked the first time that Rodgers has thrown for 3+ touchdowns in three straight contests since December 2021. Rodgers started this game 11-of-11 before he threw his first incompletion. All of this is a long way to say that Rodgers can still sling it, and the Steelers are reaping the benefits. TE Pat Freiermuth Freiermuth caught five passes today, two of them for touchdowns. At the time of writing, Freiermuth is tied for the league lead in receiving touchdowns by a tight end with four. It is clear the Steelers see the tight ends as a major part of their offense, and with their wide receiver room banged up, we could be witnessing a career year for Freiermuth. WR Germie Bernard Despite dropping a few passes, Bernard had a career day. The rookie second-round pick led the team in receiving yards with 84. It was clear from the get-go that Rodgers wanted to get the ball to Bernard in this game, even before Roman Wilson and Ben Skrownek left with injuries. Bernard has earned himself some serious playing time moving forward after his breakout performance today. Stock Down WR Health The Steelers were already a bit shorthanded heading into this contest, with Michael Pittman Jr. being placed on short-term injured reserve. The hits continued for the Steelers wide receiver room, as Roman Wilson and Ben Skrownek both suffered injuries late in the first half that caused them to miss the rest of the game. Brandon Smith saw more snaps in the second half after the injuries, but if Wilson and Skrownek are out for any period of time, it might be in the Steelers’ best interest to add to the receiver room. WR/KR Kaden Wetjen It’s just hard to see what value Kaden Wetjen has brought to the team at this moment in time. The Steelers kickoff team has been questionable at best all season long, but we have yet to see Wetjen make a single impact return to this point. We should be seeing more from someone who the Steelers used an early day 3 pick to play an immediate role. WR DK Metcalf It was a quiet game overall for Metcalf, who posted just three catches for 23 yards after his controversial quote about Colts star cornerback Sauce Gardner. Luckily for Metcalf, a lot of the pressure on him was alleviated by rookie wide receiver Germier Bernard, who led the team in receiving yards. The tight ends also had a big day for the Steelers. Pittsburgh could certainly use more from Metcalf, but clearly has plenty of options they feel comfortable with when their star receiver is quiet. Let us know what you think in the comments . full_text: (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images As the clouds in Pittsburgh parted, so, too, did the Indianapolis Colts’ defense when Jaylen Warren had the football in his hands. The dynamic running back put up two long touchdowns as the Steelers defeated the Colts 34-22 to get to 3-2 on the season. It wasn’t the most promising start for Pittsburgh’s offense, who punted on its first drive on a 4th-and-24 after three plays that netted -15 yards. The Colts turned their first drive into one of five Spencer Schrader field goals, two of which were north of 55 yards. On the ensuing drive, the Steelers went to pay dirt on the first play, with Warren taking a swing pass 80 yards to the end zone to give the Steelers a lead they would never lose. After another Colts field goal, the Steelers went 80 yards to the end zone again, this time putting together a 12-play drive that ended with a Pat Freiermuth touchdown, his first of two on the day. The Colts would answer with an 11-play drive that ended with a Tyler Warren touchdown run on fourth-and-goal, which Pittsburgh came within a second-effort push of stopping. After a Chris Boswell field goal, the Steelers took a 17-13 lead into the half. The Colts began the second-half scoring with a field goal, and then Jaylen Warren found himself in the end zone on another long score, this time a 50-yard rushing score to give the Steelers a 24-16 lead. A pair of field goals got the Colts to within two, but Aaron Rodgers hit Pat Freiermuth for another touchdown midway through the the fourth quarter to put the Steelers up by nine. A second Boswell field goal pushed the score to 34-22, which is where the game would end in a Pittsburgh win to send the Steelers to 3-2. Warren’s dominance was the biggest story of the day. His 188 yards from scrimmage were the catalyst for Pittsburgh’s offense to put up 30+ points for the second time in three weeks. Aaron Rodgers had a good showing, as well, going 22-of-31 for 235 yards and three touchdowns. It was the third straight game in which Rodgers threw for at least three scores, which ties a Steelers franchise record. On top of Warren and Freiermuth, he was given a lot of help from rookie Germie Bernard, who caught six passes for 80 yards. The Steelers’ defense kept Jonathan Taylor grounded, allowing just 45 yards on 15 carries. The Steelers yielded just 66 yards on the ground for the day, and the Colts scores just one touchdown. Pittsburgh will head south in Week 6 to Tampa Bay to face the Buccaneers, who are coming off an upset win over the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday night. It is likely to be undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels under center for the Bucs, once again. Pittsburgh is now tied for the division lead with the Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals at 3-2, though tiebreakers would still give the edge to Cleveland. title: Seahawks Droppings: Seattle practices self-flagellation, falls farther behind 49ers in NFC West
summary: The 2026 Seattle Seahawks are not a great team. At this point last season, neither were the 2025 Seattle Seahawks. This 32-29 loss to the San Francisco 49ers had a similar feeling to last year’s Week 5 38-35 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Seattle once again lost a game that they should’ve won, besieged […]
full_text: The 2026 Seattle Seahawks are not a great team. At this point last season, neither were the 2025 Seattle Seahawks. This 32-29 loss to the San Francisco 49ers had a similar feeling to last year’s Week 5 38-35 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Seattle once again lost a game that they should’ve won, besieged by turnovers on offense. They had the chance to win it at the end, but couldn’t close the deal. Just like last season, this loss drops the Seahawks to 3-2 with both teams having an early season home loss against the Niners. Seattle went on a huge run after Week 5 last season, going 14-1 over the rest of the year. As much as I would love the Seahawks to do that again, it’s highly unrealistic. Point blank, they have to play better on offense. The score makes it look like the defense got shredded, but anyone who watched it knows that they actually played really well. It was the offensive turnovers that put them in a hole. Three TD drives spanning a total of less than 30 yards will be hard to overcome. Settling for 5 FGs also is usually a recipe for failure. Even one more TD on any of those drives would’ve totally changed the game. You can wish in one hand and take a dump in the other…see which one fills up first. Seahawks Droppings Turnovers are always a factor, and they’re seen by some as lazy analysis . However, it’s a huge factor with the Seahawks under Mike Macdonald. Seattle took excellent care of the ball at the end of the season in 2025 which was a massive reason for their Super Bowl victory. Darnold’s INTs are a problem. The RB fumbles were even more egregious. Honestly, we were spoiled with Kenneth Walker III and Zach Charbonnet. Those two just did not cough the ball up. Both Emmanuel Wilson and George Holani fumbled once. Holani tried to fumble another time as he was running down the sideline and just dropped the ball. Seattle won’t be the team they want until they take care of the damn ball. Brace yourselves for a “Sam Darnold Conversation” if he keeps playing like this. Darnold will want an extension in the offseason. John Schneider has made very tough QB decisions in the past. Brian Fleury was brought in to keep Seattle playing “Seahawks Football” which means running the ball and being efficient in the passing game. Might there be another QB out there (or already on the roster) who could play that way at a fraction of the price? Jason Myers made all of his FGs and extra points, which is nice. The fact that they had to rely on him that much is never a good thing. Seattle’s offense needs to find a way to come out with TDs. Jaxon Smith-Njigba is still the only viable threat for the Seahawks offense, with five catches for 102 yards and 1 TD . Sure, he had an uncharacteristic drop on third down in the final drive. Realistically, Seattle wouldn’t have even been in the game without him. Brian Fleury needs to find a way to get others more involved. Please throw the ball to Tory Horton. Seattle’s defense kept them in the game by forcing two turnovers in the third quarter . I just wish they would’ve been able to stop Mike Evans on that 49ers drive that spanned the end of the third quarter and early fourth quarter. He was the only one doing anything for San Francisco, making ridiculous contested catches. The one thing that the defense is still struggling with is limiting teams to FGs when in the red zone. Byron Murphy was great today with two sacks. Nick Emmanwori played well. Ty Okada made impact plays in his first game back. Ernest Jones was effective. Nehemiah Pritchett was a factor again with a great read on his INT. Seattle’s defense has the horses to replicate last season’s success, but it hasn’t all come together. The offensive line got pushed around most of the game, giving up five sacks. They had some push in the run game during the third quarter, but Seattle only ran for 89 yards total. That’s not playing Seahawks football. Mike Macdonald brought up how they’re not playing complementary football in his postgame presser. The run game is a massive part of that. This game was a specific brand of frustrating Seahawks football. On one hand they played like garbage and probably should’ve been blown out. On the other, they were in position to win the game and were in my opinion the better team. I didn’t see anything about the 49ers that screamed NFL Superpower. If the Seahawks don’t step on their own junk, they probably win that game by double digits. As it is, they didn’t win the game and now fall farther behind the 49ers in the NFC West. Seattle needs to get their heads out of there a—es if they have any shot of being competitive in the NFC this year.

title: Turnovers continue to be the Seahawks’ biggest problem under Mike Macdonald
summary: The Seattle Seahawks have only lost three games dating back to last November; the San Francisco 49ers, Los Angeles Rams, and Washington Commanders bested Seattle by a combined eight points. You know what else happened? Seattle gave the ball away a lot, namely Sam Darnold, but he’s not the only guilty party. Those three losses […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 11: Renardo Green #0 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates with teammates after an interception against the Seattle Seahawks during the third quarter at Lumen Field on October 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks have only lost three games dating back to last November; the San Francisco 49ers, Los Angeles Rams, and Washington Commanders bested Seattle by a combined eight points. You know what else happened? Seattle gave the ball away a lot, namely Sam Darnold, but he’s not the only guilty party. Those three losses saw the Seahawks lose the turnover battle by a combined 11-4, with Darnold responsible for eight of those giveaways through his interceptions. But while Darnold deserves his fair share of criticism for his clear issue with ball security, the over-arching story continues to be Seattle’s outright negligence in terms of protecting the football. There have been few consistent weaknesses to point to under Mike Macdonald since he became head coach in 2024. The one thing that has been a problem for almost every portion of the Macdonald Era has been turnovers, particularly in high volume. The Seahawks have turned it over at least twice a whopping 20 times since 2024 I tweeted this stat earlier this afternoon and might as well share it here, because you do not want the Seahawks lumped in with the Cleveland Browns in any negative stat. Today marked the 20th time under Mike Macdonald in which the Seahawks turned it over 2+ times. Only the Cleveland Browns have done that more often since 2024. Week 18 vs SF through Week 1 this year is the ONLY time the Seahawks have gone consecutive games without a TO under MM. — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) October 12, 2026 (H/T Stathead ) You read that right (you did read it, right?): Seattle has turned it over at least twice in a game a whopping 20 times since 2024. That’s 20 times out of 39 regular season games and obviously 20 out of 42 overall games when you count the playoffs. About half of every game of the Macdonald era has been a multi-giveaway day for the Seahawks, so much so that one of those games was when Riq Woolen fumbled his last Seahawks interception right back to the Minnesota Vikings. But you can get away with turnovers up 26-0; you can’t do what Seattle has done twice already this season. As already noted in the tweet, the Seahawks have not so much as gone consecutive games without a turnover outside of the stretch from Week 18 against the San Francisco 49ers in 2025 through Week 1 against the New England Patriots this season . The five-game run the Seahawks had to win the NFC West, win the Super Bowl, and win on banner-raising night is the outlier, not the new norm under Macdonald. It’s easy to point to Darnold and Geno Smith (0 interceptions through five games playing in the Jets offense, by the way!) as the culprits. Yes, they have/had their turnover woes and are the main catalysts statistically, but I wish it was as simple as blaming the quarterback. The Seahawks cannot stop fumbling The Seahawks led the NFL in fumbles last season, although a lot of that was down to Sam Darnold strip sacks and some botched QB-center exchanges. They've already fumbled six times in four weeks and have been fortunate to only lose two. It's all about the ball! pic.twitter.com/HRmS7ENIhN — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) October 9, 2026 I wrote this up two days ago and it was prophetic. Three more fumbles, one of which George Holani self-forced, and two were recovered by the 49ers. Seattle has nine fumbles through five games and Darnold doesn’t even have one yet. The running back room has collectively fumbled six times in four games, which is wholly unacceptable. It’s a nice reminder of the airtight ball security Kenneth Walker and Zach Charbonnet showed as a tandem, and we won’t see Charbonnet until Week 7. Rashid Shaheed has fumbled twice on kick returns but been fortunate that neither was lost. Seattle has ranked top 10 in fumbles in each of Macdonald’s seasons, including numero uno in 2025. Fumble recoveries can generally be pinned on luck when you’ve got an oblong ball bouncing crazy directions on the field, but Seattle invites danger by having a high rate of fumbling. And shitty ball security is shitty ball security no matter who’s responsible, and the 2024 Seahawks special teams infamously gave us the duo of Dee Williams and Laviska Shenault Jr, both of whom were axed in December for the single worst display of kick return duties I’ve ever seen. Dee Williams has muffed a couple punts this year but this is first fumble on a kickoff. Regardless, ball security not where it should be for the rookie returner pic.twitter.com/jtgk12P3G2 — Dugar, Michael-Shawn (@MikeDugar) December 1, 2024 Laviska Shenault Jr with his 3rd fumble on a kickoff. This is the second one he’s lost. pic.twitter.com/OQUcxlgRI3 — Dugar, Michael-Shawn (@MikeDugar) December 1, 2024 Neither Sam Darnold nor Geno Smith is Russell Wilson in terms of ball security The upside of Russell Wilson’s style of football when he was Seahawks quarterback was a low interception rate. Unfortunately, the trade-off was a perennially high sack rate and those often functioned as turnovers, but when it was time to throw, Wilson usually took exceptional care of the ball. There were sack fumbles and botched exchanges occasionally, but the Seahawks were a low turnover team and he was a low turnover QB. Just as it was unreasonable to think Geno Smith wouldn’t toss a few careless ones away with his gun-slinging style, the same holds for Darnold. These are two reformed draft busts who are willing to take chances in a way Russ generally didn’t, and frankly neither of them has an extensive track record as a high-level quarterback. Every year in which Sam has been a full-time starter he’s thrown double-digit picks. In 2024 and 2025 he made up for it by being insanely productive and a deadly deep passer. We’re not seeing that right now and there are diminishing returns coming alongside those giveaways. Now, is it reasonable to have Sam not lead the league in turnovers again and be closer to his Minnesota Vikings form in terms of a 2.2% interception rate? Absolutely. But even in calmer waters there is probably an acceptance that even the best version of Darnold is not going to be the type of QB who is a low- or even moderate-turnover guy. This means that the environment around him (a competent run game, other players not fumbling, having a great defense to keep scores favorable) must be stronger than it would be for an elite QB in order to keep positively producing. Seattle only has a great defense and isn’t anywhere close on the other two. The Seahawks are not playing complementary football right now, and what figured to be a squashed problem during their postseason performance has returned in terrifying fashion. If the end of last season was the unusual blip in the trend, then the Seahawks are going to be at risk of this season looking a lot more like 2024 than 2025. You can focus your disappointment and ire primarily at Sam Darnold right now, but the turnovers are a team-wide issue that is seemingly getting worse.

title: Words of Prey, Week 5: Seahawks defeat Seahawks, 32-29
summary: It’s maybe weird to open with a stat. Even when everyone knows it should be points off turnovers. Screw it, let’s open with two almosts — two tantalizing almosts that very nearly mooted every Seattle Seahawks misstep that preceded. Third down, final drive, you’re already at midfield, need a field goal to tie it, touchdown […]
full_text: It’s maybe weird to open with a stat. Even when everyone knows it should be points off turnovers. Screw it, let’s open with two almosts — two tantalizing almosts that very nearly mooted every Seattle Seahawks misstep that preceded. Third down, final drive, you’re already at midfield, need a field goal to tie it, touchdown to win. coulda shoulda woulda — John Frellington (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-10-11T23:44:39.655Z Fourth down, same needs: Seahawks just fell short on 4th down. — JM =^D (@jm539581.bsky.social) 2026-10-11T23:42:26.401Z You likely know the rest of the story — replays on Cooper Kupp’s extended arms were inconclusive, the instructions are to let it stand, the officials followed their own replay rules for once, and the San Francisco 49ers kneeled out a wacky 32-29 victory over the Seattle Seahawks . Yes, wacky even by Seahawks standards. Seattle needed Jaxon Smith-Njigba to catch that ball. But if they don’t run a clumsy, execution-free run play out of their own end zone with 13 seconds left in the first half, it’s probably not necessary. Seattle needed a good replay angle that showed first down at the 40. But if Sam Darnold doesn’t throw two pretty atrocious interceptions earlier, it’s probably not necessary. The Seahawks offense needed to not commit four turnovers, three of them deep in their own end, just like they needed to take better care of the ball in Washington two weeks ago. Against San Fran for the division lead, the Hawks needed the kind of precision, discipline, ball security, pass protection and ingenious playcalling that carried them through the 2025 playoffs all the way to a Super Bowl title. Those are absent. Unfulfilled needs are spelled “L” in the standings. The Seahawks most certainly still have the omnivorous defense, which can only be faulted for one drive, those seven minutes Mike Evans spent parading around Lumen Field as Unelected Dictator of Football. The defense is great. They’re not great enough to pick up after their teammates every single week. No unit is. Because it wasn’t just the giveaways, it was when and where. On your own 18, on your own 11, in your own end zone. The Niners, credit them, killer instinct’d their way to three touchdowns and delivered just enough defense of their own down the stretch to make it stand up. And, dang it all the way to heck, it’s not like the 49ers made it extra hard to beat them. more like dre geeenlawless — John Frellington (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-10-11T21:35:58.162Z Dre Greenlaw lost his head and took an early shower. Deebo Samuel and Jake Cowing exited with injuries after Kyle Juszczyk tore his knee up during the week. Samuel fumbled and Brock Purdy gave one away too. Cowing also forgot how to signal fair catch. Which was pretty cool for everyone not named him. football — John Frellington (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-10-11T20:42:25.057Z What a game for Nehemiah Pritchett, by the way. Had the pick later, which also could’ve been a defining moment had the offense turned the giveaway into seven points. And then, there’s the JSN-shaped elephant in the room. Hell, it’s a whole herd of pachyderms at this point. A) on one ankle he was still great; B) one ankle? shee-it; C) another game Thursday, of course; D) he took a bonus hard hit late and was uncharacteristically slow to get up; E) yikes to that; F) did he drop the late pass in part because of injury; G) well, G) is actually pretty sweet: ON ONE ANKLE I SAID — John Frellington (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-10-11T22:41:27.453Z Furthermore, Sam Darnold wasn’t good. He had flashes, and he made some plays under heavy pressure that showcased levelheadedness and composure, but both picks were inexcusable and he put another ball in harm’s way over the middle to Rashid Shaheed. He took five sacks. us too, Sam — John Frellington (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-10-11T22:20:46.757Z That about sums it up. Recap? Might as well since we’re both here. Q1: Seahawks 7, 49ers 7 Predator : A.J. Barner Prey : Any d-lineman who outweighs him How : Man I love both these clips. In the first one, you get a little presnap motion and H-backer action, if that’s your sort of thing. The second is pure blocking chops, irrelevanting Romello Height right out of the picture. Barner is fast developing into the most complete tight end in Seattle hist… the most complete since Za… gosh. First such instance was on the opening drive — John Frellington (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-10-12T00:45:06.860Z Second beautiful body by Barner in the early going — John Frellington (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-10-11T20:52:50.758Z Action : In what’s become something of a pattern, the Seahawks opponent was granted a free successful run to start the game before being bottled up. CMC’s opening eight-yard gain led nowhere though, because DeMarcus Lawrence’s hands have eyes for the ball and Devon Witherspoon is sticky. Three-and-out it was. In what’s an actual pattern now, Darnold’s very first pass was picked and returned to the 18. Mike Evans would supply well-deserved punishment with a third down scramble catch inside the three and a textbook goal line slant two inches past Josh Jobe’s outstretched glove. 7-0 San Fran before your first drink was even halfway finished. Nothing came of the Seahawks’ following series until the punt return, and if Cowing didn’t see Pritchett that’s not anyone’s problem but his. Given new life at the 24, Seattle puttered toward the end zone; Darnold and Kupp connected on their third down timing so that Emanuel Wilson could breeze into the end zone through the biggest hole he’d see all day. Pictured above! Scoreless defense was played the rest of the quarter by both sides, and the 49ers almost made it a whole quarter without feeling the Wrath of Jaxon. But as the quarter drew to a close, Smith-Njigba got loose behind the defense for 38 big ones. The Seahawks were set up at midfield to start the second, and it kinda felt to summer children like myself, fresh off a Super Bowl parade earlier this very year, that the home team had weathered the worst of the storm. Q2: 49ers 21, Seahawks 13 Predator : Any 49er who attacked the left side of the Seahawks line. Prey : Jalen Sundell-Greg Zabel-Charles Cross, at key moments How : The most egregious example, of course, is the cerebellum-melting play that ended the second quarter. Jalen Sundell didn't fumble the ball, but my dude that is not decidedly NOT how you block people — John Frellington (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-10-11T22:14:33.057Z But Darnold had to escape all day, and there came successive pressures up the left side immediately after the Greenlaw ejection that turned first down just outside the red zone into a long field goal. Action : Seattle’s fifth possession stalled on the consecutive Shaheed targets, the first over the middle into triple coverage, causing personal offense to announcer Tom Brady, who used “turnover worthy play” so we know he’s done rudimentary analytics. Shaheed actually played some decent cornerback on the throw. title: Seahawks vs. Broncos odds: Opening lines for Week 6 matchup
summary: Coming off a heartbreaking 32-29 loss at home to their division rival San Francisco 49ers, the Seattle Seahawks still open as slight favorites against the inconsistent Denver Broncos in Week 6. According to the current lines at FanDuel Sportsbook, the Seahawks are a 2.5-point favorite (-110), with their money line set at -136 and Denver’s […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 11: Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks looks on prior to the game against the San Francisco 49ers at Lumen Field on October 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) | Getty Images Coming off a heartbreaking 32-29 loss at home to their division rival San Francisco 49ers, the Seattle Seahawks still open as slight favorites against the inconsistent Denver Broncos in Week 6. According to the current lines at FanDuel Sportsbook , the Seahawks are a 2.5-point favorite (-110) , with their money line set at -136 and Denver’s at +116 . The line for total points is 42.5, seemingly predicting a defensive shootout between two of the league’s most talented units. Like Seattle, the Broncos also sit at 3-2, and have already dealt with several issues through the first five weeks of the season. After promoting Davis Webb to offensive coordinator, quarterback Bo Nix struggled to adapt with his new system—subsequently leading to head coach Sean Payton taking over play calling duties last week. Although the offense put up 30 points in an upset win over the Los Angeles Rams in Week 3, it otherwise looked stagnant. They’ll face another tough test on Thursday against a Seahawks unit who ranks within the top 10 in fewest yards and points allowed per game. Although Seattle’s conceded 20+ points in each of their last three games, the numbers don’t tell the full story. They were without starting safeties Julian Love and Ty Okada against the Washington Commanders in Week 3 and allowed a touchdown in garbage time the following Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers while also contributing to the team’s astronomical 14 penalties (150 yards). Most recently, two fumbles and an interception put the 49ers in scoring territory on three seperate occasions (all of which resulted in a touchdown), but otherwise, they looked far more complete. Nicknamed “The Dark Side,” the Seahawks defense has struggled so far, but with their penalties cleaned up and no major injuries, they’re a force to be reckoned with—one Nix will certainly have to be ready for. On the other side, Denver’s defense may rank outside the top 10 in yards as well as points allowed per game, but they’ve still been sharp—meaning Seattle will also have their work cut out for them. Since returning from injury in Week 3, Darnold has a disappointing five turnovers and while the production is there, the efficiency isn’t. They posted 300+ yards of total offense against Washington and Los Angeles but were held in check against San Francisco. Now going up against arguably their most complete unit yet, reducing turnovers and scoring early are the keys to coming out on top. In his post game press conference, head coach Mike Macdonald said Zach Charbonnet (knee) is unlikely to make his season debut against the Broncos, so Seattle seemingly won’t receive an upgrade to their backfield yet and appear poised to depend on Emanuel Wilson and George Holani once again—both of whom fumbled in Week 5. The line of 42.5 total points seemingly aligns with a strong defensive showing from both sides and continued offensive struggles. But, coming off a frustrating loss against a division rival, expect the Seahawks to come out hungry and with possibly their strongest outing so far. 12s, make your voices heard on the SB Nation app! title: Winners and Losers from another Seahawks home loss to 49ers
summary: It turns out they can’t all end 41-6. The Seattle Seahawks have now lost five consecutive regular season home games to the San Francisco 49ers, this one the most bizarre and perhaps most damaging. A 32-29 loss that was well deserved given the continued turnover issues and lackluster execution. Seattle is now in a spot […]
full_text: It turns out they can’t all end 41-6. The Seattle Seahawks have now lost five consecutive regular season home games to the San Francisco 49ers, this one the most bizarre and perhaps most damaging. A 32-29 loss that was well deserved given the continued turnover issues and lackluster execution. Seattle is now in a spot that it was not at any point last season: multiple games out of first place without a tiebreaker. The season doesn’t end in October and there’s still a ton of football left, but on current form and remaining schedules it’s hard to argue the Seahawks are poised for an NFC West repeat. Let’s get to Winners and Losers. Seattle Seahawks Winners Byron Murphy II is playing at an All-Pro level The third-year defensive tackle blows up runs, sacks the quarterback (twice, in fact, when it comes to Brock Purdy), and continues to play at an elite level. For my money, he was the best defensive player on the field for Seattle, and he’s going to be paid handsomely as early as next year. Nehemiah Pritchett is balling A special teams walloping of Jacob Cowing to force a turnover, followed by a great interception off of Purdy for his second turnover involvement. Pritchett has been one of the great stories for the Seahawks in 2026, taking full advantage of Riq Woolen’s departure and his insertion into the first-team defensive rotation. Ernest Jones IV anchors the defense There’s not a lot to complain about as far as the Seahawks’ defensive showing (well, except the run defense toward the end and one particular player’s coverage struggles). Jones was so good he even got Dre Greenlaw tossed for that silly headbutt on the sidelines. Ernest picked up another sack, was tight in coverage (part of why George Kittle had a quiet day), and led the team in tackles. When Ernest racks up tackles you know it’s not an empty calories performance. Jason Myers shines and keeps Seattle in the game Five-for-five on field goals, most of which were not chippies. Myers also didn’t miss any extra points, so after a very iffy performance against the Chargers he stepped up and did his job. This is more of the Myers we expect to see on a weekly basis. Seattle Seahawks Losers It’s time to worry about Sam Darnold That was bad. Darnold is seeing ghosts again and it’s a little worrying. He threw two more dreadful interceptions and took some puzzling sacks, such that the few positive plays he made were outweighed by game-damaging negatives. I am not in “Bench Sam Darnold” mode and it’s wild we’re doing this with Drew Lock for a second different era of starting QB, but this version of Darnold is not worth a long-term investment. I question if he came back too early from injury, because he’s not ripping passes with confidence consistently and he is not taking too many really deep downfield shots. Something is off, because this is the worst he’s looked as a Seahawks quarterback. It’s a wrap for George Holani George Holani has fumbled three times before he’s even mustered up a single 10+ yard run. John Schneider praised him for his deputizing for Zach Charbonnet last playoffs but that shouldn’t have been intended for him to get this much run in the offense. I’ve seen enough. Holani isn’t even providing great pass pro, which is one of his strengths. Robert Henry Jr, I hope you learned enough of the playbook because it’s time to get some carries on Thursday. He’s an RB3 who is getting RB2 duties and there’s a chasm that is untenable. Emanuel Wilson’s ball security isn’t any better than Jadarian Price’s That’s two fumbles in as many weeks for Wilson, who scored a touchdown but left a ton of yards on the field by, well, just not being fast. He runs hard but he gets ankle-tackled a ton and has no burst. It’s the fumbling that bugs me because this is the dropoff from having K9 and Zach Charbonnet together with their airtight ball security. There is little to no payoff of an explosive play when Emanuel Wilson turns the ball over. Josh Jobe never had a chance against Mike Evans Much like the Seahawks weren’t going to re-sign Ken Walker, they weren’t going to re-sign Riq Woolen. I get annoyed when people say Riq was CB3 when the snap count reflected a split between Jobe and Woolen as CB2a/2b. Well, Woolen is gone and Jobe is getting treated like a proper CB2, which means no splitting time with anyone else and taking on tougher assignments. Mike Evans is going to Canton. Josh Jobe is probably not. Mike Evans is very tall and physical and uses his body as well as anyone out there. Josh Jobe is a small cornerback. This was a mismatch from the jump and the 49ers exploited to near perfection. I will fault Coach Macdonald and the staff for not getting Jobe on somebody else, but they seem content to keep Nehemiah Pritchett in the slot even though he’s the one with size and some physicality. Trevon Diggs played but sparingly, and he’s a ball hawk at his best but Evans probably bosses him too. The offensive line struggles to open holes and protect Sam Darnold Not that Darnold didn’t make his own pressure at times, but the offensive line was not good. Too many instant pressures on play-action, the Holani fumble for a touchdown came as a result of Jalen Sundell getting blown up in the backfield, and even stalwarts like Charles Cross had some bad moments in pass protection. And please PLEASE stop the Christian Haynes/Beau Stephens rotation. Nothing is being gained out of that. Brian Fleury needs to know his personnel and improve situational awareness Emanuel Wilson should never be getting a toss play to the weaker side of the offensive line while inside his own 10-yard line. That should never happen. It happened and he fumbled. Wilson is not that kind of running back. Now for the Holani fumble: let’s say the 49ers would’ve used their 3 timeouts to force Seattle to keep playing heading into halftime as opposed to kneeling the ball. Outside zone with Holani (again, to the weaker side of the line) is madness. You’re near your own goal line. Get into 22 personnel if you have to and run the ball up the middle. Run a draw play. Run a quick inside give and let time tick away. There is nothing good that can happen from a long developing run play near your own end zone with this set of backs and blockers. A lot of the plays Seattle is botching I put on the players more than Fleury, but the first-year OC is not blameless for the ongoing struggles on third down and getting out of bad field position. Could been a Winner but… Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s drop takes him out of the Winners column JSN has had a couple of odd drops this year. This one I put partially on Darnold for a not great ball, but someone of JSN’s caliber can catch that. It would’ve put the Seahawks in field goal range bare minimum. He still led the team with 5 catches for 102 yards and a touchdown, along with a 16-yard run that was just narrowly a backwards pass. Smith-Njigba played through a dinged up right ankle and still continues to be the focal point of Seattle’s offense, but by my count this is three times in four weeks Smith-Njigba has dropped a catch he normally makes. In many ways, that sums up the Seahawks right now: the best players are not executing properly. Final Notes I think Cooper Kupp was short of the first down, but if they had spotted it at the line to gain then it likely would’ve been upheld . We’ll see the All-22 on Monday, but the nose of the ball crossing the front of the out of bounds line is where the ball must be spotted. Based on that ruling, I believe the spot was fair, as tough as it may be to swallow. It’s the 2019 version of Dre Greenlaw stopping Jacob Hollister short of the end zone. Rashid Shaheed almost broke one again . Nearly a kick return touchdown for Shaheed, and he did at least have an explosive play as a receiver. Still not at 100 receiving yards on the season. No, it was not either re-sign Shaheed or re-sign K9. Stop peddling that narrative. The 49ers are the best team in the NFL until proven otherwise . We make fun…

title: Seahawks injury update: Zach Charbonnet not expected to play vs Broncos
summary: The Seattle Seahawks just lost to the San Francisco 49ers 32-29, with key fumbles from both Emanuel Wilson and George Holani leading to Niners TDs. Seattle has a short week, as they play the Denver Broncos on the road for Thursday Night Football. If you were hoping for an infusion at the RB position with […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks just lost to the San Francisco 49ers 32-29 , with key fumbles from both Emanuel Wilson and George Holani leading to Niners TDs. Seattle has a short week, as they play the Denver Broncos on the road for Thursday Night Football. If you were hoping for an infusion at the RB position with Zach Charbonnet, I have some bad news for you. According to Mike Macdonald, Charbonnet will not play against Denver. “Way too many giveaways at this point in the season,” Mike Macdonald said in his opening remarks. Four turnovers today — they turned into 21 49ers points — gives Seattle nine in five games. Also: Macdonald said the plan right now is that Zach Charbonnet won’t play Thursday. pic.twitter.com/VFcBmHfece — Brady Henderson (@BradyHenderson) October 12, 2026 Charbonnet is still recovering from his torn ACL from last season . He’s been ramping up in practice since his practice window was opened, but is still not quite ready to go yet according to Macdonald. Seattle is in a bit of a gauntlet in their schedule right now, having faced the 49ers with the Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs up next. With the fumble problems and ineffectiveness at times of the Seahawks running game, the hope is that Charbonnet will be a shot in the arm. Unfortunately, that shot will have to wait another week. Wilson, Holani, Velus Jones Jr, and Robert Henry Jr will continue to be the backs moving forward.

title: Seahawks-49ers score: Seattle punished for sloppiness, lose to 49ers in wild game
summary: The Seattle Seahawks are 3-2 and they are in trouble for the NFC West, and maybe the playoffs are a little less certain for the Super Bowl champions given their gauntlet of a schedule over the next three weeks. In a back-and-forth game with way more defense than the final score suggested, the Seahawks fell […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks are 3-2 and they are in trouble for the NFC West, and maybe the playoffs are a little less certain for the Super Bowl champions given their gauntlet of a schedule over the next three weeks. In a back-and-forth game with way more defense than the final score suggested, the Seahawks fell 32-29 to the San Francisco 49ers (5-0) to fall two games back (with no tiebreaker) in the division. Sam Darnold threw two terrible interceptions and generally did not perform well. George Holani’s back-breaking fumble for a touchdown before halftime gave the 49ers an eight-point lead heading into the locker room. Seattle turned it over four times to San Francisco’s three, and the 49ers scored 21 of their 32 points off of turnovers. Brock Purdy and Mike Evans toasted the Seahawks secondary, and by secondary I mean Josh Jobe. Even though Purdy threw a pick and was sacked several times, he made several clutch plays to keep drives alive and give the 49ers a win that, quite possibly when all is said and done, might be one of the moments they look back on if they do finally end their Super Bowl drought. Seahawks vs. 49ers 1st half recap The 49ers started on offense with Christian McCaffrey getting a quality 8-yard run to open the drive. Brock Purdy was nearly picked off on his first throw, then George Kittle dropped what is ordinarily a gimme for him. Seattle got the ball off a three-and-out and gave it right back. Sam Darnold was sacked on second down, setting up a 3rd and 10 pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba that was read and picked by Renardo Green. Immediate red zone possession. Purdy made the Seahawks pay with a third down conversion to Mike Evans on Josh Jobe, followed by a touchdown to Evans with Jobe in coverage. 7-0 49ers. On the board first in Seattle 😤 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/ujAnzDOJr8 — San Francisco 49ers (@49ers) October 11, 2026 If you want a little history repeating itself, the Seahawks recovered a muffed punt early last week against the Los Angeles Chargers. It happened again versus the 49ers , Would ya look at that 💥 @King_Mighty1 pic.twitter.com/7y1RFD4KJT — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 11, 2026 Short field touchdown one way? Short field touchdown the other way. A couple of conversions through the air to Emanuel Wilson and Cooper Kupp gave Seattle a goal-to-go situation. Emanuel Wilson ran right side, with A.J. Barner blocking out Romello Height and clearing the path for a walk-in score. 7-7 . Walk-in TD. Gotta love it 🔥 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/fTtH3PogTA — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 11, 2026 It was a struggle for first downs for both offenses, as you would expect given the caliber of both defenses. For the first time all season, Brock Purdy took a sack. On 3rd and 1, Byron Murphy II closed in and finished the play to bring Purdy down. Byron Murphy making his presence felt 😤 @SFvsSEA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/qVP7fNmJiA — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 The opening quarter ended with Sam Darnold hitting an explosive play to Jaxon Smith-Njigba for 38 yards, as JSN toasted Deommodore Lenoir. JSN is so perfect pic.twitter.com/0BDqxwLUT0 — Billy M (@BillyM_91) October 11, 2026 A screen to JSN gained another 16, although the stat book put this down as a running play. Seattle’s drive stalled out after that JSN touch, but Jason Myers made it 10-7 Seahawks on a 49-yard field goal. Smith-Njigba was notably dinged up when it looked like he tweaked his ankle on that aforementioned play. The 49ers were on the cusp of field goal range when Purdy was sacked for a second time by big Byron Murphy II. A key tackle by Devon Witherspoon on a Purdy scramble meant a field goal attempt was not feasible. Seattle got the ball back inside its own 9, and turned it over AGAIN. Emanuel Wilson with the fumble and Fred Warner with the punch-out. Christian McCaffrey immediately capitalized with an 11-yard touchdown run. 14-10 49ers . Craziness ensued on Seattle’s next scoring drive. Sam Darnold scrambled for a first down but got hit late by Dre Greenlaw for a personal foul penalty. Greenlaw mixed it up with the Seahawks sideline and then headbutted a helmetless Ernest Jones IV. That’s an automatic ejection! 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw was ejected after headbutting Ernest Jones IV on this play. (📺 FOX) pic.twitter.com/6LcENiGtvx — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) October 11, 2026 After the dust settled, George Holani had a wide open catch in the flat and was set for a huge gain… except he dropped the ball on his own and recovered his own fumble. It’s still a first down, but it was a big play opportunity wasted. Consecutive sacks on Sam Darnold made it a longer FG for Jason Myers, who at least was true from 50. 14-13 49ers. The 49ers were unable to score in the two-minute drill, as the Seahawks defense continued to play resolutely. Unfortunately, the offense played incompetently, and instead of kneeling the ball or doing literally anything else that’s a lot safer than an outside zone handoff near the goal line, George Holani fumbled the ball in an effort to run the clock out. Gracen Halton was on the spot for a touchdown before halftime. 21-13 49ers . GRACEN HALTON HAVE A DAY 👏 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/j24NvY7Ygl — San Francisco 49ers (@49ers) October 11, 2026 SERIOUSLY?! Three turnovers in the first half and it could’ve been more. Boos rang around Lumen Field entering the break. Seahawks vs. 49ers 2nd half recap The Seahawks got the ball on offense to start the second half, badly in need of something good to happen. Darnold threw another interception instead, this time on a pass intended for Elijah Arroyo. Another Renardo Green pick. Renardo Green sure knows how to start a half. His second INT of the game! @SFvsSEA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/EilILMpu7E — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 Arroyo took a 15-yard roughness penalty for good measure. The 49ers failed to get a first down, and Eddy Pineiro’s field goal effort drifted way wide left. No points allowed! Seattle took some advantage of the short field with a run-heavy 8-play, 33-yard drive. Jason Myers connected on a third field goal to cut the deficit to 21-16 49ers . PICK! Nehemiah Pritchett with another pick on the season and his second takeaway involvement on the afternoon. It’s Purdy’s first interception since Week 1 and the runback set up Seattle in tremendous field position. Nehemiah Picked-it 👀 @King_Mighty1 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/9NDXq5jn6e — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 11, 2026 What came next? JSN. A beautiful cut to make a move on Fred Warner and turn it into a go-ahead house call. 23-21 Seahawks. YOU ALREADY KNOW WHO IT IS 🍿 Touchdownnnn @jaxon_smith1 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/RUfMbBde6U — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 11, 2026 FUMBLE! Deebo Samuel was tripped up by Drake Thomas and dropped the ball just about as his shin hit the ground. A third 49ers turnover in his messy game! Josh Jobe on the recovery, which led to no first downs but another Jason Myers field goal. 26-21 Seahawks. Right into his hands 😤 @JoshuaMJobe with the fumble recovery. OUR BALL. 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/zhX5jMw2st — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 11, 2026 Brock Purdy and Mike Evans destroyed the Seahawks defense on a 12-play, 74-yard drive. Purdy was 7/8 for 89 yards and a touchdown to Brandin Cooks, an injury-prone receiver ironically called to action due to multiple injuries at the receiver position for the 49ers. Purdy to Evans was good for a two-point conversion, as Josh Jobe could not cope. 29-26 49ers. Rashid Shaheed was oh so close to breaking a big kick return to the house. It still set up great field position for the Seahawks, who utilized Shaheed on a play-action boot for an explosive play near the red zone. The drive stalled after Keion White sacked Darnold, and Myers came on for a tying field goal. 29-29. Smashmouth football by the 49ers offense gave them a clock-killing drive to work into field goal range. Byron Murphy II denied Kaelon…

title: Gracen Halton shines brightest for the 49ers’ defense against the Seahawks
summary: It might have been the highest-scoring defensive struggle in football history, but the San Francisco 49ers came out of Seattle with a 5-0 record. The 49ers outlasted the Seattle Seahawks to win 32-29. It was a true battle of field position, with 31 of the combined 61 points coming off turnovers, and the two teams […]
full_text: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images It might have been the highest-scoring defensive struggle in football history, but the San Francisco 49ers came out of Seattle with a 5-0 record. The 49ers outlasted the Seattle Seahawks to win 32-29. It was a true battle of field position, with 31 of the combined 61 points coming off turnovers, and the two teams combined for a season-high seven turnovers. But as they did last week against Denver, San Francisco survived to stay undefeated and, most importantly, finished the first leg of their NFC West schedule 3-0. With plenty of players to choose from, these are the three stars from the win on Sunday: 3rd star: CB Renardo Green Entering Week 5, Green was the only 49ers player to have an interception. After Sunday, he’s still the only 49er with an interception, but now with three interceptions on the season. Not even a third into the season, and Green has set a new career-high in interceptions. He actually set it with his first pick of Sam Darnold on Sunday. After the 49ers offense opened the game with a three-and-out, Seattle was faced with the same fate on its opening drive. Facing a third-and-10, Darnold looked to get Jaxon Smith-Njigba going early while converting the third down. Green, however, read it the whole way, and the corner jumped the route, making the interception and abruptly ending the Seattle drive. Four plays later, the 49ers offense opened the scoring, jumping out to a 7-0 lead. With the 49ers scoring right before the half (more on that in a second), Seattle looked to close the eight-point gap to open the second half. This time, it took Green only two plays to strike. Trying to push the ball downfield, Darnold forced a pass to Elijah Arroyo on a route that Green practically ran with him. Green snagged the pass and was given an extra 15 yards after an Arroyo stray peanut-punch attempt caught Green. San Francisco couldn’t capitalize on the second pick, as Eddy Pineiro missed a field goal attempt to push the lead to 11. And to add to his game, when matched up against Smith-Njigba, Green was targeted three times, allowing one catch for four yards, plus an interception and a pass breakup—just a quality game from the third-year corner. 2nd star: WR Mike Evans Just a reminder: Evans is doing all of this despite fracturing his ribs a couple of weeks ago. And despite it, he continues to go up and make some of the most physical catches you have ever seen. All it took was one drive for Evans to make his presence felt on Sunday. Entering the 3:02 mark in the third quarter, when the 49ers took the ball following a field goal to give Seattle a five-point lead, Evans had three receptions for 38 yards with a touchdown. An opening-play offensive pass interference hindered the drive, but Evans wiped it out with a 15-yard reception on the first-and-20. The 49ers would get a new set of downs a few plays later before going back to Evans for a gain of nine. And that’s where Evans turned it on. Facing a third-and-10, Purdy fired a laser over the middle to Evans. Evans got Josh Jobe to lose his balance, then went up to catch the ball in front of Julian Love for a 23-yard gain. The 49ers would lose the following first down on a bogus intentional grounding call, setting up a second-and-21. Again, Evans pressed the button. Purdy gave Evans the perfect back-shoulder throw with Jobe in one-on-one coverage, and Evans went up and got it, with Jobe standing no chance, for a 28-yard gain that put the ball inside the Seattle 10-yard line. The 49ers would score two plays later to go up one and opted to go for two to extend the lead to three. Purdy would roll to his left and find nothing before cutting back to his right. The pressure finally closed in and forced a tight-window pass to Evans, and the receiver caught it to give the 49ers a three-point lead. Evans finished the 74-yard drive with 75 receiving yards (not a typo) to close his day out with seven receptions for 113 yards and a touchdown. 1st star: DT Gracen Halton It felt like the rookie defensive tackle was nearing a breakout game in recent weeks and that breakout came on Sunday. Halton started his day innocently enough, stopping Emanuel Wilson for a run for no gain. He followed with his first-career sack, getting to Darnold late in the second quarter for a loss of eight yards. But it was Halton’s play at the end of the second quarter that earned him Sunday’s No. 1 star. With a Corliss Waitman punt nailing Seattle inside its own 5-yard line with 18 seconds left, Mike MacDonald faced a predicament. San Francisco had all three of its timeouts, so three kneels might not have been enough to get to halftime without having to kick the ball back to the 49ers. Instead of taking the risk of a punt to expire the first half, Macdonald opted to play with some aggression, running the ball out of Seattle’s own endzone. George Holani took the carry, and Halton was instantly there, knocking the ball free. Halton had the wherewithal to stay with the play, jumping on the ball in the end zone for the touchdown. Instead of taking things into the half down one, Macdonald’s play-calling blunder led to Halton’s score, giving the 49ers an eight-point lead. And while Seattle was able to wipe that lead by the end of the third quarter, you’d have to wonder how different the outcome would have been without Halton’s play to close the first half. Throughout the season, we will track the three stars of the season by tallying points for each star award using a complex scoring system: three points for being the first star, two for the second, and one for the third. Through Week 5, the standings are: QB Brock Purdy – 7 points WR Mike Evans – 5 points LB Fred Warner – 3 points

title: 15 Winners, 5 losers, and 1 IDK from the 49ers’ statement win over the Seahawks
summary: We witnessed a wild one in Seattle. The San Francisco 49ers’ Week 5 win over the Seahawks was the game of the year. You’d think a 61-point contest would feature two offenses that drove downfield against each other. Neither quarterback threw for more than 200 yards. Despite all of the scoring, only two of those […]
full_text: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images We witnessed a wild one in Seattle. The San Francisco 49ers’ Week 5 win over the Seahawks was the game of the year. You’d think a 61-point contest would feature two offenses that drove downfield against each other. Neither quarterback threw for more than 200 yards. Despite all of the scoring, only two of those drives traveled over 45 yards. Kyle Shanahan improved to 47-8 after winning the turnover battle. The 49ers needed all four of those turnovers to outlast their rivals on the road. The victory required every hand on deck, as attrition and ejections took a toll on the road team. Here are the winners and losers who tell the story of the 49ers’ action-packed, rollercoaster win that kept them undefeated. Winners Mike Evans You could only marvel at what Mike Evans did against a secondary thought to be among the best in the NFL. No one has had any doubt this season about who Brock Purdy wants to throw the ball to. That didn’t change on Sunday. Evans had more targets than the rest of the receivers combined. On late downs, Purdy targeted him 57.1% of the time. In the red zone, Evans got 40% of the targets. Evans finished with seven receptions on 10 targets for 113 yards. Last year, the 49ers struggled to attack the intermediate portion of the field against the Seahawks. This go-round, Evans’ average depth of target was 15.8 yards. They trusted him to get open downfield, and Evans rewarded Purdy time and time again. Seattle looked shell-shocked that Evans was capable of making the plays he did on a 12-play drive that gave the 49ers the lead into the fourth quarter. Evans kicked off with a first-down reception that beat Seattle’s boundary cornerback. A 15-yarder after taking a shot to the ribs on 1st and 20 erased a Brandin Cooks penalty. The drive looked like it would stall after a four-yard loss on second down. But on third and 10, Evans, who Tom Brady criticized for releasing outside on an in-breaking route, was too big for the defender and picked up 23 yards. Evans tortured Jobe one final time, catching a 28-yard sideline pass on 2nd and 21. It was the most impactful drive by a skill player under Kyle Shanahan that I can remember. Corliss Waitman Renardo Green’s first interception came on a 51-yard punt that was fair caught at the 11. Waitman’s next punt was fair caught, and the ensuing drive went three-and-out. Waitman’s third and fourth punts were fair caught inside the 10. Gracen Halton doesn’t score a touchdown without the punter pinning a kick inside the five. There were a couple of special teams blunders, but the punt team was excellent. Keion White The 49ers are built to defend and stop the pass. The defense is at its best when Keion White is on the field, lining up and down the line of scrimmage. Against Seattle’s offensive line, White had a 21.4% pressure rate. He had six pressures in the game, four against different players. White had a pair of run stops and a couple of tackles for loss. He overwhelmed the Seahawks upfront. Through five games, he looks like a supercharged version of what Charles Omenihu gave the Niners in 2023. Jaden Dugger Without Dre Greenlaw, Garret Wallow was the logical replacement. After all, Wallow rotated with Greenlaw throughout the season. If Week 5 taught us anything, it’s that Dugger shouldn’t come off the field. No player grew up and rose to the occasion as Dugger did against the Seahawks. Dugger already had a tackle for loss while flashing before Greenlaw’s ejection. So maybe Raheem Morris sensed Dugger could match Seattle’s physicality. Dugger finished with seven solo tackles, pressured Sam Darnold twice, and minimized the damage in coverage on three targets; he made Darnold look in different directions multiple times and, above all, looked like he belonged on the field in a playoff atmosphere away from home playing a position he hardly reps during the week. Renardo Green Green intercepted Darnold on the same sideline where he was yanked in a playoff last year. His second interception was a carbon copy of the one Purdy threw last season to Jake Tonges against the Seahawks on a similar route. Green had another pass breakup. On four targets, one completion was allowed for a grand total of one yard. The 49ers haven’t capitalized on quarterback mistakes. The cornerbacks haven’t been in positions to “bait” them. Green The offensive line Purdy had the second-longest average time to throw (3.2 seconds) among any quarterback in the NFL this week. He also had the eighth-slowest average time to pressure (2.69 seconds). There were plenty of dropbacks when Purdy had all day to scan the field. There were times when he was sped up and left the pocket prematurely. He was pressured on 38.2% of his dropbacks. For context, Darnold was pressured on 51.4% of his dropbacks. I don’t think Shanahan thought he’d have as much success running the ball, which is why they didn’t. Christian McCaffrey averaged 3.27 yards before contact. Shanahan would’ve run the ball 50 times if he knew his offensive line would generate the movement they did in the second half. Byron Murphy is a special player. He’s going to get his. He took advantage of Connor Colby. But the offensive line held Leonard Williams and Demarcus Robinson in check and prevented them from disrupting the offense. Aside from Colby, Dominick Puni allowed two pressures on 34 pass-blocking snaps, while Jake Brendel, Colton McKivitz, and Trent Williams each had one. Per Sumer Sports, McKivitz led the way with five impact plays. Colby had four, Brendel had 3, Puni had 2, and Williams had one. Losers Dre Greenlaw Greenlaw lasted 25 snaps before his emotions got the best of him. A late hit on Darnold cost the defense 15 yards. It was bad enough that the penalty occurred on Seattle’s sideline. Instead of leaving the sideline and going back to the huddle, Greenlaw looked like he was hunting for trouble. He found some when he came face to face with Ernest Jones. After headbutting Jones, who didn’t have his helmet on, Greenlaw was ejected. Dre put Dugger in a tough spot. We saw Luke Gifford play in 5-man fronts for the first time all season because Dugger filled in for Greenlaw. The domino effect from the ejection could’ve been disastrous. There’s a script where Gifford gets attacked in coverage, and Dugger looks like most rookies in a road environment. Dugger playing well doesn’t absolve Greenlaw of his actions. Deebo Samuel and Jacob Cowing’s ball security The fear is that Samuel’s hamstring injury could be serious, since he was ruled out right away. The fumble may have been a product of the shock of the injury. Nonetheless, it’s his second in as many weeks. The 49ers weren’t as fortunate to recover this one. Cowing’s fumble was less about ball security and more about decision-making. He needs to feel the gunners or see them out of his peripheral vision. His muffed punt should’ve been a fair catch. Deommodore Lenoir and Upton Stout Lenoir and Stout combined to allow eight targets to be completed for eight receptions and 125 yards. Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues to dominate this matchup. He caught all three receptions for 63 yards and a touchdown — the screen was technically Lenoir’s “man.” Lenoir gave up an out route for a first down to Cooper Kupp on third down in the low red zone. He did not seem confident. Stout also missed a tackle. Eddy Pineiro Was 2025 a mirage? Pineiro missed another kick on Sunday. He’s 31st in the NFL in field-goal percentage and 28th in extra-point percentage this season. This team has Super Bowl aspirations. Games are going to come down to the wire, especially in the postseason. The last thing you want is to trot out a kicker who makes only 2 of 3. IDKs Brock Purdy I’m torn about Purdy’s performance. I thought you could pin at least one sack and a couple of the pressures on the quarterback. He sprayed the ball and missed a couple of receivers. He was late and inaccurate on a throw to Jacob Cowing because he…
